Furthermore, when giving these refuges, they may be given by making them connected as one phrase ending with a nasal, thus: ‘buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi’; or they may be given by breaking them apart and making them end with the letter ‘m’, thus: ‘buddhaṃ. saraṇaṃ. gacchāmi.’ In the Andhakaṭṭhakathā, it is said that one should announce one's name, saying: ‘Venerable sir, I, Buddharakkhita, for as long as life lasts, go to the Buddha for refuge.’ This is not found in any other commentary, nor is it stated in the Pāli Canon. It is merely their own preference; therefore, it should not be accepted. For the refuge of one who does not speak in that way is not invalidated.

Anujānāmi bhikkhave [P 5.0970] imehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi pabbajjaṃ upasampadanti imehi buddhaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmītiādīhi evaṃ tikkhattuṃ ubhatosuddhiyā vuttehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi pabbajjañceva upasampadañca anujānāmīti attho. Tattha yasmā upasampadā parato paṭikkhittā, tasmā sā etarahi saraṇamatteneva na ruhati. Pabbajjā pana yasmā parato “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imehi tīhi saraṇagamanehi sāmaṇerapabbajja”nti anuññātā eva, tasmā sā etarahipi saraṇamatteneva ruhati. Ettāvatā hi sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhito hoti.

“I allow, bhikkhus, the going forth and the higher ordination by means of these three refuges.” This means that I allow both the going forth and the higher ordination by means of these three goings for refuge, such as “I go to the Buddha for refuge,” spoken three times with purity on both sides. Here, since the higher ordination was later prohibited, it does not now become valid by mere refuge-taking alone. However, since the going forth was later allowed with the words, “I allow, bhikkhus, the novice’s going forth by means of these three refuges,” it still becomes valid now by mere refuge-taking alone. For by this much, one is established in the state of a novice.

Sace panesa matimā hoti paṇḍitajātiko, athassa tasmiṃyeva ṭhāne sikkhāpadāni uddisitabbāni. Kathaṃ? Yathā bhagavatā uddiṭṭhāni. Vuttañhetaṃ –

But if he is intelligent and of a discerning nature, then the training rules should be recited to him right there on the spot. How? As they were recited by the Blessed One. For it has been said:

“Anujānāmi[V 0.0241], bhikkhave, sāmaṇerānaṃ dasa sikkhāpadāni, tesu ca sāmaṇerehi sikkhituṃ. Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, abrahmacariyā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇī, vikālabhojanā veramaṇī, naccagītavāditavisūkadassanā veramaṇī, mālāgandhavilepanadhāraṇamaṇḍanavibhūsanaṭṭhānā veramaṇī, uccāsayanamahāsayanā veramaṇī, jātarūparajatapaṭiggahaṇā veramaṇī”ti (mahāva. 106).

“I allow, bhikkhus, the ten training rules for novices, and for novices to train in them: Abstinence from the destruction of life; abstinence from taking what is not given; abstinence from unchaste conduct; abstinence from false speech; abstinence from fermented and distilled intoxicants, which are a cause for heedlessness; abstinence from eating at the wrong time; abstinence from dancing, singing, instrumental music, and watching shows; abstinence from wearing garlands, applying scents and cosmetics, and from occasions for adornment and beautification; abstinence from high and luxurious beds; abstinence from accepting gold and silver.”

Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “ahaṃ, bhante, itthannāmo yāvajīvaṃ pāṇātipātā veramaṇisikkhāpadaṃ

In the Andhaka commentary, however, it is said: “Venerable sir, I, so-and-so, for as long as life lasts, undertake the training rule of abstinence from the destruction of life...

Samādiyāmī”ti evaṃ saraṇadānaṃ viya sikkhāpadadānampi vuttaṃ, taṃ neva pāḷiyaṃ na aṭṭhakathāsu atthi, tasmā yathāpāḷiyāva uddisitabbāni. Pabbajjā hi saraṇagamaneheva siddhā, sikkhāpadāni pana kevalaṃ sikkhāparipūraṇatthaṃ [M 0.0252] jānitabbāni. Tasmā tāni pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayena uggahetuṃ asakkontassa yāya kāyaci bhāsāya atthavasenapi ācikkhituṃ vaṭṭati. Yāva pana attanā sikkhitabbasikkhāpadāni na jānāti, saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇaṭṭhānanisajjādīsu pānabhojanādividhimhi ca na kusalo hoti, tāva bhojanasālaṃ vā salākabhājanaṭṭhānaṃ vā aññaṃ vā tathārūpaṭṭhānaṃ na pesetabbo, santikāvacaroyeva kātabbo, bāladārako viya paṭijaggitabbo, sabbamassa kappiyākappiyaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ, nivāsanapārupanādīsu ābhisamācārikesu vinetabbo. Tenāpi “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dasahaṅgehi samannāgataṃ sāmaṇeraṃ [P 5.0971] nāsetu”nti (mahāva. 108) evaṃ parato vuttāni dasa nāsanaṅgāni ārakā parivajjetvā ābhisamācārikaṃ paripūrentena dasavidhe sīle sādhukaṃ sikkhitabbanti.

...I undertake.” Thus the giving of the training rules is stated, just like the giving of the refuges. That, however, is found neither in the Pāli nor in the other commentaries; therefore, they should be recited only according to the Pāli. For the going forth is accomplished by the goings for refuge alone, whereas the training rules are to be known merely for the sake of perfecting the training. Therefore, for one who is unable to learn them in the manner that has come down in the Pāli, it is proper to explain them in any language whatsoever by way of their meaning. However, as long as one does not know the training rules that should be learned, and is not skilled in matters such as wearing the outer robe, carrying the bowl and robes, standing, and sitting, and in the procedures for drinking and eating, one should not be sent to the dining hall, the place for distributing tickets for food, or another such place. One should be made to stay nearby and be looked after like a young child. All that is allowable and unallowable should be explained to him. He should be trained in the minor rules of conduct concerning wearing the lower robe, draping the upper robe, and so on. He also, having completely avoided the ten grounds for expulsion stated later thus—‘I allow, bhikkhus, the expulsion of a novice endowed with ten factors’—and perfecting the minor rules of conduct, should train well in the tenfold virtue.

Pabbajjākathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the going forth is concluded.

Dutiyamārakathā

The Second Discourse on Māra

35. Mayhaṃ kho bhikkhaveti mayā khoti attho. Atha vā yo mayhaṃ yoniso manasikāro, tena hetunāti attho. Puna anuppattāti ettha vibhattiṃ pariṇāmetvā mayāti vattabbaṃ.

35. In the phrase ‘Mayhaṃ kho, bhikkhave,’ the meaning is ‘mayā kho’ (by me, indeed). Or alternatively, the meaning is ‘because of that wise attention of mine.’ Again, in the text ‘anuppattā’ (has been attained), by changing the case ending, it should be stated as ‘mayā’ (by me).

Dutiyamārakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Second Discourse on Māra is concluded.

Bhaddavaggiyakathā

The Account of the Bhaddavaggiyas

36. Bhaddavaggiyāti [V 0.0242] te kira rājakumārā rūpena ca cittena ca bhaddakā vaggabandhena ca vicaranti, tasmā “bhaddavaggiyā”ti vuccanti. Tena hi voti ettha vokāro nipātamatto. Dhammacakkhuṃ udapādīti kesañci sotāpattimaggo, kesañci sakadāgāmimaggo, kesañci anāgāmimaggo udapādi. Tayopi hi ete maggā “dhammacakkhū”ti vuccanti. Te kira tuṇḍilajātake tiṃsadhuttā ahesuṃ, atha tuṇḍilovādaṃ sutvā pañcasīlāni rakkhiṃsu; idaṃ nesaṃ pubbakammaṃ.

36. They were called the ‘Bhaddavaggiyas’ because, it is said, those princes were good in form and mind, and they wandered about in a group. Therefore, they are called the ‘Bhaddavaggiyas.’ Here, in ‘tena hi vo,’ the ‘vo’ is merely a particle. The Dhamma-eye arose: for some, the path of stream-entry arose; for some, the path of once-returning; for some, the path of non-returning. Indeed, all three of these paths are called the ‘Dhamma-eye.’ It is said that in the Tuṇḍila Jātaka, they were thirty drunkards; then, having heard Tuṇḍila’s advice, they observed the five precepts. This was their past good deed.

Bhaddavaggiyakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Bhaddavaggiyas is concluded.

Uruvelapāṭihāriyakathā

The Account of the Miracle at Uruvelā

37. Pamukhoti pubbaṅgamo. Pāmokkhoti uttamo visuddhapañño.

37. `Pamukha` means ‘foremost.’ `Pāmokkha` means ‘supreme, one with purified wisdom.’

38. Anupahaccāti [M 0.0253] avināsetvā. Tejasā tejanti attano tejena nāgassa tejaṃ. Pariyādiyeyyanti abhibhaveyyaṃ, vināseyyaṃ vāti. Makkhanti kodhaṃ. Natveva ca kho arahā yathā ahanti attānaṃ “arahā aha”nti maññamāno vadati.

38. `Anupahacca` means ‘without destroying.’ `Tejasā tejaṃ` means ‘by one’s own power, the nāga’s power.’ `Pariyādiyeyyaṃ` means ‘I would overpower,’ or ‘I would destroy.’ `Makkha` means ‘anger.’ But indeed, an Arahant, conceiving of himself as ‘I am an Arahant,’ would not speak thus.

39. Nerañjarāyaṃ bhagavātiādikā gāthāyo pacchā pakkhittā.

39. The verses beginning with ‘The Blessed One at the Nerañjarā…’ were inserted later.

44-9. Vissajjeyyanti [P 5.0972] sukkhāpanatthāya pasāretvā ṭhapeyyanti attho. “Bhante āhara hattha”nti evaṃ vadanto viya oṇatoti āharahattho. Uyyojetvāti vissajjetvā. Mandāmukhiyoti aggibhājanāni vuccanti.

`Vissajjeyyaṃ` means: I would spread out and place for the purpose of drying. `Āharahattho` means 'one who is bent down as if saying, “Venerable sir, bring forth your hand.”' `Uyyojetvā` means ‘having dismissed.’ `Mandāmukhiyo` refers to ‘fire pots.’

51. Cirapaṭikāti cirakālato paṭṭhāya.

51. `Cirapaṭikā` means ‘starting from a long time ago.’

52. Kesamissantiādīsu kesā eva kesamissaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. Khārikājanti khāribhāro.

52. In `kesamissaṃ` and so forth, hair itself is `kesamissaṃ`. This principle applies everywhere. `Khārikāja` means ‘a carrying pole with a load.’

Uruvelapāṭihāriyakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Miracle at Uruvelā is concluded.

Bimbisārasamāgamakathā

The Account of the Meeting with Bimbisāra

55. Laṭṭhivaneti [V 0.0243] tāluyyāne. Suppatiṭṭhe cetiyeti aññatarasmiṃ vaṭarukkhe; tassa kiretaṃ nāmaṃ. Dvādasanahutehīti ettha ekaṃ nahutaṃ dasasahassāni. Ajjhabhāsīti tesaṃ kaṅkhācchedanatthaṃ abhāsi.

55. `Laṭṭhivana` means in the palmyra palm grove. The Suppatiṭṭha cetiya was at a certain banyan tree; this, it is said, was its name. Here, in `dvādasanahutehi`, one `nahuta` is ten thousand. `Ajjhabhāsī` means he spoke for the purpose of cutting their doubt.

Kisakovadānoti tāpasacariyāya kisasarīrattā “kisako”ti laddhanāmānaṃ tāpasānaṃ ovādako anusāsako samānoti attho. Atha vā sayaṃ kisako tāpaso samāno vadāno ca aññe ovadanto anusāsantotipi attho. Kathaṃ pahīnanti kena kāraṇena pahīnaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – “tvaṃ uruvelavāsiaggiparicārakānaṃ tāpasānaṃ sayaṃ ovādācariyo samāno kiṃ disvā pahāsi, pucchāmi taṃ etamatthaṃ kena kāraṇena tava aggihuttaṃ pahīna”nti.

`Kisakovadāna` means: being an advisor and instructor to ascetics who had received the name `kisaka` due to their emaciated bodies from ascetic practices. Alternatively, it means: being himself a frail ascetic, he was an advisor who advised and instructed others. `Kathaṃ pahīnaṃ` means for what reason was it abandoned. This is what was said: 'You, being yourself the advising teacher of the fire-worshipping ascetics of Uruvelā, having seen what, did you abandon it? I ask you concerning this matter: for what reason was your fire sacrifice abandoned?'

Dutiyagāthāya ayamattho – ete rūpādike kāme itthiyo ca yaññā abhivadanti, svāhaṃ etaṃ sabbampi rūpādikaṃ kāmappabhedaṃ khandhupadhīsu malanti ñatvā yasmā ime yiṭṭhahutappabhedā yaññā malameva vadanti, tasmā na yiṭṭhe [P 5.0973] na hute arañjiṃ; yiṭṭhe vā hute vā nābhiraminti attho.

This is the meaning of the second verse: Sacrifices praise these sensual pleasures, such as forms, and also women. I, having known that this entire variety of sensual pleasures, such as forms, is a defilement in the aggregates as clinging-bases, and because these sacrifices with their varieties of major and minor offerings speak only of defilement, therefore I did not delight in major offerings nor in minor offerings. The meaning is: I did not rejoice in major or minor offerings.

Tatiyagāthāya [M 0.0254] – atha kocarahīti atha kvacarahi. Sesaṃ uttānameva.

In the third verse: `Atha kocarahīti` means `atha kvacarahi` (if so, where then?). The rest is clear.

Catutthagāthāya – padanti nibbānapadaṃ. Santasabhāvatāya santaṃ. Upadhīnaṃ abhāvena anupadhikaṃ. Rāgakiñcanādīnaṃ abhāvena akiñcanaṃ. Tīsu bhavesu alaggatāya yaṃ kāmabhavaṃ yaññā vadanti, tasmimpi kāmabhave asattaṃ. Jātijarāmaraṇānaṃ abhāvena anaññathābhāviṃ. Attanā bhāvitena maggeneva adhigantabbaṃ, na aññena kenaci adhigametabbanti anaññaneyyaṃ. Yasmā īdisaṃ padamaddasaṃ, tasmā na yiṭṭhe na hute arañjiṃ. Tena kiṃ dasseti? Yo ahaṃ devamanussalokasampattisādhake na yiṭṭhe na hute arañjiṃ, so kiṃ vakkhāmi “ettha nāma me devamanussaloke rato mano”ti.

In the fourth verse: `Pada` means the state of Nibbāna. `Santa` because of its tranquil nature. `Anupadhika` due to the absence of the clinging-bases. `Ākiñcana` due to the absence of impediments such as lust. `Asatta` in that very realm of sensual pleasure which sacrifices speak of, due to non-clinging in the three realms of existence. `Anaññathābhāvi` due to the absence of birth, aging, and death. `Anaññaneyya` because it is to be attained only by the path developed by oneself and cannot be attained through another. Because I saw such a state, therefore I did not delight in major offerings nor in minor offerings. What does this show? 'I who did not delight in major or minor offerings which accomplish prosperity in the world of devas and humans, how could I say, “My mind delights here in the world of devas and humans”?'

56. Evaṃ sabbaloke anabhiratibhāvaṃ pakāsetvā atha kho āyasmā uruvelakassapo “sāvakohamasmī”ti evaṃ bhagavato sāvakabhāvaṃ pakāsesi. Tañca kho ākāse vividhāni pāṭihāriyāni dassetvā. Dhammacakkhunti sotāpattimaggañāṇaṃ.

56. Having thus declared his non-delight in the entire world, the Venerable Uruvelakassapa then declared his discipleship to the Blessed One, saying, 'I am a disciple.' And he declared this after displaying various miracles in the sky. `Dhammacakkhu` means the knowledge of the path of stream-entry.

57. Assāsakāti [V 0.0244] āsīsanā; patthanāti attho. Esāhaṃ bhanteti ettha pana kiñcāpi maggappaṭivedhenevassa siddhaṃ saraṇagamanaṃ, tattha pana nicchayagamanameva gato, idāni vācāya attasanniyyātanaṃ karoti. Maggavasenevāyaṃ niyatasaraṇataṃ patto, taṃ paresaṃ vācāya pākaṭaṃ karonto paṇipātagamanañca gacchanto evaṃ vadati.

57. `Assāsakā` means aspiration; that is, wishing. In `Esāhaṃ bhante`: although his going for refuge was accomplished through the penetration of the path, at that point he had only reached a firm decision. Now, he makes the dedication of himself by speech. By the power of the path, he has attained the state of certain refuge. Making that manifest to others by speech and going for the refuge of prostration, he speaks thus.

58. Siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇoti siṅgīsuvaṇṇanikkhena samānavaṇṇo. Dasavāsoti dasasu ariyavāsesu vutthavāso. Dasadhammavidūti dasakammapathavidū. Dasabhi cupetoti dasahi asekkhehi aṅgehi upeto. Sabbadhidantoti sabbesu danto; bhagavato hi cakkhuādīsu kiñci adantaṃ nāma natthi.

58. `Siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇa` means having a complexion similar to that of a `nikkha` of `siṅgī` gold. `Dasavāso` means one who has dwelt in the ten noble abidings. `Dasadhammavidū` means one who knows the ten paths of kamma. `Dasabhi upeto` means one endowed with the ten factors of one beyond training. `Sabbadhidanta` means tamed in all respects; for indeed, in the Blessed One's faculties, such as the eye, there is nothing whatsoever that is untamed.

59. Bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdīti [P 5.0974] bhagavantaṃ bhuttavantaṃ pattato ca apanītapāṇiṃ sallakkhetvā ekasmiṃ padese nisīdīti [M 0.0255] attho. Atthikānanti buddhābhivādanagamanena ca dhammasavanena ca atthikānaṃ. Abhikkamanīyanti abhigantuṃ sakkuṇeyyaṃ. Appākiṇṇanti anākiṇṇaṃ. Appasaddanti vacanasaddena appasaddaṃ. Appanigghosanti nagaranigghosasaddena appanigghosaṃ. Vijanavātanti anusañcaraṇajanassa sarīravātena virahitaṃ. “Vijanavāda”ntipi pāṭho; anto janavādena rahitanti attho. “Vijanapāta”ntipi pāṭho; janasañcāravirahitanti attho. Manussarāhaseyyakanti manussānaṃ rahassakiriyaṭṭhāniyaṃ. Paṭisallānasāruppanti vivekānurūpaṃ.

59. `Bhagavantaṃ bhuttāviṃ onītapattapāṇiṃ ekamantaṃ nisīdi` means: having observed that the Blessed One had finished his meal and had removed his hand from the bowl, he sat down in a certain place. `Atthikānaṃ` means for those who desire to go to pay homage to the Buddha and to listen to the Dhamma. `Abhikkamanīya` means possible to approach. `Appākiṇṇa` means not crowded with people. `Appasadda` means without the sound of speech. `Appanigghosa` means without the clamor of the city. `Vijanavāta` means devoid of the wind from people moving about. There is also the reading `Vijanavāda`; it means devoid of the sound of people within. There is also the reading `Vijanapāta`; it means devoid of the movement of people. `Manussarāhaseyyaka` means a place suitable for the private actions of humans. `Paṭisallānasāruppa` means suitable for seclusion.

Sāriputtamoggallānapabbajjākathā

The Story of the Going Forth of Sāriputta and Moggallāna

60. Sāriputtamoggallānāti sāriputto ca moggallāno ca. Tehi katikā katā hoti “yo paṭhamaṃ amataṃ adhigacchati, so ārocetū”ti te kira ubhopi gihikāle upatisso kolitoti evaṃ paññāyamānanāmā aḍḍhateyyasatamāṇavakaparivārā giraggasamajjaṃ agamaṃsu. Tatra nesaṃ mahājanaṃ disvā etadahosi – “ayaṃ nāma evaṃ mahāsattanikāyo appatte vassasate maraṇamukhe patissatī”ti. Atha ubhopi uṭṭhitāya parisāya aññamaññaṃ pucchitvā ekajjhāsayā paccupaṭṭhitamaraṇasaññā sammantayiṃsu “samma maraṇe sati amatenāpi bhavitabbaṃ, handa mayaṃ amataṃ pariyesāmā”ti amatapariyesanatthaṃ sañcayassa channaparibbājakassa santike saparisā [V 0.0245] pabbajitvā katipāheneva tassa ñāṇavisaye pāraṃ gantvā amataṃ apassantā pucchiṃsu “kiṃ nu kho, ācariya, aññopettha sāro atthī”ti? “Natthāvuso, ettakameva ida”nti ca sutvā “tucchaṃ idaṃ āvuso nissāraṃ, yo dāni amhesu paṭhamaṃ amataṃ adhigacchati, so itarassa ārocetū”ti katikaṃ akaṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ – “tehi katikā katā hotī”tiādi.

60. Sāriputtamoggallāna: that is, Sāriputta and Moggallāna. An agreement was made by them: 'Whoever first realizes the Deathless should inform the other.' It is said that both of them, in their lay life, were known by the names Upatissa and Kolita, and had a retinue of two hundred and fifty youths. They went to a hilltop festival. There, seeing the great crowd of people, this thought arose in them: 'This great multitude of beings, before a hundred years is reached, will fall into the mouth of death.' Then, when the assembly had risen, they questioned each other and, being of the same intention and with the perception of death established, they deliberated: 'Friend, since there is death, there must also be the Deathless. Come, let us seek the Deathless.' For the purpose of seeking the Deathless, they, together with their retinues, went forth under Sañcaya the wandering ascetic. Within just a few days, having reached the limit of his domain of knowledge, and not seeing the Deathless, they asked: 'Teacher, is there any other essence in this?' And hearing, 'Friends, there is no more; this is only this much,' they made an agreement: 'Friend, this is empty, without essence. Now, whoever among us first realizes the Deathless should inform the other.' Therefore it is said: 'An agreement was made by them,' etc.

Pāsādikena abhikkantenātiādīsu itthambhūtalakkhaṇe karaṇavacanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Atthikehi [P 5.0975] upaññātaṃ magganti etaṃ anubandhanassa kāraṇavacanaṃ; idañhi vuttaṃ hoti – “yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ bhikkhuṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandheyyaṃ, kasmā[M 0.0256]? Yasmā idaṃ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhanaṃ nāma atthikehi upaññātaṃ maggaṃ ñāto ceva upagato ca maggo”ti attho. Atha vā atthikehi amhehi “maraṇe sati amatenāpi bhavitabba”nti evaṃ kevalaṃ atthīti upaññātaṃ nibbānaṃ nāma, taṃ magganto pariyesantoti evampettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

In phrases such as 'with pleasing forward progress,' the instrumental case should be understood as indicating the characteristic of such a state. The phrase 'the path known by seekers' is a statement of reason for following. For this is what is said: 'Indeed, I should follow this monk from behind. Why? Because this act of following from behind is a path known and approached by seekers'—such is the meaning. Alternatively, the meaning here should be understood thus: by us, the seekers, it was inferred that 'since there is death, there must also be the Deathless.' Thus, that which is called Nibbāna, which was merely inferred to exist, was sought and searched for.

Piṇḍapātaṃ ādāya paṭikkamīti sudinnakaṇḍe vuttappakāraṃ aññataraṃ kuṭṭamūlaṃ upasaṅkamitvā nisīdi. Sāriputtopi kho “akālo kho tāva pañhaṃ pucchitu”nti kālaṃ āgamayamāno ekamantaṃ ṭhatvā vattapaṭipattipūraṇatthaṃ katabhattakiccassa therassa attano kamaṇḍaluto udakaṃ datvā dhotahatthapādena therena saddhiṃ paṭisanthāraṃ katvā pañhaṃ pucchi. Tena vuttaṃ – “atha kho sāriputto paribbājako”tiādi. Na tāhaṃ sakkomīti na te ahaṃ sakkomi. Ettha ca paṭisambhidāppatto thero na ettakaṃ na sakkoti. Atha kho imassa dhammagāravaṃ uppādessāmīti sabbākārena buddhavisaye avisayabhāvaṃ gahetvā evamāha.

Having taken his alms-food and returned, as described in the Sudinnakaṇḍa, he approached the base of a certain wall and sat down. Sāriputta, thinking, 'It is not yet the time to ask a question,' waited for the appropriate moment. Standing to one side, in order to fulfill his duties, he gave water from his own water pot to the Elder who had completed his meal. After the Elder had washed his hands and feet, Sāriputta exchanged friendly greetings with him and asked his question. Therefore it is said: 'Then the wanderer Sāriputta...' etc. 'I am not able' means 'I am not able for you.' Here, the Elder, who had attained the analytical knowledges, was not incapable of this much. Rather, thinking, 'I will arouse reverence for the Dhamma in him,' and grasping in all aspects that the domain of the Buddha was not his own domain, he spoke thus.

Ye dhammā hetuppabhavāti hetuppabhavā nāma pañcakkhandhā; tenassa dukkhasaccaṃ dasseti. Tesaṃ hetuṃ tathāgato āhāti tesaṃ hetu nāma samudayasaccaṃ; tañca tathāgato āhāti dasseti. Tesañca yo nirodhoti tesaṃ ubhinnampi saccānaṃ yo appavattinirodho; tañca tathāgato āhāti attho. Tenassa nirodhasaccaṃ dasseti. Maggasaccaṃ panettha sarūpato adassitampi nayato dassitaṃ hoti, nirodhe hi vutte tassa sampāpako maggo vuttova hoti. Atha vā tesañca yo nirodhoti ettha tesaṃ yo nirodho ca nirodhupāyo cāti evaṃ dvepi saccāni dassitāni hontīti. Idāni tamevatthaṃ paṭipādento āha – “evaṃvādī mahāsamaṇo”ti.

'Those phenomena that originate from a cause'—'originating from a cause' refers to the five aggregates. By this, he shows him the truth of suffering. 'The Tathāgata has declared their cause'—this shows that their cause is the truth of origin, and that the Tathāgata has declared it. 'And their cessation'—this means the non-arising cessation of both those truths; and the meaning is that the Tathāgata has declared that. By this, he shows him the truth of cessation. Here, the truth of the path, though not shown in its own form, is shown by implication; for when cessation is stated, the path that leads to it is as good as stated. Alternatively, in the phrase 'and their cessation', both truths are shown: their cessation and the means to cessation. Now, establishing that very meaning, he said: 'Thus speaks the great ascetic.'

Eseva dhammo yadi tāvadevāti sacepi ito uttari natthi, ettakameva idaṃ sotāpattiphalamattameva pattabbaṃ, tathāpi eso eva dhammoti attho. Paccabyattha padamasokanti yaṃ [P 5.0976] mayaṃ [V 0.0246] pariyesamānā vicarāma, taṃ padamasokaṃ paṭividdhāttha tumhe; pattaṃ taṃ tumhehīti attho. Adiṭṭhaṃ abbhatītaṃ bahukehi kappanahutehīti amhehi nāma idaṃ padaṃ bahukehi [M 0.0257] kappanahutehi adiṭṭhameva abbhatītaṃ; iti tassa padassa adiṭṭhabhāvena dīgharattaṃ attano mahājānibhāvaṃ dīpeti.

'This is the Dhamma, even if only this much'—the meaning is: even if there is nothing further than this, and only this much, just the fruit of stream-entry, is to be attained, even so, this itself is the Dhamma. 'You have penetrated the sorrowless state'—the meaning is: that sorrowless state for which we wander searching, you have penetrated; you have attained it. 'Unseen, passed by for many nahutas of kappas'—by us, this state has been unseen and passed by for many nahutas of kappas. Thus, by mentioning the unseen nature of that state, he reveals his own great loss over a long time.

62. Gambhīre ñāṇavisayeti gambhīre ceva gambhīrassa ca ñāṇassa visayabhūte. Anuttare upadhisaṅkhayeti nibbāne. Vimutteti tadārammaṇāya vimuttiyā vimutte. Byākāsīti “etaṃ me sāvakayugaṃ bhavissati aggaṃ bhaddayuga”nti vadanto sāvakapāramiññāṇe byākāsi. Sāva tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ upasampadā ahosīti sā ehibhikkhūpasampadāyeva tesaṃ upasampadā ahosi. Evaṃ upasampannesu ca tesu mahāmoggallānatthero sattahi divasehi arahatte patiṭṭhito, sāriputtatthero aḍḍhamāsena.

62. “In the profound sphere of knowledge” means: in that which is both profound and is the object of profound knowledge. “In the unsurpassed cessation of attachments” means: in Nibbāna. “Liberated” means: liberated by the liberation that has that as its object. “He declared” means: saying, “This pair of disciples of mine will be the foremost, auspicious pair,” he declared it in the knowledge of the perfection of a disciple. “That was the ordination of those venerables” means: that very “Come, bhikkhu” ordination was their ordination. And among them thus ordained, the Elder Mahāmoggallāna was established in Arahantship in seven days, and the Elder Sāriputta in half a month.

Atīte kira anomadassī nāma buddho loke udapādi. Tassa sarado nāma tāpaso sake assame nānāpupphehi maṇḍapaṃ katvā pupphāsaneyeva bhagavantaṃ nisīdāpetvā bhikkhusaṅghassāpi tatheva maṇḍapaṃ katvā pupphāsanāni paññapetvā aggasāvakabhāvaṃ patthesi. Patthayitvā ca sirīvaḍḍhassa nāma seṭṭhino pesesi “mayā aggasāvakaṭṭhānaṃ patthitaṃ, tvampi āgantvā ekaṃ ṭhānaṃ patthehī”ti. Seṭṭhi nīluppalamaṇḍapaṃ katvā buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ, tattha bhojetvā dutiyasāvakabhāvaṃ patthesi. Tesu saradatāpaso sāriputtatthero jāto, sirīvaḍḍho mahāmoggallānattheroti idaṃ nesaṃ pubbakammaṃ.

It is said that in the past, a Buddha named Anomadassī arose in the world. In his time, a hermit named Sarada, having made a pavilion with various flowers in his own hermitage, and having seated the Blessed One on a flower seat, and having likewise made a pavilion for the Saṅgha of bhikkhus and prepared flower seats, aspired to the state of chief disciple. And having aspired, he sent a message to a wealthy merchant named Sirīvaḍḍha, saying: “I have aspired to the position of chief disciple; you too should come and aspire to a position.” The wealthy merchant, having made a blue lotus pavilion and fed the Saṅgha of bhikkhus with the Buddha at its head there, aspired to the state of second disciple. Of these two, the hermit Sarada became the Elder Sāriputta, and Sirīvaḍḍha became the Elder Mahāmoggallāna. This was their past kamma.

63. Aputtakatāyātiādīsu yesaṃ puttā pabbajanti, tesaṃ aputtakatāya. Yāsaṃ patī pabbajanti, tāsaṃ vedhabyāya vidhavābhāvāya. Ubhayenāpi kulupacchedāya. Sañcayānīti sañcayassa antevāsikāni. Magadhānaṃ giribbajanti magadhānaṃ janapadassa giribbajaṃ nagaraṃ. Mahāvīrāti mahāvīriyavanto. Nayamānānanti nayamānesu. Bhummatthe [P 5.0977] sāmivacanaṃ, upayogatthe vā. Kā usūyā vijānatanti dhammena nayantīti evaṃ vijānantānaṃ kā issā.

63. In phrases such as “for childlessness”: for the childlessness of those whose sons go forth. For those whose husbands go forth: for their widowhood, their state of being a widow. In both cases, it is for the cutting off of the family line. “Of Sañjaya” means: the resident pupils of Sañjaya. “Giribbaja of the Magadhans” means: the city Giribbaja of the Magadhan country. “Great heroes” means: those possessing great energy. “Of those who are leading” means: among those who are leading. This is a genitive used in the sense of the locative, or in the sense of the accusative. “What envy for one who understands?” means: for those who understand thus, “They lead by the Dhamma,” what envy could there be?

Sāriputtamoggallānapabbajjākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Account of the Going Forth of Sāriputta and Moggallāna is Concluded.

Upajjhāyavattakathā

The Account of the Duties toward a Preceptor

64-5. Anupajjhāyakāti [V 0.0247] vajjāvajjaṃ upanijjhāyakena garunā virahitā. Anākappasampannāti na ākappena sampannā; samaṇasāruppācāravirahitāti attho[M 0.0258]. Uparibhojaneti bhojanassa upari. Uttiṭṭhapattanti piṇḍāya caraṇakapattaṃ. Tasmiñhi manussā ucchiṭṭhasaññino, tasmā uttiṭṭhapattanti vuttaṃ. Atha vā uṭṭhahitvā pattaṃ upanāmentīti evampettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Anujānāmi bhikkhave upajjhāyanti upajjhāyaṃ gahetuṃ anujānāmīti attho. Puttacittaṃ upaṭṭhapessatīti putto me ayanti evaṃ gehassitapemavasena cittaṃ upaṭṭhapessati. Esa nayo dutiyapadepi. Sagāravā sappatissāti garubhāvañceva jeṭṭhakabhāvañca upaṭṭhapetvā. Sabhāgavuttinoti sabhāgajīvikā. Sāhūti vātiādīni pañca padāni upajjhāyabhāvasampaṭicchanavevacanāni. Kāyena viññāpetīti evaṃ saddhivihārikena “upajjhāyo me bhante hohī”ti tikkhattuṃ vutte sace upajjhāyo “sāhū”tiādīsu pañcasu padesu yassa kassaci padassa vasena kāyena vā vācāya vā kāyavācāhi vā “gahito tayā upajjhāyo”ti upajjhāyaggahaṇaṃ viññāpeti, gahito hoti upajjhāyo. Idameva hi ettha upajjhāyaggahaṇaṃ, yadidaṃ upajjhāyassa imesu pañcasu padesu yassa kassaci padassa vācāya vā sāvanaṃ kāyena vā atthaviññāpananti. Keci pana sādhūti sampaṭicchanaṃ sandhāya vadanti. Na taṃ pamāṇaṃ, āyācanadānamattena hi gahito hoti upajjhāyo, na ettha sampaṭicchanaṃ aṅgaṃ. Saddhivihārikenāpi na kevalaṃ iminā me padena upajjhāyo gahitoti ñātuṃ vaṭṭati. “Ajjatagge dāni thero mayhaṃ bhāro, ahampi therassa bhāro”ti idampi ñātuṃ vaṭṭati.

64-5. 'Without a preceptor' means devoid of a senior who examines what is blameworthy and blameless. 'Not endowed with proper deportment' means not endowed with deportment; the meaning is, devoid of conduct befitting an ascetic. 'After the meal' means after the meal. 'Uttiṭṭhapatta' refers to the bowl for wandering for alms. Indeed, people perceive it as having leftovers, hence it is called 'uttiṭṭhapatta'. Alternatively, the meaning here should be understood as: they present the bowl after rising. 'I allow, bhikkhus, a preceptor' means: I allow the taking of a preceptor. 'He will establish a son’s attitude' means he will establish in his mind, 'This is my son,' with affection rooted in household life. This same method applies to the second term as well. 'Respectful and reverential' means having established reverence and the state of being a senior. 'Living in fellowship' means having a similar livelihood. The five phrases beginning with 'Very well' are synonyms for accepting the state of being a preceptor. 'Makes known by body' means: when a pupil says three times, 'Venerable sir, be my preceptor,' if the preceptor, by means of any of these five phrases—whether by body, speech, or both—makes known the taking of the preceptor, saying, 'The preceptor is taken by you,' then the preceptor is taken. For this indeed is the taking of a preceptor here: that is, the preceptor’s making it heard by speech or making the meaning known by body through any of these five phrases. Some, however, speak with reference to the pupil's acceptance by saying 'Very well.' That is not the standard, for the preceptor is taken merely by the act of requesting and giving; the pupil's acceptance is not a factor here. The pupil, too, should not know only, 'The preceptor has been taken by me with this phrase.' It is also fitting to know this: 'From today onwards, the elder is my responsibility, and I too am the elder’s responsibility.'

66. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanāti yaṃ vuttaṃ sammā vattitabbanti, tatra ayaṃ sammāvattanā. Kālasseva uṭṭhāya upāhanā omuñcitvāti sacassa paccūsakāle caṅkamanatthāya vā dhotapādapariharaṇatthāya vā paṭimukkā upāhanā pādagatā honti, tā kālasseva uṭṭhāya apanetvā. Dantakaṭṭhaṃ dātabbanti mahantaṃ majjhimaṃ khuddakanti [P 5.0978] tīṇi dantakaṭṭhāni upanetvā tato yaṃ tīṇi divasāni gaṇhāti, catutthadivasato paṭṭhāya tādisameva dātabbaṃ. Sace aniyamaṃ katvā yaṃ vā taṃ vā gaṇhāti, atha yādisaṃ labhati tādisaṃ dātabbaṃ.

66. Regarding 'Herein, this is the proper conduct': With reference to the statement 'one should conduct oneself properly,' this is that proper conduct. 'Rising early and removing the sandals' means: if at dawn, for the purpose of walking meditation or for protecting the washed feet, sandals that have been put on are on his feet, then rising early, he should remove them. 'A toothstick should be given' means: three toothsticks—large, medium, and small—should be presented, and from these, whichever one he takes for three days, from the fourth day onward, that same kind should be given. If, making no fixed rule, he takes whichever one, then whatever kind is obtained should be given.

Mukhodakaṃ dātabbanti sītañca uṇhañca udakaṃ upanetvā tato yaṃ tīṇi divasāni vaḷañjeti, catutthadivasato paṭṭhāya tādisameva mukhadhovanodakaṃ [M 0.0259] dātabbaṃ. Sace aniyamaṃ katvā yaṃ vā taṃ vā gaṇhāti, atha yādisaṃ labhati tādisaṃ dātabbaṃ. Sace duvidhampi vaḷañjeti, duvidhampi [V 0.0248] upanetabbaṃ. Udakaṃ mukhadhovanaṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā vaccakuṭito paṭṭhāya sammajjitabbaṃ. There vaccakuṭiṃ gate pariveṇaṃ sammajjitabbaṃ; evaṃ pariveṇaṃ asuññaṃ hoti. There vaccakuṭito anikkhanteyeva āsanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ. Sarīrakiccaṃ katvā āgantvā tasmiṃ nisinnassa “sace yāgu hotī”tiādinā nayena vuttavattaṃ kātabbaṃ. Uklāpoti kenaci kacavarena saṅkiṇṇo, sace pana añño kacavaro natthi, udakaphusitāneva honti, hatthenapi pamajjitabbo.

'Water for washing the face should be given' means: both cold and hot water should be presented. Then, whichever he uses for three days, from the fourth day onward, that same kind of water for washing the face should be given. If, making no fixed rule, he takes whichever one, then whatever kind is obtained should be given. If he uses both kinds, both should be presented. After placing the water in the place for washing the face, sweeping should begin from the latrine. When the elder has gone to the latrine, the precinct should be swept; thus, the precinct will not be unattended. A seat should be prepared even before the elder has come out from the latrine. After he has attended to his bodily needs and returned, for him who is seated there, the prescribed duties should be performed according to the method beginning with, 'If there is gruel...'. 'Uklāpa' means soiled with some rubbish. If, however, there is no other rubbish and only drops of water are present, it should be wiped even with the hand.

Saguṇaṃ katvāti dve cīvarāni ekato katvā, tā ekato katā dvepi saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā. Sabbañhi cīvaraṃ saṅghaṭitattā “saṅghāṭī”ti vuccati. Tena vuttaṃ – “saṅghāṭiyo dātabbā”ti. Nātidūre gantabbaṃ nāccāsanneti ettha sace upajjhāyaṃ nivattitvā olokentaṃ ekena vā dvīhi vā padavītihārehi sampāpuṇāti, ettāvatā nātidūre nāccāsanne gato hotīti veditabbaṃ. Pattapariyāpannaṃ paṭiggahetabbanti sace upajjhāyena bhikkhācāre yāguyā vā bhatte vā laddhe patto uṇho vā bhāriko vā hoti, attano pattaṃ tassa datvā so patto gahetabboti attho. Na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathā opātetabbāti antaraghare vā aññatra vā bhaṇamānassa aniṭṭhite tassa vacane aññā kathā na samuṭṭhāpetabbā. Ito paṭṭhāya ca pana yattha yattha nakārena paṭisedho kariyati, sabbattha dukkaṭāpatti veditabbā. Ayañhi khandhakadhammatā. Āpattisāmantā bhaṇamānoti padasodhammaduṭṭhullādivasena āpattiyā āsannavācaṃ bhaṇamāno. Nivāretabboti “kiṃ bhante īdisaṃ nāma vattuṃ vaṭṭati, āpatti [P 5.0979] na hotī”ti evaṃ pucchantena viya vāretabbo. Vāressāmīti pana katvā “mahallaka, mā evaṃ bhaṇā”ti na vattabbo.

'Saguṇaṃ katvā' means having made two robes into one; those two robes made into one should both be given as saṅghāṭis. Indeed, any robe, because it is stitched together, is called a 'saṅghāṭī'. Therefore, it is said: 'saṅghāṭis should be given.' 'One should not go too far, nor too near': regarding this, if, turning back and looking, one can reach the preceptor in one or two steps, by that much it should be known that one has gone not too far and not too near. 'What is contained in the bowl should be received' means: if, when the preceptor has received gruel or rice on the alms round, the bowl is hot or heavy, one should give one's own bowl to him and that bowl should be taken; this is the meaning. 'One should not interrupt the preceptor while he is speaking by interjecting talk' means: whether inside a house or elsewhere, while he is speaking, before his words are finished, another topic of conversation should not be raised. Furthermore, from this point onwards, wherever a prohibition is made with the particle 'na', in every such case a dukkaṭa offense should be understood. Indeed, this is the nature of the Khandhakas. 'Speaking on the verge of an offense' means speaking words close to an offense, by way of a padasodhamma offense, a duṭṭhulla offense, and so on. 'He should be restrained' means: he should be stopped as if by one asking, 'Venerable sir, is it proper to say such a thing? Is there not an offense?' However, having decided, 'I will restrain him,' one should not say, 'Old man, do not speak thus.'

Paṭhamataraṃ āgantvāti sace āsanne gāmo hoti, vihāre vā gilāno bhikkhu hoti, gāmato paṭhamataraṃ āgantabbaṃ. Sace dūre gāmo hoti, upajjhāyena saddhiṃ āgacchanto natthi, teneva saddhiṃ gāmato nikkhamitvā cīvarena pattaṃ veṭhetvā antarāmaggato paṭhamataraṃ āgantabbaṃ[M 0.0260]. Evaṃ nivattantena paṭhamataraṃ āgantvā āsanapaññāpanādi sabbaṃ kiccaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sinnaṃ hotīti tintaṃ sedaggahitaṃ. Caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvāti kaṇṇaṃ caturaṅgulappamāṇaṃ atirekaṃ katvā evaṃ cīvaraṃ saṃharitabbaṃ. Kiṃ kāraṇā? Mā majjhe bhaṅgo ahosīti. Samaṃ katvā saṃharitassa hi majjhe bhaṅgo hoti, tato niccaṃ bhijjamānaṃ dubbalaṃ hoti taṃ nivāraṇatthametaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā yathā ajja bhaṅgaṭṭhāneyeva sve na bhijjati, tathā divase divase caturaṅgulaṃ ussāretvā saṃharitabbaṃ. Obhoge kāyabandhanaṃ kātabbanti kāyabandhanaṃ saṃharitvā cīvarabhoge pakkhipitvā ṭhapetabbaṃ.

'One should arrive earlier' means: if the village is nearby, or if there is a sick bhikkhu in the monastery, one should return from the village earlier. If the village is far away and there is no one coming with the preceptor, then one should leave the village with him, wrap the bowl in the robe, and return earlier from partway along the road. Thus, when returning, having arrived earlier, all duties such as preparing the seat should be done. 'It is damp' means it is soaked, seized by sweat. 'Having raised the corner by four finger-widths' means having made the corner exceed by a measure of four finger-widths, the robe should be folded thus. For what reason? So that a crease does not form in the middle. For of a robe folded evenly, a crease forms in the middle; from that, being constantly creased, it becomes weak. This was said to prevent that. Therefore, so that it is not creased tomorrow in the very same place it was creased today, it should be folded each day by raising it four finger-widths. 'The waistband should be placed in the fold' means the waistband should be folded, placed inside the fold of the robe, and kept there.

Sace [V 0.0249] piṇḍapāto hotīti ettha yo gāmeyeva vā antaraghare vā paṭikkamane vā bhuñjitvā āgacchati, piṇḍaṃ vā na labhati, tassa piṇḍapāto na hoti, gāme abhuttassa pana laddhabhikkhassa vā hoti; tasmā “sace piṇḍapāto hotī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Sacepi tassa na hoti, bhuñjitukāmo ca hoti, udakaṃ datvā attanā laddhatopi piṇḍapāto upanetabbo. Pānīyena pucchitabboti bhuñjamāno tikkhattuṃ “pānīyaṃ bhante āhariyatū”ti pānīyena pucchitabbo. Sace kālo atthi, upajjhāye bhutte sayaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ. Sace upakaṭṭho kālo, pānīyaṃ upajjhāyassa santike ṭhapetvā sayampi bhuñjitabbaṃ.

Regarding 'If there is almsfood': here, for a preceptor who returns having eaten in the village itself, or inside a house, or in a dining hall, or who did not receive alms, for him there is no almsfood. But for one who has not eaten in the village or for one who has received alms, there is almsfood; therefore, 'If there is almsfood,' etc., was said. Even if he has none, but wishes to eat, after giving water, the almsfood obtained by oneself should be offered. 'He should be asked about water' means while he is eating, he should be asked three times about water, saying, 'Venerable sir, shall water be brought?' If there is time, after the preceptor has eaten, one should eat oneself. If the time is near, after placing water near the preceptor, one should also eat oneself.

Anantarahitāyāti taṭṭikadhammakhaṇḍādīsu yena kenaci anatthatāya paṃsusakkharamissāya bhūmiyā pattho na ṭhapetabboti attho. Sace pana kāḷavaṇṇakatā vā sudhābaddhā vā hoti nirajamattikā, tathārūpāya bhūmiyā [P 5.0980] ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati. Dhotavālikāyapi ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati. Paṃsurajasakkharādīsu na vaṭṭati. Tatra pana paṇṇaṃ vā ādhārakaṃ vā ṭhapetvā tatra nikkhipitabbo. Pārato antaṃ orato bhoganti idaṃ cīvaravaṃsādīnaṃ heṭṭhā hatthaṃ pavesetvā abhimukhena hatthena saṇikaṃ nikkhipanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Ante pana gahetvā bhogena cīvaravaṃsādīnaṃ upari nikkhipantassa bhittiyaṃ bhogo paṭihaññati, tasmā tathā na kātabbaṃ.

'On an uncovered (surface)' means the bowl should not be placed on ground mixed with dust and gravel that is not covered by something like a mat or a piece of leather. However, if the ground is made black or is bound with plaster, and is without dust or fine earth, it is permissible to place it on such ground. It is also permissible to place it on washed sand. It is not permissible on surfaces with dust, powder, gravel, and so on. There, however, having placed a leaf or a bowl-stand, the bowl should be set down on that. 'The end from the far side, the fold from the near side': this was said for the purpose of gently placing it by inserting the hand underneath the robe-pole, etc., with the hand facing oneself. However, for one who, having taken the end, tosses it by the folded part onto the robe-pole, etc., the fold strikes the wall; therefore, it should not be done in that way.

Cuṇṇaṃ sannetabbanti nhānacuṇṇaṃ udakena temetvā piṇḍi kātabbā. Ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbanti ekasmiṃ niddhūme ṭhāne ṭhapetabbaṃ. Jantāghare parikammaṃ nāma [M 0.0261] aṅgāramattikauṇhodakadānādikaṃ sabbaṃ kiccaṃ. Udakepi parikammanti aṅgapaccaṅgaghaṃsanādikaṃ sabbaṃ kiccaṃ. Pānīyena pucchitabboti jantāghare uṇhasantāpena pipāsā hoti, tasmā pucchitabbo.

'The powder should be kneaded' means bathing powder should be moistened with water and a lump should be made. 'It should be put aside' means it should be placed in a smoke-free place. 'Service in the steam-bath house' means all duties such as giving charcoal, clay, and warm water. 'Service in the water' means all duties such as rubbing the major and minor limbs. 'He should be asked about drinking water' means in the steam-bath house, thirst arises from the intense heat; therefore, he should be asked.

Sace ussahatīti sace pahoti; na kenaci gelaññena abhibhūto hoti; agilānena hi saddhivihārikena saṭṭhivassenāpi sabbaṃ upajjhāyavattaṃ kātabbaṃ, anādarena akarontassa vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ. Nakārapaṭisaṃyuttesu pana padesu gilānassāpi paṭikkhittakiriyaṃ karontassa dukkaṭameva. Appaṭighaṃsantenāti bhūmiyaṃ appaṭighaṃsantena. Kavāṭapiṭṭhanti kavāṭañca piṭṭhasaṅghātañca acchupantena. Santānakanti yaṃkiñci kīṭakulāvakamakkaṭakasuttādi. Ullokā paṭhamaṃ ohāretabbanti ullokato paṭhamaṃ ullokaṃ ādiṃkatvā avaharitabbanti attho. Ālokasandhikaṇṇabhāgāti ālokasandhibhāgā ca kaṇṇabhāgā ca antarabāhiravātapānakavāṭakāni ca gabbhassa ca cattāro koṇā pamajjitabbāti attho.

'If he is able' means if he is capable, not overcome by any illness. For by a co-resident who is not ill, even one of sixty years' standing, all duties toward the preceptor must be done. For one who does not do them out of disrespect, there is an offense of wrong-doing for the breach of duty. However, in passages connected with the negative particle, for one who is ill, doing a prohibited action is still an offense of wrong-doing. 'Without scraping' means without scraping against the floor. 'The door and its frame' means without touching the door-leaf and the door-frame. 'Cobwebs' means any kind of small insect nests, spiderwebs, and so on. 'Should be cleared first from the ceiling' means they should be removed first from the ceiling, beginning with the ceiling; this is the meaning. 'The window-joints and corners' means the parts of the window shutters, the corner parts, the inner and outer window-leaves, and the four corners of the cell should be cleaned; this is the meaning.

Yathāpaññattaṃ [V 0.0250] paññapetabbanti yathā paṭhamaṃ paññattaṃ ahosi, tatheva paññapetabbaṃ. Etadatthameva hi yathāpaññattaṃ sallakkhetvā nīharitvā ekamantaṃ nikkhipitabbanti purimavattaṃ paññattaṃ. Sace pana paṭhamaṃ ajānantena kenaci paññattaṃ ahosi, samantato bhittiṃ dvaṅgulamattena vā tivaṅgulamattena vā mocetvā paññapetabbaṃ. Idañhi paññāpanavattaṃ. Sace kaṭasārako hoti atimahanto ca, chinditvā koṭiṃ nivattetvā bandhitvā [P 5.0981] paññapetabbo. Sace koṭiṃ nivattetvā bandhituṃ na jānāti, na chinditabbo. Puratthimā vātapānā thaketabbāti puratthimāya vātapānā thaketabbā. Evaṃ sesāpi vātapānā thaketabbā.

'It should be laid out as it was arranged' means as it was laid out before, so it should be laid out. For this very purpose, the previous duty concerning 'it should be noted as it was arranged, taken out, and put aside' was prescribed. If, however, it was previously laid out by someone who did not know how, it should be laid out leaving a space of two or three finger-widths from the wall all around. For this is the duty concerning laying out. If there is a mat and it is too large, it should be cut, its edge turned back and bound, and then laid out. If one does not know how to turn back the edge and bind it, it should not be cut. 'The eastern windows should be closed' means the windows in the east should be closed. In the same way, the remaining windows should also be closed.

Vūpakāsetabboti aññattha netabbo. Vūpakāsāpetabboti añño bhikkhu vattabbo “theraṃ gahetvā aññattha gacchā”ti vivecetabbanti vissajjāpetabbaṃ. Vivecāpetabbanti añño vattabbo “theraṃ diṭṭhigataṃ vissajjāpehī”ti. Ussukkaṃ kātabbanti parivāsadānatthaṃ so so bhikkhu upasaṅkamitvā yācitabbo. Sace attanā paṭibalo hoti, attanāva dātabbo. No ce paṭibalo hoti, aññena dāpetabbo. Kinti nu khoti kena nu kho upāyena. Esa nayo sabbattha. Lahukāya vā [M 0.0262] pariṇāmeyyāti ukkhepanīyaṃ akatvā tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā kareyyāti attho. Tena hi “upajjhāyassa ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kattukāmo saṅgho”ti ñatvā ekamekaṃ bhikkhuṃ upasaṅkamitvā “mā bhante amhākaṃ upajjhāyassa kammaṃ karitthā”ti yācitabbā. Sace karontiyeva, “tajjanīyaṃ vā niyassaṃ vā karothā”ti yācitabbā. Sace karontiyeva, atha upajjhāyo “sammā vattatha bhante”ti yācitabbo. Iti taṃ sammā vattāpetvā “paṭippassambhetha bhante kamma”nti bhikkhū yācitabbā.

‘He should be made to withdraw’ means he should be led elsewhere. ‘He should be caused to withdraw’ means another monk should be told, “Taking the elder, go elsewhere.” ‘He should be made to separate’ means he should be made to relinquish. ‘He should be caused to separate’ means another monk should be told, “Make the elder relinquish his wrong view.” ‘Effort should be made’ means for the purpose of giving probation, each respective monk should be approached and requested. If he himself is capable, he should give it himself. If he is not capable, he should have another give it. ‘How then?’ means by what means. This is the method in all cases. ‘Or he might bring about a lighter penalty’ means: should one, without performing an act of suspension, perform an act of censure or an act of subordination? This is the meaning. Therefore, knowing, “The Saṅgha wishes to perform an act of suspension upon the preceptor,” one should approach each monk one by one and request, “Venerable sirs, do not perform the act upon our preceptor.” If they still perform it, one should request, “Perform an act of censure or an act of subordination.” If they still perform the act of suspension, then the preceptor should be requested, “Venerable sir, please conduct yourself properly.” Thus, having made him conduct himself properly, the monks should be requested, “Venerable sirs, please rescind the act.”

Samparivattakaṃ samparivattakanti samparivattetvā samparivattetvā. Na ca acchinne theve pakkamitabbanti yadi appamattakampi rajanaṃ gaḷati, na tāva pakkamitabbaṃ. Na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā ekaccassa patto dātabbotiādi sabbaṃ upajjhāyassa visabhāgapuggalavasena kathitaṃ. Na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā gāmo pavisitabboti piṇḍāya vā aññena vā karaṇīyena pavisitukāmena āpucchitvāva pavisitabbo. Sace upajjhāyo kālasseva vuṭṭhāya dūraṃ bhikkhācāraṃ gantukāmo hoti, “daharā piṇḍāya pavisantū”ti vatvā gantabbaṃ. Avatvā gate pariveṇaṃ gantvā upajjhāyaṃ apassantena gāmaṃ pavisituṃ vaṭṭati. Sace gāmaṃ pavisantopi passati, diṭṭhaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya āpucchituṃyeva vaṭṭati.

‘Turning over and over’ means having turned over and over. ‘One should not depart while the dripping is not cut off’ means if even a small amount of dye drips, one should not yet depart. The entire passage beginning with ‘A bowl should not be given to someone without asking the preceptor’ is spoken with reference to a person who is disagreeable to the preceptor. ‘A village should not be entered without asking the preceptor’ means: one who wishes to enter for alms-food or for other business should enter only after having asked permission. If the preceptor, having risen early, wishes to go to a distant alms-round resort, he should go only after saying, “Let the junior monks enter for alms-food.” If he has gone without saying so, it is allowable for one who, having gone to the monastic compound and not seeing the preceptor, to enter the village. If, while entering the village, one sees him, it is proper to ask permission only from the place where he was seen.

Na susānaṃ gantabbanti vāsatthāya vā dassanatthāya vā na gantabbaṃ. Na disā pakkamitabbāti [P 5.0982][V 0.0251] ettha pakkamitukāmena kammaṃ ācikkhitvā yāvatatiyaṃ yācitabbo. Sace anujānāti, sādhu; no ce anujānāti, taṃ nissāya vasato cassa uddeso vā paripucchā vā kammaṭṭhānaṃ vā na sampajjati, upajjhāyo bālo hoti abyatto, kevalaṃ attano santike vasāpetukāmatāya eva gantuṃ na deti, evarūpe nivārentepi gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Vuṭṭhānamassa āgametabbanti gelaññato vuṭṭhānaṃ assa āgametabbaṃ; na katthaci gantabbaṃ. Sace añño bhikkhu upaṭṭhāko atthi, bhesajjaṃ pariyesitvā tassa hatthe datvā “bhante ayaṃ upaṭṭhahissatī”ti vatvā gantabbaṃ.

‘One should not go to a charnel ground’ means one should not go, either for the purpose of dwelling or for the purpose of viewing foulness. Regarding ‘One should not depart to another region’: one who wishes to depart should inform of his business and request permission up to the third time. If he gives permission, it is good. If he does not give permission, and if for one living in dependence on him, recitation, questioning, or the meditation subject does not succeed, and the preceptor is foolish and incompetent, and does not give permission to go merely from a desire to make one stay in his presence—in such a case, even if he prevents it, it is allowable to depart. ‘One should await his recovery’ means one should await his recovery from illness; one should not go anywhere. If there is another monk as an attendant, one should search for medicine, give it into that attendant's hand, and depart after saying, “Venerable sir, this one will attend to you.”

Upajjhāyavattakathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the duties toward the preceptor is concluded.

Saddhivihārikavattakathā

The Discourse on the Duties towards a Co-resident

67. Upajjhāyena [M 0.0263] saddhivihārikamhi sammāvattanāyaṃ – saṅgahetabbo anuggahetabboti uddesādīhissa saṅgaho ca anuggaho ca kattabbo. Tattha uddesoti pāḷivācanaṃ. Paripucchāti pāḷiyā atthavaṇṇanā. Ovādoti anotiṇṇe vatthusmiṃ “idaṃ karohi, idaṃ mā karitthā”ti vacanaṃ. Anusāsanīti otiṇṇe vatthusmiṃ. Api ca otiṇṇe vā anotiṇṇe vā paṭhamaṃ vacanaṃ ovādo; punappunaṃ vacanaṃ anusāsanīti. Sace upajjhāyassa patto hotīti sace atirekapatto hoti. Esa nayo sabbattha. Parikkhāroti aññopi samaṇaparikkhāro. Idha ussukkaṃ nāma dhammikena nayena uppajjamānaupāyapariyesanaṃ. Ito paraṃ dantakaṭṭhadānaṃ ādiṃ katvā ācamanakumbhiyā udakāsiñcanapariyosānaṃ vattaṃ gilānasseva saddhivihārikassa kātabbaṃ. Anabhirativūpakāsanādi pana agilānassāpi kattabbameva. Cīvaraṃ rajantenāti “evaṃ rajeyyāsī”ti upajjhāyato upāyaṃ sutvā rajantena. Sesaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

67. Regarding the preceptor's proper conduct towards his co-resident: he should be gathered in and supported; thus, gathering in and support should be done for him by means of instruction and so on. Herein, 'instruction' (uddesa) means teaching the recitation of the Pāli. 'Questioning' (paripucchā) means explaining the meaning of the Pāli. 'Advice' (ovāda) is speaking about a matter not yet undertaken, saying, 'Do this; do not do that.' 'Admonition' (anusāsanī) is about a matter already undertaken. Furthermore, whether a matter is undertaken or not, the first utterance is advice; repeated utterance is admonition. 'If the preceptor has a bowl' means if he has an extra bowl. This method applies everywhere. 'Requisites' (parikkhāra) means other monastic requisites as well. Here, 'diligence' (ussukka) means searching for a means that arises in accordance with the Dhamma. From this point onwards, the duties, beginning with giving a tooth-stick and ending with pouring water into the rinsing pot, should be performed for a sick co-resident only. However, dispelling discontent and so on should indeed be done even for one who is not sick. 'By one dyeing a robe' means: by one who dyes it after hearing the method from the preceptor, who says, 'You should dye it thus.' The rest should be understood in the manner stated.

Saddhivihārikavattakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Duties towards a Co-resident is concluded.

Nasammāvattanādikathā

The Discourse on Improper Conduct and So On

68. Na sammā vattantīti yathāpaññattaṃ upajjhāyavattaṃ na pūrenti. Yo na sammā vatteyyāti yo yathāpaññattaṃ vattaṃ na pūreyya; so dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatīti attho. Paṇāmetabboti apasādetabbo. Na adhimattaṃ pemaṃ hotīti upajjhāyamhi adhimattaṃ gehassitapemaṃ na hoti. Nādhimattā [V 0.0252] bhāvanā hotīti adhimattā mettābhāvanā na hoti; vuttapaṭipakkhanayena [P 5.0983] sukkapakkho veditabbo. Alaṃ paṇāmetunti yutto paṇāmetuṃ.

68. 'They do not conduct themselves properly' means they do not fulfill the duties towards the preceptor as prescribed. 'Whoever does not conduct himself properly' means whoever does not fulfill the prescribed duties; he incurs a wrong-doing—this is the meaning. 'Should be dismissed' means should be expelled. 'There is not excessive affection' means there is not excessive householder's affection towards the preceptor. 'There is not excessive cultivation' means there is not excessive cultivation of loving-kindness; the wholesome side should be understood according to the method of the opposite. 'It is proper to dismiss' means it is fit to dismiss.

Appaṇāmento upajjhāyo sātisāro hotīti sadoso hoti, āpattiṃ āpajjati; tasmā na sammā vattanto paṇāmetabbova. Na sammāvattanāya ca yāva cīvararajanaṃ tāva vatte akariyamāne upajjhāyassa [M 0.0264] parihāni hoti. Tasmā taṃ akarontassa nissayamuttakassāpi amuttakassāpi āpattiyeva. Ekaccassa pattadānato paṭṭhāya amuttakanissayasseva āpatti.

If the preceptor does not dismiss, he is blameworthy, meaning he is at fault and incurs an offense; therefore, one who does not conduct himself properly must indeed be dismissed. And in the case of improper conduct, when the duties up to the dyeing of the robe are not performed, there is a loss for the preceptor. Therefore, for one who does not perform them, whether he is released from dependence or not released, there is indeed an offense. For a certain one, beginning from the giving of the bowl, an offense is incurred only for one who is not released from dependence.

Saddhivihārikā sammā vattanti, upajjhāyo sammā na vattati, upajjhāyassa āpatti. Upajjhāyo sammā vattati, saddhivihārikā sammā na vattanti, tesaṃ āpatti. Upajjhāye vattaṃ sādiyante saddhivihārikā bahukāpi honti, sabbesaṃ āpatti. Sace upajjhāyo “mayhaṃ upaṭṭhāko atthi, tumhe attano sajjhāyamanasikārādīsu yogaṃ karothā”ti vadati, saddhivihārikānaṃ anāpatti. Sace upajjhāyo sādiyanaṃ vā asādiyanaṃ vā na jānāti, bālo hoti, saddhivihārikā bahukā. Tesu eko vattasampanno bhikkhu “upajjhāyassa kiccaṃ ahaṃ karissāmi, tumhe appossukkā viharathā”ti evañce attano bhāraṃ katvā itare vissajjeti, tassa bhārakaraṇato paṭṭhāya tesaṃ anāpatti.

If the co-residents conduct themselves properly, but the preceptor does not conduct himself properly, the preceptor incurs an offense. If the preceptor conducts himself properly, but the co-residents do not conduct themselves properly, they incur an offense. If the preceptor delights in the duties, and the co-residents are numerous, all incur an offense. If the preceptor says, 'I have an attendant; you apply yourselves to your own recitation, mental attention, and so on,' the co-residents are without offense. If the preceptor does not understand acceptance or non-acceptance, is a fool, and the co-residents are numerous—if among them, one monk accomplished in the duties declares, 'I will perform the preceptor’s duties; you remain unconcerned,' and having thus taken the responsibility upon himself, excuses the others, then from the moment he takes on the burden, they are without offense.

Nasammāvattanādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Improper Conduct and So On is concluded.

Rādhabrāhmaṇavatthukathā

The Discourse on the Story of Rādha the Brahmin

69. Rādhabrāhmaṇavatthusmiṃ – kiñcāpi āyasmā sāriputto bhagavatā bārāṇasiyaṃ tīhi saraṇagamanehi anuññātaṃ pabbajjañceva upasampadañca jānāti, bhagavā pana taṃ lahukaṃ upasampadaṃ paṭikkhipitvā ñatticatutthakammena garukaṃ katvā upasampadaṃ anuññātukāmo. Athassa thero ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā “kathāhaṃ bhante taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ pabbājemi upasampādemī”ti āha. Buddhānañhi parisā ajjhāsayakusalā honti, ayañca buddhaparisāya aggo.

69. In the story of Rādha the Brahmin—although the Venerable Sāriputta knew of the going forth and higher ordination that had been authorized by the Blessed One in Bārāṇasī by means of the three refuges, the Blessed One, however, having rejected that light higher ordination, was desirous of authorizing the higher ordination by making it weighty through a formal act with a motion and three announcements. Then, the Elder, having known His intention, said, 'Venerable Sir, how shall I give that Brahmin the going forth and the higher ordination?' Indeed, the assemblies of the Buddhas are skilled in the intention of the Buddha, and this one was the foremost in the Buddha’s assembly.

Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalenāti ettha byatto nāma yassa sāṭṭhakathaṃ vinayapiṭakaṃ vācuggataṃ pavattati, tasmiṃ asati yassa antamaso idaṃ ñatticatutthakammavācāmattampi suggahitaṃ hoti, vācuggataṃ pavattati, ayampi imasmiṃ atthe byatto. Yo pana kāsasosasemhādinā vā gelaññena [P 5.0984][M 0.0265][V 0.0253] oṭṭhadantajivhādīnaṃ vā asampattiyā pariyattiyaṃ vā akataparicayattā na sakkoti parimaṇḍalehi padabyañjanehi kammavācaṃ sāvetuṃ, byañjanaṃ vā padaṃ vā hāpeti, aññathā vā vattabbaṃ aññathā vadati, ayaṃ appaṭibalo. Tabbiparīto imasmiṃ atthe “paṭibalo”ti veditabbo. Saṅgho ñāpetabboti saṅgho jānāpetabbo. Tato paraṃ yaṃ saṅgho jānāpetabbo, taṃ dassetuṃ “suṇātu me bhante”tiādimāha.

Herein, regarding 'by a competent and capable monk': 'competent' is the name for a monk for whom the Vinaya Piṭaka together with its commentary is mastered verbally. In his absence, a monk for whom at the very least just this text of the formal act with a motion and three announcements is well-learned and mastered verbally, is also 'competent' in this sense. However, one who, due to illness such as coughing, asthma, or phlegm disease, or due to an imperfection of the lips, teeth, tongue, and so on, or due to a lack of practice in an assembly, is not able to announce the formal procedural text with well-rounded words and syllables, who omits a syllable or a word, or recites what should be recited in one way, in another way—this one is 'incapable'. The opposite of this is to be understood as 'capable' in this sense. 'The Saṅgha should be informed' means the Saṅgha should be made to know. Thereafter, to show what the Saṅgha should be made to know, He spoke the passage beginning, 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me...'

71. Upasampannasamanantarāti upasampanno hutvā samanantarā. Anācāraṃ ācaratīti paṇṇattivītikkamaṃ karoti. Ullumpatu manti uddharatu maṃ, akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā kusale patiṭṭhapetu; sāmaṇerabhāvā vā uddharitvā bhikkhubhāve patiṭṭhāpetūti. Anukampaṃ upādāyāti anuddayaṃ paṭicca; mayi anukappaṃ katvāti attho.

71. 'Immediately after higher ordination' means: immediately after having become one with higher ordination. 'He engages in misconduct' means: he commits a transgression of a Vinaya rule. 'May you lift me up' means: may you pull me out; having made me rise from the unwholesome, may you establish me in the wholesome; or alternatively: having pulled me out from the state of a novice, may you establish me in the state of a monk. This is the meaning. 'Out of compassion' means: relying on compassion; that is, having shown compassion towards me. This is the meaning.

73. Aṭṭhitā hotīti niccappavattinī hoti. Cattāro nissayeti cattāro paccaye. Yasmā cattāro paccaye nissāya attabhāvo pavattati, tasmā te nissayāti vuccanti.

73. 'Is established' means: is of constant occurrence. 'The four supports' means: the four requisites. Because one's individual existence proceeds in dependence on the four requisites, therefore they are called 'supports'.

Rādhabrāhmaṇavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Story of Rādha the Brahmin is concluded.

Ācariyavattakathā

The Discourse on the Duties towards a Teacher

75. Kintāyaṃ bhikkhu hotīti kiṃ te ayaṃ bhikkhu hoti. Aññehi ovadiyo anusāsiyoti aññehi ovaditabbo ceva anusāsitabbo ca. Bāhullāya āvatto yadidaṃ gaṇabandhikanti gaṇabandho etassa bāhullassa atthīti gaṇabandhikaṃ, bāhullaṃ. Yaṃ idaṃ gaṇabandhikaṃ nāma bāhullaṃ, tadatthāya atilahuṃ tvaṃ āpannoti vuttaṃ hoti.

75. 'What is this monk to you?' means: What is this monk to you? 'He should be advised and instructed by others' means: he should be both advised and instructed by others. Regarding 'Inclined to abundance, that is to say, faction-forming': because there is the forming of a faction of this abundance, that abundance is called 'faction-forming.' Or, it is said: 'For the sake of whatever this abundance called faction-forming is, you have arrived too quickly.'

76. Abyattāti paññāveyyattiyena virahitā. Aññattaropi aññatitthiyapubboti pasūro paribbājako. So kira “dhammaṃ thenessāmī”ti [M 0.0266] udāyittherassa santike pabbajitvā tena sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno tassa vādaṃ āropesi. Anujānāmi bhikkhave byattena bhikkhunātiādimhi byatto pubbe bhikkhunovādakavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttalakkhaṇoyeva. Yo pana antevāsino vā saddhivihārikassa vā gilānassa sakkoti upaṭṭhānādīni kātuṃ, ayaṃ idha paṭibaloti adhippeto. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

76. 'Incompetent' means lacking sharpness of wisdom. 'Another, a former follower of another sect' refers to the wanderer Pasūra. It is said that he, thinking, 'I will steal the Dhamma,' went forth under the Elder Udāyī and, when being spoken to by him in accordance with what is proper, made an accusation against him. In the passage beginning, 'I allow, O monks, a competent monk,' 'competent' is indeed the monk with the characteristics already stated in the explanation of the training rule on admonishing nuns. However, whichever monk is able to perform the services, etc., for a sick pupil or co-resident, this one is intended here as 'capable.' And this has been said:

“Pañcahupāli[V 0.0254], aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabbaṃ, nissayo dātabbo, sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Katamehi pañcahi? Paṭibalo hoti antevāsiṃ vā saddhivihāriṃ vā gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā, anabhirataṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā [P 5.0985] vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā, uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ, abhidhamme vinetuṃ, abhivinaye vinetū”nti (pari. 418).

'Upāli, by a monk endowed with five factors, higher ordination should be given, dependence should be given, and a novice should be made to attend. With what five? He is capable of attending to a sick pupil or co-resident himself or of having another attend; of leading away one who is discontented himself or of having another lead him away; of dispelling arisen remorse according to the Dhamma; of instructing in the higher Dhamma; and of instructing in the higher Vinaya.'

77. Pakkhasaṅkantesūti titthiyapakkhasaṅkantesu. Anujānāmi bhikkhave ācariyanti ācārasamācārasikkhāpanakaṃ ācariyaṃ anujānāmi. Ācariyo bhikkhave antevāsikamhītiādi sabbaṃ “upajjhāyo bhikkhave saddhivihārikamhī”tiādinā nayena vuttavaseneva veditabbaṃ. Nāmamattameva hi ettha nānaṃ.

77. 'When they have gone over to a faction' means: when they have gone over to the faction of the sectarians. 'I allow, O monks, a teacher' means: I allow a teacher who instructs in good conduct and behavior. Everything in the passage beginning, 'A teacher, O monks, towards a pupil...' should be understood in the same way as has been stated by the method of the passage beginning, 'A preceptor, O monks, towards a co-resident.' For here the difference is only in the name.

Ācariyavattakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Duties toward a Teacher is finished.

Paṇāmanākhamanākathā

The Discourse on Dismissal and Not Pardoning

80. Antevāsikā ācariyesu na sammā vattantīti ettha pana yaṃ pubbe “nasammāvattanāya ca yāva cīvararajanaṃ, tāva vatte akariyamāne upajjhāyassa parihāni hoti, tasmā taṃ akarontassa nissayamuttakassāpi amuttakassāpi āpattiyevā”ti ca, “ekaccassa pattadānato paṭṭhāya amuttakanissayasseva āpattī”ti ca lakkhaṇaṃ vuttaṃ, na teneva lakkhaṇena nissayantevāsikassa āpatti veditabbā. Nissayantevāsikena hi yāva ācariyaṃ nissāya vasati, tāva sabbaṃ ācariyavattaṃ kātabbaṃ. Pabbajjāupasampadādhammantevāsikehi pana nissayamuttakehipi [M 0.0267] ādito paṭṭhāya yāva cīvararajanaṃ, tāva vattaṃ kātabbaṃ; anāpucchitvā pattadānādimhi pana etesaṃ anāpatti. Etesu ca pabbajjantevāsiko ca upasampadantevāsiko ca ācariyassa yāvajīvaṃ bhāro. Nissayantevāsiko ca dhammantevāsiko ca yāva samīpe vasanti, tāvadeva. Tasmā ācariyenāpi tesu sammā vattitabbaṃ. Ācariyantevāsikesu hi yo yo na sammā vattati, tassa tassa āpatti.

80. Now, in this passage, 'Pupils do not conduct themselves properly towards teachers,' whatever characteristic was stated previously—such as, 'Due to not conducting oneself properly... there is an offense,' and 'For some... there is an offense'—the offense for a pupil under dependence should not be understood by that characteristic. For a pupil under dependence, for as long as he lives depending on a teacher, all the duties towards a teacher must be done. But by pupils of going forth, higher ordination, and Dhamma, even when freed from dependence, the duties must be done from the beginning up to the dyeing of the robe; however, in the case of giving a bowl and so on without having asked, for them there is no offense. And among these, the pupil of going forth and the pupil of higher ordination are a lifelong responsibility for the teacher. The pupil under dependence and the pupil of Dhamma are a responsibility only for as long as they live nearby. Therefore, the teacher also must conduct himself properly towards them. For among teachers and pupils, whoever does not conduct himself properly, for that one there is an offense.

Paṇāmanākhamanākathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on Dismissal and Not Pardoning is finished.

Nissayapaṭippassaddhikathā

The Discourse on the Cessation of Dependence

83. Upajjhāyamhā [V 0.0255] nissayapaṭippassaddhīsu – upajjhāyo pakkanto vātiādīsu ayaṃ vinicchayo – pakkantoti tamhā āvāsā vippavasitukāmo pakkanto disaṃ gato. Evaṃ gate ca pana tasmiṃ sace vihāre nissayadāyako atthi, yassa santike aññadāpi nissayo vā gahitapubbo hoti, yo vā ekasambhogaparibhogo, tassa santike nissayo gahetabbo, ekadivasampi parihāro natthi. Sace tādiso natthi, añño lajjī pesalo atthi, tassa lajjīpesalabhāvaṃ jānantena tadaheva nissayo yācitabbo. Sace deti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. Atha pana “tumhākaṃ upajjhāyo lahuṃ āgamissatī”ti pucchati, upajjhāyena ca tathā vuttaṃ, “āma, bhante”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace vadati “tena [P 5.0986] hi upajjhāyassa āgamanaṃ āgamethā”ti vaṭṭati. Atha panassa pakatiyā pesalabhāvaṃ na jānāti, cattāri pañca divasāni tassa bhikkhuno sabhāgataṃ oloketvā okāsaṃ kāretvā nissayo gahetabbo.

83. Regarding the cessations of dependence on one’s preceptor—in such cases as 'the preceptor has departed,' this is the ruling: 'Departed' means he has left that residence, desiring to dwell away, and has gone to another region. When he has thus departed, if there is a dependence-giver in the monastery—one from whom dependence has been taken before on another occasion, or one who has shared requisites and Dhamma—dependence should be taken from him; there is no exemption even for a single day. If there is no such person, but there is another monk who is conscientious and amiable, one who knows his conscientious and amiable nature should request dependence from him on that very day. If he grants it, this is good. But if he asks, 'Will your preceptor return soon?' and the preceptor has indeed said so, one should reply, 'Yes, venerable sir.' If he says, 'In that case, wait for your preceptor’s return,' that is permissible. However, if one does not know his natural amiable nature, one should observe that monk’s compatibility for four or five days, and having created an opportunity, dependence should be taken.

Sace pana vihāre nissayadāyako natthi, upajjhāyo ca “ahaṃ katipāhena āgamissāmi, mā ukkaṇṭhitthā”ti vatvā gato, yāva āgamanā parihāro labbhati. Athāpi naṃ tattha manussā paricchinnakālato uttaripi pañca vā dasa vā divasāni vāsentiyeva, tena vihāraṃ pavatti pesetabbā “daharā mā ukkaṇṭhantu, ahaṃ asukadivasaṃ nāma [M 0.0268] āgamissāmī”ti. Evampi parihāro labbhati. Atha āgacchato antarāmagge nadīpūrena vā corādīhi vā upaddavo hoti, thero udakosakkanaṃ vā āgameti, sahāye vā pariyesati, tañce pavattiṃ daharā suṇanti, yāva āgamanā parihāro labbhati. Sace pana so “idhevāhaṃ vasissāmī”ti pahiṇati, parihāro natthi. Yattha nissayo labbhati, tattha gantabbaṃ.

But if there is no dependence-giver in the monastery, and the preceptor has departed after saying, 'I will return in a few days; do not be anxious,' an exemption is obtained until his return. Furthermore, if the people there make him stay even five or ten days beyond the time he specified, he should send news to the monastery, saying: 'Let the junior monks not be anxious; I will return on such-and-such a day.' Even in this way, an exemption is obtained. Then, if on his way back a danger arises, such as a flooded river or bandits, and the elder waits for the water to recede or seeks companions, and if the junior monks hear this news, an exemption is obtained until his return. But if he sends word saying, 'I will stay right here,' there is no exemption. One must go where dependence can be obtained.

Vibbhante pana kālaṅkate pakkhasaṅkante vā ekadivasampi parihāro natthi. Yattha nissayo labbhati, tattha gantabbaṃ. Āṇattīti pana nissayapaṇāmanā vuccati. Tasmā “paṇāmemi ta”nti vā “mā idha paṭikkamī”ti vā “nīhara te pattacīvara”nti vā “nāhaṃ tayā upaṭṭhātabbo”ti vāti iminā pāḷinayena “mā maṃ gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchī”tiādinā pāḷimuttakanayena vā yo nissayapaṇāmanāya paṇāmito hoti, tena upajjhāyo khamāpetabbo.

If the preceptor has disrobed, passed away, or gone over to another sect, there is no allowance even for a single day. One must go where dependence can be obtained. Now, expulsion from dependence is called a 'command' (āṇatti). Therefore, a disciple who has been expelled by means of expulsion from dependence—whether by the canonical method with phrases such as, 'I expel you,' or 'Do not approach here,' or 'Take out your bowl and robes,' or 'You are not to attend on me'; or by a non-canonical method with phrases such as, 'Do not ask my permission for entering the village'—that disciple should ask for the preceptor's forgiveness.

Sace āditova na khamati, daṇḍakammaṃ āharitvā tikkhattuṃ tāva sayameva khamāpetabbo. No ce khamati, tasmiṃ vihāre mahāthere gahetvā khamāpetabbo. No ce khamati, sāmantavihāre [V 0.0256] bhikkhū gahetvā khamāpetabbo. Sace evampi na khamati, aññattha gantvā upajjhāyassa sabhāgānaṃ santike vasitabbaṃ “appeva nāma sabhāgānaṃ me santike vasatīti ñatvāpi khameyyā”ti. Sace evampi na khamati, tatreva vasitabbaṃ. Tatra ce dubbhikkhādidosena na sakkā hoti vasituṃ, taṃyeva vihāraṃ āgantvā aññassa santike nissayaṃ gahetvā vasituṃ vaṭṭati. Ayamāṇattiyaṃ vinicchayo.

If from the outset he does not forgive, one should, after undertaking a penalty, first ask for forgiveness by oneself up to three times. If he does not forgive, one should ask for forgiveness having taken the senior monks in that monastery. If he does not forgive, one should ask for forgiveness having taken the monks in a nearby monastery. If even then he does not forgive, one should go elsewhere and dwell in the presence of the preceptor's associate elders, thinking, 'Perhaps, knowing that I am dwelling in the presence of his associates, he might forgive.' If even then he does not forgive, one should dwell right there. If it is not possible to dwell there due to faults such as famine, it is permissible to return to that very same monastery and dwell there, having taken dependence from another. This is the ruling on the command.

Ācariyamhā nissayapaṭippassaddhīsu ācariyo pakkanto vā [P 5.0987] hotīti ettha koci ācariyo āpucchitvā pakkamati, koci anāpucchitvā. Antevāsikopi evameva. Tatra sace antevāsiko ācariyaṃ āpucchati “asukaṃ nāma bhante ṭhānaṃ gantuṃ icchāmi kenacideva karaṇīyenā”ti, ācariyena ca “kadā gamissasī”ti vutto “sāyanhe vā rattiṃ vā uṭṭhahitvā gamissāmī”ti vadati, ācariyopi “sādhū”ti sampaṭicchati, taṅkhaṇaññeva nissayo paṭippassambhati.

Regarding the cessations of dependence from a teacher: Here, in the text 'the teacher has departed,' some teachers depart after asking leave, and some depart without asking leave. The same applies to the pupil. Therein, if the pupil asks leave of the teacher, saying, 'Venerable sir, I wish to go to such-and-such a place for some reason,' and when asked by the teacher, 'When will you go?' he replies, 'I will go in the evening, or having arisen at night,' and the teacher accepts, saying, 'Good,' then at that very moment, the dependence ceases.

Sace [M 0.0269] pana “bhante asukaṃ nāma ṭhānaṃ gantukāmomhī”ti vutte ācariyo “asukasmiṃ nāma gāme piṇḍāya caritvā pacchā jānissasī”ti vadati, so ca “sādhū”ti sampaṭicchati, tato ce gato, sugato. Sace pana na gacchati, nissayo na paṭippassambhati. Athāpi “gacchāmī”ti vutte ācariyena “mā tāva gaccha, rattiṃ mantetvā jānissāmā”ti vutto mantetvā gacchati, sugato. No ce gacchati, nissayo na paṭippassambhati. Ācariyaṃ anāpucchā pakkamantassa pana upacārasīmātikkame nissayo paṭippassambhati. Antoupacārasīmato paṭinivattantassa na paṭippassambhati.

But if, when the pupil says, 'Venerable sir, I wish to go to such-and-such a place,' the teacher says, 'You will know later, after you have gone for alms in such-and-such a village,' and the pupil accepts, saying, 'Good,' then if he goes from there, he has gone well. But if he does not go, the dependence does not cease. Furthermore, if, when the pupil says, 'I am going,' he is told by the teacher, 'Do not go just yet; we will know after consulting at night,' and then he goes after consulting, he has gone well. If he does not go, the dependence does not cease. However, for one who departs without asking the teacher, the dependence ceases upon crossing the boundary of the vicinity. For one who turns back from within the boundary of the vicinity, it does not cease.

Sace pana ācariyo antevāsikaṃ āpucchati “āvuso asukaṃ nāma ṭhānaṃ gamissāmī”ti, antevāsikena ca “kadā”ti vutte “sāyanhe vā rattibhāge vā”ti vadati, antevāsikopi “sādhū”ti sampaṭicchati, taṅkhaṇaññeva nissayo paṭippassambhati.

But if the teacher asks leave of the pupil, saying, 'Friend, I will go to such-and-such a place,' and when the pupil asks, 'When?' the teacher replies, 'In the evening or during the night,' and the pupil also accepts, saying, 'Good,' then at that very moment, the dependence ceases.

Sace pana ācariyo “sve piṇḍāya caritvā gamissāmī”ti vadati, itaro ca “sādhū”ti sampaṭicchati, ekadivasaṃ tāva nissayo na paṭippassambhati, punadivase paṭippassaddho hoti. “Asukasmiṃ nāma gāme piṇḍāya caritvā jānissāmi mama gamanaṃ vā agamanaṃ vā”ti vatvā sace na gacchati, nissayo na paṭippassambhati. Athāpi “gacchāmī”ti [V 0.0257] vutte antevāsikena “mā tāva gacchatha, rattiṃ mantetvā jānissathā”ti vutto mantetvāpi na gacchati, nissayo na paṭippassambhati.

But if the teacher says, “Tomorrow, having gone for alms, I will depart,” and the other accepts, saying, “Good,” for one day the dependence does not yet cease; it has ceased on the following day. If, having said, “Having gone for alms in such-and-such a village, I will know of my going or not going,” he does not go, the dependence does not cease. Furthermore, if, when he has said, “I am going,” he is told by the pupil, “Do not go yet; having consulted at night, you will know,” and even after consulting he does not go, the dependence does not cease.

Sace ubhopi ācariyantevāsikā kenaci karaṇīyena bahisīmaṃ gacchanti, tato ce ācariyo gamiyacitte uppanne anāpucchāva gantvā dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃ antoyeva nivattati, nissayo na paṭippassambhati. Sace dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā nivattati, paṭippassaddho hoti. Ācariyupajjhāyā dve leḍḍupāte atikkamma aññasmiṃ vihāre vasanti, nissayo paṭippassambhati.

If both the teacher and the pupil go outside the boundary on some business, and from there, when a desire to depart has arisen in the teacher, he goes without asking leave and returns from within the distance of two clod-throws, the dependence does not cease. If he returns after having gone beyond two clod-throws, it has ceased. If teachers and preceptors, having gone beyond two clod-throws, dwell in another monastery, the dependence ceases.

Ācariye vibbhante kālaṅkate pakkhasaṅkante ca taṅkhaṇaññeva paṭippassambhati. Āṇattiyaṃ pana sacepi [P 5.0988] ācariyo muñcitukāmova hutvā nissayapaṇāmanāya paṇāmeti, antevāsiko ca “kiñcāpi maṃ ācariyo paṇāmeti, atha kho hadayena muduko”ti sālayova hoti, nissayo na paṭippassambhatiyeva. Sacepi ācariyo sālayo, antevāsiko [M 0.0270] nirālayo, “na dāni imaṃ nissāya vasissāmī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhipati, evampi na paṭippassambhati. Ubhinnaṃ sālayabhāve pana na paṭippassambhatiyeva. Ubhinnaṃ dhuranikkhepena paṭippassambhati. Paṇāmitena daṇḍakammaṃ āharitvā tikkhattuṃ khamāpetabbo. No ce khamati, upajjhāye vuttanayena paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

When the teacher has disrobed, passed away, or gone over to another sect, the dependence ceases at that very moment. In the case of expulsion, however, even if the teacher, wishing to release him, expels him from dependence, but the pupil thinks, “Although my teacher expels me, he is nevertheless soft-hearted,” and remains attached, the dependence certainly does not cease. Even if the teacher is attached but the pupil is unattached and lays down the burden, thinking, “Now I will no longer live in dependence on him,” even so it does not cease. However, when both are attached, it certainly does not cease. It ceases through the laying down of the burden by both. The one who has been expelled, having undertaken a penalty, should ask for forgiveness three times. If the teacher does not forgive, one should act according to the method stated in the section on the preceptor.

Upajjhāyena vā samodhānagatoti ettha dassanasavanavasena samodhānaṃ veditabbaṃ.
