Sace hi ācariyaṃ nissāya vasanto saddhivihāriko ekavihāre cetiyaṃ vā vandantaṃ ekagāme piṇḍāya vā carantaṃ upajjhāyaṃ passati, nissayo paṭippassambhati. Upajjhāyo passati, saddhivihāriko pana na passati, na paṭippassambhati. Maggappaṭipannaṃ vā ākāsena vā gacchantaṃ upajjhāyaṃ disvā dūrattā bhikkhūti jānāti, upajjhāyoti na jānāti, na paṭippassambhati. Sace jānāti, paṭippassambhati. Uparipāsāde upajjhāyo vasati, heṭṭhā saddhivihāriko, taṃ adisvāva yāguṃ pivitvā pakkamati, āsanasālāya vā nisinnaṃ adisvāva ekamante bhuñjitvā pakkamati, dhammassavanamaṇḍape vā nisinnampi taṃ adisvāva dhammaṃ sutvā pakkamati, nissayo na paṭippassambhati. Evaṃ tāva dassanavasena samodhānaṃ veditabbaṃ.

Regarding 'or has been reunited with the preceptor,' here reunion should be understood by way of seeing and hearing. For if a co-resident, living in dependence on a teacher, sees his preceptor who is venerating a cetiya in the same monastery or wandering for alms in the same village, the dependence ceases. If the preceptor sees him, but the co-resident does not see the preceptor, it does not cease. Having seen the preceptor who is on a journey or going through the sky, if, due to the distance, he knows him only as 'a bhikkhu' and does not know him as 'the preceptor,' the dependence does not cease. If he does know him, it ceases. If the preceptor dwells on an upper floor of a storied building and the co-resident is below, and he departs after drinking gruel without seeing him; or in the dining hall, he departs after eating in a corner without seeing him seated there; or in the Dhamma-listening pavilion, he departs after hearing the Dhamma without seeing him who is also seated there, the dependence does not cease. Thus, firstly, reunion by way of seeing should be understood.

Savanavasena pana sace upajjhāyassa vihāre vā antaraghare vā dhammaṃ kathentassa anumodanaṃ [V 0.0258] vā karontassa saddaṃ sutvā “upajjhāyassa me saddo”ti sañjānāti, nissayo paṭippassambhati. Asañjānantassa na paṭippassambhatīti ayaṃ samodhāne vinicchayo.

However, by way of hearing, if, having heard the voice of the preceptor while he is teaching the Dhamma in the monastery or inside a house, or while he is giving a blessing after a meal, one recognizes it, thinking, “This is my preceptor’s voice,” the dependence ceases. For one who does not recognize it, it does not cease. This is the decision concerning reunion.

Nissayapaṭippassaddhikathā niṭṭhitā.

The discourse on the ceasing of dependence is concluded.

Upasampādetabbapañcakakathā

The Discourse on the Pentads Concerning Giving Ordination

84. Idāni yaṃ pubbe “anujānāmi bhikkhave byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena dasavassena vā atirekadasavassena vā upasampādetuṃ, nissayaṃ dātu”nti saṅkhepato upajjhāyācariyānaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ vitthārato dassetuṃ “pañcahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgatenā”tiādimāha. Tattha pañcahi aṅgehīti pañcahi aguṇaṅgehi. So hi sīlakkhandhādīhi asamannāgatattāva [P 5.0989] aguṇaṅgehi samannāgato hoti. Na upasampādetabbanti upajjhāyena [M 0.0271] hutvā na upasampādetabbaṃ. Na nissayo dātabboti ācariyena hutvā nissayo na dātabbo. Ettha ca na asekkhena sīlakkhandhenāti ca attanā na asekkhenāti ca assaddhoti ca ādīsu tīsu pañcakesu ayuttavasena paṭikkhepo kato, na āpattiaṅgavasena. Yo hi asekkhehi sīlakkhandhādīhi asamannāgato pare ca tattha samādapetuṃ asakkonto assaddhiyādidosayuttova hutvā parisaṃ pariharati, tassa parisā sīlādīhi parihāyatiyeva, na vaḍḍhati. Tasmā tena na upasampādetabbantiādi ayuttavasena vuttaṃ, na āpattiaṅgavasena. Na hi khīṇāsavasseva upajjhāyācariyabhāvo bhagavatā anuññāto. Yadi tasseva anuññāto abhavissa, “sace upajjhāyassa anabhirati uppannā hotī”tiādiṃ na vadeyya. Yasmā pana khīṇāsavassa parisā sīlādīhi na parihāyati, tasmā “pañcahi bhikkhave aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā upasampādetabba”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

84. Now, to show in detail the characteristic of preceptors and teachers that was previously stated in brief—'I allow, monks, a competent and able monk who is of ten years' standing or more than ten years' standing to give ordination, to give dependence'—the Blessed One said, 'Monks, by one endowed with five factors,' and so on. Herein, 'by five factors' means by five disqualifying factors. For, because one is not endowed with the aggregate of virtue and so on, one is indeed endowed with disqualifying factors. 'Should not give ordination' means that, having become a preceptor, one should not give ordination. 'Dependence should not be given' means that, having become a teacher, one should not give dependence. And here, in the three pentads beginning with 'not with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training,' 'not himself one beyond training,' and 'is without faith,' the rejection is made on the basis of unsuitability, not on the basis of being a factor of an offense. For if one who is not endowed with the aggregates of virtue, etc., of those beyond training, and is unable to establish others therein, leads a following while being endowed with faults such as faithlessness, the following of such a one declines in virtue, etc.; it does not grow. Therefore, 'by him, one should not be ordained,' and so on, is said on the basis of unsuitability, not on the basis of being a factor of an offense. Indeed, the state of being a preceptor or teacher was not permitted by the Blessed One only for one whose cankers are destroyed. If it had been permitted only for such a one, He would not have said, 'If for the preceptor dissatisfaction has arisen,' and so on. But since the following of one whose cankers are destroyed does not decline in virtue, etc., therefore it was said, 'Monks, by a monk endowed with five factors... one should be ordained,' and so on.

Adhisīle sīlavipannotiādīsu pārājikañca saṅghādisesañca āpanno adhisīle sīlavipanno nāma. Itare pañcāpattikkhandhe āpanno ajjhācāre ācāravipanno nāma. Sammādiṭṭhiṃ pahāya antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato atidiṭṭhiyā diṭṭhivipanno nāma. Yattakaṃ sutaṃ parisaṃ pariharantassa icchitabbaṃ, tena virahitattā appassuto. Yaṃ tena jānitabbaṃ āpattādi, tassa ajānanato duppañño. Imasmiṃ pañcake purimāni tīṇi padāni ayuttavasena vuttāni, pacchimāni dve āpattiaṅgavasena.

In 'corrupt in higher virtue,' etc., one who has fallen into a Pārājika or a Saṅghādisesa offense is called 'corrupt in higher virtue.' One who has fallen into the other five classes of offenses is called 'corrupt in conduct' with regard to transgressive conduct. One who, having abandoned right view, is endowed with a view that grasps at extremes is called 'corrupt in view' with regard to excessive view. Because of being devoid of as much learning as is desirable for one who leads a following, one is 'of little learning.' Because of not knowing that which should be known by him, such as offenses, he is 'unwise.' In this pentad, the first three terms are stated on the basis of unsuitability, while the latter two are stated on the basis of being a factor of an offense.

Āpattiṃ [V 0.0259] na jānātīti “idaṃ nāma mayā kata”nti vutte “imaṃ nāma āpattiṃ ayaṃ āpanno”ti na jānāti. Vuṭṭhānaṃ na jānātīti vuṭṭhānagāminito vā desanāgāminito vā āpattito evaṃ nāma vuṭṭhānaṃ hotīti na jānāti. Imasmiṃ pañcake purimāni dve padāni ayuttavasena vuttāni, pacchimāni tīṇi āpattiaṅgavasena.

'He does not know the offense' means: when it is said, 'Such and such a thing was done by me,' he does not know, 'This monk has fallen into such and such an offense.' 'He does not know the emergence' means: he does not know that from an offense leading to rehabilitation or from an offense leading to confession, emergence occurs in such and such a way. In this pentad, the first two terms are stated on the basis of unsuitability, while the latter three are stated on the basis of being a factor of an offense.

Ābhisamācārikāya sikkhāyāti khandhakavatte [P 5.0990] vinetuṃ na paṭibalo hotīti attho. Ādibrahmacariyakāyāti sekkhapaṇṇattiyaṃ vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti attho. Abhidhammeti nāmarūpaparicchede vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti attho. Abhivinayeti sakale vinayapiṭake vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti attho. Vinetuṃ na paṭibaloti ca sabbattha sikkhāpetuṃ na sakkotīti [M 0.0272] attho. Dhammato vivecetunti dhammena kāraṇena vissajjāpetuṃ. Imasmi pañcake sabbapadesu āpatti. Āpattiṃ na jānātītiādipañcakasmimpi sabbapadesu āpatti. Ūnadasavassapariyosānapañcakepi eseva nayo. Iti ādito tayo pañcakā, catutthe tīṇi padāni, pañcame dve padānīti sabbepi cattāro pañcakā ayuttavasena vuttā. Catutthapañcake dve padāni, pañcame tīṇi, chaṭṭhasattamaaṭṭhamā tayo pañcakāti sabbepi cattāro pañcakā āpattiaṅgavasena vuttā; sukkapakkhe aṭṭhasu anāpattiyevāti.

Regarding 'the training in proper conduct': the meaning is that he is not able to train in the duties of the Khandhakas. Regarding 'the fundamental holy life': the meaning is that he is not able to train in the rules for trainees. Regarding 'the higher Dhamma': the meaning is that he is not able to train in the analysis of mind-and-matter. Regarding 'the higher Vinaya': the meaning is that he is not able to train in the entire Vinayapiṭaka. And 'not able to train' means in all cases that he is not able to teach. 'To make him relinquish it according to the Dhamma' means to be able to have him relinquish it for a reason in accordance with the Dhamma. In this pentad, there is an offense in all items. Also in the pentad beginning 'He does not know the offense,' there is an offense in all items. In the pentad ending with 'being of less than ten years' standing,' this is also the method. Thus: the first three pentads; in the fourth, three items; and in the fifth, two items—in all, these four pentads are stated on the basis of unsuitability. In the fourth pentad, two items; in the fifth, three; and the sixth, seventh, and eighth, being three pentads—in all, these four pentads are stated on the basis of being a factor of an offense. In the bright side, in the eight pentads, there is only no offense.

Upasampādetabbapañcakakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Pentads Concerning Giving Ordination is concluded.

Upasampādetabbachakkakathā

The Discourse on the Group of Six Pertaining to Those Who Are to Be Ordained

85. Chakkesu ūnadasavassapadaṃ viseso, taṃ sabbattha āpattikaraṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Tattha ubhayāni kho panassa pātimokkhāni vitthārena na svāgatāni hontīti ubhatovibhaṅgavasena na svāgatāni. Na suvibhattānīti mātikāvibhaṅgavasena. Na suppavattīnīti vācuggatavasena. Na suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanasoti mātikāto ca vibhaṅgato ca na suṭṭhu vinicchitāni.

85. In the groups of six, the term 'less than ten years' is the distinguishing factor; in all groups of six, it entails an offense. The remainder should be understood according to the method already stated. Therein, that 'both Pātimokkhas are not well-mastered by him' means they are not well-mastered by way of the Ubhatovibhaṅga. That they 'are not well-analyzed' is by way of the analysis of the Mātikā. That they 'do not flow smoothly' is by way of recitation from memory. That they 'are not well-determined according to the rule and its details' means they are not well-determined by way of both the Mātikā and the Vibhaṅga.

Upasampādetabbachakkakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discourse on the Group of Six Pertaining to Those Who Are to Be Ordained is concluded.

Aññatitthiyapubbavatthukathā

The Discourse on the Case of One Formerly an Adherent of Another Sect

86. Aññatitthiyapubbavatthusmiṃ [V 0.0260] – yo tāva ayaṃ pasūro, so titthiyapakkantakattā na upasampādetabbo. Yo pana aññopi nayidha pabbajitapubbo āgacchati, tasmiṃ yaṃ kattabbaṃ taṃ dassetuṃ “yo so bhikkhave aññopī”tiādimāha. Tattha tassa cattāro māse parivāso dātabboti ayaṃ titthiyaparivāso nāma; appaṭicchannaparivāsotipi vuccati. Ayaṃ pana naggaparibbājakasseva ājīvakassa vā [M 0.0273] acelakassa vā dātabbo[P 5.0991]. Sace sopi sāṭakaṃ vā vāḷakambalādīnaṃ aññataraṃ titthiyaddhajaṃ vā nivāsetvā āgacchati, nāssa parivāso dātabbo. Aññassa pana tāpasapaṇḍaraṅgādikassa na dātabbova.

86. In the case of one formerly an adherent of another sect: first, this Pasūra, because he went over to the side of the sectarians, is not to be given the higher ordination. But to show what is to be done in the case of another who comes, one who has not formerly gone forth in this Dispensation, He said the passage beginning, “Monks, whoever else…” Therein, the passage means: this probation is to be given to him. This is called the probation for sectarians; it is also called the probation for an unconcealed period. This, however, is to be given only to a naked wanderer, an Ājīvaka, or an Acelaka. If even such a one comes having put on a cloth, or another banner of the sectarians such as a blanket made of animal hair, probation is not to be given to him. But for another, such as an ascetic or a white-clad wanderer, it is not to be given at all.

Paṭhamaṃ kesamassuntiādinā tassa āditova sāmaṇerapabbajjaṃ dasseti. Evaṃ pabbājentehi pana tasmiṃ saṅghamajjhe nisinneyeva “tvaṃ pabbājehi, tvaṃ ācariyo hohi, tvaṃ upajjhāyo hohī”ti therā bhikkhū na vattabbā. Evaṃ vuttā hi sace tassa ācariyupajjhāyabhāvena jigucchantā na sampaṭicchanti, atha so “nayime mayhaṃ saddahantī”ti kujjhitvāpi gaccheyya. Tasmā taṃ ekamantaṃ netvā tassa ācariyupajjhāyā pariyesitabbā.

By the passage beginning, 'First, his hair and beard...', it shows his going forth as a novice from the very beginning. However, when causing him to go forth in this way, while he is sitting in the midst of the Saṅgha, the elder monks should not be addressed thus: 'You cause him to go forth,' 'You be his teacher,' 'You be his preceptor.' For if the elders, having been spoken to thus, do not accept, being disgusted with the state of being his teacher and preceptor, then he, thinking, 'These monks do not trust me,' might become angry and leave. Therefore, having led him to a secluded place, a teacher and preceptor should be sought for him.

87. Evaṃ kho bhikkhave aññatitthiyapubbo ārādhako hoti, evaṃ anārādhakoti ayamassa parivāsavattadassanatthaṃ mātikā. Kathañca bhikkhavetiādi tasseva vibhaṅgo. Tattha atikālena gāmaṃ pavisatīti bhikkhūnaṃ vattakaraṇavelāyameva gāmaṃ piṇḍāya pavisati. Atidivā paṭikkamatīti kulagharesu itthipurisadārakadārikādīhi saddhiṃ gehassitakathaṃ kathento tattheva bhuñjitvā bhikkhūsu pattacīvaraṃ paṭisāmetvā uddesaparipucchādīni vā karontesu paṭisallīnesu vā āgacchati; na upajjhāyavattaṃ nācariyavattaṃ karoti, aññadatthu vasanaṭṭhānaṃ pavisitvā niddāyati. Evampi bhikkhave aññatitthiyapubbo anārādhako hotīti evampi karonto parivāsavattassa sampādako pūrako na hoti.

87. 'In this way, monks, one formerly of another sect is compliant; in that way, he is non-compliant'—this is the mātikā for the purpose of showing the observances of probation. The passage beginning, 'And how, monks...' is the detailed analysis of that. Therein, 'he enters the village at an unseasonable time' means he enters the village for alms at the very time for the monks' performance of duties. 'He returns late in the day' means that, having conversed on worldly matters with women, men, boys, and girls in the houses of families and having eaten right there, he returns when the monks have put away their bowls and robes and are engaged in recitation and questioning, or are in seclusion. He does not perform the duties toward his preceptor, nor the duties toward his teacher; instead, having entered his dwelling place, he sleeps. 'In this way too, monks, one formerly of another sect is non-compliant' means that by acting in this way, he is not one who accomplishes or fulfills the observances of probation.

Vesiyāgocaro vātiādīsu vesiyāti āmisakiñcikkhasampadānādinā sulabhajjhācārā rūpūpajīvikā itthiyo. Vidhavāti matapatikā vā pavutthapatikā vā itthiyo; tā yena kenaci saddhiṃ mittabhāvaṃ patthenti. Thullakumārikāti yobbannappattā yobbannātītā vā kumāriyo; tā purisādhippāyāva vicaranti, yena kenaci saddhiṃ mittabhāvaṃ patthenti. Paṇḍakāti ussannakilesā avūpasantapariḷāhā napuṃsakā; te pariḷāhavegābhibhūtā yena [P 5.0992] kenaci saddhiṃ mittabhāvaṃ patthenti[V 0.0261]. Bhikkhuniyoti samānapabbajjā itthiyo; tāhi saddhiṃ khippameva vissāso hoti, tato sīlaṃ bhijjati.

In the passage beginning, 'Or one who frequents prostitutes,' 'prostitutes' (vesiyā) means women who live by means of their physical form, whose transgressions are easily obtained by means of giving some small material thing. 'Widows' (vidhavā) means women whose husbands are dead or whose husbands are living abroad; they seek friendship with any man whatsoever. 'Mature maidens' (thullakumārikā) means maidens who have reached or passed the age of youth; they wander about with intentions fixed on men and seek friendship with any man whatsoever. 'Paṇḍakas' means neuter persons of intense defilements, with unallayed torment; overwhelmed by the force of their torment, they seek friendship with any man whatsoever. 'Nuns' (bhikkhunī) means women who share the same state of having gone forth; familiarity with them arises quickly, and from that, one's virtue is broken.

Tattha [M 0.0274] vesiyānaṃ kulesu kulupako hutvā piṇḍapātacariyādīhi vā apadisitvā sinehasanthavajātena hadayena abhiṇhadassanasallāpakāmatāya tāsaṃ santikaṃ upasaṅkamanto “vesiyāgocaro”ti vuccati, so nacirasseva “asukavesiyā saddhiṃ gato”ti vattabbataṃ pāpuṇāti. Esa nayo sabbattha. Sace pana vesiyādayo salākabhattādīni denti, bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ gantvā saddhiṃyeva bhuñjitvā vā gahetvā vā āgantuṃ vaṭṭati. Gilānā bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ vā dhammaṃ vā desetuṃ uddesaparipucchādīni vā dātuṃ gacchantehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Yo pana tathā āgantvā mittasanthavavasena gacchati, ayaṃ anārādhako hoti.

Therein, one who, having become a frequenter of the families of prostitutes, or having made a pretext of going on alms round and so forth, approaches them with a mind in which affection and intimacy have arisen, out of a desire for constant seeing and conversation, is called 'one who frequents prostitutes.' Before long, he reaches the state of being spoken of thus: 'He has gone with such-and-such a prostitute.' This is the method in all cases. If, however, prostitutes and others give ticket-food and so forth, it is proper to go with the monks, and having eaten together with them or having taken it, to return. It is proper to go with monks who are going to admonish sick nuns, or to teach the Dhamma, or to give recitation and ask questions. But whoever, not going in that way, goes by way of forming a friendship, this one is non-compliant.

Uccāvacāni karaṇīyānīti mahantakhuddakāni kammāni. Tattha ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā samaggena saṅghena sannipatitvā kattabbāni cetiyamahāpāsādapaṭisaṅkharaṇādīni kammāni uccāni nāma. Cīvaradhovanarajanādīni khandhakapariyāpannāni ca aggisālavattādīni ābhisamācārikāni avacāni nāma. Tattha na dakkho hotīti tesu kammesu cheko susikkhito na hoti. Na analasoti uṭṭhānavīriyasampanno na hoti; “bhikkhusaṅghassa kammaṃ atthī”ti sutvā pageva bhattakiccaṃ katvā gabbhantaraṃ pavisitvā yāvadatthaṃ supitvā sāyaṃ nikkhamati. Tatrupāyāyāti tesu kammesu upāyabhūtāya. Vīmaṃsāyāti ṭhānuppattikavīmaṃsāya. “Idamevaṃ kattabbaṃ, idamevaṃ na kattabba”nti tasmiṃyeva khaṇe uppannapaññāya samannāgato na hoti. Na alaṃ kātuṃ na alaṃ saṃvidhātunti sahatthāpi kātuṃ samattho na hoti; “gaṇhatha bhante, gaṇha dahara, gaṇha sāmaṇera, sace tumhe vā na karissatha, amhe vā na karissāma, ko dāni imaṃ karissatī”ti evaṃ ussāhaṃ janetvā saṃvidhātuṃ aññamaññaṃ kāretumpi samattho na hoti. Bhikkhūhi “kammaṃ karissāmā”ti vutte kiñci rogaṃ apadisati, bhikkhūnaṃ kammaṃ karontānaṃ samīpeneva vicarati, sīsameva dasseti, ayampi anārādhako hoti.

"Duties of various kinds" means major and minor tasks. Herein, tasks to be done by the unified Sangha having assembled after striking the bell, such as the repairing of a cetiya or a great mansion, are called major tasks. Tasks such as washing and dyeing robes, those included in the Khandhakas, and the duties of proper conduct such as the duties in the fire-hall, are called minor tasks. Herein, "he is not skilled" means in those tasks he is not clever or well-trained. "He is not diligent" means he is not endowed with initiative and energy; having heard, "There is work for the Sangha of bhikkhus," he does his meal duties early, enters an inner room, sleeps as long as he wishes, and comes out in the evening. "With resourcefulness for that" means with the means for those tasks. "With discernment" means with discernment that arises according to the situation. He is not endowed with the wisdom that arises in that very moment, thinking, "This should be done thus, this should not be done thus." "Not able to do, not able to arrange" means he is not capable of doing it even with his own hands; he is not capable of generating effort and arranging things or getting one another to do it by saying, "Take it, venerable sirs; take it, junior; take it, sāmaṇera. If you will not do it, or if we will not do it, who now will do this?" When it is said by the bhikkhus, "We will do the work," he points to some illness. He wanders about near the bhikkhus who are doing the work; he only shows his head. This one also is one who does not gratify.

Na tibbacchando hotīti balavacchando na [P 5.0993] hoti. Uddeseti pāḷipariyāpuṇane. Paripucchāyāti atthasavane. Adhisīleti pātimokkhasīle. Adhicitteti lokiyasamādhibhāvanāya. Adhipaññāyāti lokuttaramaggabhāvanāya.

"He does not have keen desire" means he does not have strong desire. In recitation, that is, in learning the Pāḷi; in questioning, that is, in hearing the meaning; in higher virtue, that is, in the virtue of the Pātimokkha; in higher mind, that is, in the development of mundane concentration; in higher wisdom, that is, in the development of the supramundane path.

Saṅkanto [M 0.0275] hotīti idhāgato hoti. Tassa satthunoti tassa titthāyatanasāmikassa. Tassa diṭṭhiyāti [V 0.0262] tassa santakāya laddhiyā. Idāni sāyeva laddhi yasmā tassa titthakarassa khamati ceva ruccati ca “idameva sacca”nti ca daḷhaggāhena gahitā; tasmā tassa khanti ruci ādāyoti vuccati. Tena vuttaṃ – “tassa khantiyā tassa ruciyā tassa ādāyassā”ti. Avaṇṇe bhaññamāneti garahāya bhaññamānāya. Anabhiraddhoti aparipuṇṇasaṅkappo; no paggahitacitto. Udaggoti abbhunnatakāyacitto. Idaṃ bhikkhave saṅghātanikaṃ aññatitthiyapubbassa anārādhanīyasminti bhikkhave yamidaṃ tassa satthuno tasseva ca laddhiyā avaṇṇe bhaññamāne “kiṃ ime paraṃ garahantī”ti kāyavacīvikāranibbattakaṃ anattamanattaṃ, buddhādīnañca avaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanattaṃ, yañca tasseva satthuno tasseva ca laddhiyā vaṇṇe bhaññamāne attamanattaṃ, buddhādīnañca vaṇṇabhaṇane anattamanattaṃ, idaṃ aññatitthiyapubbassa anārādhanīyasmiṃ saṅghātanikaṃ, anārādhake parivāsavattaṃ apūrake kamme idaṃ liṅgaṃ, idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ, idamacalappamāṇanti vuttaṃ hoti. Evaṃ anārādhako kho bhikkhave aññatitthiyapubbo āgato na upasampādetabboti ito ekenapi aṅgena samannāgato na upasampādetabbo. Sukkapakkhe sabbaṃ vuttavipallāsena veditabbaṃ.

"He has come over" means he has come here. "Of that teacher" means of that master of the heretical basis. "Of his view" means of his own doctrine. Now, that very doctrine, because it is agreeable to and preferred by that sectarian teacher, and is held with the firm grasp, "This alone is true," is therefore called his acceptance, preference, and adherence. Thus it was said: "of his acceptance, of his preference, of his adherence." "When dispraise is spoken" means when censure is spoken. "He is not gratified" means his intention is unfulfilled; his mind is not uplifted. "Elated" means his body and mind are uplifted. "Bhikkhus, this is a collective sign for one formerly of another sect who does not gratify" means: Bhikkhus, this dissatisfaction—which produces a particular action of body and speech, thinking, "Why do these ones censure another?"—that arises when dispraise of that teacher and of that very doctrine is spoken; and the satisfaction that arises when dispraise of the Buddha and others is spoken; and the satisfaction that arises when praise of that very teacher and that very doctrine is spoken; and the dissatisfaction that arises when praise of the Buddha and others is spoken—this is a collective sign for one formerly of another sect in the case of not gratifying. In the case of one who does not gratify, who does not fulfill the duties of probation, this is the sign, this is the characteristic, this is the unshakeable measure—this is the meaning. "Thus, bhikkhus, a former member of another sect who has come and does not gratify should not be given the higher ordination" means: one endowed with even one of these factors should not be given the higher ordination. In the positive case, everything should be understood by way of the reverse of what has been said.

Evaṃ ārādhako kho bhikkhaveti evaṃ nātikālena gāmappavesanā nātidivā paṭikkamanaṃ, na vesiyādigocaratā, sabrahmacārīnaṃ kiccesu dakkhatādi, uddesādīsu tibbacchandatā, titthiyānaṃ avaṇṇabhaṇane attamanatā, buddhādīnaṃ avaṇṇabhaṇane anattamanatā, titthiyānaṃ vaṇṇabhaṇane anattamanatā, buddhādīnaṃ vaṇṇabhaṇane attamanatāti imesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ titthiyavattānaṃ paripūraṇena [P 5.0994] ārādhako paritosako bhikkhūnaṃ aññatitthiyapubbo āgato upasampādetabbo.

"Thus, bhikkhus, one who gratifies..." means: Thus, by fulfilling these eight duties for former sectarians—namely, not entering the village too early and not returning too late in the day; not having prostitutes and the like as his resort; skill and so forth in the duties towards fellow celibates; keen desire in recitation and so forth; satisfaction when dispraise of the sectarians is spoken; dissatisfaction when dispraise of the Buddha and others is spoken; dissatisfaction when praise of the sectarians is spoken; and satisfaction when praise of the Buddha and others is spoken—a former member of another sect who has come, who gratifies and satisfies the bhikkhus, should be given the higher ordination.

Sace pana upasampadamāḷakepi ekaṃ vattaṃ bhindati, puna cattāro māse parivasitabbaṃ. Yathā pana bhinnasikkhāya sikkhamānāya puna sikkhāpadāni ca sikkhāsammuti ca diyyati, evaṃ nayimassa kiñci puna dātabbamatthi. Pubbe dinnaparivāsoyeva hi tassa parivāso. Tasmā puna cattāro māse parivasitabbaṃ. Sace parivasanto antarā aṭṭha samāpattiyo nibbatteti, lokiyadhammo [M 0.0276] nāma kuppanasabhāvo, na upasampādetabbo. Cattāro māse pūritavattova upasampādetabbo. Sace pana parivasanto cattāri mahābhūtāni pariggaṇhati, upādārūpāni paricchindati, nāmarūpaṃ vavatthapeti, tilakkhaṇaṃ āropetvā vipassanaṃ ārabhati, lokiyadhammo nāma kuppanasabhāvo, neva upasampādetabbo. Sace pana vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā sotāpattimaggaṃ paṭilabhati, paripuṇṇaṃyeva hoti vattaṃ. Samūhatāni sabbadiṭṭhigatāni abbuḷhaṃ vicikicchāsallaṃ [V 0.0263] taṃdivasameva upasampādetabbo. Sacepi titthiyaliṅge ṭhito sotāpanno hoti, parivāsakiccaṃ natthi, tadaheva pabbājetvā upasampādetabbo.

But if, even in the ordination enclosure, he breaks one duty, he must live on probation again for four months. Just as for a female trainee who has broken the training, the training rules and the training agreement are given again, so for this one, there is nothing that needs to be given again. For the probation previously given is indeed his probation. Therefore, he must live on probation again for four months. If, while living on probation, in the interim, he brings about the eight attainments, a worldly phenomenon is of an unstable nature; he should not be given the higher ordination. Only one who has fulfilled the duties for four months should be given the higher ordination. But if, while living on probation, he comprehends the four great elements, delineates derived forms, and begins insight meditation by applying the three characteristics, a worldly phenomenon is of an unstable nature; he should certainly not be given the higher ordination. But if, having developed insight, he attains the path of stream-entry, the duty is indeed fulfilled. All wrong views are uprooted, the dart of doubt is pulled out; he should be given the higher ordination that very day. Even if, while established in the guise of a sectarian, he becomes a stream-enterer, there is no need for probation; he should be given the going-forth and the higher ordination on that very day.

Upajjhāyamūlakaṃ cīvaraṃ pariyesitabbanti upajjhāyaṃ issaraṃ katvā tassa cīvaraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ. Pattampi tatheva. Tasmā yadi upajjhāyassa pattacīvaraṃ atthi, “imassa dehī”ti vattabbo. Atha natthi, aññe dātukāmā honti, tehipi upajjhāyasseva dātabbaṃ “idaṃ tumhākaṃ katvā imassa dethā”ti. Kasmā? Titthiyā nāma vilomā honti “saṅghena me pattacīvaraṃ dinnaṃ, kiṃ mayhaṃ tumhesu āyatta”nti vatvā ovādānusāsaniṃ na kareyyuṃ, upajjhāyena pana āyattajīvikattā tassa vacanakaro bhavissati. Tenassa “upajjhāyamūlakaṃ cīvaraṃ pariyesitabba”nti vuttaṃ. Bhaṇḍukammāyāti kesoropanatthaṃ. Bhaṇḍukammakathā parato āgamissati.

A robe should be sought that is rooted in the preceptor—this means, having made the preceptor the authority, a robe should be sought for that former sectarian novice. The bowl also should be sought in the same way. Therefore, if the preceptor has a bowl and robe, one should say, 'Give this to him.' If he does not, and others wish to give, they too should give it only to the preceptor, saying, 'Having made this your property, give it to him.' Why? Because sectarians are contrary. They might say, 'The Saṅgha has given me a bowl and robe. What of mine is dependent on you?' and not follow the admonition and instruction. But because his livelihood is dependent on the preceptor, he will do his bidding. Therefore, it is said for him, 'A robe should be sought that is rooted in the preceptor.' `Bhaṇḍukammāya` is for the purpose of shaving the hair. The discussion on `bhaṇḍukamma` will come later.

Aggikāti aggiparicaraṇakā. Jaṭilakāti tāpasā. Ete bhikkhave kiriyavādinoti ete kiriyaṃ na paṭibāhanti, “atthi kammaṃ, atthi kammavipāko”ti [P 5.0995] evaṃdiṭṭhikā. Sabbabuddhā hi nekkhammapāramiṃ pūrayamānā etadeva pabbajjaṃ pabbajitvā pūresuṃ, mayāpi tatheva pūritā, na etesaṃ sāsane pabbajjā vilomā, tasmā upasampādetabbā, na tesaṃ parivāso dātabboti. Imāhaṃ bhikkhave ñātīnaṃ āveṇikaṃ parihāraṃ dammīti imaṃ ahaṃ tesaṃ pāṭekkaṃ odissakaṃ parihāraṃ dadāmi. Kasmā evamāha? Te hi titthāyatane pabbajitāpi sāsanassa avaṇṇakāmā na honti, amhākaṃ ñātiseṭṭhassa sāsananti vaṇṇavādinova honti, tasmā evamāhāti.

`Aggikā` means those who attend to the fire. `Jaṭilakā` means ascetics. 'These, Bhikkhus, are affirmers of action' means: these do not obstruct action; they hold the view, 'There is kamma, there is the result of kamma.' Indeed, all Buddhas, while fulfilling the perfection of renunciation, went forth into this very ascetic life and thus fulfilled it. I too fulfilled it in the same way. The going forth in their teaching is not contrary; therefore, they should be fully ordained. Probation should not be given to them. 'Bhikkhus, I grant this special dispensation to my relatives' means: I give this individual and specific dispensation to them. Why did he say this? Because, although they have gone forth in the abode of sectarians, they are not those who desire dispraise of the Dispensation. They are only speakers of praise, saying, 'It is the Dispensation of our most excellent relative.' Therefore, he said this.

Aññatitthiyapubbavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Story of Former Sectarians is concluded.

Pañcābādhavatthukathā

The Discussion on the Story of the Five Afflictions

88. Magadhesu [M 0.0277] pañca ābādhā ussannā hontīti magadhanāmake janapade manussānañca amanussānañca pañca rogā ussannā vuḍḍhippattā phātippattā honti. Jīvakakomārabhaccakathā cīvarakkhandhake āvibhavissati. Na bhikkhave pañcahi ābādhehi phuṭṭho pabbājetabboti ye te kuṭṭhādayo pañca ābādhā ussannā, tehi phuṭṭho abhibhūto na pabbājetabbo.

88. 'In Magadha, five diseases were abundant' means: in the country named Magadha, five diseases among humans and non-humans were abundant, had reached growth, and had proliferated. The discussion on Jīvaka Komārabhacca will become manifest in the Cīvarakkhandhaka. 'Bhikkhus, one afflicted by the five diseases should not be given the going forth' means: one who is afflicted and overwhelmed by those five abundant diseases, such as leprosy, should not be given the going forth.

Tattha kuṭṭhanti rattakuṭṭhaṃ vā hotu kāḷakuṭṭhaṃ vā, yaṃkiñci kiṭibhadaddukacchuādippabhedampi sabbaṃ [V 0.0264] kuṭṭhamevāti vuttaṃ. Tañce nakhapiṭṭhippamāṇampi vaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhitaṃ hoti, na pabbājetabbo. Sace pana nivāsanapārupanehi pakatipaṭicchanne ṭhāne nakhapiṭṭhippamāṇaṃ avaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhitaṃ hoti, vaṭṭati. Mukhe pana hatthapādapiṭṭhesu vā sacepi avaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhitaṃ nakhapiṭṭhito ca khuddakatarampi, na vaṭṭatiyevāti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tikicchāpetvā pabbājentenāpi pakativaṇṇe jāteyeva pabbājetabbo. Godhāpiṭṭhisadisacuṇṇaokiraṇakasarīrampi pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati.

Therein, `kuṭṭha` means: whether it be red leprosy or black leprosy, or any other kind such as `kiṭibha`, `daddu`, or `kacchu`—all, it is said, is just `kuṭṭha`. If it is even the size of the back of a little fingernail and is in a state of growth, he should not be given the going forth. But if, in a place naturally covered by the lower and upper robes, it is the size of the back of a little fingernail and is in a state of non-growth, it is allowable. But on the face, or on the backs of the hands or feet, even if it is in a state of non-growth and is even smaller than the back of a little fingernail, it is not allowable at all; so it is said in the Kurundī. Even when giving the going forth after having had it treated, one should do so only when the natural skin color has arisen. It is not allowable to give the going forth to one whose body is sprinkled with powder resembling the back of an iguana.

Gaṇḍoti medagaṇḍo vā hotu añño vā yo koci kolaṭṭhimattakopi ce vaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhito gaṇḍo hoti, na pabbājetabbo. Paṭicchannaṭṭhāne pana kolaṭṭhimatte avaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhito [P 5.0996] vaṭṭati. Mukhādike appaṭicchannaṭṭhāne avaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhitopi na vaṭṭati. Tikicchāpetvā pabbājentenāpi sarīraṃ sañchaviṃ kāretvāva pabbājetabbo. Uṇṇigaṇḍā nāma honti gothanā viya aṅgulikā viya ca tattha tattha lambanti, etepi gaṇḍāyeva. Tesu sati pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Daharakāle khīrapiḷakā yobbannakāle ca mukhe kharapiḷakā nāma honti, mahallakakāle nassanti, na tā gaṇḍasaṅkhyaṃ gacchanti, tāsu sati pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Aññe pana sarīre kharapiḷakā nāma aparā padumakaṇṇikā nāma honti, aññā sāsapabījakā nāma sāsapamattā eva sakalasarīraṃ pharanti, tā sabbā kuṭṭhajātikā eva. Tāsu sati na pabbājetabbo.

`Gaṇḍa` means: whether it be a fatty tumor or another kind, any tumor whatsoever, even if it is the size of a jujube seed and is in a state of growth, he should not be given the going forth. But in a concealed place, if it is the size of a jujube seed and in a state of non-growth, it is allowable. In an unconcealed place such as the face, even if it is in a state of non-growth, it is not allowable. Even when giving the going forth after having had it treated, one should do so only after having made the body have good, clear skin. There are things called `uṇṇigaṇḍā`; they hang down here and there like a cow's teats or like little fingers. These too are just tumors. If they are present, it is not allowable to give the going forth. In childhood there are milk-pimples, and in youth, on the face there are milk-pimples; in old age, they disappear. They do not go into the count of tumors. If they are present, it is allowable to give the going forth. But there are other rough pimples on the body, and others called `padumakaṇṇikā`. Others called `sāsapabījakā`, being just the size of mustard seeds, spread over the whole body. All of these are of the nature of leprosy. If they are present, he should not be given the going forth.

Kilāsoti [M 0.0278] na bhijjanakaṃ na paggharaṇakaṃ padumapuṇḍarīkapattavaṇṇaṃ kuṭṭhaṃ, yena gunnaṃ viya sabalaṃ sarīraṃ hoti, tasmiṃ kuṭṭhe vuttanayeneva vinicchayo veditabbo. Sosoti sosabyādhi; tasmiṃ sati na pabbājetabbo. Apamāroti pittummāro vā yakkhummāro vā; tattha pubbaverikena amanussena gahito duttikiccho hoti. Appamattakepi pana apamāre sati na pabbājetabbo.

`Kilāsa` is a type of leprosy that does not break open and does not ooze fluid, having the color of a lotus or white lotus leaf, by which the body becomes mottled like that of cattle. The decision concerning this leprosy should be understood according to the method already stated. `Sosa` is a wasting disease; if it is present, he should not be given the going forth. `Apamāra` is madness from deranged bile or madness from being seized by a yakkha. Among these, one seized by a non-human who was a former enemy is difficult to cure. But even if the madness is minor, he should not be given the going forth.

Pañcābādhavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The Discussion on the Story of the Five Afflictions is concluded.

Rājabhaṭavatthukathā

The Discussion on the Story of the Royal Servant

90. Rājabhaṭavatthusmiṃ – paccantaṃ uccinathāti paccantaṃ vaḍḍhetha. Core palāpetvā corabhayena vuṭṭhite gāme āvāsāpetvā ārakkhaṃ datvā kasikammādīni pavattāpethāti vuttaṃ hoti. Rājā pana sotāpannattā “core ghātetha, hanathā”ti na āṇāpeti. Upajjhāyassa deva sīsaṃ [V 0.0265] chinditabbantiādi sabbaṃ “pabbajjāya upajjhāyo seṭṭho, tato ācariyo, tato gaṇo”ti cintetvā idaṃ vohāre aḍḍavinicchaye āgatanti āhaṃsu. Na bhikkhave rājabhaṭo pabbājetabboti ettha amacco vā hotu mahāmatto vā sevako vā kiñci ṭhānantaraṃ patto vā appatto vā, yo koci rañño bhattavetanabhaṭo, sabbo rājabhaṭoti saṅkhyaṃ gacchati, so na pabbājetabbo. Tassa pana puttanattabhātukā ye rājato bhattavetanaṃ na gaṇhanti, te pabbājetuṃ [P 5.0997] vaṭṭati. Yo pana rājato laddhaṃ nibaddhabhogaṃ vā māsasaṃvaccharaparibbayaṃ vā raññoyeva niyyāteti, puttabhātuke vā taṃ ṭhānaṃ sampaṭicchāpetvā rājānaṃ “na dānāhaṃ devassa bhaṭo”ti āpucchati, yena vā yaṃ kammakāraṇā vetanaṃ gahitaṃ, taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ hoti, yo vā pabbajassūti raññā anuññāto hoti, tampi pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati.

90. Regarding the case of a royal servant—'Clear the border area' means 'Develop the border area.' Having driven out thieves, and having resettled the villages that were abandoned due to fear of thieves, having provided protection, cause farming and other work to proceed. This is the meaning. However, the king, being a stream-enterer, does not command, 'Kill the thieves, strike them down.' Regarding the statement, 'O king, the preceptor's head should be cut off,' and so on—having considered, 'In the going forth, the preceptor is highest, then the teacher, then the group,' they submitted that this came from a legal text, in an incomplete judgment. Herein, in 'Monks, a royal servant should not be ordained': whether an official, a great minister, or a servant, whether he has attained some rank or not—whoever is a servant of the king receiving food and wages, all are counted as a royal servant; he should not be ordained. However, his sons, grandsons, or brothers who do not receive food and wages from the king, it is proper to ordain them. But one who returns to the king a fixed income or a monthly and yearly allowance received from him; or who, having had his sons or brothers accept his position, takes leave of the king, saying, 'I am no longer Your Majesty's servant'; or for whom the work for which the wages were taken has been completed; or who is permitted by the king to go forth—it is also proper to ordain him.

Rājabhaṭavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The Story of the Royal Servant is concluded.

Coravatthukathā

The Story of a Thief

91. Coravatthūsu – manussā passitvāti yehi gihikāle diṭṭhapubbo ye ca “ayaṃ so”ti aññesaṃ suṇanti, te passitvā ubbijjantipi…pe… dvārampi [M 0.0279] thakenti. Ye pana na jānanti, tesaṃ gharesu bhikkhaṃ labhati. Na bhikkhaveti bhagavā sayaṃ dhammassāmī, tasmā āyatiṃ akaraṇatthāya bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññapento evamāha. Tattha dhajaṃ bandhitvā viya vicaratīti dhajabandho. Mūladevādayo viya loke pākaṭoti vuttaṃ hoti. Tasmā yo gāmaghātaṃ vā panthaduhanaṃ vā nagare sandhicchedādikammaṃ vā karonto vicarati, paññāyati ca “asuko nāma idaṃ idaṃ karotī”ti, so na pabbājetabbo. Yo pana rājaputto rajjaṃ patthento gāmaghātādīni karoti, so pabbājetabbo. Rājāno hi tasmiṃ pabbajite tussanti, sace pana na tussanti, na pabbājetabbo. Pubbe mahājane pākaṭo coro pacchā corakammaṃ pahāya pañcasīlādīni samādiyati, tañce manussā evaṃ jānanti, pabbājetabbo. Ye pana ambalabujādicorakā sandhicchedādicorā eva vā adissamānā theyyaṃ karonti, pacchāpi iminā nāma idaṃ katanti na paññāyanti, tepi pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati.

In the cases of thieves—'when people see' means: those by whom he was seen before in his lay life, and those who hear from others, 'This is he'—they, upon seeing him, become agitated... and even bar their doors. But from those who do not know him, he receives alms in their houses. The Blessed One, being himself the Lord of the Dhamma, therefore, for the sake of non-commission in the future, laid down a training rule for the monks and said thus. Therein, 'one who wanders about as if having tied on a banner' is a notorious bandit (dhajabandha). It is said that he is notorious in the world like Mūladeva and others. Therefore, one who wanders about committing village destruction, or highway robbery, or acts like housebreaking in a city, and is known as 'so-and-so does this and that,' he should not be ordained. But a prince who, aspiring to the kingdom, commits village destruction and so on, he may be ordained. For kings are pleased when he has gone forth. But if they are not pleased, he should not be ordained. A thief, formerly notorious among the populace, who afterwards abandons thievery and undertakes the five precepts and so on—if people know him as such, he may be ordained. But those petty thieves of mangoes, breadfruit, and so on, or even housebreakers and so on, who commit theft unseen, and are not known afterwards as 'this was done by so-and-so,' it is also proper to ordain them.

92. Kāraṃ bhinditvāti aṭṭabandhanādiṃ bhinditvā. Abhayūvarāti ettha bhayena uparamantīti bhayūvarā, ete pana laddhābhayattā na bhayūvarāti abhayūvarā; pakārassa cettha vakāro katoti veditabbo. Na bhikkhave kārabhedako pabbājetabboti kāro vuccati bandhanāgāraṃ. Idha pana andubandhanaṃ [P 5.0998][V 0.0266] vā hotu saṅkhalikabandhanaṃ vā rajjubandhanaṃ vā gāmabandhanaṃ vā nigamabandhanaṃ vā nagarabandhanaṃ vā purisagutti vā janapadabandhanaṃ vā dīpabandhanaṃ vā, yo etesu yaṃkiñci bandhanaṃ bhinditvā vā chinditvā vā muñcitvā vā vivaritvā vā passamānānaṃ vā apassamānānaṃ vā palāyati, so kārabhedakoti saṅkhyaṃ gacchati. Tasmā īdiso kārabhedako coro dīpabandhanaṃ bhinditvā dīpantaraṃ gatopi na pabbājetabbo. Yo pana na coro, kevalaṃ hatthakammaṃ akaronto “evaṃ no apalāyanto karissatī”ti rājayuttādīhi baddho, so kāraṃ bhinditvā palātopi pabbājetabbo. Yo pana gāmanigamapaṭṭanādīni keṇiyā gahetvā taṃ asampādento bandhanāgāraṃ pavesito hoti, so palāyitvā āgato na pabbājetabbo. Yopi kasikammādīhi dhanaṃ sampādetvā jīvanto “nidhānaṃ iminā laddha”nti pesuññaṃ upasaṃharitvā kenaci bandhāpito hoti, taṃ tattheva pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati, palāyitvā gataṃ pana gataṭṭhāne pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati.

91. 'Having broken the prison' means having broken confinement such as stocks and so on. Herein, regarding 'abhayūvarā': those who desist out of fear are 'bhayūvarā'. But these, because they have obtained fearlessness, are not 'bhayūvarā', hence 'abhayūvarā'; and here it should be understood that the letter 'p' has been made into 'v'. 'Monks, a prison-breaker should not be ordained.' 'Kārā' is called a house of confinement. Here, whether it be confinement in stocks, or confinement in chains, or confinement by rope, or village confinement, or market-town confinement, or city confinement, or custody by men, or district confinement, or island confinement—whoever flees, whether seen or unseen, by breaking, or cutting, or untying, or opening any of these confinements, he is counted as a prison-breaker. Therefore, such a prison-breaking thief, even having broken island confinement and gone to another island, should not be ordained. But one who is not a thief, who, merely for not doing manual labor, is bound by royal officials and others with the thought, 'Thus he will do our work without fleeing'—even if he breaks confinement and flees, he may be ordained. But one who, having taken on lease villages, market-towns, ports, etc., and not fulfilling the payment, is put into a house of confinement—if he flees and comes, he should not be ordained. Also one who, while living by earning wealth through farming etc., is caused to be bound by someone who brings slander, saying, 'A treasure has been found by this one'—it is not proper to ordain him right there. But if he has fled and gone, it is proper to ordain him in the place he has gone to.

93. Na [M 0.0280] bhikkhave likhitakoti ettha likhitako nāma na kevalaṃ “yattha passati tattha hantabbo”ti, atha kho yo koci corikaṃ vā aññaṃ vā garuṃ rājāparādhaṃ katvā palāto, rājā ca naṃ paṇṇe vā potthake vā “itthannāmo yattha dissati, tattha gahetvā māretabbo”ti vā “hatthapādānissa chinditabbānī”ti vā “ettakaṃ nāma daṇḍaṃ āharāpetabbo”ti vā likhāpeti, ayaṃ likhitako nāma, so na pabbājetabbo.

92. Herein, in 'Monks, one who is proscribed': a proscribed person (likhitako) is not merely one about whom it is written, 'Wherever one sees him, there he is to be killed.' But rather, it is anyone who, having committed theft or another serious offense against the king, has fled, and the king has it written on a leaf or in a book: 'Wherever so-and-so is seen, there he is to be seized and killed,' or 'His hands and feet are to be cut off,' or 'Such-and-such a fine is to be exacted from him.' This is called a proscribed person. He should not be ordained.

94. Kasāhato katadaṇḍakammoti ettha yo vacanapesanādīni akaronto haññati, na so katadaṇḍakammo. Yo pana keṇiyā vā aññathā vā kiñci gahetvā khāditvā puna dātuṃ asakkonto “ayameva te daṇḍo hotū”ti kasāhi haññati, ayaṃ kasāhato katadaṇḍakammo. So ca kasāhi vā hato hotu addhadaṇḍakādīnaṃ vā aññatarena, yāva allavaṇo hoti, tāva na pabbājetabbo. Vaṇe pana pākatike katvā pabbājetabbo. Sace pana jāṇūhi vā kapparehi vā nāḷikerapāsāṇādīhi vā ghātetvā mutto hoti, sarīre cassa gaṇṭhiyo paññāyanti, na pabbājetabbo. Phāsukaṃ [P 5.0999] katvā eva gaṇṭhīsu sannisinnāsu pabbājetabbo.

94. Regarding 'one punished by flogging, on whom a penalty has been inflicted': Herein, whoever is tormented for not carrying out spoken instructions, errands, and so forth, is not one on whom a penalty has been inflicted. However, one who, having taken and consumed something by purchase or by other means, is unable to repay it and is tormented with whips, being told, 'Let this very thing be your punishment,' this person is one punished by flogging, on whom a penalty has been inflicted. And whether he is tormented with whips or with one of various things such as a half-length staff, as long as he has a raw wound, for that long he should not be ordained. He should be ordained only after the wound has returned to its natural state. But if he has been tormented with knees, elbows, or with things such as coconut shells or stones and released, and lumps are apparent on his body, he should not be ordained. He should be ordained only after he is comfortable and the lumps have subsided.

95. Lakkhaṇāhato katadaṇḍakammoti ettha katadaṇḍakammabhāvo purimanayeneva veditabbo. Yassa pana nalāṭe vā ūruādīsu vā tattena lohena lakkhaṇaṃ āhataṃ hoti, so sace bhujisso yāva allavaṇo hoti, tāva na pabbājetabbo. Sacepissa vaṇā ruḷhā honti, chaviyā [V 0.0267] samaparicchedā, lakkhaṇaṃ na paññāyati, timaṇḍalavatthassa uttarāsaṅge kate paṭicchannokāse ce hoti, pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati, appaṭicchannokāse ce na vaṭṭati.

95. Regarding 'one punished by branding, on whom a penalty has been inflicted': Herein, the state of having had a penalty inflicted should be understood in the same way as before. However, for one on whose forehead, thighs, or other parts a mark has been struck with hot iron, if he is a freeman, he should not be ordained as long as the wound is raw. Even if his wounds have healed and are level with the skin, it is allowable to ordain him if the mark is in a place that is concealed when the upper robe is worn; if it is in an unconcealed place, it is not allowable.

Coravatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The section on the matter of the thief is concluded.

Iṇāyikavatthukathā

The section on the matter of the debtor

96. Na bhikkhave iṇāyikoti ettha iṇāyiko nāma yassa pitipitāmahehi vā iṇaṃ gahitaṃ hoti, sayaṃ vā iṇaṃ gahitaṃ hoti, yaṃ vā āthapetvā mātāpitūhi kiñci gahitaṃ hoti, so taṃ [M 0.0281] iṇaṃ paresaṃ dhāretīti iṇāyiko. Yaṃ pana aññe ñātakā āthapetvā kiñci gaṇhanti, so na iṇāyiko. Na hi te taṃ āthapetuṃ issarā, tasmā taṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati, itaraṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace panassa ñātisālohitā “mayaṃ dassāma, pabbājetha na”nti iṇaṃ attano bhāraṃ karonti, añño vā koci tassa ācārasampattiṃ disvā “pabbājetha naṃ, ahaṃ iṇaṃ dassāmī”ti vadati, pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Tesu asati bhikkhunā tathārūpassa upaṭṭhākassāpi ārocetabbaṃ “sahetuko satto iṇapalibodhena na pabbajatī”ti. Sace so paṭipajjati, pabbājetabbo. Sacepi attano kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ atthi, “etaṃ dassāmī”ti pabbājetabbo. Sace pana neva ñātakādayo paṭipajjanti, na attano dhanaṃ atthi, “pabbājetvā bhikkhāya caritvā mocessāmī”ti pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace pabbājeti dukkaṭaṃ. Palātopi ānetvā dātabbo. No ce deti, sabbaṃ iṇaṃ gīvā hoti. Ajānitvā pabbājayato anāpatti. Passantena pana ānetvā iṇasāmikānaṃ dassetabbo. Apassantassa gīvā na hoti.

96. Regarding 'Monks, do not ordain a debtor': Herein, one called a 'debtor' is a person whose father or grandfather took a debt, or who has taken a debt himself, or one whose parents took something by placing him as security; because he bears that debt for others, he is called a debtor. However, one for whom other relatives take something by placing him as security is not a debtor. Indeed, they are not authorized to place him as security. Therefore, it is allowable to ordain him; the other case is not allowable. But if his blood relatives make the debt their own burden, saying, 'We will repay it; ordain him,' or if some other person, seeing his good conduct, says, 'Ordain him; I will repay the debt,' it is allowable to ordain him. In their absence, the monk should inform even a suitable supporter, saying: 'A being with potential cannot go forth due to the obstacle of debt.' If that person undertakes it, he should be ordained. Even if the preceptor has his own allowable goods, he may ordain him, thinking, 'I will give this.' However, if neither the relatives nor others undertake it, and the preceptor has no wealth of his own, it is not allowable to ordain him thinking, 'Having ordained him, I will get him released by means of the alms round.' If he does ordain him, there is a `dukkaṭa` offense. Even if the ordained person runs away, he should be brought back and given over. If he does not give him over, the entire debt becomes a liability. For one who ordains him without knowing, there is no offense. However, upon seeing him, the preceptor should bring him and show him to the creditors. For one who does not see him, there is no liability.

Sace iṇāyiko aññaṃ desaṃ gantvā pucchiyamānopi “nāhaṃ kassaci kiñci dhāremī”ti vatvā pabbajati, iṇasāmiko ca taṃ pariyesanto tattha gacchati, daharo taṃ disvā palāyati, so ca theraṃ upasaṅkamitvā “ayaṃ bhante kena pabbājito, mama ettakaṃ nāma dhanaṃ gahetvā [P 5.1000] palāto”ti vadati, therena vattabbaṃ “mayā upāsaka ‘aṇaṇo aha’nti vadanto pabbājito, kiṃ dāni karomi, passa me pattacīvaramatta”nti ayaṃ tattha sāmīci. Palāte pana gīvā na hoti.

If a debtor goes to another region and, even when asked, says, 'I owe nothing to anyone,' and then goes forth, and the creditor, searching for him, goes there, and the young monk, seeing him, flees, and the creditor approaches the elder and says, 'Venerable sir, by whom was this one ordained? He took such and such wealth from me and fled,' then the elder should say, 'Lay follower, I ordained him when he said, "I am without debt." What can I do now? See, I have only my bowl and robes.' This is the proper conduct in that situation. But if he flees, there is no liability.

Sace pana naṃ therassa sammukhāva disvā “ayaṃ mama iṇāyiko”ti vadati, “tava iṇāyikaṃ [V 0.0268] tvameva jānāhī”ti vattabbo. Evampi gīvā na hoti. Sacepi so “pabbajito ayaṃ idāni kuhiṃ gamissatī”ti vadati, therena “tvaṃyeva jānāhī”ti vattabbo. Evampissa palāte gīvā na hoti. Sace pana thero “kuhiṃ dāni ayaṃ gamissati, idheva acchatū”ti vadati, so ce palāyati, gīvā hoti. Sace so sahetukasatto hoti vattasampanno, therena “īdiso aya”nti vattabbaṃ. Iṇasāmiko ce “sādhū”ti vissajjeti, iccetaṃ kusalaṃ. Sace pana “upaḍḍhupaḍḍhaṃ dethā”ti vadati, dātabbaṃ. Aparena samayena atiārādhako hoti, “sabbaṃ dethā”ti [M 0.0282] vuttepi dātabbameva. Sace pana uddesaparipucchādīsu kusalo hoti bahūpakāro bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhācāravattena pariyesitvāpi iṇaṃ dātabbamevāti.

But if, seeing him in the elder's presence, the creditor says, 'This is my debtor,' he should be told, 'You yourself know your debtor.' Even so, there is no liability. Even if the creditor says, 'This one is ordained; where will he go now?' the elder should say, 'You yourself know.' Even so, if the disciple flees, there is no liability for the elder. But if the elder says, 'Where will he go now? Let him stay right here,' and he flees, there is a liability. If the disciple is a being with potential and endowed with good conduct, the elder should say, 'This one is of such a nature.' If the creditor says, 'Good,' and releases him from the debt, this is skillful. But if he says, 'Give it in installments,' it should be given. If at a later time the disciple becomes very accomplished in his duties, even when told by the creditor, 'Give all,' it should indeed be given. But if he is skilled in recitation, questioning, and so forth, and is of great help to the monks, the debt should indeed be given, even if it means seeking the means through the practice of the alms round.

Iṇāyikavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The section on the matter of the debtor is concluded.

Dāsavatthukathā

The section on the matter of a slave

97. Na bhikkhave dāsoti ettha cattāro dāsā – antojāto, dhanakkīto, karamarānīto, sāmaṃ dāsabyaṃ upagatoti. Tattha antojāto nāma jātidāso gharadāsiyā putto. Dhanakkīto nāma mātāpitūnaṃ santikā putto vā sāmikānaṃ santikā dāso vā dhanaṃ datvā dāsacārittaṃ āropetvā kīto. Ete dvepi na pabbājetabbā. Pabbājentena tattha tattha cārittavasena adāsaṃ katvā pabbājetabbā.

97. Here, in the passage beginning 'Monks, not a slave,' there are four kinds of slaves: one born inside the house, one bought with wealth, one brought as a prisoner of war, and one who has himself approached the state of being a slave. Among these, 'one born inside the house' is a slave by birth, the son of a female house-slave. 'One bought with wealth' is one who is bought, either a son from his parents or a slave from his owners, by giving wealth and imposing the conduct of a slave. These two are not to be given the going forth. By the preceptor who wishes to give the going forth, they are to be given the going forth only after having been made not a slave, according to the custom in that particular place.

Karamarānīto nāma tiroraṭṭhaṃ vilopaṃ vā katvā upalāpetvā vā tiroraṭṭhato bhujissamānusakāni āharanti, antoraṭṭheyeva vā katāparādhaṃ kiñci gāmaṃ rājā “vilumpathā”ti āṇāpeti, tato mānusakānipi āharanti. Tattha sabbe purisā dāsā, itthiyo dāsiyo. Evarūpo karamarānīto dāso yehi ānīto, tesaṃ santike vasanto vā bandhanāgāre baddho vā purisehi rakkhiyamāno vā na pabbājetabbo. Palāyitvā pana gato, gataṭṭhāne pabbājetabbo. Raññā [P 5.1001] tuṭṭhena “karamarānītake muñcathā”ti vatvā vā sabbasādhāraṇena vā nayena bandhanā mokkhe kate pabbājetabbova.

'One brought as a prisoner of war' is to be understood thus: they bring free persons from a foreign country, either by plundering the foreign country or by deception. Or, within their own country, a king may order, 'Plunder it!' regarding a certain village that has committed an offense, and from there also they bring people. In that case, all the men are male slaves and the women are female slaves. Such a slave brought as a prisoner of war is not to be given the going forth, whether he is living in the presence of those who brought him, is bound in a prison, or is being guarded by men. But if, having fled, he has gone away, he is to be given the going forth in the place where he has gone. If a king, being pleased, says, 'Release the prisoners of war,' or if a release from bondage is made by a general decree, he is certainly to be given the going forth.

Sāmaṃ dāsabyaṃ upagato nāma jīvitahetu vā ārakkhahetu vā “ahaṃ te dāso”ti sayameva dāsabhāvaṃ upagato. Rājūnaṃ hatthiassagomahiṃsagopakādayo viya, tādiso dāso na pabbājetabbo. Rañño vaṇṇadāsīnaṃ puttā honti amaccaputtasadisā, tepi na pabbājetabbā. Bhujissitthiyo [V 0.0269] asaṃyatā vaṇṇadāsīhi saddhiṃ vicaranti, tāsaṃ putte pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace sayameva paṇṇaṃ [M 0.0283] āropenti, na vaṭṭati. Bhaṭiputtakagaṇādīnaṃ dāsāpi tehi adinnā na pabbājetabbā. Vihāresu rājūhi ārāmikadāsā nāma dinnā honti, tepi pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Bhujisse pana katvā pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Mahāpaccariyaṃ “antojātadhanakkītake ānetvā bhikkhusaṅghassa ārāmike demāti denti, takkaṃ sīse āsittakasadisāva honti, te pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ. Kurundiyaṃ pana “ārāmikaṃ demāti kappiyavohārena denti, yena kenaci vohārena dinno hotu, neva pabbājetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Duggatamanussā saṅghaṃ nissāya jīvissāmāti vihāre kappiyakārakā honti, etepi pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Yassa mātāpitaro dāsā, mātā eva vā dāsī, pitā adāso, taṃ pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Yassa pana mātā adāsī, pitā dāso, taṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhussa ñātakā vā upaṭṭhākā vā dāsaṃ denti “imaṃ pabbājetha, tumhākaṃ veyyāvaccaṃ karissatī”ti attanovāssa dāso atthi, bhujisso katova pabbājetabbo. Sāmikā dāsaṃ denti “imaṃ pabbājetha, sace abhiramissati, adāso vibbhamissati ce, amhākaṃ dāsova bhavissatīti ayaṃ tāvakāliko nāma, taṃ pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Nissāmikadāso hoti, sopi bhujisso katova pabbājetabbo. Ajānanto pabbājetvā vā upasampādetvā vā pacchā jānāti, bhujissaṃ kātumeva vaṭṭati.

'One who has himself approached the state of being a slave' means one who, for the sake of livelihood or for protection, has himself approached the state of being a slave, saying, 'I am your slave.' Like the elephant-keepers, horse-keepers, cowherds, and buffalo-herdsmen of kings, such a slave is not to be given the going forth. The sons of a king's courtesans, who are like the sons of ministers, are also not to be given the going forth. The sons of unrestrained free women who associate with courtesans may be given the going forth. If the women themselves are entered onto the register of courtesans, it is not permissible to ordain their sons. Slaves belonging to groups such as the worshippers of the deity Kumāra, if not given by them, are not to be given the going forth. Slaves called monastery attendants, who have been given to monasteries by kings, are also not to be given the going forth. But it is permissible to give them the going forth after having made them free persons. In the Mahāpaccariya it is said: 'When they bring those born in the household and those bought with wealth and give them to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha as monastery attendants, saying, "We give these monastery attendants," they are just like toddy poured on the head; it is permissible to give them the going forth.' But in the Kurundī it is said: 'They give them saying, "We give a monastery attendant," using proper terminology. Whether given by this or any other terminology, he is never to be given the going forth.' Poor people who think, 'We will live by depending on the Saṅgha,' and become monastery workers in a monastery—it is permissible to give these the going forth as well. He whose parents are slaves, or whose mother only is a slave while his father is not a slave, is not to be given the going forth. But he whose mother is not a slave while his father is a slave—it is permissible to give him the going forth. If relatives or supporters of a bhikkhu give a slave, saying, 'Give this one the going forth; he will perform services for you,' or if the bhikkhu himself has a slave, he is only to be given the going forth after being made a free person. Owners may give a slave, saying, 'Give this one the going forth. If he delights in the holy life, he is not a slave. But if he disrobes, he will be our slave as before.' This is called a temporary freedman, and it is not permissible to give him the going forth, as is said in the Kurundī. There may be a slave without an owner; he too is only to be given the going forth after being made a free person. If one, not knowing, gives the going forth or the higher ordination and finds out later, it is proper to arrange for the person's freedom.

Imassa ca atthassa pakāsanatthaṃ idaṃ vatthuṃ vadanti – ekā kira kuladāsī ekena saddhiṃ anurādhapurā palāyitvā rohaṇe vasamānā [P 5.1002] puttaṃ paṭilabhi, so pabbajitvā upasampannakāle lajjī kukkuccako ahosi. Athekadivasaṃ mātaraṃ pucchi – “kiṃ upāsike tumhākaṃ bhātā vā bhaginī vā natthi, na kañci ñātakaṃ passāmī”ti. “Tāta, ahaṃ anurādhapure kuladāsī, tava pitarā saddhiṃ palāyitvā idha vasāmī”ti. Sīlavā bhikkhu “asuddhā kira me pabbajjā”ti saṃvegaṃ labhitvā mātaraṃ tassa kulassa nāmagottaṃ pucchitvā anurādhapuraṃ āgamma tassa kulassa gharadvāre aṭṭhāsi. “Aticchatha bhante”ti vuttepi nātikkami, te āgantvā “kiṃ bhante”ti pucchiṃsu. “Tumhākaṃ itthannāmā dāsī palātā atthī”ti? Atthi bhante. Ahaṃ tassā putto, sace maṃ tumhe anujānātha, pabbajjaṃ labhāmi, tumhe mayhaṃ sāmikāti[M 0.0284]. Te haṭṭhatuṭṭhā hutvā “suddhā bhante tumhākaṃ pabbajjā”ti taṃ bhujissaṃ katvā mahāvihāre vasāpesuṃ catūhi paccayehi paṭijaggantā. Thero taṃ kulaṃ nissāya vasamānoyeva arahattaṃ pāpuṇīti.

And to make this meaning clear, they tell this story. It is said that a certain family's female slave fled from Anurādhapura with a man and, while living in Rohaṇa, she bore a son. He, having gone forth, at the time of his higher ordination became conscientious and scrupulous. Then one day he asked his mother, 'Upāsikā, is it that you have no brother or sister? I do not see any relative.' She said, 'My son, I am a family slave in Anurādhapura. Having fled with your father, I am living here.' The virtuous bhikkhu, thinking, 'It seems my ordination is impure,' experienced a sense of spiritual urgency. Having asked his mother the name and clan of that family, he came to Anurādhapura and stood at the door of that family's house. Even when it was said, 'Pass by, venerable sir,' he did not pass by. They came and asked, 'What is it, venerable sir?' He asked, 'Do you have a runaway female slave of such-and-such a name?' 'Yes, venerable sir.' 'I am her son. If you give your consent for me, I may retain my ordination. You are my masters.' They, being joyful and pleased, said, 'Venerable sir, your ordination is pure.' Having made him a free person, they had him dwell in the Mahāvihāra, attending to him with the four requisites. The elder, while dwelling depending on that family, attained Arahantship.

Dāsavatthukathā niṭṭhitā.

The section concerning slaves is concluded.

Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthādikathā

The Story of the Goldsmith's Shaven-headed Son and Other Matters

98-9. Kammārabhaṇḍūti [V 0.0270] tulādhāramuṇḍako suvaṇṇakāraputto, pañcasikho taruṇadārakoti vuttaṃ hoti. Saṅghaṃ apaloketuṃ bhaṇḍukammāyāti saṅghaṃ bhaṇḍukammatthāya āpucchituṃ anujānāmīti attho. Tatrāyaṃ āpucchanavidhi – sīmāpariyāpanne bhikkhū sannipātetvā pabbajjāpekkhaṃ tattha netvā “saṅghaṃ bhante imassa dārakassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmī”ti tikkhattuṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā sakiṃ vā vattabbaṃ. Ettha ca “imassa dārakassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchāmī”tipi “imassa samaṇakaraṇaṃ āpucchāmī”tipi “imassa pabbājanaṃ āpucchāmī”tipi “ayaṃ samaṇo hotukāmo”tipi “ayaṃ pabbajitukāmo”tipi vattuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

98-9. ‘Kammārabhaṇḍu’ means the young boy, the shaven-headed son of a goldsmith who carries the scales, who has five topknots. ‘To inform the Saṅgha for the head-shaving’ means ‘I permit asking the Saṅgha for the purpose of the head-shaving.’ Herein, this is the procedure for asking: Having assembled the bhikkhus included within the boundary, and having brought the aspirant for the going-forth there, it should be stated three times, or twice, or once: ‘Venerable Sirs, I ask the Saṅgha about the head-shaving of this boy.’ And in this context, it is also permissible to say: ‘I ask about the head-shaving of this boy,’ or ‘I ask about making this one a recluse,’ or ‘I ask about giving the going-forth to this one,’ or ‘This one wishes to become a recluse,’ or ‘This one wishes to go forth.’

Sace sabhāgaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, dasa vā vīsaṃ vā tiṃsaṃ vā bhikkhū vasantīti paricchedo paññāyati, tesaṃ ṭhitokāsaṃ vā nisinnokāsaṃ vā gantvāpi purimanayeneva āpucchitabbaṃ. Pabbajjāpekkhaṃ vināva daharabhikkhū vā sāmaṇere vā pesetvāpi “eko bhante pabbajjāpekkho atthi tassa bhaṇḍukammaṃ [P 5.1003] āpucchāmā”tiādinā nayena āpucchāpetuṃ vaṭṭati.

If there is a common residence, and it is known that ten, twenty, or thirty bhikkhus are dwelling there, one should go to their standing place or sitting place and ask in the same manner as before. It is permissible, even without the aspirant for the going-forth, to have the asking done by sending junior bhikkhus or sāmaṇeras, according to the method beginning with, ‘Venerable Sirs, there is one aspirant for the going-forth; we ask about his head-shaving.’

Sace keci bhikkhū senāsanaṃ vā gumbādīni vā pavisitvā niddāyanti vā samaṇadhammaṃ vā karonti, āpucchakā ca pariyesantāpi adisvā “sabbe āpucchitā amhehī”ti saññino honti, pabbajjā nāma lahukaṃ kammaṃ, tasmā pabbajito supabbajitova pabbājentassāpi anāpatti.

If some bhikkhus, having entered a lodging or a thicket and so on, are either sleeping or practicing the duties of a recluse, and those who are asking, even after searching, do not see them and perceive, ‘All have been asked by us,’ the going-forth is a light formal act. Therefore, the one who has gone forth is well gone-forth, and there is no offense for the one who gives the going-forth.

Sace pana mahāvihāro hoti anekabhikkhusahassāvāso, sabbe bhikkhū sannipātetumpi dukkaraṃ, pageva paṭipāṭiyā āpucchituṃ, khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ vā ṭhatvā nadīsamuddādīni vā gantvā pabbājetabbo. Yo pana navamuṇḍo vā hoti vibbhantako vā nigaṇṭhādīsu aññataro vā dvaṅgulakeso [M 0.0285] vā ūnadvaṅgulakeso vā, tassa kesacchedanakiccaṃ natthi, tasmā bhaṇḍukammaṃ anāpucchitvāpi tādisaṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. Dvaṅgulātirittakeso pana yo hoti antamaso ekasikhāmattadharopi, so bhaṇḍukammaṃ āpucchitvāva pabbājetabbo. Upālivatthu mahāvibhaṅge vuttanayameva.

However, if it is a large monastery inhabited by thousands of bhikkhus, it is difficult even to assemble all the bhikkhus, let alone to ask them in succession. He should be given the going-forth after standing in a sectional boundary or after going to a river, sea, or the like. But as for one who is newly shaven, or has recently disrobed, or is one of the Nigaṇṭhas or the like, or has hair two finger-breadths long or less than two finger-breadths long, for him there is no need to cut the hair. Therefore, it is permissible to give the going-forth to such a person even without asking about the head-shaving. However, one whose hair exceeds two finger-breadths in length—even if he wears only a single topknot—must be given the going-forth only after asking about the head-shaving. The story of Upāli is just as stated in the Mahāvibhaṅga.

100. Ahivātakarogenāti māribyādhinā; yatra hi so rogo uppajjati, taṃ kulaṃ dvipadacatuppadaṃ sabbaṃ nassati, yo bhittiṃ vā chadanaṃ vā bhinditvā palāyati, tirogāmādigato [V 0.0271] vā hoti, so muccati. Tathā cettha pitāputtā mucciṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ – “pitāputtakā sesā hontī”ti.

100. ‘By the snake-wind disease’ means by a deadly disease. For wherever that disease arises, that entire family—all two-footed and four-footed beings—perishes. Whoever breaks through a wall or a roof and flees, or has gone to another village or the like, is saved. And so, in this case, only the father and son were saved. Therefore it was said by the compilers of the canon, ‘The father and son were the ones remaining.’

Kākuḍḍepakanti yo vāmahatthena leḍḍuṃ gahetvā nisinno sakkoti āgatāgate kāke uḍḍāpetvā purato nikkhittaṃ bhattaṃ bhuñjituṃ, ayaṃ kākuḍḍepako nāma, taṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati.

‘One who can scare away crows’ means one who, while sitting, is able, by taking a clod of earth in his left hand, to make the approaching crows fly away and to eat the food placed before him. This one is called a ‘crow-scarer.’ It is permissible to give the going-forth to him.

102. Ittaroti appamattako; katipāhameva vāso bhavissatīti attho.

102. ‘For a short time’ means for a small amount; the meaning is that the residence will be for only a few days.

103. Ogaṇenāti parihīnagaṇena; appamattakena bhikkhusaṅghenāti attho. Abyattena yāvajīvanti ettha sacāyaṃ vuḍḍhataraṃ ācariyaṃ na labhati, upasampadāya saṭṭhivasso vā sattativasso vā hotu, navakatarassāpi byattassa santike ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā “ācariyo me āvuso hohi, āyasmato nissāya vacchāmī”ti evaṃ tikkhattuṃ vatvā nissayo gahetabbova. Gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchantenāpi ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā añjaliṃ paggahetvā gāmappavesanaṃ āpucchāmi ācariyā”ti vattabbaṃ. Esa nayo sabbaāpucchanesu. Pañcakachakkesu cettha yattakaṃ sutaṃ nissayamuttakassa [P 5.1004] icchitabbaṃ, taṃ bhikkhunovādakavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tassa natthitāya ca appassuto; atthitāya ca bahussutoti veditabbo. Sesaṃ vuttanayeneva.

103. ‘By a diminished group’ means by a deficient group; the meaning is by a small Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Regarding ‘(dependence) on an incompetent one for life,’ herein, if this incompetent bhikkhu does not find a more senior teacher, then even if he is sixty or seventy years in higher ordination, he must take dependence from even a more junior but competent bhikkhu. He should do so by sitting on his haunches, raising his joined palms, and saying three times, ‘Venerable friend, be my teacher; I will live in dependence on the venerable one.’ Even when asking permission to enter a village, one should sit on one's haunches, raise the joined palms, and say, ‘Teacher, I ask permission to enter the village.’ This is the method in all cases of asking. And herein, regarding the Fives and Sixes, whatever amount of learning is to be desired for one freed from dependence, that is stated in the commentary on the Bhikkhunovādaka. Due to its absence, one is to be known as of little learning; due to its presence, as of great learning. The remainder is as has been explained.

Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthādikathā niṭṭhitā.

The Story of the Goldsmith's Shaven-headed Son and Other Matters is concluded.

Rāhulavatthukathā

The Story of Rāhula

105. Yena [M 0.0286] kapilavatthu tena cārikaṃ pakkāmīti ettha ayaṃ anupubbikathā. Suddhodanamahārājā kira bodhisattassa abhinikkhamanadivasato paṭṭhāya “mama putto buddho bhavissāmīti nikkhanto, jāto nu kho buddho”ti pavattisavanatthaṃ ohitasotova viharati. So bhagavato padhānacariyañca sambodhiñca dhammacakkappavattanādīni ca suṇanto “idāni kira me putto rājagahaṃ upanissāya viharatī”ti sutvā ekaṃ amaccaṃ āṇāpesi – “ahaṃ tāta vuḍḍho mahallako, sādhu me jīvantasseva puttaṃ dassehī”ti. So “sādhū”ti paṭissuṇitvā purisasahassaparivāro rājagahaṃ gantvā bhagavato pāde vanditvā nisīdi. Athassa bhagavā dhammakathaṃ kathesi, so pasīditvā pabbajjañceva upasampadañca yāci. Tato naṃ bhagavā ehibhikkhūpasampadāya upasampādesi[V 0.0272], so sapariso arahattaṃ patvā tattheva phalasamāpattisukhaṃ anubhavamāno vihāsi. Rājā teneva upāyena aparepi aṭṭha dūte pahiṇi, tepi sabbe saparisā tatheva arahattaṃ patvā tattheva vihariṃsu. “Iminā nāma kāraṇena te nāgacchantī”ti rañño koci pavattimattampi ārocento natthi.

105. Regarding the phrase 'He set out on a journey towards Kapilavatthu,' here is the sequential account. It is said that King Suddhodana, from the day the Bodhisatta went forth, thinking, 'My son has left, intending to become a Buddha,' remained ever with an attentive ear to hear news, wondering, 'Has he now become a Buddha?' Hearing about the Blessed One's austere practice, his full awakening, the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma, and other events, he learned, 'It is said that my son is now dwelling near Rājagaha.' Thereupon, he commanded a minister, saying, 'Dear one, I am old and aged. Please, let me see my son while I am still alive.' The minister agreed, saying 'Very well,' and, accompanied by a thousand men, went to Rājagaha. He paid homage at the Blessed One's feet and sat down. Then the Blessed One delivered a Dhamma talk, and the minister, his heart filled with confidence, requested both the going forth and the higher ordination. Then the Blessed One ordained him with the 'Come, bhikkhu' ordination. He, along with his retinue, attained arahantship and remained right there, experiencing the bliss of fruition attainment. The king, by the same means, sent eight more messengers; they too, all of them with their retinues, attained arahantship in the same way and remained right there. There was no one at all to inform the king of even a shred of news, saying, 'It is for this reason that they do not return.'

Atha rājā bodhisattena saddhiṃ ekadivasaṃjātaṃ kāḷudāyiṃ nāma amaccaṃ pahiṇitukāmo purimanayeneva yāci, so “sace ahaṃ pabbajituṃ labhāmi, dassessāmī”ti āha. Taṃ rājā “pabbajitvāpi me puttaṃ dassehī”ti pahiṇi; sopi purisasahassaparivāro gantvā tatheva saparivāro arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. So ekadivasaṃ sambhatesu sabbasassesu vissaṭṭhakammantesu janapadamanussesu pupphitesu thalajajalajapupphesu paṭipajjanakkhame magge bhagavantaṃ vanditvā saṭṭhimattāhi gāthāhi gamanavaṇṇaṃ vaṇṇesi. Bhagavā “kimeta”nti pucchi. “Bhante tumhākaṃ pitā suddhodanamahārājā mahallakomhi, jīvantasseva me puttaṃ dassehī”ti maṃ pesesi, sādhu bhante bhagavā ñātakānaṃ saṅgahaṃ karotu, kālo cārikaṃ pakkamitunti. Tena hi [P 5.1005] saṅghassa ārocehi, “bhikkhū gamiyavattaṃ pūressantī”ti. “Sādhu bhante”ti thero tathā akāsi. Bhagavā aṅgamagadhavāsīnaṃ kulaputtānaṃ dasahi sahassehi kapilavatthuvāsīnaṃ dasahīti sabbeheva vīsatisahassehi [M 0.0287] khīṇāsavehi parivuto rājagahā nikkhamitvā rājagahato saṭṭhiyojanikaṃ kapilavatthuṃ divase divase yojanaṃ gacchanto dvīhi māsehi pāpuṇissāmīti aturitacārikaṃ pakkāmi. Tena vuttaṃ – “yena kapilavatthu tena cārikaṃ pakkāmī”ti.

Then the king, wishing to send a minister named Kāḷudāyī, who had been born on the same day as the Bodhisatta, requested him in the same manner as before. He replied, 'If I am permitted to go forth, I will show him.' The king sent him, saying, 'Even after going forth, show me my son.' He too, accompanied by a thousand men, went and, just like the others, attained arahantship with his retinue. One day, when all the crops had been gathered, when the people of the countryside were released from their work, when the terrestrial and aquatic flowers were in bloom, and when the roads were fit for travel, he paid homage to the Blessed One and praised the journey with sixty verses. The Blessed One asked, 'What is this?' 'Venerable sir, your father, King Suddhodana, sent me, saying: “I am old; show me my son while I am still alive.” Please, venerable sir, may the Blessed One show kindness to his relatives. It is time to set out on a journey.' 'In that case, inform the Saṅgha that the monks are to fulfill the duties of travel.' 'Very well, venerable sir,' the elder did so. The Blessed One, surrounded by twenty thousand who had destroyed the cankers—ten thousand from among the sons of good family of Aṅga and Magadha, and ten thousand from Kapilavatthu—departed from Rājagaha. He set out on an unhurried journey, thinking, 'I will reach Kapilavatthu, which is sixty yojanas from Rājagaha, by traveling one yojana per day, arriving in two months.' Therefore it was said: 'He set out on a journey towards Kapilavatthu.'

Evaṃ pakkante ca bhagavati udāyitthero nikkhantadivasato paṭṭhāya suddhodanamahārājassa gehe bhattakiccaṃ karoti. Rājā theraṃ parivisitvā pattaṃ gandhacuṇṇena ubbaṭṭetvā uttamabhojanassa pūretvā “bhagavato dehī”ti therassa hatthe ṭhapeti. Theropi tatheva karoti. Iti bhagavā antarāmagge raññoyeva piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuñji. Theropi ca bhattakiccāvasāne divase divase rañño āroceti “ajja bhagavā ettakaṃ āgato”ti, buddhaguṇapaṭisaṃyuttāya ca kathāya sākiyānaṃ bhagavati saddhaṃ uppādesi. Teneva naṃ bhagavā “etadaggaṃ, bhikkhave, mama sāvakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kulappasādakānaṃ yadidaṃ kāḷudāyī”ti etadagge ṭhapesi.

And so, when the Blessed One had departed, the elder Udāyī, from the day of departure, performed the meal service at King Suddhodana’s residence. The king would serve the elder, and after rubbing his bowl with fragrant powder and filling it with the finest food, he would place it in the elder’s hands, saying, 'Give this to the Blessed One.' The elder, too, did just so. Thus, along the way, the Blessed One consumed only the almsfood from the king. And the elder, at the conclusion of the meal service each and every day, would inform the king, 'Today the Blessed One has come this far,' and with talk connected to the virtues of the Buddha, he caused faith in the Blessed One to arise among the Sākyans. For this very reason, the Blessed One placed him in the foremost position, saying, 'Monks, foremost among my monk disciples who inspire confidence in families is this Kāḷudāyī.'

Sākiyāpi kho anuppatte bhagavati “amhākaṃ ñātiseṭṭhaṃ passissāmā”ti sannipatitvā bhagavato vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vīmaṃsamānā nigrodhasakkassa ārāmo ramaṇīyoti sallakkhetvā tattha sabbaṃ paṭijagganavidhiṃ kāretvā gandhapupphādihatthā paccuggamanaṃ karontā sabbālaṅkārapaṭimaṇḍite daharadahare [V 0.0273] nāgarikadārake ca dārikāyo ca paṭhamaṃ pahiṇiṃsu, tato rājakumāre ca rājakumārikāyo ca tesaṃ anantarā sāmaṃ gantvā gandhapupphacuṇṇādīhi pūjayamānā bhagavantaṃ gahetvā nigrodhārāmameva agamaṃsu. Tatra bhagavā vīsatisahassakhīṇāsavaparivuto paññattavarabuddhāsane nisīdi. Sākiyā mānajātikā mānathaddhā, te “siddhatthakumāro amhehi daharatarova amhākaṃ kaniṭṭho, bhāgineyyo, putto, nattā”ti cintetvā daharadahare rājakumāre āhaṃsu [P 5.1006] – “tumhe vandatha, mayaṃ tumhākaṃ piṭṭhito nisīdissāmā”ti.

When the Blessed One arrived, the Sākyans gathered, thinking, 'We will see our foremost kinsman.' After investigating a dwelling place for the Blessed One and noting that the park of Nigrodha the Sākyan was delightful, they had all preparations made there. Holding perfumes, flowers, and other offerings in their hands, they went to welcome him. First, they sent ahead the very young city boys and girls, adorned with all their ornaments. Then came the princes and princesses, and immediately after them, the Sākyans themselves went. Worshipping the Blessed One with perfumes, flowers, and powders, they escorted him to the Nigrodhārāma itself. There, the Blessed One, surrounded by twenty thousand who had destroyed the cankers, sat down on the prepared, excellent Buddha-seat. The Sākyans are a proud clan, stiff with pride. They thought, 'Prince Siddhattha is younger than us; he is our younger brother, nephew, son, or grandson.' Thinking thus, they said to the very young princes, 'You pay homage; we will sit behind you.'

Tesu evaṃ nisinnesu bhagavā tesaṃ ajjhāsayaṃ oloketvā “na maṃ ñātī vandanti, handa ne vandāpayissāmī”ti abhiññāpādakaṃ catutthajjhānaṃ samāpajjitvā vuṭṭhāya iddhiyā ākāsaṃ abbhuggantvā tesaṃ sīse pādapaṃsuṃ okiramāno [M 0.0288] viya kaṇḍambamūle yamakapāṭihāriyasadisaṃ pāṭihāriyamakāsi. Rājā taṃ acchariyaṃ disvā āha – “bhagavā tumhākaṃ maṅgaladivase brāhmaṇassa vandanatthaṃ upanītānaṃ pāde vo parivattitvā brāhmaṇassa matthake patiṭṭhite disvāpi ahaṃ tumhe vandiṃ, ayaṃ me paṭhamavandanā. Vappamaṅgaladivase jambucchāyāya sirisayane nipannānaṃ vo jambucchāyāya aparivattanaṃ disvāpi pāde vandiṃ, ayaṃ me dutiyavandanā.
