Even one who is making a recitation must ask the elder. Having asked one elder, if another elder arrives while one is reciting, there is no need to ask again. If an elder arrives while one has stopped, thinking, 'I will rest,' one must ask again when beginning anew. This same principle applies to one who is reciting what was begun before the Saṅgha's elder arrived. When one has been given permission by a Saṅgha's elder, 'You may recite at your pleasure without asking me,' it is proper to recite at one's pleasure. However, when another elder arrives, one must recite only after asking him.

151. Attanā vā attānaṃ sammannitabbaṃti attanā vā attā sammannitabbo; pucchantena pana parisaṃ oloketvā sace attano upaddavo natthi, vinayo pucchitabbo.

151. The phrase 'One may authorize oneself by oneself' means that one may be authorized by oneself. However, the one asking should observe the assembly, and if there is no danger to oneself, the Vinaya should be asked about.

153. Katepi okāse puggalaṃ tulayitvāti “atthi nu kho me ito upaddavo, natthī”ti evaṃ upaparikkhitvā. Puramhākanti paṭhamaṃ amhākaṃ. Paṭikaccevāti paṭhamatarameva. Puggalaṃ tulayitvā okāsaṃ kātunti “bhūtameva nu kho āpattiṃ vadati, abhūta”nti evaṃ upaparikkhitvā okāsaṃ kātuṃ anujānāmīti attho.

153. As for 'katepi okāse puggalaṃ tulayitvā', this means having investigated thus after weighing the person even when an opportunity has been given: "Will there be danger to me from this person, or will there not be?" As for 'puramhākaṃ', it means 'first, upon us'. As for 'paṭikacceva', it means 'at the very first'. As for 'puggalaṃ tulayitvā okāsaṃ kātuṃ', the meaning is: I allow the granting of an opportunity after having investigated thus: "Is he speaking of an offense that is indeed true, or of one that is untrue?"

Adhammakammapaṭikkosanādikathā

Discourse on Denouncing Unrighteous Acts and So Forth

154. Adhammakammaṃ vuttanayameva. Paṭikkositunti vāretuṃ. Diṭṭhimpi āvikātunti “adhammakammaṃ idaṃ na me khamatī”ti evaṃ aññassa santike attano diṭṭhiṃ pakāsetuṃ. Catūhi pañcahītiādi [V 0.0322] tesaṃ anupaddavatthāya vuttaṃ. Sañcicca na sāventīti yathā na suṇanti evaṃ bhaṇissāmāti sañcicca saṇikaṃ uddisanti.

154. An unrighteous act is just as has been explained. 'Paṭikkosituṃ' means 'to prevent'. 'Diṭṭhimpi āvikātuṃ' means to declare one's own view in the presence of another thus: "This act is an unrighteous act; it does not please me." The phrase beginning 'catūhi pañcahi' was said for the sake of their being without danger. As for 'sañcicca na sāventi', it means they recite softly and intentionally, with the thought, "We will recite in such a way that they do not hear."

155. Therādhikanti therādhīnaṃ; therāyattaṃ bhavitunti attho. “Therādheyya”ntipi pāṭho, tasmā therena sayaṃ vā uddisitabbaṃ, añño vā ajjhesitabbo. Ajjhesanavidhānañcettha dhammajjhesane vuttanayameva. So na [M 0.0341] jānāti uposathaṃ vātiādīsu cātuddasikapannarasikabhedena duvidhaṃ, saṅghauposathādibhedena navavidhañca uposathaṃ na jānāti, catubbidhaṃ uposathakammaṃ na jānāti, duvidhaṃ pātimokkhaṃ na jānāti, navavidhaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ na jānāti. Yo tattha bhikkhu byatto paṭibaloti ettha kiñcāpi daharassāpi byattassa pātimokkho anuññāto. Atha kho ettha [P 5.1060] ayamadhippāyo. Sace therassa pañca vā cattāro vā tayo vā pātimokkhuddesā nāgacchanti; dve pana akhaṇḍā suvisadā vācuggatā honti, therāyattova pātimokkhā. Sace pana ettakampi visadaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti, byattassa bhikkhuno āyatto hoti.

155. 'Therādhikaṃ' means under the authority of the elder; the meaning is that it is to be dependent on the elder. There is also the reading 'therādheyyaṃ'; therefore, the elder himself should recite, or another may be requested. And here, the procedure for requesting is just as was explained in the section on requesting the Dhamma. In the passage beginning 'so na jānāti uposathaṃ vā', it means he does not know the Uposatha, which is twofold by division into the fourteenth-day and fifteenth-day types, and ninefold by division into the Saṅgha-uposatha and so on; he does not know the fourfold Uposatha-kamma; he does not know the twofold Pātimokkha; he does not know the ninefold Pātimokkha-uddesa. Here, in 'whichever monk there is who is competent and capable', although the Pātimokkha is allowed even for a junior monk who is competent, nevertheless, this is the intention here: If five, four, or three Pātimokkha recitations do not come to the elder, but two are unbroken, very clear, and learned by heart, the Pātimokkha is indeed dependent on the elder. But if he is not able to make even this much clear, it becomes dependent on a competent monk.

Sāmantā āvāsāti sāmantaṃ āvāsaṃ. Sajjukanti tadaheva āgamanatthāya. Navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetunti ettha yo sakkoti uggahetuṃ, evarūpo āṇāpetabbo, na bālo.

'Sāmantā āvāsā' means a nearby residence. 'Sajjukaṃ' means for the purpose of returning on that very day. Here, in 'one should send a junior monk', a junior of such a kind who is able to learn should be sent, not a foolish one.

Pakkhagaṇanādiuggahaṇānujānanakathā

Discourse on the Authorization of Learning the Counting of Fortnights and So Forth

156. Katimī bhanteti ettha katīnaṃ pūraṇīti katimī. Kālavatoti kālasseva; pagevāti attho.

156. Herein, in the phrase 'Katimī, bhante', 'katimī' means 'the ordinal of how many'. 'Kālavato' means 'very early'; this is the meaning of 'pageva'.

158. Yaṃ kālaṃ saratīti ettha sāyampi “ajjuposatho samannāharathā”ti ārocetuṃ vaṭṭati.

158. Herein, regarding 'at whatever time he remembers', it is fitting to announce even in the evening, 'Today is the Uposatha; bear it in mind.'

159. Therena bhikkhunā navaṃ bhikkhuṃ āṇāpetunti etthāpi kiñci kammaṃ karonto vā sadākālameva eko vā bhāranittharaṇako vā sarabhāṇakadhammakathikādīsu aññataro vā na uposathāgārasammajjanatthaṃ āṇāpetabbo, avasesā pana vārena āṇāpetabbā. Sace āṇatto sammuñjaniṃ tāvakālikampi na labhati, sākhābhaṅgaṃ kappiyaṃ kāretvā sammajjitabbaṃ, tampi alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti.

159. Here also, regarding 'an elder monk may order a junior monk': one who is doing some work, or is always alone, or is discharging a responsibility, or is one among those such as a reciter or a Dhamma-speaker, should not be ordered for the purpose of sweeping the Uposatha hall; but the remaining ones should be ordered in turn. If the one who was ordered does not obtain a broom, even for temporary use, he should have a broken branch made allowable and sweep. For one who does not obtain even that, whatever is obtained is considered allowable.

160. Āsanapaññāpanāṇattiyampi [V 0.0323] vuttanayeneva āṇāpetabbo. Āṇattena ca sace uposathāgāre āsanāni natthi, saṅghikāvāsatopi āharitvā paññapetvā puna āharitabbāni. Āsanesu asati kaṭasārakepi taṭṭikāyopi paññapetuṃ vaṭṭati, taṭṭikāsupi asati sākhābhaṅgāni kappiyaṃ [M 0.0342] kāretvā paññapetabbāni, kappiyakārakaṃ alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti.

160. Regarding the instruction for arranging seats also, one should be ordered in the same manner as previously stated. And by the one ordered, if there are no seats in the Uposatha hall, they should be brought from the Saṅgha's dwelling, arranged, and then brought back again. If seats are unavailable, it is fitting to arrange even rush-mats or wicker-mats. If even those mats are unavailable, broken branches should be made allowable and arranged. For one who does not find a lay attendant to make them allowable, whatever is obtained is considered allowable.

161. Padīpakaraṇepi vuttanayeneva āṇāpetabbo. Āṇāpentena ca “amukasmiṃ nāma okāse telaṃ vā vaṭṭi vā kapallikā vā atthi, taṃ gahetvā karohī”ti vattabbo. Sace telādīni natthi, pariyesitabbāni, pariyesitvā alabhantassa laddhakappiyaṃ hoti. Apica kapāle aggipi jāletabbo.

161. Regarding the making of a lamp also, one should be ordered in the same manner as previously stated. And the one giving the order should say, 'In such-and-such a place there is oil, or a wick, or a lamp-dish; take them and prepare it.' If oil and so forth are not available, they should be sought. For one who does not find them after searching, whatever is obtained is considered allowable. Moreover, a fire should also be lit in a potsherd.

Disaṃgamikādivatthukathā

Discourse on the Case of Travelers and So Forth

163. Saṅgahetabboti “sādhu bhante āgatāttha, idha bhikkhā sulabhā sūpabyañjanaṃ atthi, vasatha anukkaṇṭhamānā”ti evaṃ piyavacanena saṅgahetabbo. Punappunaṃ tathākaraṇavasena [P 5.1061] anuggahetabbo. “Āma vasissāmī”ti paṭivacanadāpanena upalāpetabbo. Atha vā catūhi paccayehi saṅgahetabbo ceva anuggahetabbo ca. Piyavacanena upalāpetabbo, kaṇṇasukhaṃ ālapitabboti attho. Cuṇṇādīhi upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Āpatti dukkaṭassāti sace sakalopi saṅgho na karoti, sabbesaṃ dukkaṭaṃ. Idha neva therā na daharā muccanti, sabbehi vārena upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Attano vāre anupaṭṭhahantassa āpatti. Tena pana mahātherānaṃ pariveṇasammajjanadantakaṭṭhadānādīni na sāditabbāni. Evampi sati mahātherehi sāyaṃpātaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ āgantabbaṃ. Tena pana tesaṃ āgamanaṃ ñatvā paṭhamataraṃ mahātherānaṃ upaṭṭhānaṃ gantabbaṃ. Sacassa saddhiṃcarā bhikkhuupaṭṭhākā atthi, “mayhaṃ upaṭṭhākā atthi, tumhe appossukkā viharathā”ti vattabbaṃ. Athāpissa saddhiṃcarā natthi, tasmiṃyeva pana vihāre eko vā dve vā vattasampannā vadanti “mayaṃ therassa kattabbaṃ karissāma, avasesā phāsu viharantū”ti sabbesaṃ anāpatti.

163. One should be welcomed with kind words, thus: “Venerable sir, it is good that you have come. Here, almsfood is easy to obtain, and there are curries and condiments. Please dwell without anxiety.” One should be supported by doing so again and again. One should be persuaded by causing him to give the reply, “Yes, I will stay.” Or else, one should be both welcomed and supported with the four requisites. The meaning is: one should be persuaded with kind words and addressed in a way that is pleasant to the ear. One should be attended to with bath powder and so forth. 'An offense of wrong-doing': if the entire Saṅgha does not do it, it is a dukkaṭa for all. Here, neither the elders nor the juniors are exempt; he should be attended to by all in turn. For one who does not attend on his own turn, there is an offense. However, that visiting monk should not accept such services as the sweeping of the great elders' cells, the giving of tooth-sticks, and so forth. Even so, the great elders should come to attend in the evening and morning. But he, the visiting monk, knowing of their coming, should go to attend on the great elders first. If he has accompanying monks as attendants, he should say, “I have attendants; you may dwell with few concerns.” But if he has no accompanying monks, and in that very monastery one or two monks accomplished in their duties say, “We will do what should be done for the elder; let the rest dwell comfortably,” there is no offense for anyone.

So āvāso gantabboti uposathakaraṇatthāya anvaddhamāsaṃ gantabbo. So ca kho utuvasseyeva, vassāne pana yaṃ kattabbaṃ, taṃ dassetuṃ “vassaṃ vasanti bālā abyattā”tiādimāha. Tattha na bhikkhave tehi bhikkhūhi tasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃ vasitabbanti purimikāya pātimokkhuddesakena vinā na vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ. Sace so vassūpagatānaṃ pakkamati [V 0.0324][M 0.0343] vā, vibbhamati vā, kālaṃ vā karoti, aññasmiṃ satiyeva pacchimikāya vasituṃ vaṭṭati, asati aññattha gantabbaṃ, agacchantānaṃ dukkaṭaṃ. Sace pana pacchimikāya pakkamati vā vibbhamati vā kālaṃ vā karoti, māsadvayaṃ vasitabbaṃ.

'That residence should be gone to' means it should be gone to every half-month for the purpose of performing the Uposatha. And that, indeed, only in the winter and summer seasons. But as for the rainy season, to show what should be done, the Blessed One said, “Fools and the unwise dwell for the rains…” and so on. Therein, 'Monks, those monks should not dwell for the rains in that residence' means one should not enter the rains-residence for the earlier period without a reciter of the Pātimokkha. If that one—among those who have entered the rains—departs, or disrobes, or dies, it is proper to dwell for the later period only if another is present. If there is not another, one must go elsewhere; for those who do not go, it is an offense of wrong-doing. But if during the later period he departs, or disrobes, or dies, one should dwell for two months.

Pārisuddhidānakathā

Discourse on the Giving of Purity

164. Kāyena viññāpetīti pārisuddhidānaṃ yena kenaci aṅgapaccaṅgena viññāpeti jānāpeti; vācaṃ pana nicchāretuṃ sakkonto vācāya viññāpeti; ubhayathā sakkonto kāyavācāhi. Saṅghena tattha gantvā uposatho kātabboti sace bahū tādisā gilānā honti, saṅghena paṭipāṭiyā ṭhatvā sabbe hatthapāse kātabbā. Sace dūre dūre honti, saṅgho nappahoti, taṃ [P 5.1062] divasaṃ uposatho na kātabbo, natveva vaggena saṅghena uposatho kātabbo.

164. “Informs by body” means one informs or makes known the giving of purity by any major or minor limb. But if one is able to utter speech, one informs by speech; if able in both ways, by body and speech. “The Uposatha should be performed by the Saṅgha going there”: if there are many such sick monks, the Saṅgha, standing in order, should bring all within hand’s reach. If they are far apart and the Saṅgha is not sufficient, the Uposatha should not be performed that day; the Uposatha should certainly not be performed by a factional Saṅgha.

Tattheva pakkamatīti saṅghamajjhaṃ anāgantvā tatova katthaci gacchati. Sāmaṇero paṭijānātīti “sāmaṇero aha”nti evaṃ paṭijānāti; bhūtaṃyeva vā sāmaṇerabhāvaṃ āroceti, pacchā vā sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ tiṭṭhatīti attho. Esa nayo sabbattha.

“Departs from there” means without going into the midst of the Saṅgha, one goes somewhere from that very place. “A novice declares” means one declares thus: “I am a novice”; or one announces the true state of being a novice; or afterwards, one stands in the state of being a novice—this is the meaning. This is the method in all cases.

Saṅghappatto pakkamatīti sabbantimena paricchedena uposathatthāya sannipatitānaṃ catunnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ hatthapāsaṃ patvā pakkamati. Esa nayo sabbattha. Ettha ca ekena bahūnampi āhaṭā pārisuddhi āhaṭāva hoti. Sace pana so antarāmagge aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ disvā yesaṃ anena pārisuddhi gahitā, tesañca attano ca pārisuddhiṃ deti, tasseva pārisuddhi āgacchati, itarā pana bilāḷasaṅkhalikapārisuddhi nāma hoti. Sā na āgacchati.

“Having reached the Saṅgha, he departs” means that, by the final boundary, having come within hand’s reach of the four monks gathered for the Uposatha, he departs. This is the method in all cases. And here, the purity of even many monks brought by one is considered brought. But if, on the way, he sees another monk and gives to him the purity of those from whom it was received, as well as his own, only his own purity arrives; the other, however, is called a “cat’s chain” purity. That does not arrive.

Sutto na ārocetīti āgantvā supati, “asukena pārisuddhi dinnā”ti na āroceti. Pārisuddhihārakassa anāpattīti ettha sace sañcicca nāroceti, dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati, pārisuddhi pana āhaṭāva hoti. Asañcicca anārocitattā panassa anāpatti, ubhinnampi ca uposatho katoyeva hoti.

“One who is asleep does not report” means one arrives and falls asleep, not reporting, “Purity was given by so-and-so.” Regarding “There is no offense for the bearer of the purity”: here, if one intentionally does not report, one incurs an offense of wrong-doing, but the purity is considered brought. However, because of not reporting unintentionally, there is no offense for him, and the Uposatha is considered performed for both.

Chandadānakathā

Discourse on the Giving of Consent

165. Chandadānepi [M 0.0344] pārisuddhidāne vuttasadisoyeva vinicchayo. Pārisuddhiṃ dentena chandampi [V 0.0325] dātunti ettha sace pārisuddhimeva deti na chandaṃ, uposatho kato hoti. Yaṃ pana saṅgho aññaṃ kammaṃ karoti, taṃ akataṃ hoti. Chandameva deti na pārisuddhiṃ, bhikkhusaṅghassa uposathopi kammampi katameva hoti, chandadāyakassa pana uposatho akato hoti. Sacepi koci bhikkhu nadiyā vā sīmāya vā uposathaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā āgacchati, “kato mayā uposatho”ti acchituṃ na labhati, sāmaggī vā chando vā dātabbo.

165. In the giving of consent also, the decision is the same as that stated for the giving of purity. Here, if one gives only purity and not consent, his Uposatha is considered done, but any other formal act the Saṅgha performs is considered not done by him. If one gives only consent and not purity, both the Uposatha and the formal act of the Saṅgha of monks are considered done, but the Uposatha of the consent-giver is considered not done. Even if a monk, having undertaken the Uposatha in a river or in a consecrated boundary, comes, he is not allowed to remain, saying, 'I have performed the Uposatha'; either concord or consent must be given.

167. Saratipi uposathaṃ napi saratīti ekadā sarati, ekadā na sarati. Atthi neva saratīti yo ekantaṃ neva sarati, tassa sammutidānakiccaṃ natthi. Anāgacchantopi kammaṃ na kopeti.

167. “Sometimes remembers the Uposatha, and sometimes does not remember” means: at one time one remembers, at another time one does not. “There is one who never remembers”: for one who certainly never remembers, there is no duty of giving the formal designation of insanity. Even by not coming, he does not invalidate the formal act.

Saṅghuposathādikathā

Discourse on the Community Uposatha and Related Matters

168. So deso sammajjitvāti taṃ desaṃ sammajjitvā, upayogatthe paccattaṃ. Pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyantiādi pana uttānatthameva[P 5.1063]. Kasmā panetaṃ vuttaṃ? Uposathassa pubbakaraṇādidassanatthaṃ. Tenāhu aṭṭhakathācariyā –

168. Regarding the phrase 'So deso sammajjitvā' (that place, having been swept): it means 'taṃ desaṃ sammajjitvā' (having swept that place), where the nominative is used in the sense of the accusative. Furthermore, the phrase beginning with 'pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyantiādi' (water for drinking and water for use) has an obvious meaning. Why, then, was this stated? For the purpose of showing the preliminary duties and so forth for the Uposatha. Therefore, the commentators have said:

“Sammajjanī padīpo ca, udakaṃ āsanena ca;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakaraṇanti vuccati”.

“Sweeping, and a lamp, and water together with a seat; these are called the 'preliminary duties' of the Uposatha.”

Iti imāni cattāri “pubbakaraṇa”nti akkhātāni.

Thus, these four are declared as the 'preliminary duties'.

“Chandapārisuddhiutukkhānaṃ, bhikkhugaṇanā ca ovādo;

Uposathassa etāni, pubbakiccanti vuccati.

“The reporting of consent, of purity, and of the season; the counting of the monks; and the request for exhortation; these are called the 'preliminary functions' of the Uposatha.”

Iti imāni pañca pubbakaraṇato pacchā kattabbāni “pubbakicca”nti akkhātāni.

Thus, these five, although they are to be performed after the preliminary duties, are declared as the 'preliminary functions'.

“Uposatho yāvatikā ca bhikkhū kammappattā,

Sabhāgāpattiyo ca na vijjanti;

Vajjanīyā ca puggalā tasmiṃ na honti,

Pattakallanti vuccati”.

“[When] it is the Uposatha day, and however many monks are fit for the formal act, and there exist no similar offenses, and persons who should be excluded are not present therein—this is called 'a suitable time' (pattakalla).”

Iti [V 0.0326] imāni cattāri “pattakalla”nti akkhātānīti.

Thus, these four are declared as the 'suitable conditions' (pattakalla).

Tehi [M 0.0345] saddhinti tehi āgatehi saddhiṃ etāni pubbakaraṇādīni katvā uposatho kātabbo. Ajja me uposathoti ettha sace pannaraso hoti, “ajja me uposatho pannaraso”tipi adhiṭṭhātuṃ vaṭṭati. Cātuddasikepi eseva nayo.

Regarding 'Tehi saddhiṃ' (together with them): having performed these preliminary duties and so forth together with those monks who have arrived, the Uposatha should be carried out. In the phrase 'Ajja me uposatho' (Today is my Uposatha), if it is the fifteenth-day Uposatha, it is proper to determine it thus: 'Today is my fifteenth-day Uposatha.' This same method applies also to the fourteenth-day Uposatha.

Āpattipaṭikammavidhikathā

Discourse on the Method for Remedying Offenses

169. Bhagavatā paññattaṃ “na sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo”ti idaṃ “yassa siyā āpattī”tiādivacaneneva pārisuddhidānapaññāpanena ca pārisuddhiuposathapaññāpanena ca paññattaṃ hotīti veditabbaṃ. Itthannāmaṃ āpattinti thullaccayādīsu ekissā nāmaṃ gahetvā “thullaccayaṃ āpattiṃ pācittiyaṃ āpatti”nti evaṃ vattabbaṃ. Taṃ paṭidesemīti idaṃ “taṃ tumhamūle, taṃ tuyhamūle paṭidesemī”ti vuttepi suvuttameva hoti. Passasīti idañca “passasi āvuso taṃ āpattiṃ, passatha bhante taṃ āpatti”nti evaṃ vattabbaṃ. Āma passāmīti idaṃ pana “āma bhante passāmi, āma āvuso passāmī”ti evaṃ vuttampi suvuttameva hoti. Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsīti ettha pana sace vuḍḍhataro “āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāthā”ti vattabbo. Evaṃ vuttena pana “sādhu suṭṭhu saṃvarissāmī”ti [P 5.1064] vattabbameva.

169. It should be understood that this, which was laid down by the Blessed One—'The Uposatha is not to be performed by one who has an offense'—was laid down by the teaching beginning 'Whosoever should have an offense...', by the regulation on the giving of purity, and by the regulation on the Uposatha of purity. Regarding 'an offense of such-and-such a name', having taken the name of one among the offenses beginning with thullaccaya, it should be said thus: 'I have fallen into a thullaccaya offense,' or 'I have fallen into a pācittiya offense.' This phrase 'I confess it' (taṃ paṭidesemi) is well-said even when spoken as 'I confess it in your presence' (taṃ tumhamūle paṭidesemi) or 'I confess it in your presence' (taṃ tuyhamūle paṭidesemi). And this word 'Do you see?' (passasi) should be spoken thus: 'Friend, do you see that offense?' (passasi āvuso taṃ āpattiṃ) or 'Venerable Sirs, do you see that offense?' (passatha bhante taṃ āpattiṃ). Furthermore, this reply 'Yes, I see' (āma passāmi) is well-said even when spoken thus: 'Yes, Venerable Sir, I see' (āma bhante passāmi) or 'Yes, friend, I see' (āma āvuso passāmi). Furthermore, regarding 'You should restrain yourself in the future' (āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsi), if the other is a senior, it should be said, 'You should restrain yourself in the future' (āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāthā). And by the one who is spoken to thus, it is indeed proper to say, 'Good, I will restrain myself well' (sādhu suṭṭhu saṃvarissāmi).

Yadā nibbematikoti ettha sace panesa nibbematiko na hoti, vatthuṃ kittetvāva desetuṃ vaṭṭatīti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ desanāvidhi – sace meghacchanne sūriye “kālo nu kho no”ti vematiko bhuñjati, tena bhikkhunā “ahaṃ bhante vematiko bhuñjiṃ”, sace kālo atthi, “sambahulā dukkaṭā āpattiyo āpannomhi, no ce atthi, “sambahulā pācittiyā āpannomhī”ti evaṃ vatthuṃ kittetvā “ahaṃ bhante yā tasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ sambahulā dukkaṭā vā pācittiyā vā āpattiyo āpanno, tā tumhamūle paṭidesemī”ti vattabbaṃ. Esa nayo sabbāpattīsu.

Regarding the phrase 'When one is without doubt': If, however, one is not without doubt, it is proper to confess only after having stated the matter—so it is said in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā. Therein, this is the method of confession: If, when the sun is covered by clouds, a monk eats while in doubt, thinking, 'Is it now the proper time or not?', that monk, having stated the matter thus—'Venerable Sir, I ate while in doubt. If it was the proper time, I have fallen into many dukkaṭa offenses; if it was not, I have fallen into many pācittiya offenses'—should then say: 'Venerable Sir, whatever many dukkaṭa or pācittiya offenses I have fallen into in that matter, those I confess in your presence.' This is the method for all offenses.

Na bhikkhave sabhāgā āpattīti ettha yaṃ dvepi janā vikālabhojanādinā sabhāgavatthunā āpattiṃ āpajjanti, evarūpā vatthusabhāgā “sabhāgā”ti [M 0.0346] vuccati. Vikālabhojanappaccayā āpannaṃ pana anatirittabhojanapaccayā āpannassa santike desetuṃ vaṭṭati. Yāpi cāyaṃ vatthusabhāgā, sāpi desitā sudesitāva. Aññaṃ pana desanapaccayā desako, paṭiggahaṇappaccayā [V 0.0327] paṭiggahako cāti ubhopi dukkaṭaṃ āpajjanti, taṃ nānāvatthukaṃ hoti, tasmā aññamaññaṃ desetuṃ vaṭṭati.

Regarding 'Monks, not a similar offense': Here, when two persons fall into an offense from a similar basis (sabhāgavatthu), such as eating at the wrong time, such an offense that is similar by way of its basis is called 'similar' (sabhāgā). However, it is proper to confess an offense incurred due to eating at the wrong time in the presence of one who has incurred an offense due to eating food that was not left over. And even this offense that is similar by way of its basis, when it is confessed, is indeed well-confessed. However, for another reason, both the confessor, on account of confessing, and the receiver, on account of receiving the confession, fall into a dukkaṭa offense. That new offense has a different basis. Therefore, it is proper for them to confess to one another.

170. Sāmanto bhikkhu evamassa vacanīyoti ettha sabhāgoyeva vattabbo. Visabhāgassa hi vuccamāne bhaṇḍanakalahasaṅghabhedādīnipi honti, tasmā tassa avatvā “ito vuṭṭhahitvā paṭikarissāmī”ti ābhogaṃ katvā uposatho kātabboti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ.

170. Regarding the phrase 'A nearby monk should be spoken to thus': Here, only a monk of a similar disposition should be spoken to. For indeed, if a monk of a dissimilar disposition is spoken to, quarrels, disputes, schisms in the Community, and so forth may arise. Therefore, without speaking to him, having made the mental resolve, 'Having risen from here, I will make amends,' the Uposatha should be performed—so it is said in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā.

Anāpattipannarasakādikathā

Discourse on the Fifteen Cases of Non-Offense and so forth

172. Anāpattipannarasake – te na jāniṃsūti sīmaṃ okkantāti vā okkamantīti vāti na jāniṃsu. Athaññe āvāsikā bhikkhū āgacchantīti gāmaṃ vā araññaṃ vā kenaci karaṇīyena gantvā tesaṃ nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ āgacchanti. Vaggā samaggasaññinoti tesaṃ sīmaṃ okkantattā vaggā; sīmaṃ okkantabhāvassa ajānanato samaggasaññino.

172. In the fifteen cases of non-offense: As for 'they did not know,' they did not know that they had entered the boundary or were entering it. Then other resident monks arrive, meaning, having gone to a village or a forest for some duty, they come to the place where those monks are seated. As for 'divided, but with the perception of being united': because of their having entered the boundary, they are divided; because of not knowing the fact of having entered the boundary, they have the perception of being united.

173. Vaggāvaggasaññipannarasake – te jānantīti pabbate vā thale vā ṭhitā sīmaṃ okkante vā okkamante vā passanti. Vematikapannarasakaṃ [P 5.1065] uttānameva.

173. In the fifteen cases of perceiving the assembly as divided or undivided: As for 'they know,' standing on a mountain or on high ground, they see those who have entered the boundary or are entering it. The fifteen cases of doubt are self-evident.

175. Kukkuccapakatapannarasake – yathā icchāya abhibhūto “icchāpakato”ti vuccati, evaṃ pubbabhāge sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvāpi karaṇakkhaṇe akappiye akappiyasaññitāsaṅkhātena kukkuccena abhibhūtā “kukkuccapakatā”ti veditabbā.

175. In the fifteen cases of being affected by remorse: Just as one who is overcome by desire is called 'one affected by desire,' so too 'those affected by remorse' should be understood as follows: even after having made a determination in the preliminary stage, at the moment of the act, they are overcome by remorse concerning an unallowable matter, a remorse characterized by perceiving the unallowable as unallowable.

176. Bhedapurekkhārapannarasake – akusalabalavatāya thullaccayaṃ vuttaṃ.

176. In the fifteen cases of having division as a goal: a grave offense is stated due to the strength of the unwholesome mind.

Sīmokkantikapeyyālakathā

Discourse on the Repetitive Passage concerning Entering the Boundary

177. Āvāsikenaāgantukapeyyāle – yathā purime āvāsikenaāvāsikapeyyāle “te na jānanti athaññe āvāsikā”tiādi vuttaṃ, evaṃ “te na jānanti athaññe āgantukā”tiādinā nayena [M 0.0347] sabbaṃ veditabbaṃ. Āgantukenaāvāsikapeyyāle pana – yathā purimapeyyāle “āvāsikā bhikkhū sannipatantī”ti āgataṃ, evaṃ “āgantukā bhikkhū sannipatantī”ti ānetabbaṃ[V 0.0328]. Āgantukenaāgantukapeyyāle pana – ubhayapadesu āgantukavasena yojetabboti.

177. In the repetitive passage concerning the resident and the visiting monk: just as in the previous repetitive passage concerning the resident and the resident monk it was said, 'they do not know, then other resident monks...' and so forth, in the same way, everything should be understood by the method of 'they do not know, then other visiting monks...' and so forth. But in the repetitive passage concerning the visiting monk and the resident monk: just as in the previous repetitive passage it is found, 'the resident monks assemble,' so too 'the visiting monks assemble' should be supplied. But in the repetitive passage concerning the visiting monk and the visiting monk: in both positions, it should be connected by way of the visiting monk.

178. Āvāsikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cātuddaso hoti, āgantukānaṃ pannarasoti ettha yesaṃ pannaraso, te tiroraṭṭhato vā āgatā, atītaṃ vā uposathaṃ cātuddasikaṃ akaṃsūti veditabbā. Āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbanti āvāsikehi “ajjuposatho cātuddaso”ti pubbakicce kariyamāne anuvattitabbaṃ, na paṭikkositabbaṃ. Na akāmā dātabbāti na anicchāya dātabbā.

178. In the passage, 'For the resident monks it is the fourteenth day of the half-month, for the visiting monks it is the fifteenth': here, those for whom it is the fifteenth should be understood as either having come from another region, or as having performed the previous Uposatha as a fourteenth-day Uposatha. As for 'The residents should be followed': when the resident monks are performing the preliminary duties, saying, 'Today is the fourteenth Uposatha,' one should follow them; one should not oppose them. As for 'It should not be given unwillingly': consent should not be given without desire.

Liṅgādidassanakathā

The Discourse on Seeing Signs, etc.

179. Āvāsikākāranti āvāsikānaṃ ākāraṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha. Ākāro nāma yena tesaṃ vattasampannā vā na vāti ācārasaṇṭhānaṃ gayhati. Liṅgaṃ nāma yaṃ te tattha tattha līne gamayati; adissamānepi jānāpetīti attho. Nimittaṃ nāma yaṃ disvā te atthīti ñāyanti. Uddeso nāma yena te evarūpaparikkhārāti uddisanti; apadesaṃ labhantīti attho. Sabbametaṃ supaññattamañcapīṭhādīnañceva padasaddādīnañca adhivacanaṃ, yathāyogaṃ pana yojetabbaṃ. Āgantukākārādīsupi eseva nayo. Tattha aññātakanti aññesaṃ santakaṃ. Pādānaṃ dhotaṃ udakanissekanti pādānaṃ dhotānaṃ udakanissekaṃ. Bahuvacanassa ekavacanaṃ veditabbaṃ. “Pādānaṃ dhotaudakanisseka”nti vā pāṭho; pādānaṃ dhovanaudakanissekanti attho.

179. ‘Āvāsikākāranti’ means the disposition (ākāra) of the resident monks (āvāsikānaṃ). This is the principle in all instances. Disposition (ākāra) is that by which their well-established conduct (ācārasaṇṭhānaṃ) is grasped (gayhati), as to whether they are accomplished in the observances (vattasampannā) or not. Sign (liṅga) is that which makes known (gamayati) those who are hidden (līne) in various places; the meaning is that it makes them known (jānāpeti) even when they are unseen (adissamānepi). Mark (nimitta) is that which, having been seen (disvā), they are known (ñāyanti) to exist. Indication (uddesa) is that by which they are pointed out (uddisanti) as having requisites of such a nature; the meaning is that they receive a designation (apadesaṃ labhanti). All this is a term (adhivacanaṃ) for well-laid-out beds, chairs, and so forth, and for the sound of footsteps and so forth, but it should be applied as is appropriate. In the case of the disposition of visiting monks and so forth, this is the same principle. Herein, ‘unrecognized’ (aññātakaṃ) means belonging to others. ‘Pādānaṃ dhotaṃ udakanissekanti’ means the remaining water (udakanissekaṃ) from the washed (dhotānaṃ) feet (pādānaṃ). The singular is to be understood for the plural. Alternatively, the reading is ‘pādānaṃ dhotaudakanissekaṃ’; the meaning is the remaining water from the washing of the feet.

180. Nānāsaṃvāsakādivatthūsu – samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhinti “samānasaṃvāsakā ete”ti diṭṭhiṃ. Na pucchantīti tesaṃ laddhiṃ [P 5.1066] na pucchanti; apucchitvāva vattapaṭivattiṃ katvā ekato uposathaṃ karonti. Nābhivitarantīti nānāsaṃvāsakabhāvaṃ maddituṃ abhibhavituṃ na sakkonti; taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na nissajjāpentīti attho.

180. In matters concerning those of different communion, etc. — ‘samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhinti’ means the view (diṭṭhiṃ) that ‘these are of the same communion (samānasaṃvāsakā).’ ‘Na pucchanti’ (they do not ask) means they do not ask about their doctrine (laddhiṃ); without asking, having performed the practice of the observances (vattapaṭipattiṃ), they perform the Uposatha together. ‘Nābhivitaranti’ (they do not overcome) means they are not able to crush (maddituṃ) or overcome (abhibhavituṃ) the state of being of different communion (nānāsaṃvāsakabhāvaṃ); the meaning is that they cannot make them abandon (na nissajjāpenti) that view.

Nagantabbagantabbavārakathā

The Discourse on the Section Concerning Where One Should and Should Not Go

181. Sabhikkhukā āvāsāti yasmiṃ āvāse uposathakārakā bhikkhū atthi, tamhā āvāsā yaṃ na sakkoti tadaheva āgantuṃ[M 0.0348], so āvāso uposathaṃ akatvā na gantabbo. Aññatra saṅghenāti saṅghappahonakehi bhikkhūhi vinā. Aññatra antarāyāti pubbe vuttaṃ dasavidhaṃ antarāyaṃ [V 0.0329] vinā. Sabbantimena pana paricchedena attacatutthena antarāye vā sati gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Anāvāsoti navakammasālādiko yo koci padeso. Yathā ca āvāsādayo na gantabbā; evaṃ sace vihāre uposathaṃ karonti, uposathādhiṭṭhānatthaṃ sīmāpi nadīpi na gantabbā. Sace panettha koci bhikkhu hoti, tassa santikaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Vissaṭṭhauposathāpi āvāsā gantuṃ vaṭṭati; evaṃ gato adhiṭṭhātumpi labhati. Āraññakenāpi bhikkhunā uposathadivase gāme piṇḍāya caritvā attano vihārameva āgantabbaṃ. Sace aññaṃ vihāraṃ okkamati, tattha uposathaṃ katvāva āgantabbaṃ, akatvā na vaṭṭati.

181. ‘A monastery with monks’ (sabhikkhukā āvāsā) means a monastery where there are monks who perform the Uposatha. From that monastery, one should not go (na gantabbo) to a monastery to which one is not able to return on that very day, without having performed the Uposatha. ‘Except for the Saṅgha’ (aññatra saṅghena) means without monks sufficient for a Saṅgha. ‘Except for an obstacle’ (aññatra antarāyāti) means without the ten kinds of obstacles mentioned before. However, by the very last determination, it is allowable to go, being oneself the fourth, or when there is an obstacle. ‘A non-residence’ (anāvāso) means any place such as a new work hall. And just as one should not go to monasteries and so forth, similarly, if they perform the Uposatha in their own dwelling, they should not go to a boundary (sīmā) or a river for the purpose of determining the Uposatha. If some monk is there, it is allowable to go to him. It is also allowable to go from a monastery where the Uposatha has been dismissed; having gone thus, one may also determine it. A forest-dwelling monk, on the Uposatha day, having wandered for alms in a village, should return to his own dwelling. If he enters another dwelling, he must return only after having performed the Uposatha there; it is not allowable to return without having done so.

182. Yaṃ jaññā sakkomi ajjeva gantunti yaṃ jāneyya ajjeva tattha gantuṃ sakkomīti; evarūpo āvāso gantabbo. Tattha bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ uposathaṃ karontenāpi hi iminā neva uposathantarāyo kato bhavissatīti.

182. Regarding the phrase, 'That which one might know, “I am able to go today itself”': this means a monastery about which one might know, 'I am able to go there today itself.' Such a monastery may be gone to. For indeed, by this monk who has gone, even in performing the Uposatha there with the monks, no obstacle to the Uposatha will have been created.

Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanakathā

The Discourse on Pointing Out a Person to be Avoided

183. Bhikkhuniyā nisinnaparisāyātiādīsu hatthapāsupagamanameva pamāṇaṃ. Aññatra avuṭṭhitāya parisāyāti idañhi pārivāsiyapārisuddhidānaṃ nāma parisāya vuṭṭhitakālato paṭṭhāya na vaṭṭati, avuṭṭhitāya pana vaṭṭati. Tenāha – “aññatra avuṭṭhitāya parisāyā”ti. Tassa lakkhaṇaṃ bhikkhunivibhaṅge parivāsiyachandadānavaṇṇanato gahetabbaṃ. Anuposatheti cātuddasiko ca pannarasiko cāti ime dve uposathe ṭhapetvā aññasmiṃ divase. Aññatra saṅghasāmaggiyāti yā kosambakabhikkhūnaṃ viya bhinne saṅghe puna saṅghasāmaggī kariyati, tathārūpiṃ saṅghasāmaggiṃ ṭhapetvā[P 5.1067]. Tadā ca “suṇātu me bhante saṅgho ajjuposatho sāmaggī”ti vatvā kātabbo. Ye pana kismiñcideva appamattake uposathaṃ ṭhapetvā puna samaggā honti, tehi uposatheyeva kātabboti.

183. In such phrases as 'in an assembly where a bhikkhunī is seated,' the measure is only the approaching into hand's reach. Regarding 'Except for an assembly that has not risen': this so-called 'giving of purity to one on probation' is not allowable starting from the time the assembly has risen, but it is allowable for an assembly that has not yet risen. Therefore, it was said: 'except for an assembly that has not risen.' Its characteristic should be understood from the explanation on the giving of consent for one on probation in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga. As for 'not on an Uposatha day': setting aside these two Uposatha days, namely the fourteenth-day and the fifteenth-day, it means on any other day. As for 'Except for the harmony of the Saṅgha': it means setting aside such a harmony of the Saṅgha that is re-established when the Saṅgha is split, like that of the monks of Kosambī. And at that time, it should be done by stating in the motion: 'Venerable sirs, may the Saṅgha hear me. Today is the harmony Uposatha.' However, those monks who, having suspended the Uposatha for some insignificant reason, become harmonious again—by them, the Uposatha should be performed on the Uposatha day itself.

Uposathakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Uposatha Section is finished.

3. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhakaṃ

3. The Section on Entering the Rains-residence

Vassūpanāyikānujānanakathā

The Discourse on the Authorization of the Rains-residence

184. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhake [M 0.0349][V 0.0330] – apaññattoti ananuññāto asaṃvihito vā. Te idha bhikkhūti te bhikkhū, idhasaddo nipātamatto. Saṅghātaṃ āpādentāti vināsaṃ āpādentā. Saṅkasāyissantīti appossukkā nibaddhavāsaṃ vasissanti. Sakuntakāti sakuṇā. Vassāne vassaṃ upagantunti vassānanāmake temāse vassaṃ upagantabbanti attho. Kati nu kho vassūpanāyikāti kati nu kho vassūpagamanāni. Aparajjugatāyāti ettha aparajjugatāya assāti aparajjugatā, tassā aparajjugatāya; atikkantāya aparasmiṃ divaseti attho. Dutiyanayepi māso gatāya assāti māsagatā, tassā māsagatāya; atikkantāya māse paripuṇṇeti attho. Tasmā āsāḷhīpuṇṇamāya anantare pāṭipadadivase, āsāḷhīpuṇṇamito vā aparāya puṇṇamāya anantare pāṭipadadivaseyeva vihāraṃ paṭijaggitvā pānīyaṃ paribhojanīyaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā sabbaṃ cetiyavandanādisāmīcikammaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā “imasmiṃ vihāre imaṃ temāsaṃ vassaṃ upemī”ti sakiṃ vā dvattikkhattuṃ vā vācaṃ nicchāretvā vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ.

184. In the Section on Entering the Rains-residence: 'Not yet laid down' means not yet permitted or not yet arranged. As for 'those monks here,' it means 'those monks'; the word 'here' is merely a particle. As for 'they bring about destruction,' it means causing ruin. As for 'they will become stained,' it means they will live without exertion, in a fixed residence. As for 'like birds,' it means birds. As for 'they should enter the Rains in the rainy season,' the meaning is that one should enter the Rains-residence in the three-month period called the rainy season. As for 'How many Rains-entries are there?' it means how many enterings of the Rains are there? Regarding 'on the day after it has passed' (aparajjugatāya): here, the word is explained thus: it is called aparajjugatā because for that (full-moon day) that has passed (gatāya), there is a next day (aparajju). 'For that aparajjugatā, when it has passed' means on the next day. In the second method as well, it is called māsagatā because for that (full-moon day) that has passed (gatāya), a month (māso) has gone by. 'For that māsagatā, when it has passed' means when a month is complete. Therefore, either on the first day of the waning moon immediately following the Āsāḷhī full-moon day, or on the very first day of the waning moon immediately following the next full-moon day after the Āsāḷhī full-moon, having tidied up the monastery, having set up drinking water and water for use, having completed all respectful duties such as venerating the cetiya, one should enter the Rains-residence by uttering the words, 'In this monastery I enter upon the Rains for these three months,' once, or two or three times.

Vācaṃ nicchāretvā vassaṃ upagantabbaṃ.

Having uttered the words, one should enter the Rains-residence.

Vassānecārikāpaṭikkhepādikathā

The Discourse on the Prohibition of Wandering During the Rains, etc.

185-6. Yo pakkameyyāti ettha anapekkhagamanena vā aññattha aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpanena vā āpatti veditabbā. Yo atikkameyyāti ettha vihāragaṇanāya āpattiyo veditabbā. Sace hi taṃ divasaṃ vihārasatassa upacāraṃ okkamitvā atikkamati, sataṃ āpattiyo. Sace pana vihārūpacāraṃ atikkamitvā aññassa vihārassa upacāraṃ anokkamitvāva nivattati, ekā eva āpatti. Kenaci antarāyena purimikaṃ anupagatena pacchimikā upagantabbā.

185-6. In the phrase, “Whoever should depart,” an offense should be understood as occurring either by departing without concern or by causing dawn to arise elsewhere. In the phrase, “Whoever should transgress,” offenses should be understood according to the count of monasteries. For if on that day, having entered and passed beyond the precincts of one hundred monasteries, one transgresses, there are one hundred offenses. But if, having transgressed the precincts of one's own monastery, one turns back without having entered the precincts of another monastery, there is only one offense. By a bhikkhu who, due to some obstacle, has not entered upon the earlier Rains-residence, the later Rains-residence should be entered upon.

Vassaṃ [V 0.0331] ukkaḍḍhitukāmoti vassanāmakaṃ [P 5.1068] paṭhamamāsaṃ ukkaḍḍhitukāmo, sāvaṇamāsaṃ akatvā puna āsāḷhīmāsameva kattukāmoti attho. Āgame juṇheti āgame māseti attho. Anujānāmi bhikkhave rājūnaṃ anuvattitunti ettha vassukkaḍḍhane bhikkhūnaṃ kāci parihāni nāma natthīti anuvattituṃ [M 0.0350] anuññātaṃ, tasmā aññasmimpi dhammike kamme anuvattitabbaṃ. Adhammike pana na kassaci anuvattitabbaṃ.

“Wishing to postpone the Rains-residence” means wishing to postpone the first month, called the month of the rains; the meaning is wishing not to observe the month of Sāvaṇa but to observe the month of Āsāḷhī again. “In the coming bright fortnight” means in the coming month. In the phrase, “I allow, O bhikkhus, to follow kings,” it was permitted to follow because in postponing the Rains-residence, there is no loss whatsoever for the bhikkhus. Therefore, one should also follow in other lawful acts. But in an unlawful act, one should not follow anyone.

Sattāhakaraṇīyānujānanakathā

The Discourse on the Permission for Seven-Day Duties

187-8. Sattāhakaraṇīyesu – sattāhakaraṇīyena gantunti sattāhabbhantare yaṃ kattabbaṃ taṃ sattāhakaraṇīyaṃ, tena sattāhakaraṇīyena karaṇabhūtena gantuṃ anujānāmīti attho. Pahite gantunti imehi sattahi bhikkhuādīhi dūte pahiteyeva gantuṃ anujānāmīti attho. Sattāhaṃ sannivatto kātabboti sattāheyeva sannivattitabbo, aṭṭhamo aruṇo tattheva na uṭṭhāpetabboti attho.

187-8. Regarding seven-day duties: “To go for a seven-day duty” means that which should be done within seven days is a seven-day duty; the meaning is, I allow one to go on account of that seven-day duty which has become the reason. “To go when sent” means, I allow one to go only when a messenger is sent by these seven persons, beginning with a bhikkhu. “A return should be made within seven days” means one should return within seven days only; the meaning is, the eighth dawn should not be made to arise right there, in the place one has reached.

Bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ uddissāti ito paṭṭhāya vaccakuṭi jantāgharaṃ jantāgharasālāti imāni tīṇi parihīnāni.

Beginning from the phrase, “Dedicating to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha,” these three are omitted: the latrine, the steam-bath house, and the hall for the steam-bath house.

189. Udositādīni udositasikkhāpadādīsu vuttāneva. Rasavatīti bhattagehaṃ vuccati. Vāreyyaṃ sañcarittasikkhāpade vuttameva. Purāyaṃ suttanto palujjatīti yāva ayaṃ suttanto na palujjati, yāva ayaṃ suttanto na vinassati. Aññataraṃ vā panassa kiccaṃ hoti karaṇīyaṃ vāti etena parisaṅkhataṃ yaṃkiñci karaṇīyaṃ saṅgahitaṃ hoti. Sabbattha ca “icchāmi dānañca dātuṃ dhammañca sotuṃ bhikkhū ca passitu”nti imināva kappiyavacanena pesite gantabbaṃ, etesaṃ vā vevacanena. Peyyālakkamo pana evaṃ veditabbo, yathā “upāsakena saṅghaṃ uddissa vihārādayo kārāpitā honti, sambahule bhikkhū uddissa, ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ uddissa, bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ uddissa, sambahulā bhikkhuniyo, ekaṃ bhikkhuniṃ, sambahulā sikkhamānāyo, ekaṃ sikkhamānaṃ, sambahule sāmaṇere, ekaṃ sāmaṇeraṃ, sambahulā sāmaṇeriyo, ekaṃ sāmaṇeriṃ uddissa attano atthāya nivesanaṃ kārāpitaṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ; evameva “upāsikāya, bhikkhunā, bhikkhuniyā, sikkhamānāya, sāmaṇerena, sāmaṇeriyā saṅghaṃ uddissā”ti sabbaṃ vattabbaṃ. Etesu sattappakāresu karaṇīyesu [P 5.1069] pahite gantabbaṃ.

189. Things beginning with 'udosita' (storehouse) are just as stated in the training rules beginning with the Udosita-sikkhāpada. 'Rasavatī' is said to be the kitchen. 'Vāreyyaṃ' (marriage arrangement) is just as stated in the Sañcaritta-sikkhāpada (the training rule on acting as a go-between). “Before this discourse is destroyed” means as long as this discourse is not yet destroyed, as long as this discourse has not yet perished. By this phrase, ‘Or if there is some business or duty for him to do,’ any arranged or prepared task whatsoever that is to be done is included. And in all cases, one should go only when sent with this suitable phrase: “I wish to give a gift, to listen to the Dhamma, and to see the bhikkhus,” or with a synonym of these words. The sequence of the peyyāla (elision marker), however, should be understood in this way: just as it is said, “A male lay follower has had monasteries, etc., built, dedicating them to the Saṅgha; dedicating them to many bhikkhus; dedicating them to one bhikkhu; dedicating them to the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha; dedicating them to many bhikkhunīs; dedicating them to one bhikkhunī; dedicating them to many female probationers; dedicating them to one female probationer; dedicating them to many male novices; dedicating them to one male novice; dedicating them to many female novices; dedicating them to one female novice; or has had a residence built for his own benefit.” In the very same way, it should all be stated for: “By a female lay follower... dedicating to the Saṅgha,” “by a bhikkhu,” “by a bhikkhunī,” “by a female probationer,” “by a male novice,” and “by a female novice.” When sent on account of these seven kinds of duties, one should go.

Pañcannaṃappahitepianujānanakathā

The Discourse on Permitting [Travel] for the Five [Types of Persons] Even When Not Sent For

193. Pañcannaṃ [V 0.0332] sattāhakaraṇīyenāti etesaṃ bhikkhuādīnaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ “gilānabhattaṃ vā gilānupaṭṭhākabhattaṃ vā bhesajjaṃ vā pariyesissāmi[M 0.0351], pucchissāmi vā, upaṭṭhahissāmi vā”ti evamādinā parato vitthāretvā dassitena kāraṇena appahitepi gantabbaṃ, pageva pahite. Bhikkhu gilāno hoti, anabhirati uppannā hoti, kukkuccaṃ uppannaṃ hoti, diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, garudhammaṃ ajjhāpanno hoti parivāsāraho, mūlāya paṭikassanāraho hoti, mānattāraho, abbhānāraho, saṅgho kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, kataṃ vā saṅghena kammaṃ hotīti etehi dasahi kāraṇehi bhikkhussa santikaṃ gantabbaṃ. Bhikkhuniyā santikaṃ navahi kāraṇehi gantabbaṃ, sikkhamānāya santikaṃ chahi – ādito catūhi, sikkhā kuppitā hoti, upasampajjitukāmā hotīti. Sāmaṇerassāpi chahi – ādito catūhi, vassaṃ pucchitukāmo upasampajjitukāmo hotīti. Sāmaṇeriyā upasampadaṃ apanetvā sikkhāpadaṃ dātukāmo hotīti iminā saddhiṃ pañcahi. Parato mātāpitūnaṃ anuññātaṭṭhānepi eseva nayo. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “ye mātāpitūnaṃ upaṭṭhākā ñātakā vā aññātakā vā tesampi appahite gantuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ neva aṭṭhakathāyaṃ, na pāḷiyā vuttaṃ, tasmā na gahetabbaṃ.

193. Regarding 'for the five [types of persons] for whom the seven-day allowance applies': for these fellow practitioners, beginning with bhikkhus, for a reason shown and elaborated upon later, such as, 'I will search for food for the sick, or food for one attending the sick, or medicine; or I will ask about the sick person; or I will attend [to them],' one should go even when not sent for—how much more so when sent for. One may go to a bhikkhu for these ten reasons: he is sick; dissatisfaction has arisen; remorse has arisen; a wrong view has arisen; having committed a grave offense, he is deserving of probation; he is deserving of being sent back to the beginning; he is deserving of mānatta; he is deserving of rehabilitation; the Saṅgha wishes to perform an act; or an act has been performed by the Saṅgha. One may go to a bhikkhunī for nine reasons. One may go to a sikkhamānā for six reasons: the first four, and also when her training has been disrupted, or when she wishes to attain higher ordination. For a sāmaṇera also, for six reasons: the first four, and also when he wishes to ask about the rains-residence, or when he wishes to attain higher ordination. For a sāmaṇerī, with this [reason]—wishing to give the training rule, having set aside higher ordination—it is five reasons [in total]. Later, this same method applies also in a place permitted for [visiting] one's parents. However, in the Andhaka commentary it is said, 'It is allowable to go even when not sent for to those attendants of one's parents, whether they are relatives or non-relatives.' That was said neither in the [ancient] commentary nor in the Pāḷi; therefore, it should not be accepted.

Pahiteyevaanujānanakathā

The Explanation on Permitting [Travel] Only When Sent For

199. Bhikkhugatikoti ekasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vasanakapuriso. Undriyatīti palujjati. Bhaṇḍaṃ chedāpitanti dabbasambhārabhaṇḍaṃ chedāpitaṃ. Āvahāpeyyunti āharāpeyyuṃ. Dajjāhanti dajje ahaṃ. Saṅghakaraṇīyenāti ettha yaṃkiñci uposathāgārādīsu senāsanesu cetiyachattavedikādīsu vā kattabbaṃ, antamaso bhikkhuno puggalikasenāsanampi, sabbaṃ saṅghakaraṇīyameva. Tasmā tassa nipphādanatthaṃ dabbasambhārādīni vā āharituṃ vaḍḍhakīppabhutīnaṃ bhattavetanādīni vā dāpetuṃ gantabbaṃ.

199. `Bhikkhugatika` means a man who dwells together with bhikkhus in a single monastery. `Undriyati` means it is perishing. `Bhaṇḍaṃ chedāpitaṃ` means goods consisting of building materials have been caused to be cut. `Āvahāpeyyunti` means 'if they should cause [them] to be brought.' `Dajjāhanti` is to be divided as `dajje ahaṃ`, 'I would give.' Here, regarding 'for the Saṅgha's business': whatever is to be done in dwellings such as the Uposatha hall, or on things such as the cetiya's umbrella and platform, even down to a bhikkhu's personal dwelling—all is indeed the Saṅgha's business. Therefore, for the purpose of its completion, one should go either to bring building materials and so forth, or to cause food, wages, and so forth to be given to carpenters and others.

Ayaṃ panettha pāḷimuttakaratticchedavinicchayo – dhammasavanatthāya animantitena gantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace ekasmiṃ mahāvāse paṭhamaṃyeva katikā katā hoti – “asukadivasaṃ nāma sannipatitabba”nti[P 5.1070], nimantitoyeva nāma hoti, gantuṃ vaṭṭati. “Bhaṇḍakaṃ dhovissāmī”ti gantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace pana [M 0.0352] ācariyupajjhāyā pahiṇanti, vaṭṭati. Nātidūre vihāro hoti, tattha gantvā ajjeva āgamissāmīti sampāpuṇituṃ na sakkoti, vaṭṭati. Uddesaparipucchādīnaṃ atthāyapi [V 0.0333] gantuṃ na vaṭṭati. “Ācariyaṃ passissāmī”ti pana gantuṃ labhati. Sace pana naṃ ācariyo “ajja mā gacchā”ti vadati, vaṭṭati. Upaṭṭhākakulaṃ vā ñātikulaṃ vā dassanāya gantuṃ na labhatīti.

This here is the decision, independent of the Pāḷi, on the breaking of the night-stay: It is not allowable for one who is uninvited to go for the purpose of hearing the Dhamma. If in a large dwelling-place an agreement has been made beforehand—'On such-and-such a day, we must assemble'—then one is indeed considered invited, and it is allowable to go. It is not allowable to go thinking, 'I will wash the goods.' But if the teacher and preceptor send [him], it is allowable. If the monastery is not too far, and having gone there with the intention, 'I will return this very day,' one is returning but is not able to arrive back [before dawn], it is allowable. It is not allowable to go even for the purpose of recitation, questioning, and so forth. But one is permitted to go thinking, 'I will see the teacher.' And if the teacher says to him, 'Do not go today,' it is allowable [to stay]. One is not permitted to go to see a supporter's family or a relative's family.

Antarāyeanāpattivassacchedakathā

Discourse on Not Incurring an Offense for Breaking the Rains-Residence Due to an Obstacle

201. Yena gāmo tena gantuntiādīsu sace gāmo avidūraṃ gato hoti, tattha piṇḍāya caritvā vihārameva āgantvā vasitabbaṃ. Sace dūraṃ gato, sattāhavārena aruṇo uṭṭhāpetabbo. Na sakkā ce hoti, tatreva sabhāgaṭṭhāne vasitabbaṃ. Sace manussā yathāpavattāni salākabhattādīni denti, “na mayaṃ tasmiṃ vihāre vasimhā”ti vattabbā. “Mayaṃ vihārassa vā pāsādassa vā na dema, tumhākaṃ dema, yattha katthaci vasitvā bhuñjathā”ti vutte pana yathāsukhaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ, tesaṃyeva taṃ pāpuṇāti. “Tumhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne pāpuṇāpetvā bhuñjathā”ti vutte pana yattha vasanti, tattha netvā vassaggena pāpuṇāpetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ.

201. Regarding passages such as, 'One should go where the village is,' the decision should be understood thus: If the village has moved to a place not far away, one should go for alms-food there and, having returned, reside only in the monastery. If it has gone far, one should cause the dawn to arise [at the original monastery] by the seven-day period. If one is not able to do so, one should reside there in a place of like-minded individuals. If the people give customary alms such as ticket-meals, one should say, 'We no longer reside in that monastery.' However, if it is said, 'We do not give to the monastery or to the storied building; we give to you. Residing wherever you may be, please partake,' then one may partake as is convenient; it reaches them only. But if it is said, 'Having it delivered to your dwelling place, please partake,' then one should have it brought to where they are residing and, having it delivered according to the rains-residence count or seniority, one should partake.

Sace pavāritakāle vassāvāsikaṃ denti, yadi sattāhavārena aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpayiṃsu, gahetabbaṃ. Chinnavassehi pana “na mayaṃ tattha vasimha, chinnavassā maya”nti vattabbaṃ. Yadi “yesaṃ amhākaṃ senāsanaṃ pāpitaṃ, te gaṇhantū”ti vadanti, gahetabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana vihāre upanikkhittakaṃ mā vinassīti idha āhaṭaṃ cīvarādivebhaṅgiyabhaṇḍaṃ, taṃ tattheva gantvā apaloketvā bhājetabbaṃ. “Ito ayyānaṃ cattāro paccaye dethā”ti kappiyakārakānaṃ dinne khettavatthuādike tatruppādepi eseva nayo. Saṅghikañhi vebhaṅgiyabhaṇḍaṃ antovihāre vā bahisīmāya vā hotu, bahisīmāya ṭhitānaṃ apaloketvā bhājetuṃ [P 5.1071] na vaṭṭati. Ubhayattha ṭhitampi pana antosīmāya ṭhitānaṃ apaloketvā bhājetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

If, at the time of Pavāraṇā, they give the rains-residence robe, and if they caused the dawn to arise [at the original monastery] by the seven-day period, it should be accepted. However, those with a broken rains-residence should say, 'We did not reside there for the full three months; we are ones with a broken rains-residence.' If they say, 'Let those take it to whom our lodging has been assigned,' it should be accepted. Furthermore, whatever distributable goods, such as robes, deposited in the monastery were brought here with the thought, 'May it not be lost,' one should go to that very place and, having made an announcement, distribute them. When fields, land, and so on are given to the stewards with the instruction, 'From this, give the four requisites to the venerable ones,' this same method applies also to the requisites arising therefrom. Indeed, distributable goods belonging to the Saṅgha, whether they are inside the monastery or outside the boundary, are not allowable to be distributed after announcing it to those staying outside the boundary. However, goods situated in both places are indeed allowable to be distributed after announcing it to those staying inside the boundary.

Saṅghabhedeanāpattivassacchedakathā

Discourse on Not Incurring an Offense for Breaking the Rains-Residence Due to a Schism in the Saṅgha

202. Saṅgho [M 0.0353] bhinnoti ettha bhinne saṅghe gantvā karaṇīyaṃ natthi, yo pana “bhijjissatī”ti āsaṅkito, taṃ sandhāya “bhinno”ti vuttaṃ. Sambahulāhi bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinnoti ettha na bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinnoti daṭṭhabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ “na kho upāli bhikkhunī saṅghaṃ bhindatī”ti. Etā pana nissāya anubalaṃ katvā yaṃ saṅghaṃ “bhikkhū bhindeyyu”nti āsaṅkā hoti, taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

202. Regarding 'The Saṅgha is divided': Here, when the Saṅgha is already divided, there is nothing to be done by going. However, with reference to a Saṅgha that is suspected of being about to be divided, it was said, 'divided.' Regarding 'The Saṅgha is divided by many bhikkhunīs': Here, it should not be understood that the Saṅgha is divided by bhikkhunīs. For this was said [by the Blessed One]: 'Indeed, Upāli, a bhikkhunī does not divide the Saṅgha.' However, this was said with reference to a Saṅgha where, relying on these [bhikkhunīs] and gaining supporting strength, there is a suspicion that 'the bhikkhus might divide it'.

Vajādīsuvassūpagamanakathā

The Discourse on Entering the Rains-Residence in a Cowherd's Village and Other Places

203. Vajoti [V 0.0334] gopālakānaṃ nivāsaṭṭhānaṃ. Yena vajoti ettha vajena saddhiṃ gatassa vassacchede anāpatti.

203. A `vaja` is a dwelling place of cowherds. Herein, regarding the phrase `yena vajo`, for a monk who has gone along with a cowherd's village, there is no offense for the breaking of the Rains-residence.

Upakaṭṭhāyāti āsannāya. Satthe vassaṃ upagantunti ettha vassūpanāyikadivase tena bhikkhunā upāsakā vattabbā “kuṭikā laddhuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. Sace karitvā denti, tattha pavisitvā “idha vassaṃ upemī”ti tikkhattuṃ vattabbaṃ. No ce denti, sālāsaṅkhepena ṭhitasakaṭassa heṭṭhā upagantabbaṃ. Tampi alabhantena ālayo kātabbo. Satthe pana vassaṃ upagantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Ālayo nāma “idha vassaṃ vasissāmī”ti cittuppādamattaṃ. Sace maggappaṭipanneyeva satthe pavāraṇadivaso hoti, tattheva pavāretabbaṃ. Atha sattho antovasseyeva bhikkhunā patthitaṭṭhānaṃ patvā atikkamati, patthitaṭṭhāne vasitvā tattha bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pavāretabbaṃ. Athāpi sattho antovasseyeva antarā ekasmiṃ gāme tiṭṭhati vā vippakirati vā, tasmiṃyeva gāme bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vasitvā pavāretabbaṃ, apavāretvā tato paraṃ gantuṃ na vaṭṭati.

`Upakaṭṭhāya` means 'being near'. Herein, regarding 'to enter the Rains-residence in a caravan', on the day for entering the Rains-residence, that monk should say to the lay supporters, 'It is proper to obtain a small hut.' If they make one and give it, having entered it, it should be said three times, 'Herein I enter the Rains-residence.' If they do not give one, he should enter the Rains-residence under a collection of carts arranged in the manner of a hall. If he does not obtain even that, an `ālaya` should be made. However, it is not proper to enter the Rains-residence in the caravan itself. `Ālaya` means merely the arising of the thought, 'I will dwell here for the Rains-residence.' If the Pavāraṇā day occurs while the caravan is still on the road, the Pavāraṇā should be performed right there. If the caravan, while still within the Rains-residence period, reaches and passes the destination desired by the monk, he should stay at his desired destination and perform the Pavāraṇā there together with the monks. And if the caravan, while still within the Rains-residence period, stops or disperses in a certain village along the way, he should stay in that very village and perform the Pavāraṇā together with the monks. It is not proper to go further than that place without having performed the Pavāraṇā.

Nāvāyaṃ vassaṃ upagacchantenāpi kuṭiyaṃyeva upagantabbaṃ. Pariyesitvā alabhantena ālayo kātabbo. Sace antotemāsaṃ nāvā samuddeyeva hoti, tattheva pavāretabbaṃ. Atha nāvā kūlaṃ labhati, ayañca parato gantukāmo hoti, gantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Nāvāya laddhagāmeyeva vasitvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pavāretabbaṃ. Sacepi nāvā anutīrameva aññattha gacchati, bhikkhu ca paṭhamaṃ laddhagāmeyeva vasitukāmo, nāvā gacchatu bhikkhunā tattheva vasitvā bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ pavāretabbaṃ[P 5.1072].

Even by a monk entering the Rains-residence on a boat, it should be entered in a small hut itself. If, after searching, he does not obtain one, an `ālaya` should be made. If, within the three-month period, the boat is still on the ocean, the Pavāraṇā should be performed right there. If the boat reaches the shore, and this monk wishes to go further, it is not proper to go. He should dwell in the very village reached by the boat and perform the Pavāraṇā together with the monks. Even if the boat goes elsewhere along the shore, and the monk wishes to dwell in the first village reached, let the boat go; the monk should stay right there and perform the Pavāraṇā together with the monks.

Iti [M 0.0354] vaje satthe nāvāyanti tīsu ṭhānesu natthi vassacchede āpatti, pavāretuñca labhati. Purimesu pana “vāḷehi ubbāḷhā hontī”tiādīsu saṅghabhedapariyantesu vatthūsu kevalaṃ anāpatti hoti, pavāretuṃ pana na labhati.

Thus, in these three places—a cowherd's village, a caravan, and a boat—there is no offense for the breaking of the Rains-residence, and one is permitted to perform the Pavāraṇā. However, in the former cases, beginning with 'they are oppressed by wild animals' and ending with the cases concerning schism in the Saṅgha, there is merely no-offense, but one is not permitted to perform the Pavāraṇā.

204. Na bhikkhave rukkhasusireti ettha suddhe rukkhasusireyeva na vaṭṭati; mahantassa pana rukkhasusirassa anto padaracchadanaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvā pavisanadvāraṃ yojetvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati. Rūkkhaṃ chinditvā khāṇukamatthake padaracchadanaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvāpi vaṭṭatiyeva. Rukkhaviṭabhiyāti [V 0.0335] etthāpi suddhe viṭapamatte na vaṭṭati. Mahāviṭape pana aṭṭakaṃ bandhitvā tattha padaracchadanaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvā upagantabbaṃ. Asenāsanikenāti yassa pañcannaṃ chadanānaṃ aññatarena channaṃ yojitadvārabandhanaṃ senāsanaṃ natthi, tena na upagantabbaṃ. Na bhikkhave chavakuṭikāyanti chavakuṭikā nāma ṭaṅkitamañcādibhedā kuṭi, tattha upagantuṃ na vaṭṭati. Susāne pana aññaṃ kuṭikaṃ katvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati. Na bhikkhave chatteti etthāpi catūsu thambhesu chattaṃ ṭhapetvā āvaraṇaṃ katvā dvāraṃ yojetvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati, chattakuṭikā nāmesā hoti. Cāṭiyāti etthāpi mahantena kapallena chatte vuttanayena kuṭiṃ katvā upagantuṃ vaṭṭati.

204. Herein, regarding 'Monks, not in a tree hollow,' it is not proper to enter the Rains-residence in a mere tree hollow. However, having made a plank-roofed hut inside a large tree hollow and fitted it with an entrance door, it is proper to enter the Rains-residence. Having cut a tree and made a plank-roofed hut on top of the stump, it is also proper to enter. Herein also, regarding 'in a tree-fork,' it is not proper in a mere tree-fork. However, on a large tree-fork, having constructed a platform and made a plank-roofed hut on it, one should enter the Rains-residence. Regarding 'by one without a dwelling': one for whom there is no dwelling that is covered by one of the five kinds of roofing and fitted with a door-frame should not enter the Rains-residence. Regarding 'Monks, not in a charnel-ground hut': a charnel-ground hut is a hut of various kinds, such as one with a suspended cot; it is not proper to enter the Rains-residence there. However, having made another kind of hut in the charnel ground, it is proper to enter. Herein also, regarding 'Monks, not under an umbrella': having placed an umbrella on four posts, made an enclosure, and fitted a door, it is proper to enter the Rains-residence; this is called an 'umbrella-hut'. Herein also, regarding 'in a large pot': having made a hut with a large potsherd in the manner described for the umbrella, it is proper to enter the Rains-residence.

Adhammikakatikādikathā

The Discourse on Unrighteous Agreements and the Like

205. Evarūpā katikāti ettha aññāpi yā īdisī adhammikā katikā hoti, sā na kātabbāti attho. Tassā lakkhaṇaṃ mahāvibhaṅge vuttaṃ.

205. Regarding 'an agreement of such a kind': here, the meaning is that any other such unrighteous agreement that there may be should not be made. Its characteristic is stated in the Mahāvibhaṅga.

207-8. Paṭissave ca āpatti dukkaṭassāti ettha na kevalaṃ “imaṃ temāsaṃ idha vassaṃ vasathā”ti etasseva paṭissave āpatti, “imaṃ temāsaṃ bhikkhaṃ gaṇhatha, ubhopi mayaṃ idha vassaṃ vasissāma, ekato uddisāpessāmā”ti [P 5.1073] evamādināpi tassa tassa paṭissave dukkaṭaṃ. Tañca kho paṭhamaṃ suddhacittassa pacchā visaṃvādanapaccayā, paṭhamampi asuddhacittassa pana paṭissave pācittiyaṃ, visaṃvādane dukkaṭanti pācittiyena saddhiṃ dukkaṭaṃ yujjati.

207-8. Regarding 'And for a promise, there is an offense of wrong-doing': here, an offense is not incurred merely for the promise, 'Dwell here for this three-month period of the Rains.' Rather, for each and every promise made with words such as, 'Accept alms for this three-month period; we shall both dwell here for the Rains; we shall recite the Pātimokkha together,' there is an offense of wrong-doing. And that offense occurs for one whose mind is initially pure, because of the condition of deceiving later. However, for one whose mind is impure even at first, there is a `pācittiya` offense for the promise, and an offense of wrong-doing for the act of deceiving. Thus, an offense of wrong-doing together with a `pācittiya` is applicable.

So [M 0.0355] tadaheva akaraṇīyotiādīsu sace vassaṃ anupagantvā vā pakkamati, upagantvā vā sattāhaṃ bahiddhā vītināmeti, purimikā ca na paññāyati, paṭissave ca āpatti. Vassaṃ upagantvā pana aruṇaṃ anuṭṭhāpetvā tadaheva sattāhakaraṇīyena pakkamantassāpi antosattāhe nivattantassa anāpatti, ko pana vādo dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvā antosattāhe nivattantassa. Dvīhatīhaṃ vasitvāti etthāpi nirapekkheneva upacārātikkame vassacchedo veditabbo. Sace idha vasissāmīti ālayo atthi, asatiyā pana vassaṃ na upeti, gahitasenāsanaṃ suggahitaṃ, chinnavasso na hoti, pavāretuṃ labhatiyeva.

In passages such as 'So on that very day it is not to be done': if one departs without having entered upon the Rains-residence, or having entered upon it, spends seven days outside, then the first Rains-residence is not established, and there is an offense for breaking the promise. However, for one who, having entered upon the Rains-residence, departs on that very day for a seven-day matter without letting the dawn arise, there is no offense if they return within the seven days; what then is to be said of one who, having stayed for two or three days, returns within the seven days? Here also, in the phrase 'having stayed for two or three days,' the breaking of the Rains-residence should be understood as occurring upon transgressing the boundary without any attachment to returning. If there is the attachment, 'I will dwell here,' but due to mindlessness one does not enter upon the Rains-residence, the accepted lodging is well-accepted, one does not have a broken Rains-residence, and one indeed obtains the right to perform Pavāraṇā.

Sattāhaṃ anāgatāya pavāraṇāyāti ettha navamito paṭṭhāya gantuṃ vaṭṭati, āgacchatu vā mā vā, anāpatti. Sesaṃ uttānamevāti.

Regarding the phrase 'with seven days remaining until the Pavāraṇā': here, it is permissible to leave from the ninth day before onward. Whether one returns or not, there is no offense. The rest is self-evident.

Vassūpanāyikakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Chapter on Entering upon the Rains-Residence is concluded.

4. Pavāraṇākkhandhakaṃ

4. The Chapter on the Pavāraṇā

Aphāsukavihārakathā

The Discourse on Uncomfortable Dwelling

209. Pavāraṇākkhandhake [M 0.0356][V 0.0336] – neva ālapeyyāma na sallapeyyāmāti ettha ālāpo nāma paṭhamavacanaṃ; sallāpo pacchimavacanaṃ. Hatthavilaṅghakenāti hatthukkhepakena. Pasusaṃvāsanti pasūnaṃ viya saṃvāsaṃ. Pasavopi hi attano uppannaṃ sukhadukkhaṃ aññamaññassa na ārocenti, paṭisanthāraṃ na karonti, tathā etepi na akaṃsu; tasmā nesaṃ saṃvāso “pasusaṃvāso”ti vuccati. Esa nayo sabbattha. Na bhikkhave mūgabbataṃ titthiyasamādānanti “imaṃ temāsaṃ na kathetabba”nti evarūpaṃ vatasamādānaṃ na kātabbaṃ; adhammakatikā hesā. Aññamaññānulomatāti aññamaññaṃ vattuṃ anulomabhāvo. “Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto”ti [P 5.1074] hi vadantaṃ sakkā hoti kiñci vattuṃ; na itaraṃ. Āpattivuṭṭhānatā vinayapurekkhāratāti āpattīhi vuṭṭhānabhāvo vinayaṃ purato katvā caraṇabhāvo. “Vadantu maṃ āyasmanto”ti hi evaṃ vadanto āpattīhi vuṭṭhahissati, vinayañca purakkhatvā viharissatīti vuccati.

209. In the Pavāraṇā Chapter: Regarding 'we should neither address one another nor converse,' here, `ālāpa` means the first utterance; `sallāpa` means a subsequent utterance. 'By a hand-signal' (`hatthavilaṅghakena`) means by raising the hand. 'Living like animals' (`pasusaṃvāsaṃ`) means living in the manner of animals. For animals do not communicate their own pleasure and pain to one another, nor do they extend courtesies; similarly, these monks also did not do so. Therefore, their cohabitation is called 'living like animals.' This is the principle in all cases. Regarding 'Monks, the vow of silence is an undertaking of the heretics,' such an undertaking of a vow as 'one should not speak for these three months' should not be made; for this is an unrighteous agreement. 'Mutual agreeableness' (`aññamaññānulomatā`) is the state of being agreeable to speak to one another. For it is possible to say something to one who says, 'Let the venerable ones speak to me,' but not to the other. 'Rising from offenses and prioritizing the Discipline' (`āpattivuṭṭhānatā vinayapurekkhāratā`) is the state of rising from offenses and the state of conducting oneself having placed the Discipline foremost. For one who speaks thus, 'Let the venerable ones speak to me,' is said to be one who will rise from offenses and one who will dwell prioritizing the Discipline.

210. Suṇātu me bhante saṅgho ajja pavāraṇā, yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ, saṅgho pavāreyyāti ayaṃ sabbasaṅgāhikā nāma ñatti; evañhi vutte tevācikaṃ dvevācikaṃ ekavācikañca pavāretuṃ vaṭṭati. Samānavassikaṃ na vaṭṭati. “Tevācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vutte pana tevācikameva vaṭṭati, aññaṃ na vaṭṭati. “Dvevācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vutte dvevācikañca tevācikañca vaṭṭati, ekavācikañca samānavassikañca na vaṭṭati. “Ekavācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vutte pana ekavācika-dvevācika-tevācikāni vaṭṭanti, samānavassikameva na vaṭṭati. “Samānavassika”nti vutte sabbaṃ vaṭṭati.

210. 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me. Today is Pavāraṇā. If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha perform Pavāraṇā.' This is called the all-inclusive motion (`sabbasaṅgāhikā ñatti`). For when this is stated, it is permissible to perform the Pavāraṇā with three statements (`tevācika`), with two statements (`dvevācika`), and with one statement (`ekavācika`). It is not permissible to perform the `samānavassika` Pavāraṇā. However, when it is stated, 'Let the Saṅgha perform the `tevācika` Pavāraṇā,' it is permissible to perform only the `tevācika`; another is not permissible. When it is stated, 'Let the Saṅgha perform the `dvevācika` Pavāraṇā,' it is permissible to perform the `dvevācika` and the `tevācika`; the `ekavācika` and the `samānavassika` are not permissible. When it is stated, 'Let the Saṅgha perform the `ekavācika` Pavāraṇā,' the `ekavācika`, `dvevācika`, and `tevācika` are permissible; only the `samānavassika` is not permissible. When `samānavassika` is stated, all are permissible.

211. Acchantīti nisinnāva honti, na uṭṭhahanti. Tadamantarāti tadantarā; tāvatakaṃ kālanti attho.

211. 'They remain' (`acchantīti`) means they remain seated, they do not rise. 'Immediately after that' (`tadamantarāti`) means `tadantarā` (immediately after); the meaning is 'for that period of time' (`tāvatakaṃ kālaṃ`).

Pavāraṇābhedakathā

Discourse on the Divisions of Pavāraṇā

212. Cātuddasikā [M 0.0357][V 0.0337] ca pannarasikā cāti ettha cātuddasikāya “ajja pavāraṇā cātuddasī”ti evaṃ pubbakiccaṃ kātabbaṃ, pannarasikāya “ajja pavāraṇā pannarasī”ti.

212. Regarding 'on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth': Herein, on the fourteenth, the preliminary duty should be performed thus: 'Today is the Pavāraṇā, the fourteenth.' On the fifteenth, it should be performed thus: 'Today is the Pavāraṇā, the fifteenth.'

Pavāraṇakammesu sace ekasmiṃ vihāre pañcasu bhikkhūsu vasantesu ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā cattāro gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, catūsu tīsu vā vasantesu ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā tayo vā dve vā saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, sabbametaṃ adhammenavaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ.

Regarding Pavāraṇā procedures: If, in a single monastery where five bhikkhus are residing, the Pavāraṇā of one is brought and the four perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for a group (`gaṇañatti`); or where four or three are residing, the Pavāraṇā of one is brought and the three or the two perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for the Saṅgha (`saṅghañatti`)—all this is a Pavāraṇā procedure that is unlawful and divisive.

Sace pana sabbepi pañca janā ekato sannipatitvā gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, cattāro tayo vā dve vā vasantā ekato sannipatitvā saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, sabbametaṃ adhammenasamaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ.

If, however, all five persons assemble together and perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for a group (`gaṇañatti`); or if four, three, or two who are residing assemble together and perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for the Saṅgha (`saṅghañatti`)—all this is a Pavāraṇā procedure that is unlawful but in concord.

Sace pañcasu janesu ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā cattāro saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, catūsu tīsu vā ekassa pavāraṇaṃ āharitvā tayo vā dve vā gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, sabbametaṃ dhammenavaggaṃ pavāraṇakammaṃ[P 5.1075].

If, among five persons, the Pavāraṇā of one is brought and the four perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for the Saṅgha (`saṅghañatti`); or among four or three, the Pavāraṇā of one is brought and the three or the two perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for a group (`gaṇañatti`)—all this is a Pavāraṇā procedure that is lawful but divisive.

Sace pana sabbepi pañca janā ekato sannipatitvā saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, cattāro vā tayo vā ekato sannipatitvā gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārenti, dve aññamaññaṃ pavārenti, ekako vasanto adhiṭṭhānapavāraṇaṃ karoti, sabbametaṃ dhammenasamaggaṃ nāma pavāraṇakammanti.

If, however, all five persons assemble together and perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for the Saṅgha (`saṅghañatti`); or if four or three assemble together and perform the Pavāraṇā having established a motion for a group (`gaṇañatti`); or if two perform the Pavāraṇā with each other; or if one residing alone performs the Pavāraṇā of determination—all this is called a Pavāraṇā procedure that is lawful and in concord.

Pavāraṇādānānujānanakathā

Discourse on the Giving and Authorization of the Pavāraṇā

213. Dinnā hoti pavāraṇāti ettha evaṃ dinnāya pavāraṇāya pavāraṇāhārakena saṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ pavāretabbaṃ – “tisso bhante bhikkhu saṅghaṃ pavāreti diṭṭhena vā sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā, vadatu taṃ bhante saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya, passanto paṭikarissati. Dutiyampi…pe… tatiyampi bhante tisso bhikkhu saṅghaṃ pavāreti…pe… paṭikarissatī”ti[V 0.0338]. Sace pana vuḍḍhataro hoti, “āyasmā bhante tisso”ti vattabbaṃ; evañhi tena tassatthāya pavāritaṃ hotīti.

213. Regarding 'The Pavāraṇā has been given': Herein, when the Pavāraṇā has been given thus, the bearer of the Pavāraṇā, having approached the Saṅgha, should perform the invitation in this way: 'Venerable sirs, the bhikkhu Tissa invites the Saṅgha based on what has been seen, heard, or suspected. Let the Saṅgha, venerable sirs, speak to him out of compassion; seeing it, he will make amends. For a second time… For a third time, venerable sirs, the bhikkhu Tissa invites the Saṅgha… he will make amends.' If, however, he is an elder, it should be said: 'The venerable Tissa, venerable sirs…' For in this way the Pavāraṇā is performed by that one on his behalf.

Pavāraṇaṃ [M 0.0358] dentena chandampi dātunti ettha chandadānaṃ uposathakkhandhake vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Idhāpi ca chandadānaṃ avasesakammatthāya. Tasmā sace pavāraṇaṃ dento chandaṃ deti, vuttanayena āhaṭāya pavāraṇāya tena ca bhikkhunā saṅghena ca pavāritameva hoti. Atha pavāraṇameva deti, na chandaṃ, tassa ca pavāraṇāya ārocitāya saṅghena ca pavārite sabbesaṃ suppavāritaṃ hoti, aññaṃ pana kammaṃ kuppati. Sace chandameva deti na pavāraṇaṃ, saṅghassa pavāraṇā ca sesakammāni ca na kuppanti, tena pana bhikkhunā appavāritaṃ hoti. Pavāraṇadivase pana bahisīmāyaṃ pavāraṇaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā āgatenapi chando dātabbo, tena saṅghassa pavāraṇakammaṃ na kuppati.

Regarding 'By one giving the Pavāraṇā, consent should also be given': Herein, the giving of consent should be understood according to the method stated in the Uposathakkhandhaka. And here too, the giving of consent is for the sake of the remaining formal acts. Therefore, if one giving the Pavāraṇā also gives consent, when the Pavāraṇā is brought in the prescribed manner, it is considered that both that bhikkhu and the Saṅgha have performed the Pavāraṇā. If, however, he gives only the Pavāraṇā and not the consent, when his Pavāraṇā has been announced and the Saṅgha has performed the Pavāraṇā, it is well-performed for all, but any other formal act is invalidated. If he gives only the consent and not the Pavāraṇā, the Saṅgha's Pavāraṇā and the remaining formal acts are not invalidated, but that bhikkhu has not performed the Pavāraṇā. Furthermore, on the Pavāraṇā day, consent should also be given by one who has arrived after having made the determination for Pavāraṇā outside the boundary; thereby the Saṅgha's Pavāraṇā procedure is not invalidated.

218. Ajja me pavāraṇāti ettha sace cātuddasikā hoti, “ajja me pavāraṇā cātuddasī”ti sace pannarasikā “ajja me pavāraṇā pannarasī”ti evaṃ adhiṭṭhātabbaṃ.

218. Regarding 'Today is my Pavāraṇā': Herein, if it is the fourteenth, it should be determined thus: 'Today is my Pavāraṇā, the fourteenth.' If it is the fifteenth, it should be determined thus: 'Today is my Pavāraṇā, the fifteenth.'

219. Tadahupavāraṇāya āpattintiādi vuttanayameva.

219. The phrase beginning 'An offense on the day of Pavāraṇā' is according to the method already stated.

Anāpattipannarasakādikathā

Discourse on the Fifteen Cases of No Offense, and so forth

222. Puna pavāretabbanti puna pubbakiccaṃ katvā ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā saṅghattherato paṭṭhāya pavāretabbaṃ. Sesaṃ uposathakkhandhakavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

222. One should invite again, meaning: having performed the preliminary duties and established the motion, one should invite, beginning from the elder of the Saṅgha. The remainder should be understood by the very method stated in the commentary on the Uposathakkhandhaka.

228. Āgantukehi [P 5.1076] āvāsikānaṃ anuvattitabbanti “ajja pavāraṇā cātuddasī”ti etadeva pubbakiccaṃ kātabbaṃ. Pannarasikavārepi eseva nayo. Āvāsikehi nissīmaṃ gantvā pavāretabbanti assāvasāne ayaṃ pāḷimuttakavinicchayo – sace purimikāya pañca bhikkhū vassaṃ upagatā, pacchimikāyapi pañca, purimehi ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavārite pacchimehi tesaṃ santike pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo, na ekasmiṃ uposathagge dve ñattiyo ṭhapetabbā. Sacepi pacchimikāya upagatā cattāro tayo dve eko vā hoti, eseva nayo. Atha purimikāya cattāro pacchimikāyapi cattāro tayo dve eko vā eseva nayo. Athāpi purimikāya tayo, pacchimikāyapi tayo dve vā, eseva nayo.
