Idañhettha lakkhaṇaṃ – sace purimikāya upagatehi pacchimikāya [V 0.0339] upagatā thokatarā [M 0.0359] ceva honti samasamā ca, saṅghapavāraṇāya gaṇaṃ pūrenti, saṅghapavāraṇāvasena ñatti ṭhapetabbāti.

228. The visiting bhikkhus should comply with the resident bhikkhus, meaning: this very preliminary duty should be performed, stating, 'Today is the Pavāraṇā of the fourteenth.' This is also the method on the occasion of the fifteenth. 'The resident bhikkhus should perform Pavāraṇā after going outside the boundary,' and at the end of this, there is this decision independent of the Pāḷi canon: If five bhikkhus have entered the rains-residence in the earlier period, and five also in the later period, when the Pavāraṇā has been performed by the earlier ones after establishing the motion, the Pārisuddhi Uposatha should be performed by the later ones in their presence. Two motions should not be established in one Uposatha hall. If those who entered in the later period are four, three, two, or one, this is the very method. And if there are four in the earlier period, and in the later period also four, three, two, or one, this is the very method. And if there are three in the earlier period, and in the later period also three or two, this is the very method. Herein, this is the defining rule: If those who entered in the later period are fewer than or equal to those who entered in the earlier period, and they complete the group for a Saṅgha Pavāraṇā, the motion should be established by way of a Saṅgha Pavāraṇā.

Sace pana purimikāya tayo, pacchimikāya eko hoti, tena saddhiṃ te cattāro honti, catunnaṃ saṅghañattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavāretuṃ na vaṭṭati. Gaṇañattiyā pana so gaṇapūrako hoti, tasmā gaṇavasena ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā purimehi pavāretabbaṃ. Itarena tesaṃ santike pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Sace purimikāya dve pacchimikāya dve vā eko vā hoti, eseva nayo. Sace purimikāya eko, pacchimikāyapi eko hoti, ekena ekassa santike pavāretabbaṃ, ekena pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Sace pana purimavassūpagatehi pacchimavassūpagatā ekenapi adhikatarā honti, paṭhamaṃ pātimokkhaṃ uddisitvā pacchā thokatarehi tesaṃ santike pavāretabbaṃ.

If, however, there are three in the earlier period and one in the later period, together with that one they become four. It is not allowable for the four to perform Pavāraṇā by establishing a Saṅgha motion. But for a group motion, that one is a completer of the group; therefore, having established the motion by way of a group, the earlier ones should perform Pavāraṇā. The Pārisuddhi Uposatha should be performed by the other one in their presence. If there are two in the earlier period and two or one in the later period, this is the very method. If there is one in the earlier period and one also in the later period, Pavāraṇā should be performed by the one in the presence of the other, and the Pārisuddhi Uposatha should be performed by the other. If, however, those who entered the rains-residence in the later period are more numerous than those who entered in the earlier period, even by one, having first recited the Pātimokkha, afterwards Pavāraṇā should be performed by the fewer ones in their presence.

Kattikacātumāsiniyā pavāraṇāya pana sace paṭhamaṃ vassūpagatehi mahāpavāraṇāya pavāritehi pacchā upagatā adhikatarā vā samasamā vā honti, pavāraṇāñattiṃ ṭhapetvā pavāretabbaṃ. Tehi pavārite pacchā itarehi pārisuddhiuposatho kātabbo. Atha mahāpavāraṇāya pavāritā bahū bhikkhū honti, pacchimavassūpagatā [P 5.1077] thokatarā vā eko vā, pātimokkhe uddiṭṭhe pacchā tesaṃ santike tena pavāretabbaṃ.

Furthermore, at the Pavāraṇā of the four-month Kattika period, if those who entered later are more numerous than or equal in number to those who had first entered the rains-residence and performed Pavāraṇā at the Mahāpavāraṇā, one should perform Pavāraṇā after establishing the Pavāraṇā motion. When Pavāraṇā has been performed by them, afterwards the Pārisuddhi Uposatha should be performed by the others. If those who performed Pavāraṇā at the Mahāpavāraṇā are many bhikkhus, and those who entered the rains-residence in the later period are fewer or one, then after the Pātimokkha has been recited, Pavāraṇā should be performed by him in their presence.

233. Na ca bhikkhave appavāraṇāya pavāretabbaṃ, aññatra saṅghasāmaggiyāti ettha kosambakasāmaggīsadisāva sāmaggī veditabbā. “Ajja pavāraṇā sāmaggī”ti evañcettha pubbakiccaṃ kātabbaṃ. Ye pana kismiñcideva appamattake pavāraṇaṃ ṭhapetvā samaggā honti, tehi pavāraṇāyameva pavāraṇā kātabbā. Sāmaggīpavāraṇaṃ karontehi ca paṭhamapavāraṇaṃ ṭhapetvā pāṭipadato paṭṭhāya yāva kattikacātumāsinī puṇṇamā, etthantare kātabbā, tato pacchā vā pure vā na vaṭṭati.

233. And, bhikkhus, the Pavāraṇā should not be performed when there is an objection, except for the sake of the Saṅgha's concord. Herein, the concord should be understood as being just like the concord of the Kosambī bhikkhus. And herein, the preliminary duty should be performed thus: 'Today is the Pavāraṇā of concord.' But those who, on account of some trifling matter, having suspended the Pavāraṇā, become concordant, by them the Pavāraṇā should be performed on the Pavāraṇā day itself. And by those performing the concord-Pavāraṇā, having suspended the first Pavāraṇā, it should be performed in the interval beginning from the first day of the waning moon up until the full moon of the four-month Kattika period. It is not allowable after or before that.

Dvevācikādipavāraṇākathā

The Account of the Two-Statement and Other Pavāraṇās

234. Dvevācikaṃ pavāretunti ettha ñattiṃ ṭhapentenāpi “yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṃ saṅgho dvevācikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vattabbaṃ, ekavācike “ekavācikaṃ [M 0.0360] pavāreyyā”ti, samānavassikepi “samānavassikaṃ pavāreyyā”ti vattabbaṃ, ettha ca bahūpi samānavassā ekato pavāretuṃ labhanti.

234. Regarding 'should perform the two-statement Pavāraṇā': here, even when proposing the motion, one should say, 'If it is the proper time for the Saṅgha, the Saṅgha should perform the two-statement Pavāraṇā.' In the case of a one-statement Pavāraṇā, one should say, '...should perform the one-statement Pavāraṇā'; in the case of the same-vassa Pavāraṇā also, one should say, '...should perform the same-vassa Pavāraṇā.' And here, many monks of the same vassa may perform the Pavāraṇā together.

Pavāraṇāṭhapanakathā

The Account of Suspending the Pavāraṇā

236. Bhāsitāya [V 0.0340] lapitāya apariyositāyāti ettha sabbasaṅgāhikañca puggalikañcāti duvidhaṃ pavāraṇāṭhapanaṃ. Tattha sabbasaṅgāhike “suṇātu me bhante saṅgho…pe… saṅgho tevācikaṃ pavāre” iti sukārato yāva rekāro, tāva bhāsitā lapitā apariyositāva hoti pavāraṇā. Etthantare ekapadepi ṭhapentena ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā. ‘Yya’kāre pana patte pariyositā hoti, tasmā tato paṭṭhāya ṭhapentena ṭhapitāpi aṭṭhapitā hoti. Puggalikaṭhapane pana – “saṅghaṃ bhante pavāremi…pe… tatiyampi bhante saṅghaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā…pe… passanto paṭī”ti saṅkārato yāva ayaṃ sabbapacchimo ‘ṭi’kāro tāva bhāsitā lapitā apariyositāva hoti pavāraṇā, etthantare ekapadepi ṭhapentena ṭhapitā hoti pavāraṇā, “karissāmī”ti vutte pana pariyositā hoti, tasmā “karissāmī”ti etasmiṃ pade patte ṭhapitāpi aṭṭhapitā hoti. Esa nayo dvevācikaekavācikasamānavassikāsupi. Etāsupi [P 5.1078] hi ṭikārāvasānaṃyeva ṭhapanakhettanti.

236. Here, regarding 'spoken, uttered, but not completed,' the suspension of the Pavāraṇā is of two kinds: communal and personal. In the communal suspension, from the syllable 'su' up to the syllable 're' of the statement 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha hear me… the Saṅgha should perform the three-statement Pavāraṇā,' the Pavāraṇā is spoken and uttered, but is not yet completed. Within this interval, if one suspends it even at a single word, the Pavāraṇā is suspended. However, upon reaching the syllable 'yya,' it is completed. Therefore, from that point onward, even if one suspends it, it is not suspended. In the case of personal suspension, from the syllable 'saṃ' of 'saṅghaṃ bhante pavāremi…' up to this very last syllable 'ṭi' of '…tatiyampi bhante saṅghaṃ pavāremi diṭṭhena vā… passanto paṭi[karissāmi],' the Pavāraṇā is spoken and uttered, but is not yet completed. Within this interval, if one suspends it even at a single word, the Pavāraṇā is suspended. However, when 'karissāmi' is said, it is completed. Therefore, upon reaching this word 'karissāmi,' even if it is suspended, it is not suspended. This is the method also for the two-statement, one-statement, and same-vassa Pavāraṇās, for in these cases too, the domain for suspension is only what ends with the syllable 'ṭi'.

237. Anuyuñjiyamānoti “kimhi naṃ ṭhapesī”ti parato vuttanayena pucchiyamāno. Omadditvāti etāni “alaṃ bhikkhu mā bhaṇḍana”ntiādīni vacanāni vatvā, vacanomaddanā hi idha omaddanāti adhippetā. Anuddhaṃsitaṃ paṭijānātīti “amūlakena pārājikena anuddhaṃsito ayaṃ mayā”ti evaṃ paṭijānāti. Yathādhammanti saṅghādisesena anuddhaṃsane pācittiyaṃ; itarehi dukkaṭaṃ. Nāsetvāti liṅganāsanāya nāsetvā.

237. 'Being questioned' means being asked in the manner stated later, 'On what grounds did you suspend it?' 'Having crushed down' means having said such words as 'Enough, monk, do not quarrel,' and so on; for here, 'crushing down' is intended to mean suppression by speech. 'He admits to having disgraced' means he admits thus: 'This monk has been disgraced by me with a groundless Pārājika charge.' 'According to the Dhamma' means there is a Pācittiya offense for disgracing with a Saṅghādisesa charge; for other charges, there is a Dukkaṭa. 'Having removed' means having removed by way of destroying the sign [of a monk].

238. Sāssa yathādhammaṃ paṭikatāti ettakameva vatvā pavārethāti vattabbā, asukā nāma āpattīti idaṃ pana na vattabbaṃ, etañhi kalahassa mukhaṃ hoti.

238. Having said only this much, 'It has been properly dealt with for her according to the Dhamma,' it should be said, 'You all should perform the Pavāraṇā.' However, one should not say, 'The offense is such-and-such,' for this is a source of quarrels.

Vatthuṭhapanādikathā

Discourse on Setting Aside the Matter, and so forth

239. Idaṃ vatthu paññāyati na puggaloti ettha corā kira araññavihāre pokkharaṇito macche gahetvā pacitvā khāditvā agamaṃsu. So [M 0.0361] taṃ vippakāraṃ disvā ārāme vā kiñci dhuttena kataṃ vippakāraṃ disvā “bhikkhussa iminā kammena bhavitabba”nti sallakkhetvā evamāha. Vatthuṃ ṭhapetvā saṅgho pavāreyyāti “yadā taṃ puggalaṃ jānissāma, tadā naṃ codessāma. Idāni pana saṅgho pavāretū”ti ayamettha attho. Idāneva naṃ vadehīti sace iminā [V 0.0341] vatthunā kañci puggalaṃ parisaṅkasi, idāneva naṃ apadisāhīti attho. Sace apadisati, taṃ puggalaṃ anuvijjitvā pavāretabbaṃ; no ce apadisati, upaparikkhitvā jānissāmāti pavāretabbaṃ.

239. Here, in the case of “This matter is evident, not the person”: It is said that in a forest monastery, thieves caught fish from a pond, cooked them, ate them, and departed. That monk, having seen that improper state of affairs, or having seen some improper act done by a rogue in the monastery, reflected, “This must be the deed of a monk,” and spoke thus. As for “The Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā, having set aside the matter,” the meaning here is this: “When we come to know that person, then we will accuse him. But for now, let the Saṅgha perform Pavāraṇā.” As for “You should speak of him right now,” the meaning is this: “If, on account of this matter, you suspect any person, you should point him out right now.” If he points someone out, the Pavāraṇā should be performed after investigating that person. If he does not point anyone out, the Pavāraṇā should be performed, saying, “We will know after examining.”

Ayaṃ puggalo paññāyati na vatthūti ettha eko bhikkhu mālāgandhavilepanehi cetiyaṃ vā pūjesi, ariṭṭhaṃ vā pivi, tassa tadanurūpo sarīragandho ahosi; so taṃ gandhaṃ sandhāya “imassa bhikkhuno evarūpo sarīragandho”ti vatthuṃ pakāsento evamāha. Puggalaṃ ṭhapetvā saṅgho pavāreyyāti etaṃ puggalaṃ ṭhapetvā saṅgho pavāretu. Idāneva naṃ vadehīti yaṃ tvaṃ puggalaṃ ṭhapesi, tassa puggalassa idāneva dosaṃ vada. Sace ayamassa dosoti vadati, taṃ [P 5.1079] puggalaṃ sodhetvā pavāretabbaṃ. Atha nāhaṃ jānāmīti vadati, upaparikkhitvā jānissāmāti pavāretabbaṃ.

Here, in the case of “This person is evident, not the matter”: A certain monk honored a cetiya with flowers, perfumes, and ointments, or he drank a medicinal infusion of ariṭṭha, and a corresponding scent arose from his body. That monk, referring to that scent and revealing the matter, spoke thus: “This monk has such a body scent.” As for “The Saṅgha should perform Pavāraṇā, having set aside the person,” it means: “Let the Saṅgha perform Pavāraṇā, having set aside this person.” As for “You should speak of him right now,” it means: “You should state right now the fault of the person whom you have set aside.” If he says, “This is his fault,” the Pavāraṇā should be performed after clearing that person. Or, if he says, “I do not know,” the Pavāraṇā should be performed, saying, “We will know after investigating.”

Idaṃ vatthu ca puggalo ca paññāyatīti purimanayeneva corehi macche gahetvā pacitvā paribhuttaṭṭhānañca gandhādīhi nahānaṭṭhānañca disvā “pabbajitassa kamma”nti maññamāno so evamāha. Idāneva naṃ vadehīti idāneva tena vatthunā parisaṅkitaṃ puggalaṃ vadehi; idaṃ pana ubhayampi disvā diṭṭhakālato paṭṭhāya vinicchinitvāva pavāretabbaṃ. Kallaṃ vacanāyāti kallaṃ codanāya; codetuṃ vaṭṭatīti attho. Kasmā? Pavāraṇato pubbe avinicchitattā pacchā ca disvā coditattāti. Ukkoṭanakaṃ pācittiyanti idañhi ubhayaṃ pubbe pavāraṇāya disvā vinicchinitvāva bhikkhū pavārenti, tasmā puna taṃ ukkoṭentassa āpatti.

As for “This matter and the person are evident”: In the manner of the previous examples, having seen the place where fish were eaten by thieves and the place where bathing was done with perfumes and so on, that monk, thinking, “This is the deed of a renunciant,” speaks thus. As for “You should speak of him right now,” it means: “You should now speak of the person suspected on account of that matter.” However, having seen both of these, the Pavāraṇā should be performed only after having decided, starting from the time of seeing. As for “It is suitable for speaking,” it means it is suitable for accusation; the meaning is that it is proper to accuse. Why? Because of it not having been decided before the Pavāraṇā, and because of the accusation being made after having seen it later. As for the Pācittiya offense for reopening a matter: For, the monks perform Pavāraṇā only after having seen both these things before the Pavāraṇā and having come to a decision; therefore, for one who reopens that matter again, there is an offense.

Bhaṇḍanakārakavatthukathā

The Account of the Quarrel-makers

240. Dve tayo uposathe cātuddasike kātunti ettha catutthapañcamā dve, tatiyo pana pakatiyāpi catuddasikoyevāti. Tasmā [M 0.0362] tatiyacatutthā vā tatiyacatutthapañcamā vā dve tayo cātuddasikā kātabbā. Atha catutthe kate suṇanti, pañcamo cātuddasiko kātabbo. Evampi dve cātuddasikā honti. Evaṃ karontā bhaṇḍanakārakānaṃ terase vā cātuddase vā ime pannarasīpavāraṇaṃ pavāressanti. Evaṃ pavārentehi ca bahisīmāya sāmaṇere ṭhapetvā “te āgacchantī”ti sutvā lahuṃ lahuṃ sannipatitvā pavāretabbaṃ. Etamatthaṃ dassetuṃ “te ce bhikkhave…pe… tathā karontū”ti vuttaṃ.

240. Herein, regarding 'two or three Uposathas should be made fourteenths', the decision should be understood thus: the fourth and fifth are two Uposathas, but the third is by nature also a fourteenth. Therefore, the third and fourth, or the third, fourth, and fifth, should be made two or three fourteenths. Then, if the fourth Uposatha is observed and they hear that the others are coming, the fifth should be made a fourteenth Uposatha. In this way also, there are two fourteenths. Acting thus, these monks will perform the Pavāraṇā of the fifteenth day on the thirteenth or fourteenth. And while performing Pavāraṇā thus, having placed novices outside the boundary, upon hearing, “They are coming,” they should quickly assemble and perform Pavāraṇā. To show this meaning, it was said, “If, bhikkhus, those… and so on… let them act thus.”

Asaṃvihitāti [V 0.0342] saṃvidahanarahitā āgamanajānanatthāya akatasaṃvidahitā; aviññātāva hutvāti attho. Tesaṃ vikkhitvāti “kilantattha muhuttaṃ vissamathā”tiādinā nayena sammohaṃ katvāti attho. No ce labhethāti no ce bahisīmaṃ gantuṃ labheyyuṃ; bhaṇḍanakārakānaṃ sāmaṇerehi ca daharabhikkhūhi ca nirantaraṃ anubaddhāva honti. Āgame juṇheti yaṃ sandhāya āgame juṇhe pavāreyyāmāti ñattiṃ ṭhapesuṃ, tasmiṃ āgame juṇhe komudiyā [P 5.1080] cātumāsiniyā akāmā pavāretabbaṃ, avassaṃ pavāretabbaṃ, na hi taṃ atikkamitvā pavāretuṃ labbhati. Tehi ce bhikkhave bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāneti evaṃ cātumāsiniyā pavāriyamāne.

‘Unprepared’ (asaṃvihitā) means lacking arrangement, not having made arrangements for the purpose of knowing their arrival; the meaning is, being unannounced. ‘Having scattered them’ (tesaṃ vikkhitvā) means having caused them confusion by the method of saying, “You are tired, rest for a moment,” and so on. ‘If they do not obtain’ (no ce labhetha) means if they are not able to go outside the boundary; they are constantly followed by the novices and young bhikkhus of the quarrel-makers. Regarding ‘on the coming full moon’ (āgame juṇhe): it refers to that on which they established the motion, “We will perform Pavāraṇā on the coming full moon.” On that coming full moon, the Komudī of the four-month season, Pavāraṇā must be performed unwillingly; it must certainly be performed, for it is not permitted to perform Pavāraṇā by transgressing that day. ‘While those bhikkhus, O bhikkhus, are performing Pavāraṇā’ (tehi ce bhikkhave bhikkhūhi pavāriyamāne) means thus, while performing Pavāraṇā on the full moon of the four-month season.

Pavāraṇāsaṅgahakathā

The Account of the Compendium of Pavāraṇā

241. Aññataro phāsuvihāroti taruṇasamatho vā taruṇavipassanā vā. Paribāhirā bhavissāmāti anibaddharattiṭṭhānadivāṭṭhānādibhāvena bhāvanānuyogaṃ sampādetuṃ asakkontā bāhirā bhavissāma. Sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabbanti iminā chandadānaṃ paṭikkhipati. Bhinnassa hi saṅghassa samaggakaraṇakāle tiṇavatthārakasamathe imasmiñca pavāraṇāsaṅgaheti imesu tīsu ṭhānesu chandaṃ dātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Pavāraṇāsaṅgaho nāmāyaṃ vissaṭṭhakammaṭṭhānānaṃ thāmagatasamathavipassanānaṃ sotāpannādīnañca na dātabbo. Taruṇasamathavipassanālābhino pana sabbe vā hontu, upaḍḍhā vā, ekapuggalo vā ekassapi vasena dātabboyeva. Dinne pavāraṇāsaṅgahe [M 0.0363] antovasse parihārova hoti, āgantukā tesaṃ senāsanaṃ gahetuṃ na labhanti. Tehipi chinnavassehi na bhavitabbaṃ, pavāretvā pana antarāpi cārikaṃ pakkamituṃ labhantīti dassanatthaṃ “tehi ce bhikkhave”tiādimāha. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

241. ‘A certain comfortable dwelling’ (aññataro phāsuvihāro) refers to either newly developed tranquility (samatha) or newly developed insight (vipassanā). ‘We will be outsiders’ (paribāhirā bhavissāma) means: being unable to accomplish the application to meditation due to not having a fixed place for night and day, we will become outsiders. By ‘All must gather in one place’ (sabbeheva ekajjhaṃ sannipatitabbaṃ), the giving of consent is rejected. For in these three instances—at the time of creating harmony for a divided Saṅgha, in the legal question settled by covering with grass, and in this compendium of Pavāraṇā—it is not proper to give consent. This so-called compendium of Pavāraṇā should not be given to those whose meditation subjects are forgotten, those who have attained strength in tranquility and insight, or to stream-enterers and so on. However, for those who are attainers of new tranquility and insight—whether they are all, half, or a single individual—it must be given even for the sake of one person. When the compendium of Pavāraṇā has been given, it serves as a protection within the Rains-residence; incoming bhikkhus are not able to take their lodging. And they should not become ones with a broken Rains-residence. But after performing Pavāraṇā, they are permitted to depart on a journey even in the interim. To show this, He said, “If, bhikkhus, those…” and so on. The rest is self-evident everywhere.

Pavāraṇākkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Pavāraṇā Khandhaka is concluded.

5. Cammakkhandhakaṃ

5. The Chapter on Hides

Soṇakoḷivisavatthukathā

The Story of Soṇa Koḷivisa

242. Cammakkhandhake [M 0.0364][V 0.0343] – issariyādhipaccanti issarabhāvena ca adhipatibhāvena ca samannāgataṃ. Rajjanti rājabhāvaṃ, raññā kattabbakiccaṃ vā. Soṇo nāma koḷivisoti ettha soṇoti tassa nāmaṃ; koḷivisoti gottaṃ. Pādatalesu lomānīti rattesu pādatalesu sukhumāni añjanavaṇṇāni kammacittīkatāni lomāni jātāni honti. So kira pubbe asītisahassānaṃ purisānaṃ jeṭṭhapuriso hutvā tehi saddhiṃ paccekabuddhassa vasanaṭṭhāne paṇṇasālaṃ katvā attano sassirikaṃ uṇṇapāvārakaṃ paccekabuddhassa pādehi akkamanaṭṭhāne pādapuñchanikaṃ katvā ṭhapesi. Temāsaṃ pana sabbeva paccekabuddhaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃsu. Ayaṃ tassa ca tesañca asītiyā gāmikasahassānaṃ [P 5.1081] pubbayogo.

242. In the Chapter on Hides—‘issariyādhipacca’ means endowed with lordship and supremacy, by way of being a lord and by way of being supreme. ‘Rajja’ refers to kingship or duties to be performed by a king. ‘Soṇa named Koḷivisa’—here, Soṇa is his name, and Koḷivisa is his clan. ‘Hair on the soles of his feet’—on his red soles, fine hairs the color of antimony, made variegated by kamma, had grown. It is said that in a past life, he was the chief of eighty thousand men, and together with them he built a leaf hut at the dwelling place of a Paccekabuddha. He placed his own splendid woolen blanket as a foot-wiping mat where the Paccekabuddha would step. For three months, they all attended to the Paccekabuddha. This was his and those eighty thousand village headmen’s past connection.

Asītigāmikasahassānīti tesu gāmesu vasantānaṃ kulaputtānaṃ asītisahassāni. Kenacideva karaṇīyenāti kenaci karaṇīyena viya; na panassa kiñci karaṇīyaṃ atthi aññatra tassa dassanā. Rājā kira tānipi asītikulaputtasahassāni sannipātāpento “evaṃ aparisaṅkanto soṇo āgamissatī”ti sannipātāpesi. Diṭṭhadhammike attheti “kasivaṇijjādīni dhammena kattabbāni, mātāpitaro dhammena positabbā”ti evamādinā nayena idhalokahite atthe anusāsitvā. So no bhagavāti so amhākaṃ bhagavā tumhe samparāyike atthe anusāsissatīti attho.

‘Eighty thousand gāmikas’ means eighty thousand young men from good families living in those villages. ‘For some business or other’ means as if for some business; but he had no business other than seeing him. The king, it is said, had those eighty thousand young men from good families assembled, thinking, ‘In this way, Soṇa will come without suspicion.’ ‘Visible benefits’ means having instructed them in benefits visible in this life, such as ‘Farming and trade should be done righteously, parents should be supported righteously,’ and so on. ‘That Blessed One is ours’ means that Blessed One, our Blessed One, will instruct you in benefits relating to the future life.

Bhagavantaṃ paṭivedemīti bhagavantaṃ jānāpemi. Pāṭikāya nimujjitvāti sopānassa heṭṭhā aḍḍhacandapāsāṇe nimujjitvā. Yassa dāni bhante bhagavā kālaṃ maññatīti yassa tesaṃ hitakiriyatthassa bhagavā kālaṃ jānāti. Vihārapacchāyāyanti vihārapaccante chāyāyaṃ. Samannāharantīti pasādavasena punappunaṃ manasi karonti. Bhiyyosomattāyāti bhiyyosomattāya puna visiṭṭhataraṃ dassehīti attho. Antaradhāyatīti adassanaṃ hoti.

‘I inform the Blessed One’ means I make known to the Blessed One. ‘Having plunged into the pāṭikā’ means having plunged into the half-moon stone at the foot of the stairs. ‘Now, venerable sir, whatever the Blessed One thinks is the right time’ means for whatever action for their benefit the Blessed One knows the time. ‘In the shade of the monastery’ means in the shade at the edge of the monastery. ‘They attend’ means they repeatedly bring to mind with faith. ‘For the sake of even greater excellence’ means for the sake of even greater excellence, show something even more distinguished—this is the meaning. ‘He disappears’ means he becomes unseen.

Soṇassa pabbajjākathā

The Story of Soṇa's Going Forth

243. Lohitena [M 0.0365][V 0.0344] phuṭo hotīti lohitena makkhito hoti. Gavāghātananti yattha gāvo haññanti, tādisoti attho. Kusalo nāma vīṇāya vādanakusalo. Vīṇāya tantissareti vīṇāya tantiyā sare. Accāyatāti atiāyatā kharamucchitā. Saravatīti sarasampannā. Kammaññāti kammakkhamā. Atisithilāti mandamucchanā. Same guṇe patiṭṭhitāti majjhime sare ṭhapetvā mucchitā. Vīriyasamataṃ adhiṭṭhahāti vīriyasampayuttasamataṃ adhiṭṭhāhi, vīriyaṃ samathena yojehīti attho. Indriyānañca samataṃ paṭivijjhāti saddhādīnaṃ indriyānaṃ samataṃ samabhāvaṃ. Tattha saddhaṃ paññāya, paññañca saddhāya, vīriyaṃ samādhinā, samādhiñca vīriyena yojayamāno indriyānaṃ samataṃ paṭivijjha. Tattha ca nimittaṃ gaṇhāhīti tasmiṃ samathe sati, yena ādāse mukhabimbeneva nimittena uppajjitabbaṃ[P 5.1082], taṃ samathanimittaṃ vipassanānimittaṃ magganimittaṃ phalanimittañca gaṇhāhi, nibbattehīti attho.

243. "Smeared with blood" means stained with blood. "A place for slaughtering cattle" means a place where cattle are killed; such is the meaning. "Skilled" means one skilled in playing the lute. "The sound of the lute's string" means the sound of the lute's string. "Overly taut" means they are overly stretched and played harshly. "Melodious" means endowed with sound. "Workable" means suitable for the task. "Too slack" means a weak playing. "Established on an even quality" means having been set in the middle sound, they are played. "Establish the balance of energy" means: establish tranquility associated with energy; connect energy with tranquility. Such is the meaning. "And penetrate the balance of the faculties" means the balance, the state of being equal, of the faculties such as faith and so on. Therein, while balancing faith with wisdom, and wisdom with faith, energy with concentration, and concentration with energy, penetrate the balance of the faculties. "And grasp the sign therein" means: when that tranquility is present, by which sign it should arise, just as a reflection of the face should arise in a mirror, grasp that sign of tranquility, that sign of insight, that sign of the path, and that sign of the fruit; produce it. Such is the meaning.

244. Aññaṃ byākareyyanti arahā ahanti jānāpeyyaṃ. Cha ṭhānānīti cha kāraṇāni. Adhimutto hotīti paṭivijjhitvā paccakkhaṃ katvā ṭhito hoti. Nekkhammādhimuttotiādi sabbaṃ arahattavasena vuttaṃ. Arahattañhi sabbakilesehi nikkhantattā nekkhammaṃ, teheva pavivittattā paviveko, byāpajjābhāvato abyāpajjaṃ, upādānassa khayante uppannattā upādānakkhayo, taṇhākkhayante uppannattā taṇhakkhayo, sammohābhāvato asammohoti ca vuccati.

244. "Should I declare another attainment" means: should I make it known, "I am an Arahant." "Six grounds" means six reasons. "Is resolved" means he stands, having penetrated and made it directly evident. "Resolved on renunciation," and so on—all this was said by the power of Arahantship. Indeed, Arahantship is called "renunciation" because of having departed from all defilements; "seclusion" because of being secluded from those very things; "non-ill will" because of the absence of ill will; "the destruction of clinging" because it arises at the end of the destruction of clinging; "the destruction of craving" because it arises at the end of the destruction of craving; and it is called "non-delusion" because of the absence of delusion.

Kevalaṃ saddhāmattakanti paṭivedharahitaṃ kevalaṃ paṭivedhapaññāya asammissaṃ saddhāmattakaṃ. Paṭicayanti punappunaṃ karaṇena vuḍḍhiṃ. Vītarāgattāti maggappaṭivedhena rāgassa vigatattāyeva nekkhammasaṅkhātaṃ arahattaṃ paṭivijjhitvā ṭhito hoti. Phalasamāpattivihāreneva viharati, tanninnamānasoyeva hotīti attho. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo.

"Mere faith alone" means mere faith that is devoid of penetration, unmixed with the wisdom of penetration. "Increase" means growth by means of doing again and again. "Being free from lust" means he stands having penetrated the fruit of Arahantship, called 'renunciation,' only because of the departure of lust through the penetration of the path. He dwells only by means of the abiding in the attainment of fruition; he is one whose mind is inclined towards that. Such is the meaning. In the remaining terms also, this is the method.

Lābhasakkārasilokanti [M 0.0366] catupaccayalābhañca tesaṃyeva sukatabhāvañca vaṇṇabhaṇanañca. Nikāmayamānoti icchamāno patthayamāno. Pavivekādhimuttoti viveke adhimutto ahanti evaṃ arahattaṃ byākarotīti attho.

"Gain, honor, and fame" means the gain of the four requisites, the state of those very things being well-made, and the speaking of one's praise. "Desiring" means wishing and aspiring. "Resolved on seclusion" means he declares the fruit of Arahantship thus: "I am resolved on seclusion." Such is the meaning.

Sīlabbataparāmāsanti sīlañca vatañca parāmasitvā gahitagahaṇamattaṃ. Sārato paccāgacchantoti [V 0.0345] sārabhāvena jānanto. Abyāpajjādhimuttoti abyāpajjaṃ arahattaṃ byākarotīti attho. Imināva nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo.

"Grasping at precepts and vows" means merely the view that is held after wrongly considering precepts and vows. "Returns to the essence" means knowing as essential. "Resolved on non-ill will" means he declares the fruit of Arahantship, which is non-ill will; such is the meaning. By this very method, the meaning should be understood in all instances.

Bhusāti balavanto. Nevassa cittaṃ pariyādiyantīti etassa khīṇāsavassa cittaṃ gahetvā ṭhātuṃ na sakkonti. Amissīkatanti amissakataṃ. Kilesāhi ārammaṇena saddhiṃ cittaṃ missaṃ karonti, tesaṃ abhāvā amissīkataṃ. Ṭhitanti patiṭṭhitaṃ. Āneñjappattanti acalanappattaṃ. Vayañcassānupassatīti [P 5.1083] tassa cittassa uppādampi vayampi passati.

"Fierce" means powerful. "They do not overwhelm his mind" means they are not able to seize and hold the mind of this one whose cankers are destroyed. "Unmixed" means made unmixed. Indeed, defilements make the mind mixed with an object; due to their absence, it is made unmixed. "Steady" means established. "Attained to imperturbability" means having reached the unshakable state. "And he observes its passing away" means he sees both the arising and the passing away of that mind.

Nekkhammaṃ adhimuttassāti arahattaṃ paṭivijjhitvā ṭhitassa. Sesapadehipi arahattameva kathitaṃ. Upādānakkhayassāti upayogatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Asammohañca cetasoti cittassa ca asammohaṃ adhimuttassa. Disvā āyatanuppādanti āyatanānaṃ uppādañca vayañca disvā. Sammā cittaṃ vimuccatīti sammā hetunā nayena imāya vipassanāya paṭipattiyā phalasamāpattivasena cittaṃ vimuccati, nibbānārammaṇe adhimuccati. Santacittassāti nibbutacittassa. Tādinoti iṭṭhāniṭṭhe anunayapaṭighehi akampiyattā tādī, tassa tādino.

“Of one who is resolved on renunciation” means of one who stands having penetrated Arahantship. By the remaining terms also, Arahantship itself is spoken of. “Of the destruction of clinging” is a word in the genitive case used in the sense of the accusative. “And a mind of non-delusion” means of one who is resolved on the non-delusion of the mind. “Having seen the arising of the sense-bases” means having seen the arising and passing away of the sense-bases. “The mind is rightly liberated” means by the right cause, by the method, by this practice of insight, by the power of the attainment of fruition, the mind is liberated; it becomes resolved on Nibbāna as its object. “Of one with a peaceful mind” means of one with an extinguished mind. “Of such a one” means because of being unshaken by attraction and repulsion in regard to desirable and undesirable objects, one is called ‘tādī’ (such a one); of that ‘tādī’.

Diguṇādiupāhanapaṭikkhepakathā

The Discourse on the Rejection of Double-layered and Other Footwear

245. Aññaṃ byākarontīti arahattaṃ byākaronti. Attho ca vuttoti yena arahāti ñāyati, so attho vutto. Suttattho pana suttavaṇṇanatoyeva gahetabbo. Attā ca anupanītoti ahaṃ arahāti evaṃ byañjanavasena attā na upanīto. Atha ca panidhekacce moghapurisāti aññe pana tucchapurisā hasamānā viya asantameva aññaṃ vacanamattena santaṃ katvā byākaronti. Ekapalāsikanti ekapaṭalaṃ[M 0.0367]. Asītisakaṭavāheti ettha dve sakaṭabhārā eko vāhoti veditabbo. Sattahatthikañca anīkanti ettha cha hatthiniyo eko ca hatthīti idamekaṃ anīkaṃ. Īdisāni satta anīkāni sattahatthikaṃ anīkaṃ nāma. Diguṇāti dvipaṭalā. Tiguṇāti tipaṭalā. Gaṇaṅguṇūpāhanāti catupaṭalato paṭṭhāya vuccati.

245. “Declaring ‘another’” means they declare Arahantship. “And the meaning has been stated” means: the meaning by which one is known as an Arahant has been stated. The meaning of the Sutta, however, should be taken only from the Sutta commentary. “And the self is not presented” means: the self is not presented by way of the expression, “I am an Arahant.” “But here some foolish people” means: but other worthless men, as if mocking, declare Arahantship, which is non-existent, making it seem existent by mere words. “Single-soled” means having one layer. In the phrase “eighty cart-loads,” two cart-loads should be understood as one ‘vāha.’ “And a troop of seven elephants” means: here, six female elephants and one male elephant are one troop. Seven such troops are called a “troop of seven elephants.” “Double-layered” means having two layers. “Triple-layered” means having three layers. Starting from four layers, it is called “footwear with multiple layers” (gaṇaṅguṇūpāhanā).

Sabbanīlikādipaṭikkhepakathā

The Discourse on the Rejection of All-Blue and Other Footwear

246. Sabbanīlikāti sabbāva nīlikā. Esa nayo sabbapītikādīsupi. Tattha ca nīlikā umāpupphavaṇṇā hoti, pītikā kaṇikārapupphavaṇṇā, lohitikā jayasumanapupphavaṇṇā[V 0.0346], mañjiṭṭhikā mañjiṭṭhavaṇṇā eva, kaṇhā addāriṭṭhakavaṇṇā, mahāraṅgarattā satapadipiṭṭhivaṇṇā, mahānāmarattā sambhinnavaṇṇā hoti paṇḍupalāsavaṇṇā. Kurundiyaṃ pana [P 5.1084] “padumapupphavaṇṇā”ti vuttā. Etāsu yaṃkiñci labhitvā rajanaṃ coḷakena puñchitvā vaṇṇaṃ bhinditvā dhāretuṃ vaṭṭati. Appamattakepi bhinne vaṭṭatiyeva.

246. “All-blue” means entirely blue. This same method applies to “all-yellow” and so on. Among these, the blue is the color of a flax flower; the yellow is the color of a kaṇikāra flower; the red is the color of a jayasumana flower; the crimson is the color of madder itself; the black is the color of a wet soapberry; the deeply-dyed is the color of a centipede’s back; the one dyed with many dyes has a mixed color, the color of a pale leaf. In the Kurundī commentary, however, it is said to be “the color of a lotus flower.” Having obtained any of these, it is permissible to wear them after wiping the dye with a rough cloth and altering the color. Even if only a small amount is altered, it is still permissible.

Nīlakavaddhikāti yāsaṃ vaddhāyeva nīlā. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Etāpi vaṇṇabhedaṃ katvā dhāretabbā. Khallakabaddhāti paṇhipidhānatthaṃ tale khallakaṃ bandhitvā katā. Puṭabaddhāti yonakaupāhanā vuccati, yā yāvajaṅghato sabbapādaṃ paṭicchādeti. Pāliguṇṭhimāti paliguṇṭhitvā katā; yā upari pādamattameva paṭicchādeti, na jaṅghaṃ. Tūlapuṇṇikāti tūlapicunā pūretvā katā. Tittirapattikāti tittirapattasadisā vicittabaddhā. Meṇḍavisāṇavaddhikāti kaṇṇikaṭṭhāne meṇḍakasiṅgasaṇṭhāne vaddhe yojetvā katā. Ajavisāṇavaddhikādīsupi eseva nayo. Vicchikāḷikāpi tattheva vicchikanaṅguṭṭhasaṇṭhāne vaddhe yojetvā katā. Morapiñchaparisibbitāti talesu vā vaddhesu vā morapiñchehi suttakasadisehi parisibbitā. Citrāti vicitrā; etāsu yaṃkiñci labhitvā, sace tāni khallakādīni apanetvā sakkā honti vaḷañjituṃ, vaḷañjetabbā. Tesu pana sati vaḷañjantassa dukkaṭaṃ. Sīhacammaparikkhaṭā nāma pariyantesu cīvare anuvātaṃ viya sīhacammaṃ yojetvā katā. Lūvakacammaparikkhaṭāti pakkhibiḷālacammaparikkhaṭā[M 0.0368]. Etāsupi yā kāci labhitvā taṃ cammaṃ apanetvā dhāretabbā.

“Footwear with blue straps” are those whose straps are blue. This same method applies in all cases. These too should be worn after altering the color. “Bound with a heel-cover” are those made by tying a heel-cover onto the sole for the purpose of covering the heel. “Bound with a pouch” are called Yonian footwear, which cover the entire foot up to the shin. “Wrapped around” are those made by wrapping; they cover only the upper part of the foot, not the shin. “Stuffed with cotton” are those made by filling with cotton wool. “With partridge-feather patterns” are those with variegated straps resembling partridge feathers. “With ram’s horn straps” are those made by attaching straps shaped like a ram’s horn at the point where the straps meet. This same method applies to those with goat’s horn straps and so on. “With scorpion patterns” are also made by attaching straps shaped like a scorpion’s tail at that same place. “Sewn with peacock feathers” are those sewn all around on the soles or on the straps with peacock feathers that resemble fine thread. “Variegated” means multi-colored. Having obtained any of these, if it is possible to use them after removing the heel-cover and so on, they should be so used. However, for one who uses them while those things are still present, there is an offense of wrongdoing. “Bordered with lion skin” are those made by attaching lion skin at the edges, like the border on a robe. “Bordered with lūvaka skin” means bordered with the skin of a flying squirrel. Among these too, having obtained any one, it should be worn after removing that skin.

247. Omukkanti paṭimuñcitvā apanītaṃ. Navāti aparibhuttā.

247. “Taken off” means having put on and then removed. “New” means not yet used.

Ajjhārāmeupāhanapaṭikkhepakathā

The Discourse on the Prohibition of Footwear within the Monastery

248. Abhijīvanikassāti yena sippena abhijīvanti, jīvikaṃ kappenti, tassa kāraṇāti attho. Idha kho taṃ bhikkhaveti ettha tanti nipātamattaṃ, idha kho bhikkhave sobheyyāthāti [P 5.1085] attho. Yaṃ tumheti ye tumhe. Atha vā yadi tumheti vuttaṃ hoti. Yadisaddassa hi atthe ayaṃ nipāto. Ācariyesūtiādimhi pabbajjācariyo, upasampadācariyo, nissayācāriyo, uddesācariyoti ime cattāropi idha ācariyā eva. Avassikassa chabbasso ācariyamatto. So hi catuvassakāle taṃ nissāya vacchati; evaṃ ekavassassa sattavasso, duvassassa aṭṭhavasso, tivassassa navavasso, catuvassassa dasavasso. Imepi ācariyamattā eva[V 0.0347]. Upajjhāyassa sandiṭṭhasambhattā pana sahāyabhikkhū, ye vā pana keci dasahi vassehi mahantatarā te sabbepi upajjhāyamattā nāma. Ettakesu bhikkhūsu anupāhanesu caṅkamantesu saupāhanassa caṅkamato āpatti.

248. “For the sake of livelihood” means: for the reason of whatever craft by which they live and make a living. In “Idha kho taṃ bhikkhave,” the word “taṃ” is merely a particle; the meaning is, “Here, O monks, you would be resplendent.” “Yaṃ tumhe” means “those of you.” Alternatively, it is said to mean “if you.” For this particle “yaṃ” is in the sense of the word “yadi.” Regarding “teachers” and so forth: in this Dispensation, these four are indeed teachers: the going-forth teacher, the higher-ordination teacher, the dependence teacher, and the recitation teacher. For a monk without seniority, a six-vassa monk is like a teacher. For at the time of four vassas, he will live in dependence on him. Similarly, a seven-vassa monk for a one-vassa monk, an eight-vassa monk for a two-vassa monk, a nine-vassa monk for a three-vassa monk, and a ten-vassa monk for a four-vassa monk. These too are merely like teachers. Furthermore, fellow monks who are seen and associated with the preceptor, or any others who are more senior by ten vassas—all these are called “like a preceptor.” Among such monks walking without footwear, for one walking with footwear, there is an offense.

249. Pādakhīlābādho nāma pādato khīlasadisaṃ maṃsaṃ nikkhantaṃ hoti.

249. The affliction called “foot-stake” is when flesh resembling a stake has come out from the foot.

251. Tiṇapādukāti yena kenaci tiṇena katapādukā. Hintālapādukāti khajjūrīpattehi katapādukā; hintālapattehipi na vaṭṭatiyeva. Kamalapādukāti kamalatiṇaṃ nāma atthi, tena katapādukā; usīrapādukātipi vadanti. Kambalapādukāti uṇṇāhi katapādukā. Asaṅkamanīyāti bhūmiyaṃ suppatiṭṭhitā niccalā asaṃhāriyā.

251. “Grass footwear” means footwear made from any kind of grass. “Hintāla-palm footwear” means footwear made from date-palm leaves; even with hintāla-palm leaves, it is not allowable at all. “Kamala footwear” means: there is a grass called kamala grass, and it is footwear made from that; they also call it “usīra footwear.” “Woolen footwear” means footwear made from wool. “Immovable” means well-established on the ground, unmoving, and not to be carried away.

252. Aṅgajātaṃ chupantīti aṅgajāteneva aṅgajātaṃ chupanti. Ogāhetvā mārentīti anto udake daḷhaṃ gahetvā mārenti.

252. 'They touch the genital organ' means they touch the genital organ with the genital organ itself. 'They kill by submerging' means they kill by seizing them firmly inside the water.

Yānādipaṭikkhepakathā

The Discourse on the Prohibition of Vehicles and so forth

253. Itthiyuttenāti [M 0.0369] dhenuyuttena. Purisantarenāti purisasārathinā. Purisayuttenāti goṇayuttena. Itthantarenāti itthisārathinā. Gaṅgāmahiyāyāti gaṅgāmahakīḷikāya. Purisayuttaṃ hatthavaṭṭakanti ettha purisayuttaṃ itthisārathi vā hotu, purisasārathi vā vaṭṭati. Hatthavaṭṭakaṃ pana itthiyo vā vaṭṭentu purisā vā, vaṭṭatiyeva. Yānugghātenāti yānaṃ abhiruhantassa sabbo kāyo calati tappaccayā. Sivikanti pīṭhakasivikaṃ. Pāṭaṅkinti vaṃse laggetvā kataṃ paṭapotalikaṃ.

253. 'Yoked with a female' means yoked with a cow. 'With a man intervening' means with a male driver. 'Yoked with a male' means yoked with an ox. 'With a woman intervening' means with a female driver. 'At the Ganges festival' means like at the time of the great Ganges festival play. Regarding 'a vehicle yoked with a male, a hand-turned one': a vehicle yoked with a male animal is allowable whether it has a female driver or a male driver. Furthermore, a hand-turned vehicle is allowable whether women or men turn it. 'Due to the shaking of the vehicle' means: because the whole body of one mounting the vehicle moves. 'Palanquin' means a palanquin made of planks. 'Sling' means a cloth sling made by hanging it on a bamboo pole.

254. Uccāsayanamahāsayananānīti [P 5.1086] ettha uccāsayananti pamāṇātikkantaṃ mañcaṃ. Mahāsayananti akappiyattharaṇaṃ, āsandīādīsu āsandīti pamāṇātikkantāsanaṃ. Pallaṅkoti pādesu vāḷarūpāni ṭhapetvā kato. Gonakoti dīghalomako mahākojavo; caturaṅgulādhikāni kira tassa lomāni. Cittakāti vānacitro uṇṇāmayattharaṇo. Paṭikāti uṇṇāmayo setattharaṇo. Paṭalikāti ghanapupphako uṇṇāmayalohitattharaṇo; yo āmalakapaṭṭotipi vuccati. Tūlikāti pakatitūlikāyeva. Vikatikāti sīhabyagghādirūpavicitro uṇṇāmayattharaṇo. Uddalomīti ekato uggatalomaṃ uṇṇāmayattharaṇaṃ; “uddhalomī”tipi pāṭho. Ekantalomīti ubhato uggatalomaṃ uṇṇāmayattharaṇaṃ. Kaṭṭissanti ratanaparisibbitaṃ koseyyakaṭṭissamayaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ[V 0.0348]. Koseyyanti ratanaparisibbitaṃ kosiyasuttamayaṃ paccattharaṇaṃ; suddhakoseyyaṃ pana vaṭṭati.

254. In 'high beds and great beds,' 'high bed' means a bed that exceeds the allowed measure. 'Great bed' means an unallowable covering. Among these, 'a long chair' (āsandī) is a seat that exceeds the allowed measure. 'A couch with animal figures' (pallaṅka) is one made by placing figures of beasts of prey on its feet. 'A fleecy rug' (gonaka) is a large rug with long fleece; its fleece is said to exceed four finger-breadths. 'A patterned rug' (cittaka) is a woolen covering variegated by weaving. 'A white rug' (paṭikā) is a white woolen covering. 'A flowered rug' (paṭalikā) is a red woolen covering with thick flower patterns; it is also called 'one with an āmalaka-leaf pattern.' 'A mattress' (tūlikā) is just an ordinary cotton-filled mattress. 'A figured rug' (vikatikā) is a woolen covering variegated with figures of lions, tigers, and so on. 'A one-sided fleece' (uddalomī) is a woolen covering with the fleece raised on one side; there is also the reading 'uddhalomī'. 'A two-sided fleece' (ekantalomī) is a woolen covering with the fleece raised on both sides. 'A silk coverlet interwoven with gold' (kaṭṭissa) is a covering made of silk interwoven with gold thread and sewn with jewel-threads. 'A silk coverlet' (koseyya) is a covering made of silk thread and sewn with jewel-threads; however, a purely silk covering is allowable.

Kuttakanti soḷasannaṃ nāṭakitthīnaṃ ṭhatvā naccanayoggaṃ uṇṇāmayaattharaṇaṃ. Hatthattharaassattharāti hatthiassapiṭṭhīsu attharaṇakaattharaṇā eva. Rathattharepi eseva nayo. Ajinappaveṇīti ajinacammehi mañcappamāṇena sibbitvā katā paveṇī. Kadalīmigapavarapaccattharaṇanti kadalīmigacammaṃ nāma atthi, tena kataṃ pavarapaccattharaṇaṃ, uttamapaccattharaṇanti attho. Taṃ kira setavatthassa upari kadalīmigacammaṃ pattharitvā sibbitvā karonti. Sauttaracchadanti saha uttaracchadanena; uparibaddhena rattavitānena [P 5.1087] saddhinti attho[M 0.0370]. Setavitānampi heṭṭhā akappiyapaccattharaṇe sati na vaṭṭati, asati pana vaṭṭati. Ubhatolohitakūpadhānanti sīsūpadhānañca pādūpadhānañcāti mañcassa ubhatolohitakūpadhānaṃ, etaṃ na kappati. Yaṃ pana ekameva upadhānaṃ ubhosu passesu rattaṃ vā hoti, padumavaṇṇaṃ vā citraṃ vā, sace pamāṇayuttaṃ, vaṭṭati. Mahāupadhānaṃ pana paṭikkhittaṃ.

'A dancing-rug' (kuttaka) is a woolen covering suitable for sixteen dancing women to stand and dance upon. 'Elephant-covers and horse-covers' are simply coverings spread on the backs of elephants and horses. The same principle applies to a chariot-covering. 'A layered hide covering' (ajinappaveṇī) is a layered covering made by sewing together hides of the black antelope to the size of a bed. 'An excellent covering of kadalī deer hide' means: there is a hide called kadalī deer hide, and it is an excellent covering made from it; the meaning is 'a supreme covering.' It is said that they make it by spreading the kadalī deer hide over a white cloth and sewing it. 'With a canopy' means together with an upper covering; the meaning is together with a red canopy tied above. A white canopy is also not allowable if there is an unallowable covering underneath, but if there is not, it is allowable. 'Having red cushions at both ends' refers to both a head-cushion and a foot-cushion; thus, for a bed to have red cushions at both ends is not allowable. However, a single cushion that is red, or lotus-colored, or variegated on both sides, is allowable if it is of proper size. But a large cushion has been rejected by the Blessed One.

Sabbacammapaṭikkhepādikathā

The Discourse on the Prohibition of All Hides and So Forth

255. Dīpicchāpoti dīpipotako. Ogumphiyantīti bhittidaṇḍakādīsu veṭhetvā bandhanti.

255. `Dīpicchāpa` means a leopard cub. `Ogumphiyanti` means they wrap and bind to wall-posts and so forth.

256. Abhinisīditunti abhinissāya nisīdituṃ; apassayaṃ katvā nisīditunti attho. Gilānena bhikkhunā saupāhanenāti ettha gilāno nāma yo na sakkoti anupāhano gāmaṃ pavisituṃ.

256. `Abhinisīdituṃ` means to sit down relying on something; the meaning is to sit down having made a support. Regarding 'a sick monk with footwear on,' here 'sick' refers to one who is unable to enter a village without footwear.

257. Kuraraghareti evaṃnāmake nagare; etenassa gocaragāmo vutto. Papatake pabbateti papatanāmake pabbate; etenassa nivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ vuttaṃ. Soṇoti tassa nāmaṃ. Koṭiagghanakaṃ pana kaṇṇapiḷandhanakaṃ dhāreti, tasmā “kuṭikaṇṇo”ti vuccati; koṭikaṇṇoti attho. Pāsādikanti pasādajanakaṃ. Pasādanīyanti idaṃ tasseva atthavevacanaṃ. Uttamadamathasamathanti uttamaṃ damathañca samathañca paññañca samādhiñca kāyūpasamañca cittūpasamañcātipi attho. Dantanti sabbesaṃ visūkāyikavipphanditānaṃ upacchinnattā dantaṃ; khīṇakilesanti attho. Guttanti saṃvaraguttiyā guttaṃ. Santindriyanti yatindriyaṃ. Nāganti āguvirahitaṃ. Tiṇṇaṃ me vassānaṃ accayenāti [V 0.0349] mama pabbajjādivasato paṭṭhāya tiṇṇaṃ vassānaṃ accayena. Upasampadaṃ alatthanti ahaṃ upasampadaṃ alabhiṃ[P 5.1088]. Kaṇhuttarāti kaṇhamattikuttarā; upari vaḍḍhitakaṇhamattikāti attho. Gokaṇṭakahatāti gunnaṃ khurehi akkantabhūmito samuṭṭhitehi gokaṇṭakehi upahatā. Te kira gokaṇṭake ekapaṭalikā upāhanā rakkhituṃ na sakkonti; evaṃ kharā honti. Eragū, moragū, majjārū, jantūti imā catassopi tiṇajātiyo; etehi kaṭasārake ca taṭṭikāyo ca karonti. Ettha eragūti [M 0.0371] erakatiṇaṃ; taṃ oḷārikaṃ. Moragūtiṇaṃ tambasīsaṃ mudukaṃ sukhasamphassaṃ, tena katataṭṭikā nipajjitvā vuṭṭhitamatte puna uddhumātā hutvā tiṭṭhati. Majjārunā sāṭakepi karonti. Jantussa maṇisadiso vaṇṇo hoti. Senāsanaṃ paññapesīti bhisiṃ vā kaṭasārakaṃ vā paññapesi; paññapetvā ca pana soṇassa āroceti – “āvuso satthā tayā saddhiṃ ekāvāse vasitukāmo, gandhakuṭiyaṃyeva te senāsanaṃ paññatta”nti.

257. In the city named Kuraraghara; by this, his alms-resort village is stated. On the mountain named Papataka; by this, his dwelling place is stated. Soṇa was his name. He wore an ear-ornament worth a koṭi, therefore he is called 'Kuṭikaṇṇa'; the meaning is Soṇa, the lay follower with an ear-ornament worth a koṭi. `Pāsādika` means inspiring confidence. `Pasādanīya` is a synonym for that. `Uttamadamathasamatha` also has the meaning: supreme taming and calming, wisdom and concentration, and the pacification of body and mind. `Danta` means tamed because all restless bodily movements are cut off; or, one whose defilements are destroyed. `Gutta` means guarded by the guard of restraint. `Santindriya` means one with restrained senses. `Nāga` means free from offense. 'After the passing of my three years' means after the passing of three years starting from the day of my going forth. 'I obtained higher ordination' means I obtained higher ordination. `Kaṇhuttarā` means having black soil on top; the meaning is 'with black soil spread over it'. `Gokaṇṭakahatā` means afflicted by cow-thorns that have arisen from ground trodden by cows' hooves. It is said that those cow-thorns are so rough that a single-layered sandal cannot protect against them. Eragū, moragū, majjārū, and jantū are these four types of grass; with them they make mats and small carpets. Here, `eragū` is eraka grass; it is coarse. Moragū grass has a copper-colored tip, is soft, and pleasant to the touch; a small carpet made from it, just after one has lain down and risen, stands puffed up again. With majjārū they even make cloths. Jantū grass has a color like a jewel. 'He prepared a lodging' means he spread out a cushion or a grass mat; and having prepared it, he informed Soṇa: 'Friend, the Teacher wishes to dwell in the same residence with you; your lodging has been prepared in the fragrant hut itself.'

258. Ayaṃ khvassa kāloti ayaṃ kho kālo bhaveyya. Paridassīti paridassesi. “Idañcidañca vadeyyāsīti yaṃ me upajjhāyo jānāpesi, tassa ayaṃ kālo bhaveyya, handa dāni ārocemi taṃ sāsana”nti ayamettha adhippāyo.

258. `Ayaṃ khvassa kālo` means: this would be the time for that message. `Paridassī` means: he indicated. The intention here is: 'This would be the time for that matter of which my preceptor informed me, saying, “You should speak of this and that.” Come now, I shall announce that message.'

259. Vinayadharapañcamenāti anussāvanācariyapañcamena. Anujānāmi bhikkhave sabbapaccantimesu janapadesu guṇaṅguṇūpāhananti ettha manussacammaṃ ṭhapetvā yena kenaci cammena upāhanā vaṭṭati. Upāhanakosakasatthakosakakuñcikakosakesupi eseva nayo. Cammāni attharaṇānīti ettha pana yaṃkiñci eḷakacammaṃ ajacammañca attharitvā nipajjituṃ vā nisīdituṃ vā vaṭṭati. Migacamme eṇīmigo vātamigo pasadamigo kuraṅgamigo migamātuko rohitamigoti [P 5.1089] etesaṃyeva cammāni vaṭṭanti. Aññesaṃ pana –

259. `With a Vinaya expert as the fifth` means with the announcer of the formal act as the fifth. Regarding 'I allow, monks, in all border regions, multi-layered footwear,' here, excepting human skin, footwear made of any kind of hide is allowable. This same principle applies to cases for footwear, knives, and keys. Regarding 'hide coverings,' here, it is allowable to spread any sheepskin or goatskin to lie down or sit upon. Regarding the hides of deer, only the hides of these are allowable: the eṇī deer, vāta deer, pasada deer, kuraṅga deer, migamātuka deer, and rohita deer. But for others—

Makkaṭo kāḷasīho ca, sarabho kadalīmigo;

Ye ca vāḷamigā keci, tesaṃ cammaṃ na vaṭṭati.

The monkey and the black lion, the sarabha and the kadalī deer; and whatever other fierce beasts there are, their hide is not allowable.

Tattha vāḷamigāti sīhabyagghaacchataracchā; na kevalañca etesaṃyeva, yesaṃ pana cammaṃ vaṭṭatīti vuttaṃ, te ṭhapetvā avasesā antamaso gomahiṃsasasabiḷārādayopi sabbe imasmiṃ atthe vāḷamigātveva veditabbā. Etesañhi sabbesaṃ cammaṃ na vaṭṭati. Na tāva taṃ gaṇanūpagaṃ yāva na hatthaṃ gacchatīti yāva āharitvā vā na dinnaṃ, tumhākaṃ bhante cīvaraṃ uppannanti pahiṇitvā vā nārocitaṃ, tāva gaṇanaṃ na upeti. Sace anadhiṭṭhitaṃ, vaṭṭati; adhiṭṭhitañca gaṇanaṃ na upetīti attho. Yadā pana ānetvā vā dinnaṃ hoti, uppannanti vā sutaṃ, tato paṭṭhāya dasāhameva parihāraṃ labhatīti.

Here, 'fierce beasts' refers to lions, tigers, bears, and hyenas. And it is not only the hides of these that are not allowable. Rather, setting aside those whose hides are stated to be allowable, all the rest—even down to cows, buffaloes, hares, cats, and the like—are to be understood as 'fierce beasts' in this context. Indeed, the hides of all these are not allowable. Regarding 'it does not enter the reckoning until it has come to hand,' this means that as long as it has not been brought and given, or a message has not been sent and announced, 'Venerable sir, a robe has arisen for you,' it does not enter into the reckoning. If it is an undetermined robe, it is allowable; and a determined robe also does not enter the reckoning—this is the meaning. But when it has been brought and given, or when it is heard, 'It has arisen,' from that point onward, one obtains a grace period of only ten days.

Cammakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Chapter on Hides is concluded.

6. Bhesajjakkhandhakaṃ

6. The Chapter on Medicaments

Pañcabhesajjādikathā

The Discourse on the Five Medicines and So Forth

260. Bhesajjakkhandhake [M 0.0372][V 0.0351] – sāradikena ābādhenāti saradakāle uppannena pittābādhena, tasmiñhi kāle vassodakenapi tementi, kaddamampi maddanti, antarantarā ātapopi kharo hoti, tena tesaṃ pittaṃ koṭṭhabbhantaragataṃ hoti. Āhāratthañca phareyyāti āhāratthaṃ sādheyya.

260. In the Chapter on Medicaments – 'By the autumn disease' means by a bile disorder arisen in the autumn season, for at that time they are moistened even by rainwater, they tread on mud, and the heat is harsh at intervals; therefore, their bile enters into the intestines. 'And it might serve the purpose of food' means it might accomplish the purpose of food.

261. Nacchādentīti na jiranti, na vātarogaṃ paṭippassambhetuṃ sakkonti. Senesitānīti siniddhāni. Bhattācchādakenāti bhattaṃ arocikena.

261. 'They do not cover' means they are not digested, or they are not able to calm wind-disease. 'Oily' means greasy foods. 'By that which spoils the meal' means because of that which causes a lack of appetite for the meal.

262. Acchavasantiādīsu nissaggiyavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayeneva vinicchayo veditabbo. Kāle paṭiggahitantiādīsu majjhanhike avītivatte paṭiggahetvā pacitvā parissāvetvā cāti attho. Telaparibhogena [P 5.1090] paribhuñjitunti sattāhakālikatelaparibhogena paribhuñjituṃ.

262. Regarding 'they dwell' and so on, the decision should be understood only by the method stated in the explanation of the Nissaggiya rules. Regarding 'received at the proper time' and so on, the meaning is: having received it, cooked it, and strained it before midday has passed. 'To consume with the use of oil' means to consume by way of using oil that is allowable for seven days.

263. Mūlabhesajjādi vinicchayopi khuddakavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttoyeva. Tasmā idha yaṃ yaṃ pubbe avuttaṃ taṃ tadeva vaṇṇayissāma. Vacattanti setavacaṃ. Nisadaṃ nisadapotakanti pisanasilā ca pisanapoto ca. Phaggavanti latājāti. Nattamālanti karañjaṃ. Hiṅguhiṅgujatuhiṅgusipāṭikā hiṅgujātiyoyeva. Takatakapattitakapaṇṇiyo lākhājātiyo.

263. The decision on root medicines and so on has already been stated in the explanation of the Khuddaka training rule. Therefore, here we will explain only that which was not stated before. 'Vaca' means white sweet flag. 'Nisada and nisadapota' mean a grinding stone and a small grinding stone. 'Phaggava' is a type of creeper. 'Nattamāla' is the karañja plant. Hingu, hingujatu, and hingusipāṭikā are all types of asafoetida. Taka, takapatti, and takapaṇṇī are types of lac.

Sāmuddanti samuddatīre vālukā viya santiṭṭhati. Kāḷaloṇanti pakatiloṇaṃ. Sindhavanti setavaṇṇaṃ pabbate uṭṭhahati. Ubbhidanti bhūmito aṅkuraṃ uṭṭhahati. Bilanti dabbasambhārehi saddhiṃ pacitaṃ, taṃ rattavaṇṇaṃ.

'Sea salt' is that which is found on the seashore like sand. 'Black salt' means natural salt. 'Saindhava salt' is that which is white in color and arises on a mountain. 'Efflorescent salt' is that which emerges from the ground like a sprout. 'Bila salt' is that which is cooked together with various substances; it is red in color.

264-6. Kāyo vā duggandhoti kassaci assādīnaṃ viya kāyagandho hoti, tassāpi sirīsakosumbādicuṇṇāni vā gandhacuṇṇāni vā sabbāni vaṭṭanti. Chakaṇanti gomayaṃ. Rajananippakkanti [V 0.0352] rajanakasaṭaṃ. Pākatikacuṇṇampi koṭṭetvā udakena temetvā nhāyituṃ vaṭṭati; etampi rajananippakkasaṅkhepameva gacchati.

'Or the body is foul-smelling' means that for some person there is a body odor like that of horses and so on; for such a one, powders of sirīsa, kosumbā, and so on, or fragrant powders, are all allowable. 'Chakaṇa' means cow dung. 'Cooked dye' means the dregs of dye. Even natural powder, having been pounded and moistened with water, is allowable for bathing; this also is included under the category of 'cooked dye'.

Āmakamaṃsañca [M 0.0373] khādi āmakalohitañca pivīti na taṃ bhikkhu khādi na pivi, amanusso khāditvā ca pivitvā ca pakkanto, tena vuttaṃ – “tassa so amanussikābādho paṭippassambhī”ti.

'And he ate raw flesh and drank raw blood': a monk did not eat it, did not drink it. A non-human being, having eaten and drunk it, departed. Therefore it was said by the compilers of the canon: 'For him, that non-human affliction subsided.'

Añjananti sabbasaṅgāhikavacanametaṃ. Kāḷañjananti ekā añjanajāti. Rasañjanaṃ nānāsambhārehi kataṃ. Sotañjananti [P 5.1091] nadīsotādīsu uppajjanakaṃ añjanaṃ. Geruko nāma suvaṇṇageruko. Kapallanti dīpasikhato gahitamasi. Añjanūpapiṃsanehīti añjanena saddhiṃ ekato piṃsitabbehi, na hi kiñci aññanūpapiṃsanaṃ na vaṭṭati. Candananti lohitacandanādikaṃ yaṃkiñci. Tagarādīni pākaṭāni, aññānipi nīluppalādīni vaṭṭantiyeva.

'Eye-salve' is a comprehensive term. 'Black eye-salve' is one kind of eye-salve. 'Rasañjana' is made with various ingredients. 'Sotañjana' is eye-salve that arises in river currents and so on. 'Geruka' is golden ochre. 'Soot' is ash taken from the flame of a lamp. 'With substances to be ground with eye-salve' means with things that should be ground together with the eye-salve; for indeed, any substance to be ground along with the eye-salve is allowable. 'Candana' means red sandalwood and so on, any kind whatsoever. Tagara and so on are well-known; others too, such as the blue lotus and so on, are indeed allowable.

Aṭṭhimayanti manussaṭṭhiṃ ṭhapetvā avasesaaṭṭhimayaṃ. Dantamayanti hatthidantādisabbadantamayaṃ. Visāṇamayepi akappiyaṃ nāma natthi, naḷamayādayo ekantakappiyāyeva. Salākaṭṭhāniyanti yattha salākaṃ odahanti, taṃ susiradaṇḍakaṃ vā thavikaṃ vā anujānāmīti attho. Aṃsabaddhakoti añjanitthavikāya aṃsabaddhako. Yamakanatthukaraṇinti samasotāhi dvīhi panāḷikāhi ekaṃ natthukaraṇiṃ.

'Made of bone' means made of any remaining bones, having set aside human bones. 'Made of tooth' means made of any teeth whatsoever, such as elephant tusks. In the case of 'made of horn' also, there is nothing called unallowable; those made of reed and so on are certainly allowable. 'A place for the applicator' means a place where they put the applicator; the meaning is, 'I allow a hollow stick or a small bag.' 'Shoulder-fastened' means a shoulder-strap for the eye-salve bag. 'A twin nose-implement' means one nose-implement with two tubes of equal flow.

267. Anujānāmi bhikkhave telapākanti yaṃkiñci bhesajjapakkhittaṃ sabbaṃ anuññātameva hoti. Atipakkhittamajjānīti ativiya khittamajjāni; bahuṃ majjaṃ pakkhipitvā yojitānīti attho.

267. 'I allow, O monks, oil decoctions' means that any medicine whatsoever that has been added is already permitted. 'With too much intoxicant added' means having an excessive amount of intoxicant put in; the meaning is, prepared by adding and combining a large amount of intoxicant.

Aṅgavātoti hatthapāde vāto. Sambhārasedanti nānāvidhapaṇṇabhaṅgasedaṃ. Mahāsedanti mahantaṃ sedaṃ; porisappamāṇaṃ āvāṭaṃ aṅgārānaṃ pūretvā paṃsuvālikādīhi pidahitvā tattha nānāvidhāni vātaharaṇapaṇṇāni santharitvā telamakkhitena gattena tattha nipajjitvā samparivattantena sarīraṃ sedetuṃ anujānāmīti attho. Bhaṅgodakanti nānāpaṇṇabhaṅgakuthitaṃ udakaṃ; tehi paṇṇehi ca udakena ca siñcitvā siñcitvā sedetabbo. Udakakoṭṭhakanti udakakoṭṭhe cāṭiṃ vā doṇiṃ vā uṇhodakassa pūretvā tattha pavisitvā sedakammakaraṇaṃ anujānāmīti attho.

'Limb-wind' means wind in the hands and feet. 'Herbal steam treatment' means a steam treatment with various kinds of broken leaves. 'Great steam treatment' means a major steam treatment; the meaning is, 'I allow the body to be steamed by filling a pit the size of a man with coals, covering it with soil, sand, and so on, spreading various kinds of wind-dispelling leaves upon it, and, with the body anointed with oil, lying down there and turning over and over.' 'Leaf-water' means water boiled with various broken leaves; one should be steamed by repeatedly sprinkling with those leaves and that water. 'Water chamber' means, 'I allow the performance of a steam treatment by filling a jar or a trough in a water chamber with hot water and entering it'; this is the meaning.

Pabbavāto [M 0.0374][V 0.0353] hotīti pabbe pabbe vāto vijjhati. Lohitaṃ mocetunti satthakena lohitaṃ [P 5.1092] mocetuṃ. Pajjaṃ abhisaṅkharitunti yena phālitapādā pākatikā honti; taṃ nāḷikerādīsu nānābhesajjāni pakkhipitvā pajjaṃ abhisaṅkharituṃ; pādānaṃ sappāyabhesajjaṃ pacitunti attho. Tilakakkena atthoti piṭṭhehi tilehi attho. Kabaḷikanti vaṇamukhe sattupiṇḍaṃ pakkhipituṃ. Sāsapakuḍḍenāti sāsapapiṭṭhena. Vaḍḍhamaṃsanti adhikamaṃsaṃ āṇi viya uṭṭhahati. Loṇasakkharikāya chinditunti khurena chindituṃ. Vikāsikanti telarundhanapilotikaṃ. Sabbaṃ vaṇapaṭikammanti yaṃkiñci vaṇaparikammaṃ nāma atthi; sabbaṃ anujānāmīti attho.

'Joint-wind' means wind pierces at every joint. 'To let blood' means to let blood with a small knife. 'To prepare a remedy for the feet' means that by which cracked feet become normal; to prepare that remedy for the feet by putting various medicines in a coconut and so on; the meaning is to cook a suitable medicine for the feet. 'There is a need for sesame paste' means there is a need for ground sesame. 'A poultice' means to place a lump of meal in the opening of a wound. 'With mustard powder' means with ground mustard. 'Proud flesh' means excess flesh that rises up like a peg. 'To cut with salt-gravel' means to cut with a razor. 'A plug' means a piece of cloth for stopping up oil. 'All wound treatment' means whatever is called wound care; the meaning is, 'I allow all of it.'

268. Sāmaṃ gahetvāti idaṃ na kevalaṃ sappadaṭṭhasseva, aññasmimpi daṭṭhavise sati sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ; aññesu pana kāraṇesu paṭiggahitameva vaṭṭati. Kato na puna paṭiggahetabboti sace bhūmippatto, paṭiggahetabbo; appattaṃ pana gahetuṃ vaṭṭati.

268. 'Having taken it oneself': this is not only for one who has been bitten by a snake; when there is venom from another kind of bite, it should be taken by oneself and consumed. In other cases, however, only that which has been formally received is allowable. 'What is produced should not be received again': if it has reached the ground, it should be formally received; but that which has not yet reached it is allowable to be taken by oneself.

269. Gharadinnakābādhoti vasīkaraṇapānakasamuṭṭhitarogo. Sītāloḷinti naṅgalena kasantassa phāle laggamattikaṃ udakena āloḷetvā pāyetuṃ anujānāmīti attho.

269. 'Gharadinnaka illness' refers to an illness arising from a potion that makes one compliant. 'Cool stirred-water' means, for one plowing with a plow, the fine earth stuck to the plowshare may be stirred with water and given to drink; 'I allow this' is the meaning.

Duṭṭhagahaṇikoti vipannagahaṇiko; kicchena uccāro nikkhamatīti attho. Āmisakhāranti sukkhodanaṃ jhāpetvā tāya chārikāya paggharitaṃ khārodakaṃ. Muttaharītakanti gomuttaparibhāvitaṃ harītakaṃ. Abhisannakāyoti ussannadosakāyo. Acchakañjiyanti taṇḍulodakamaṇḍo. Akaṭayusanti asiniddho muggapacitapānīyo. Kaṭākaṭanti sova dhotasiniddho. Paṭicchādanīyenāti maṃsarasena.

'Impaired digestion' means one with a malfunctioning digestive system; the meaning is that feces is passed with difficulty. 'Food-alkali' is the alkaline water that has dripped from the ash of burnt dry rice. 'Urine-myrobalan' means myrobalan infused with cow's urine. 'A congested body' means a body with excessive humors. 'Clear gruel' is the clear part of rice-washing water. 'Unprepared broth' means unrefined mung bean broth. 'Prepared and unprepared' means the same, but washed and refined. 'As a covering' means with meat broth.

Guḷādianujānanakathā

The Discourse on the Allowance of Jaggery and Other Such Items

272. Sace bhikkhave pakkāpi muggā jāyantīti pakkā muggā sacepi jāyanti, yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjitabbā. Pakkattā hi te kappiyā eva.

272. Regarding 'Monks, if even cooked mung beans sprout': if cooked mung beans should sprout, they may be consumed as is convenient. For, because they have been cooked, they are indeed allowable.

274. Antovutthanti [P 5.1093][M 0.0375] akappiyakuṭiyaṃ vutthaṃ. Sāmaṃ pakkanti ettha yaṃkiñci āmisaṃ bhikkhuno pacituṃ na vaṭṭati. Sacepissa uṇhayāguyā sulasipaṇṇāni vā siṅgiveraṃ vā loṇaṃ vā pakkhipanti, tampi cāletuṃ na vaṭṭati, “yāguṃ nibbāpemī”ti pana cāletuṃ vaṭṭati. Uttaṇḍulabhattaṃ labhitvāpi pidahituṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace pana manussā pidahitvāva denti, vaṭṭati; “bhattaṃ [V 0.0354] vā mā nibbāyatū”ti pidahituṃ vaṭṭati. Khīratakkādīsu pana sakiṃ kuthitesu aggiṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭati, punapākassa anuññātattā. Ukkapiṇḍakāpi khādantīti biḷāmūsikagodhāmaṅgusā khādanti. Damakāti vighāsādā.

274. 'Dwelling within' means having dwelt in an unallowable dwelling. Regarding 'cooking for oneself': in this context, it is not allowable for a bhikkhu to cook any kind of food. If they add basil leaves, ginger, or salt to his hot gruel, it is not allowable to stir even that. However, it is allowable to stir it thinking, 'I will cool the gruel.' Even having received rice with uncooked grains, it is not allowable to cover it. But if people give it already covered, it is allowable; or it is allowable to cover it thinking, 'May the rice not get cold.' For milk, buttermilk, and the like, once they have boiled, it is allowable to apply fire, because reheating has been allowed. Regarding '[beings who] also eat firebrand-like lumps': this means cats, mice, monitor lizards, and mongooses eat them. 'Tamers' means eaters of leftovers.

276. Tato nīhaṭanti yattha nimantitā bhuñjanti, tato nīhaṭaṃ.

276. 'Brought from there' means brought from the place where, having been invited, they eat.

278. Vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhanti vane ceva paduminigacche ca jātaṃ. Abījanti taruṇaphalaṃ, yassa bījaṃ na aṅkuraṃ janeti. Nibbaṭṭabījanti bījaṃ nibbaṭṭetvā apanetvā paribhuñjitabbakaṃ ambapanasādi.

278. 'Grown in the forest' and 'grown in a pond' means that which is grown in the forest and in a lotus thicket. 'Seedless' means young fruit whose seed does not produce a sprout. 'With the seed removed' means that which is to be consumed after having extracted and removed the seed, such as mango, jackfruit, and other such fruits.

279. Duropayo vaṇoti dukkhena ruhati, dukkhena pākatiko hotīti attho. Dupparihāraṃ satthanti sambādhe dukkhena satthaṃ parihareyyaṃ. Satthakammaṃ vā vatthikammaṃ vāti yathāparicchinne okāse yena kenaci satthena vā sūciyā vā kaṇṭakena vā sattikāya vā pāsāṇasakkhalikāya vā nakhena vā chindanaṃ vā phālanaṃ vā vijjhanaṃ vā lekhanaṃ vā na kātabbaṃ; sabbañhetaṃ satthakammameva hoti. Yena kenaci pana cammena vā vatthena vā vatthipīḷanampi na kātabbaṃ; sabbañhetaṃ vatthikammameva hoti. Ettha ca sambādhassa sāmantā dvaṅgulāti idaṃ satthakammaṃyeva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vatthikammaṃ pana sambādheyeva [P 5.1094] paṭikkhittaṃ. Tattha pana khāraṃ ādātuṃ yena kenaci rajjukena vā bandhituṃ vaṭṭati. Yadi tena chijjati, succhinnaṃ. Aṇḍavuḍḍhirogepi satthakammaṃ na vaṭṭati, tasmā aṇḍaṃ phāletvā bījāni uddharitvā “arogaṃ karissāmī”ti na kattabbaṃ. Aggitāpanabhesajjālimpanesu pana paṭikkhepo natthi. Vaccamagge bhesajjamakkhitā ādānavaṭṭi vā veḷunāḷikā vā vaṭṭati, yāya khārakammaṃ vā karonti, telaṃ vā pavesenti.

279. 'A wound that is difficult to heal' means it heals with difficulty; the meaning is that it returns to its natural state with difficulty. 'A knife hard to handle' means in a confined place, one would handle a knife with difficulty. Regarding 'surgery or enema treatment': in a designated area, one should not perform cutting, splitting, piercing, or scraping with any kind of knife, needle, thorn, small spear, stone chip, or nail; for all this is indeed surgery. Furthermore, one should not perform the pressing of a boil with any kind of hide or cloth; for all this is indeed enema treatment. And here, the phrase 'two finger-breadths around the confined area' is said in reference to surgery only. Enema treatment, however, is prohibited only in the confined area itself. But there, it is allowable to apply an alkaline solution or to bind with any kind of small cord. If it is cut by that, it is well cut. In the case of a disease of a swollen testicle, surgery is not allowable; therefore, one should not act thinking, 'I will make him well,' by splitting the scrotum and extracting the testicles. However, there is no prohibition on heating with fire and anointing with medicine. In the anal passage, a suppository smeared with medicine is allowable, as is a bamboo tube by which they perform the alkaline treatment or insert oil.

280. Pavattamaṃsanti [M 0.0376] matassa maṃsaṃ. Māghātoti taṃ divasaṃ na labbhā kenaci kiñci jīvitā voropetuṃ. Potthanikanti maṃsacchedanasatthakaṃ vuccati. Kimpimāyāti kimpi imāya. Na bhagavā ussahatīti na bhagavā sakkoti. Yatra hi nāmāti yasmā nāma. Paṭivekkhīti vīmaṃsi; paṭipucchīti vuttaṃ hoti. Appaṭivekkhitvāti appaṭipucchitvā. Sace pana asukamaṃsanti jānāti, paṭipucchanakiccaṃ natthi, ajānantena pana pucchitvāva khāditabbaṃ.

280. 'Readily available meat' means the flesh of a dead animal. 'Let there be no slaughter' means on that day, it is not permitted that anyone should deprive any being of life. 'A butcher's knife' is the term for a small knife for cutting flesh. 'What of this?' is the meaning of `kimpimāya`. 'The Blessed One is not able' is the meaning of `na bhagavā ussahati`. 'Since indeed' is the meaning of `yatra hi nāma`. 'He investigated' (`paṭivekkhīti`) means he examined; it is said to mean 'he asked in return' (`paṭipucchi`). 'Without having investigated' (`appaṭivekkhitvā`) means without having asked. But if one knows, "It is such-and-such meat," there is no need to ask; but one who does not know should eat only after having asked.

Hatthimaṃsādipaṭikkhepakathā

Discourse on the Prohibition of Elephant Flesh, etc.

281. Sunakhamaṃsanti [V 0.0355] ettha araññakokā nāma sunakhasadisā honti, tesaṃ maṃsaṃ vaṭṭati. Yo pana gāmasunakhiyā vā kokena kokasunakhiyā vā gāmasunakhena saṃyogā uppanno, tassa maṃsaṃ na vaṭṭati, so hi ubhayaṃ bhajatīti. Ahimaṃsanti kassaci apādakassa dīghajātikassa maṃsaṃ na vaṭṭati. Sīhamaṃsādīni pākaṭāneva.

281. Herein, regarding 'dog flesh': those called 'forest wolves' (araññakokā) are similar to domestic dogs, and their flesh is permissible. However, the flesh of one born from the union of a village bitch with a wolf, or of a she-wolf with a village dog, is not permissible, for it partakes of both. Regarding 'snake flesh': the flesh of any legless, long-bodied creature is not permissible. The cases of lion flesh and so forth are self-evident.

Ettha ca manussamaṃsaṃ sajātitāya paṭikkhittaṃ, hatthiassamaṃsaṃ rājaṅgatāya, sunakhamaṃsañca ahimaṃsañca paṭikūlatāya, sīhamaṃsādīni pañca attano anupaddavatthāyāti. Imesaṃ manussādīnaṃ dasannaṃ maṃsampi aṭṭhipi lohitampi cammampi lomampi sabbaṃ na vaṭṭati, yaṃkiñci ñatvā vā añatvā vā khādantassa āpattiyeva. Yadā jānāti, tadā desetabbā. “Apucchitvā khādissāmī”ti gaṇhato paṭiggahaṇe dukkaṭaṃ, “pucchitvā khādissāmī”ti gaṇhato anāpatti. Uddissa kataṃ pana jānitvā khādantasseva āpatti, pacchā jānanto āpattiyā na kāretabboti.

And herein, human flesh is prohibited on account of being of the same species; elephant and horse flesh on account of being royal appurtenances; dog flesh and snake flesh on account of being repulsive; and the five, lion flesh and so forth, for the sake of one's own safety from danger. Of these ten—humans and so forth—their flesh, bones, blood, skin, and hair are all impermissible. For one who eats any of these, whether knowingly or unknowingly, there is an offense. When one comes to know, it must be confessed. For one who takes it thinking, 'I will eat without asking,' there is a dukkaṭa offense in the act of receiving. For one who takes it thinking, 'I will eat after asking,' there is no offense. However, an offense is incurred only by one who eats what was prepared specifically for them, knowing it to be so. One who finds out afterwards should not be charged with an offense.

Yāgumadhugoḷakādikathā

Discourse on Gruel, Honey-Balls, etc.

282. Ekattakoti [P 5.1095] ekako, natthi me dutiyoti attho. Pahūtaṃ yāguñca madhugoḷakañca paṭiyādāpetvāti so kira satasahassaṃ vayaṃ katvā paṭiyādāpesi. Anumodanāgāthāpariyosāne “patthayataṃ icchata”nti padānaṃ “alameva dātu”nti iminā sambandho. Sace pana “patthayatā icchatā”ti pāṭho atthi, soyeva gahetabbo.

282. The meaning of 'ekattako' is 'alone; there is no second to me.' Regarding 'having had abundant gruel and honey-balls prepared,' it is said that he had them prepared after making an expenditure of one hundred thousand. At the conclusion of the verses of appreciation, the words 'patthayataṃ icchataṃ' are connected with 'alameva dātuṃ.' If, however, the reading 'patthayatā icchatā' exists, that very one should be adopted.

283. Bhojjayāgunti yā pavāraṇaṃ janeti. Yadaggenāti yaṃ ādiṃ katvā. Saggā te āraddhāti sagganibbattakapuññaṃ upacitanti attho. Yathādhammo [M 0.0377] kāretabboti paramparabhojanena kāretabbo, bhojjayāguyā hi pavāraṇā hotīti.

283. Regarding 'edible gruel' (bhojjayāgu): it is that which gives rise to the pavāraṇā (expression of satisfaction). Regarding 'yadaggena': it means 'having made which the beginning.' Regarding 'saggā te āraddhā': the meaning is 'merit that leads to rebirth in heaven has been accumulated.' Regarding 'one should be dealt with according to the rule' (yathādhammo kāretabbo): one should be dealt with under the training rule on consecutive eating (paramparabhojana), because the pavāraṇā occurs on account of edible gruel.

284. Nāhaṃ taṃ kaccānāti tasmiṃ kira avasiṭṭhaguḷe devatā sukhumojaṃ pakkhipiṃsu, sā aññesaṃ pariṇāmaṃ na gacchati, tasmā evamāha. Gilānassa guḷanti tathārūpena byādhinā gilānassa pacchābhattaṃ guḷaṃ anujānāmīti attho.

284. Regarding 'I do not, Kaccāna': it is said that deities infused a subtle nutritive essence into that remaining lump of molasses. That essence is not digested in the bodies of others; therefore, he spoke thus. Regarding 'molasses for the sick': the meaning is, 'For one who is sick with a disease of such a nature, I allow molasses after the mealtime.'

Pāṭaligāmavatthukathā

The Story of Pāṭaligāma

285. Sabbasantharinti [V 0.0356] yathā sabbaṃ santhataṃ hoti, evaṃ.

285. Completely spread: In such a way that everything is spread.

286. Sunidhavassakārāti sunidho ca vassakāro ca dve brāhmaṇā magadharañño mahāmattā mahāmaccā. Vajjīnaṃ paṭibāhāyāti vajjirājakulānaṃ āyamukhapacchindanatthaṃ. Vatthūnīti gharavatthūni. Cittāni namanti nivesanāni māpetunti tā kira devatā vatthuvijjāpāṭhakānaṃ sarīre adhimuccitvā evaṃ cittāni nāmenti. Kasmā? Amhākaṃ yathānurūpaṃ sakkāraṃ karissantīti attho. Tāvatiṃsehīti loke kira sakkaṃ devarājānaṃ vissakammañca upādāya tāvatiṃsā paṇḍitāti saddo abbhuggato, tenevāha tāvatiṃsehīti, tāvatiṃsehi saddhiṃ mantetvā viya māpentīti attho. Yāvatā ariyaṃ āyatananti yattakaṃ ariyamanussānaṃ osaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ nāma atthi. Yāvatā vaṇippathoti [P 5.1096] yattakaṃ vāṇijānaṃ ābhatabhaṇḍassa rāsivaseneva kayavikkayaṭṭhānaṃ nāma atthi. Idaṃ agganagaranti tesaṃ ariyāyatanavaṇippathānaṃ idaṃ agganagaraṃ bhavissati. Puṭabhedananti puṭabhedanaṭṭhānaṃ mocanaṭṭhānanti vuttaṃ hoti. Aggito vātiādīsu samuccayattho vā saddo. Tatra hi ekassa koṭṭhāsassa aggito, ekassa udakato, ekassa abbhantarato, aññamaññabhedā antarāyo bhavissati. Uḷumpanti pāragamanatthāya āṇiyo ākoṭetvā kataṃ. Kullanti valliādīhi bandhitvā kataṃ.

286. Sunidha and Vassakāra: Sunidha and Vassakāra were two brahmin great ministers of the king of Magadha. 'To obstruct the Vajjis' means for the purpose of cutting off the source of revenue of the Vajji royal families. 'Sites' means dwelling sites. 'They incline their minds, they have residences built': It is said that deities, having possessed the bodies of experts in site-lore, thus incline their minds. Why? With the thought, 'They will do us fitting honor'; this is the meaning. 'By the Tāvatiṃsa gods': It is said that in the world, the fame 'the Tāvatiṃsa are wise' has arisen by taking Sakka, king of the gods, and Vissakamma as examples. For that reason, the Blessed One said, 'by the Tāvatiṃsa gods.' The meaning is that they have them built as if having consulted with the Tāvatiṃsa gods. 'As far as the noble sphere' means as much as there is a place of resort for noble people. 'As far as the trade route' means as much as there is a place for buying and selling for merchants, characterized by heaps of imported goods. 'This will be the chief city' means this will become the chief city of those noble spheres and trade routes. 'Bundle-breaking' means a place for breaking open bundles, a place for unloading; so it is said. In 'from fire, or...' and so on, the word 'or' has the sense of combination. For there, danger will arise for one part from fire, for another from water, and for another from internal mutual division. 'A raft (uḷumpa)' is something made by hammering in pegs for the purpose of going to the far shore. 'A raft (kulla)' is something made by binding with vines and the like.

Aṇṇavanti sabbantimena paricchedena yojanamattaṃ gambhīrassa ca puthullassa ca udakaṭṭhānassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Saranti idha nadī adhippetā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ye [M 0.0378] gambhīraṃ vitthataṃ taṇhāsaraṃ taranti, te ariyamaggasaṅkhātaṃ setuṃ katvāna visajja pallalāni anāmasitvāva udakabharitāni ninnaṭṭhānāni; ayaṃ pana idaṃ appamattakaṃ udakaṃ uttaritukāmopi kullañhi parijano bandhati, buddhā pana buddhasāvakā ca vinā eva kullena tiṇṇā medhāvino janāti.

`Aṇṇava` (ocean): This is a designation for a body of water that, by its ultimate definition, is a yojana in measure, and is both deep and wide. By `sara` (lake), a river is intended here. This is what is said: Those who cross the deep and wide river of craving, they, having made the bridge called the Noble Path and abandoning the mire, cross without even touching the low-lying places filled with water. This company of people, however, though wishing to cross this small amount of water, binds together a raft. But the wise people—the Buddhas and the disciples of the Buddha—have crossed without a raft at all.

287. Ananubodhāti abujjhanena. Sandhāvitanti bhavato bhavaṃ gamanavasena sandhāvitaṃ. Saṃsaritanti punappunaṃ gamanavasena saṃsaritaṃ. Mamañceva tumhākañcāti mayā ca tumhehi ca. Atha vā sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritanti sandhāvanaṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ mamañceva tumhākañca ahosīti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Saṃsitanti saṃsaritaṃ.
