Regarding 'He should be attended to by the Sangha': for whom there are no preceptor and so on in that monastery, who is a visiting monk, a solitary wandering monk—he is the burden of the Sangha. Therefore, he should be attended to by the Sangha. If they do not attend, there is an offense for the entire Sangha. However, among those who are looking after him by taking turns, whoever does not look after him on his own turn, for him alone there is an offense. Even the Elder of the Sangha is not exempt from his turn. If the entire Sangha takes on the burden for one person, or if one monk endowed with the observances looks after him, thinking, 'I myself will look after him,' the Sangha is freed from the offense.

366. Abhikkamantaṃ vā abhikkamatītiādīsu vaḍḍhantaṃ vā ābādhaṃ “idaṃ nāma me paribhuñjantassa vaḍḍhati, idaṃ paribhuñjantassa parihāyati, idaṃ paribhuñjantassa tiṭṭhatī”ti yathābhūtaṃ nāvikarotīti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Nālanti na patirūpo, na yutto upaṭṭhātuṃ. Bhesajjaṃ saṃvidhātunti bhesajjaṃ yojetuṃ asamattho hoti. Āmisantaroti āmisaṃ assa antaranti āmisantaro. Antaranti kāraṇaṃ vuccati; āmisakāraṇā yāgubhattapattacīvarāni patthento upaṭṭhātīti attho.

366. In such phrases as 'advancing or it advances,' regarding an increasing illness, the meaning should be understood thus: he does not make it clear as it truly is that 'for me, when consuming this particular thing, the illness increases; when consuming this, it decreases; when consuming this, it stays the same.' 'Not able' means not suitable, not fit to attend. 'To prepare medicine' means he is unable to compound medicine. 'Having a material interior' means material gain is his motive, therefore he is called `āmisantaro`. 'Interior' is a term for 'reason'; the meaning is that he attends while desiring gruel, rice, a bowl, and robes for the reason of material gain.

Matasantakakathā

Discourse on the Property of the Deceased

367. Kālaṅkateti [V 0.0390] kālakiriyāya. Gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātunti ettha anantaraṃ vuttāya kammavācāya dinnampi apaloketvā dinnampi dinnameva hoti, vaṭṭati.

367. Regarding `Kālaṅkata` (passed away), this refers to the act of dying. In the context of 'it should be given to the attendants of the sick,' whether it is given by a formal act (`kammavācā`) spoken of immediately after, or given by an act of announcement (`apalokana`), it is considered properly given; it is allowable.

369. Yaṃ tattha lahubhaṇḍaṃ yaṃ tattha garubhaṇḍanti ettha lahubhaṇḍagarubhaṇḍānaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ parato vaṇṇayissāma. Gilānupaṭṭhākalābhe pana ayaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya vinicchayo –

369. Regarding the phrase ‘whatever light goods are there, whatever heavy goods are there,’ the distinction between light and heavy goods will be explained later. But concerning the gain for attendants of the sick, this is the decision from the outset:

Sace sakale bhikkhusaṅghe upaṭṭhahante kālaṃ karoti, sabbepi sāmikā. Atha ekaccehi vāre kate ekaccehi akateyeva kālaṃ karoti, tattha ekacce ācariyā vadanti – “sabbepi attano vāre sampatte kareyyuṃ, tasmā sabbepi sāmino”ti. Ekacce vadanti – “yehi jaggito te eva labhanti, itare na labhantī”ti. Sāmaṇere kālaṅkate sace cīvaraṃ atthi, gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātabbaṃ. No ce atthi yaṃ atthi, taṃ dātabbaṃ. Aññasmiṃ parikkhāre sati cīvarabhāgaṃ katvā dātabbaṃ.

If he passes away while the entire community of monks is attending to him, then all are owners. But if he passes away when some have performed their turn and some have not yet performed it, some teachers say: ‘All would attend when their turn arrives, therefore all are owners.’ Others say: ‘Only those who attended to him receive a share; the others do not.’ When a novice passes away, if there is a robe, it should be given to the attendants of the sick. If there is no robe, whatever there is should be given. If there are other requisites, a portion equivalent to a robe should be made and given.

Bhikkhu [M 0.0415] ca sāmaṇero ca sace samaṃ upaṭṭhahiṃsu, samako bhāgo dātabbo. Atha sāmaṇerova upaṭṭhahati, bhikkhussa saṃvidahanamattameva hoti, sāmaṇerassa jeṭṭhakabhāgo dātabbo. Sace sāmaṇero bhikkhunā ānītaudakena yāguṃ pacitvā paṭiggāhāpanamattameva karoti, bhikkhu upaṭṭhahati, bhikkhussa jeṭṭhakabhāgo dātabbo.

If a bhikkhu and a novice attended equally, an equal share should be given. But if only the novice attends, and the bhikkhu's part is merely to manage things, the larger share should be given to the novice. If a novice cooks gruel with water brought by a bhikkhu and only does as much as having it be received, while the bhikkhu attends, the larger share should be given to the bhikkhu.

Bahū bhikkhū samaggā hutvā upaṭṭhahanti, sabbesaṃ samako bhāgo dātabbo. Yo panettha [P 5.1134] visesena upaṭṭhahati, tassa viseso kātabbo. Yena pana ekadivasampi gilānupaṭṭhākavasena yāgubhattaṃ vā pacitvā dinnaṃ, nahānaṃ vā paṭiyāditaṃ, sopi gilānupaṭṭhākova. Yo samīpaṃ anāgantvā bhesajjataṇḍulādīni peseti, ayaṃ gilānupaṭṭhāko na hoti. Yo pariyesitvā gāhāpetvā āgacchati, ayaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākova.

If many bhikkhus attend in harmony, an equal share should be given to all. Whoever among them attends with special effort, a special portion should be made for them. Furthermore, one by whom, even for a single day, in the capacity of an attendant to the sick, gruel or food has been cooked and given, or a bath has been prepared, is also an attendant of the sick. One who, without coming near, sends medicine, rice, and so on, is not an attendant of the sick. One who, having searched for and procured items, comes, is indeed an attendant of the sick.

Eko vattasīsena jaggati; eko paccāsāya, matakāle ubhopi paccāsīsanti, ubhinnampi dātabbaṃ. Eko upaṭṭhahitvā gilānassa vā kammena attano vā kammena katthaci gato “puna āgantvā jaggissāmī”ti, etassapi dātabbaṃ. Eko ciraṃ upaṭṭhahitvā “idāni na [V 0.0391] sakkomī”ti dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā gacchati, sacepi taṃdivasameva gilāno kālaṃkaroti, upaṭṭhākabhāgo na dātabbo.

One attends with duty as the main principle; another attends with expectation. If at the time of death both expect a share, it should be given to both. One who, having attended, has gone somewhere on the sick person's business or on their own business, thinking, ‘I will return and attend,’ a share should also be given to this one. One who, having attended for a long time, gives up the responsibility and leaves, thinking, ‘Now I am unable,’—even if the sick person dies that very day, the attendant’s share should not be given.

Gilānupaṭṭhāko nāma gihi vā hotu pabbajito vā, antamaso mātugāmopi, sabbe bhāgaṃ labhanti. Sace tassa bhikkhuno pattacīvaramattameva hoti, aññaṃ natthi; sabbaṃ gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃyeva dātabbaṃ. Sacepi sahassaṃ agghati, aññaṃ pana bahumpi parikkhāraṃ te na labhanti; saṅghasseva hoti. Avasesaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ bahukañceva mahagghañca, ticīvaraṃ appagghaṃ; tato gahetvā ticīvaraparikkhāro dātabbo. Sabbañcetaṃ saṅghikatova labbhati.

An attendant of the sick—be it a layperson, a monastic, or even, at the very least, a woman—all receive a share. If that bhikkhu has only a bowl and robes and nothing else, all of it should be given only to the attendants of the sick, even if it is worth a thousand. However, they do not receive other requisites, even if there are many; it becomes the property of the Sangha. If the remaining goods are abundant and of great value, while the three robes are of little value, then having taken from those goods, the requisites that accompany the three robes should be given. And all this is received from the Sangha's property.

Sace pana so jīvamānoyeva sabbaṃ attano parikkhāraṃ nissajjitvā kassaci adāsi, koci vā vissāsaṃ aggahesi, yassa dinnaṃ, yena ca gahitaṃ, tasseva hoti. Tassa ruciyā eva gilānupaṭṭhākā labhanti, aññesaṃ adatvā dūre ṭhapitaparikkhārāpi tattha tattha saṅghasseva honti. Dvinnaṃ santakaṃ hoti avibhattaṃ, ekasmiṃ kālaṅkate itaro sāmī[M 0.0416]. Bahūnampi santake eseva nayo. Sabbesu matesu saṅghikaṃ hoti. Sacepi avibhajitvā saddhivihārikādīnaṃ denti adinnameva hoti. Vibhajitvā dinnaṃ pana sudinnaṃ. Taṃ tesu matesupi saddhivihārikādīnaṃyeva hoti, na saṅghassa.

Furthermore, if he, while still alive, relinquished all his own requisites and gave them to someone, or if someone took them based on trust, it belongs to the one to whom it was given and by whom it was taken. The attendants of the sick receive a share only by the wish of that new owner. Requisites placed at a distance, not having been given to others, belong to the Saṅgha of that particular place. If the property of two bhikkhus is undivided, when one passes away, the other is the owner. This same principle applies to the property of many. When all have passed away, it becomes Saṅgha property. Even if they give it to their co-residents and others without having divided it, it is not considered given. But what is given after being divided is well-given. That property belongs only to the co-residents and others even after those original owners have passed away; it does not belong to the Saṅgha.

Kusacīrādipaṭikkhepakathā

The Discussion on the Rejection of Grass-Cloth and the Like

371. Kusacīrādīsu [P 5.1135] akkanāḷanti akkanāḷamayaṃ. Potthakoti makacimayo vuccati. Sesāni paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttāni. Tesu potthake eva dukkaṭaṃ. Sesesu thullaccayānīti. Akkadussakadalidussaerakadussāni pana potthakagatikāneva.

371. Among grass-cloth and the like, 'akkanāḷa' refers to a robe made from the stalk of the Calotropis gigantea plant. 'Potthaka' is said to be a robe made from makaci bark-fiber. The remaining terms have been explained in the commentary on the first Pārājika. Among these, only on account of a potthaka robe is there a dukkaṭa offense. On account of the remaining ones, there are thullaccaya offenses. Furthermore, cloth made from akka, kadali, or eraka has the same nature as potthaka cloth.

372. Sabbanīlakādīni rajanaṃ dhovitvā puna rajitvā dhāretabbāni. Na sakkā ce honti dhovituṃ, paccattharaṇāni vā kātabbāni. Dupaṭṭacīvarassa vā majjhe dātabbāni. Tesaṃ vaṇṇanānattaṃ upāhanāsu vuttanayameva. Acchinnadasadīghadasāni dasā chinditvā dhāretabbāni. Kañcukaṃ labhitvā phāletvā rajitvā paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Veṭhanepi eseva nayo. Tirīṭakaṃ pana rukkhachallimayaṃ; taṃ pādapuñchanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati.

372. Robes that are entirely blue and the like should be washed to remove the dye, then re-dyed and worn. If they cannot be washed, they should be made into spread-coverings or placed in the middle of a double-layered robe. The diversity of their colors is just according to the method explained in the section on footwear. Robes with uncut fringes or long fringes should be worn after cutting the fringes. Having obtained a jacket, it is allowable to split it, dye it, and use it. In the case of a head-wrap, this is the same method. A tirīṭaka robe, however, is made of tree bark; it is allowable to make it into a foot-wiping cloth.

374. Patirūpe gāhaketi sace koci bhikkhu “ahaṃ tassa gaṇhāmī”ti gaṇhāti, dātabbanti [V 0.0392] attho. Evametesu tevīsatiyā puggalesu soḷasa janā na labhanti, satta janā labhantīti.

374. Regarding 'a suitable recipient': if some monk takes it, saying, 'I will take it for him,' it should be given. This is the meaning. Thus, among these twenty-three persons, sixteen persons do not receive, and seven persons do receive.

Saṅghebhinnecīvaruppādakathā

The Account of the Arising of Robes when the Saṅgha is Split

376. Saṅgho bhijjatīti bhijjitvā kosambakabhikkhū viya dve koṭṭhāsā honti. Ekasmiṃ pakkheti ekasmiṃ koṭṭhāse dakkhiṇodakañca gandhādīni ca denti, ekasmiṃ cīvarāni. Saṅghassevetanti sakalassa saṅghassa dvinnampi koṭṭhāsānaṃ etaṃ hoti, ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā dvīhipi pakkhehi ekato bhājetabbaṃ. Pakkhassevetanti evaṃ dinne yassa koṭṭhāsassa udakaṃ dinnaṃ, tassa udakameva hoti; yassa cīvaraṃ dinnaṃ, tasseva cīvaraṃ. Yattha pana dakkhiṇodakaṃ pamāṇaṃ hoti, tattha eko pakkho dakkhiṇodakassa [M 0.0417] laddhattā cīvarāni labhati, eko cīvarānameva laddhattāti ubhohipi ekato hutvā yathāvuḍḍhaṃ bhājetabbaṃ. Idaṃ kira parasamudde lakkhaṇanti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmiṃyeva pakkheti ettha pana itaro pakkho anissaroyeva. Cīvarapesanavatthūni pākaṭāneva.

376. Regarding 'the Saṅgha is split': having been split, like the monks of Kosambī, they become two factions. Regarding 'in one faction': in one faction they offer dedication-water and perfumes and the like, and in another, they offer robes. Regarding 'it is for the Saṅgha': this belongs to the entire Saṅgha, to both factions; having struck a bell, it should be divided together by both factions. Regarding 'it is for the faction': when given thus, to whichever faction the water was given, it is only their water; to whichever faction the robe-cloth was given, it is only their robe-cloth. But where dedication-water is the standard, one faction receives robes on account of having received the dedication-water, and another on account of having received the robes themselves; therefore both factions should come together and divide according to seniority. This, it is said, is the practice on the other shore of the ocean, as stated in the Mahā-aṭṭhakathā. Here, however, regarding 'in that very faction', the other faction has no authority. The matters concerning the sending of robe-cloth are evident.

Aṭṭhacīvaramātikākathā

The Account of the Eight Categories for Robes

379. Idāni ādito paṭṭhāya vuttacīvarānaṃ paṭilābhakhettaṃ dassetuṃ [P 5.1136] “aṭṭhimā bhikkhave mātikā”tiādimāha. Sīmāya detītiādi puggalādhiṭṭhānanayena vuttaṃ. Ettha pana sīmāya dānaṃ ekā mātikā, katikāya dānaṃ dutiyā…pe… puggalassa dānaṃ aṭṭhamā. Tattha sīmāya dammīti evaṃ sīmaṃ parāmasitvā dento sīmāya deti nāma. Esa nayo sabbattha.

379. Now, starting from the beginning, in order to show the field for acquiring the aforementioned robes, the Blessed One said the passage beginning with, ‘Monks, these are the eight categories.’ The passage beginning with ‘One gives to the boundary’ is stated according to the method of determination by an individual. Here, however, giving to the boundary is one category; giving to an agreement is the second... and so on... giving to an individual is the eighth. Therein, one who gives having specified the boundary, saying, ‘I give to the boundary,’ is called ‘one who gives to the boundary.’ This is the method in all cases.

Sīmāya deti, yāvatikā bhikkhū antosīmagatā tehi bhājetabbantiādimhi pana mātikāniddese sīmāya detīti ettha tāva khaṇḍasīmā, upacārasīmā, samānasaṃvāsasīmā, avippavāsasīmā, lābhasīmā, gāmasīmā, nigamasīmā, nagarasīmā, abbhantarasīmā, udakukkhepasīmā, janapadasīmā, raṭṭhasīmā, rajjasīmā, dīpasīmā, cakkavāḷasīmāti pannarasa sīmā veditabbā.

However, in the detailed explanation of the categories beginning with, ‘One gives to the boundary; it should be divided by as many monks as are within the boundary,’ with regard to this category ‘one gives to the boundary,’ fifteen boundaries should first be known: a partial boundary, a vicinity boundary, a shared-residence boundary, a non-separation boundary, a gains boundary, a village boundary, a market-town boundary, a city boundary, an inner boundary, a water-splash boundary, a district boundary, a country boundary, a kingdom boundary, an island boundary, and a world-sphere boundary.

Tattha khaṇḍasīmā sīmākathāyaṃ vuttāva. Upacārasīmā parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepena aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānena paricchinnā hoti. Apica bhikkhūnaṃ dhuvasannipātaṭṭhānato [V 0.0393] vā pariyante ṭhitabhojanasālato vā nibaddhavasanakaāvāsato vā thāmamajjhimassa purisassa dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃ anto upacārasīmā veditabbā, sā pana āvāsesu vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhati, parihāyantesu parihāyati. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana “bhikkhūsupi vaḍḍhantesu vaḍḍhatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tasmā sace vihāre sannipatitabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ ekābaddhā hutvā yojanasatampi pūretvā nisīdanti, yojanasatampi upacārasīmāva hoti, sabbesaṃ lābho pāpuṇāti. Samānasaṃvāsaavippavāsasīmādvayampi vuttameva.

Therein, the partial boundary has already been stated in the Discussion on Boundaries. The vicinity boundary is defined by the enclosure of an enclosed monastery, or by the place suitable for an enclosure for an unenclosed one. Furthermore, the vicinity boundary should be known as the area within two clod-throws of a man of medium strength, measured from the monks' regular meeting place, or from the dining hall situated at the edge, or from a permanent dwelling. And that boundary expands when the dwellings increase and contracts when they decrease. However, in the Mahāpaccarī it is said, ‘It also expands when the monks increase.’ Therefore, if they sit, having become a single contiguous group with the monks assembled in the monastery and filling up even a hundred yojanas, the vicinity boundary becomes even a hundred yojanas, and the gain reaches all of them. The pair of boundaries—the shared-residence and non-separation boundaries—have also been stated.

Lābhasīmā [M 0.0418] nāma neva sammāsambuddhena anuññātā, na dhammasaṅgāhakattherehi ṭhapitā; apica kho rājarājamahāmattā vihāraṃ kāretvā gāvutaṃ vā aḍḍhayojanaṃ vā yojanaṃ vā samantato paricchinditvā “ayaṃ amhākaṃ vihārassa lābhasīmā”ti nāmalikhitake thambhe nikhaṇitvā “yaṃ etthantare uppajjati, sabbaṃ taṃ amhākaṃ vihārassa demā”ti sīmaṃ ṭhapenti, ayaṃ lābhasīmā nāma. Gāmanigamanagaraabbhantaraudakukkhepasīmāpi vuttā eva. Janapadasīmā nāma – kāsikosalaraṭṭhādīnaṃ anto bahū janapadā honti, tattha [P 5.1137] ekeko janapadaparicchedo janapadasīmā. Raṭṭhasīmā nāma kāsikosalādiraṭṭhaparicchedo. Rajjasīmā nāma “coḷabhogo keraḷabhogo”ti evaṃ ekekassa rañño āṇāpavattiṭṭhānaṃ. Dīpasīmā nāma samuddantena paricchinnamahādīpā ca antaradīpā ca. Cakkavāḷasīmā nāma cakkavāḷapabbateneva paricchinnā.

What is called the gains-boundary was not permitted by the Perfectly Enlightened One, nor was it established by the Elder Compilers of the Dhamma. But rather, kings and royal ministers, having had a monastery built, demarcate a gāvuta, or half a yojana, or a yojana all around it, and having erected pillars inscribed with the name, declaring, ‘This is the gains-boundary of our monastery,’ they establish the boundary, saying, ‘Whatever arises within this area, we give it all to our monastery.’ This is called the gains-boundary. The village, market-town, city, inner, and water-splash boundaries have also been stated. The district-boundary is: within countries such as Kāsi and Kosala there are many districts; therein, the demarcation of each single district is the district-boundary. The country-boundary is the demarcation of countries such as Kāsi and Kosala. The kingdom-boundary is the place where the command of each king prevails, such as ‘the domain of the Coḷas,’ ‘the domain of the Keraḷas.’ The island-boundary is the great islands and the intermediate islands, demarcated by the ocean's edge. The world-sphere-boundary is that which is demarcated by the Cakkavāḷa mountain itself.

Evametāsu sīmāsu khaṇḍasīmāya kenaci kammena sannipatitaṃ saṅghaṃ disvā “ettheva sīmāya saṅghassa demī”ti vutte yāvatikā bhikkhū antokhaṇḍasīmagatā, tehi bhājetabbaṃ. Tesaṃyeva hi taṃ pāpuṇāti. Aññesaṃ sīmantarikāya vā upacārasīmāya vā ṭhitānampi na pāpuṇāti. Khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhite pana rukkhe vā pabbate vā ṭhitassa heṭṭhā vā pathavīvemajjhagatassa pāpuṇātiyeva. “Imissā upacārasīmāya saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnaṃ pana khaṇḍasīmāsīmantarikāsu ṭhitānampi pāpuṇāti. “Samānasaṃvāsasīmāya dammī”ti dinnaṃ pana khaṇḍasīmāsīmantarikāsu ṭhitānaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Avippavāsasīmālābhasīmāsu dinnaṃ tāsu sīmāsu antogatānaṃ pāpuṇāti. Gāmasīmādīsu dinnaṃ tāsaṃ sīmānaṃ abbhantare baddhasīmāya ṭhitānampi pāpuṇāti. Abbhantarasīmāudakukkhepasīmāsu dinnaṃ tattha antogatānaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Janapadaraṭṭharajjadīpacakkavāḷasīmāsupi gāmasīmādīsu vuttasadisoyeva vinicchayo.

Thus, among these boundaries, in a partial-boundary, having seen the Saṅgha assembled for some formal act, when it is said, ‘I give to the Saṅgha in this very boundary,’ it should be divided by as many monks as are within the partial-boundary. For it reaches only them. It does not reach others, even those standing in the intermediate-boundary or the vicinity-boundary. However, it certainly reaches one standing on a tree or a mountain situated in the partial-boundary, or one who has gone into the middle of the earth below. However, what is given with the words, ‘I give to the Saṅgha in this vicinity-boundary,’ reaches even those standing in the partial and intermediate boundaries. However, what is given with the words, ‘I give in the shared-residence-boundary,’ does not reach those standing in the partial and intermediate boundaries. What is given in the non-separation and gains boundaries reaches those who are within those boundaries. What is given in the village-boundaries and so on reaches even those standing in a consecrated boundary within those boundaries. What is given in the inner and water-splash boundaries reaches only those who are within them. Also in the district, country, kingdom, island, and world-sphere boundaries, the ruling is just like that stated for the village-boundaries and so on.

Sace pana jambudīpe ṭhito “tambapaṇṇidīpe saṅghassa dammī”ti deti, tambapaṇṇidīpato ekopi [V 0.0394] gantvā sabbesaṃ gaṇhituṃ labhati. Sacepi tatreva eko sabhāgabhikkhu sabhāgānaṃ bhāgaṃ gaṇhāti, na vāretabbo. Evaṃ tāva yo sīmaṃ parāmasitvā deti, tassa dāne vinicchayo veditabbo.

But if one standing in Jambudīpa gives, saying, ‘I give to the Saṅgha in Tambapaṇṇidīpa,’ even one monk may go from Tambapaṇṇidīpa and is permitted to receive it for all of them. And if, right there, one monk of the same group takes the share for those of the same group, he should not be prevented. Thus, first, the ruling on the giving of one who gives having specified the boundary should be understood.

Yo [M 0.0419] pana asukasīmāyāti vattuṃ na jānāti, kevalaṃ sīmāti vacanamattameva jānanto vihāraṃ gantvā “sīmāya dammī”ti vā “sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghassa dammī”ti vā bhaṇati, so pucchitabbo – “sīmā nāma bahuvidhā, katarasīmaṃ sandhāya bhaṇasī”ti[P 5.1138]? Sace vadati – “ahaṃ asukasīmāti na jānāmi, sīmaṭṭhakasaṅgho bhājetvā gaṇhātū”ti katarasīmāya bhājetabbaṃ? Mahāsīvatthero kirāha – “avippavāsasīmāyā”ti. Tato naṃ āhaṃsu – “avippavāsasīmā nāma tiyojanāpi hoti, evaṃ sante tiyojane ṭhitā lābhaṃ gaṇhissanti, tiyojane ṭhatvā āgantukavattaṃ pūretvā ārāmaṃ pavisitabbaṃ bhavissati, gamiko tiyojanaṃ gantvā senāsanaṃ āpucchissati, nissayapaṭipannassa tiyojanātikkame nissayo paṭippassambhissati, pārivāsikena tiyojanaṃ atikkamitvā aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpetabbaṃ bhavissati, bhikkhuniyā tiyojane ṭhatvā ārāmappavesanaṃ āpucchitabbaṃ bhavissati, sabbampetaṃ upacārasīmāya paricchedavaseneva kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Tasmā upacārasīmāyameva bhājetabba”nti.

But if a person does not know how to say, ‘in such-and-such a boundary,’ and knowing only the mere word ‘boundary,’ goes to the monastery and says, ‘I give to the boundary,’ or ‘I give to the Saṅgha established in the boundary,’ he should be asked, ‘Boundaries, by name, are of many kinds; referring to which boundary do you speak?’ If he says, ‘I do not know “such-and-such a boundary”; let the Saṅgha established in the boundary divide and take it,’ in which boundary should it be divided? The Elder Mahāsīva, it is said, stated, ‘In the non-separation-boundary.’ Then they said to him, ‘A non-separation-boundary can be as large as three yojanas. This being so, those standing at three yojanas would receive the gain. It would be necessary to fulfill the duties for incoming monks while standing at three yojanas before entering the monastery. A traveling monk, having gone three yojanas, would have to ask for lodging. For one living in dependence, upon exceeding three yojanas, the dependence would cease. A probationer would have to cause dawn to arise after having crossed three yojanas. A bhikkhunī would have to ask for permission to enter the monastery while standing at three yojanas. All this is proper to do only by virtue of the delimitation of the vicinity-boundary. Therefore, it should be divided only in the vicinity-boundary.’”

Katikāyāti samānalābhakatikāya. Tenevāha – “sambahulā āvāsā samānalābhā hontī”ti. Tatrevaṃ katikā kātabbā, ekasmiṃ vihāre sannipatitehi bhikkhūhi yaṃ vihāraṃ saṅgaṇhitukāmā samānalābhaṃ kātuṃ icchanti, tassa nāmaṃ gahetvā asuko nāma vihāro porāṇakoti vā buddhādhivutthoti vā appalābhoti vā yaṃkiñci kāraṇaṃ vatvā taṃ vihāraṃ iminā vihārena saddhiṃ ekalābhaṃ kātuṃ saṅghassa ruccatīti tikkhattuṃ sāvetabbaṃ. Ettāvatā tasmiṃ vihāre nisinnopi idha nisinnova hoti, tasmiṃ vihārepi saṅghena evameva kātabbaṃ. Ettāvatā idha nisinnopi tasmiṃ nisinnova hoti. Ekasmiṃ lābhe bhājiyamāne itarasmiṃ ṭhitassa bhāgaṃ gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ ekena vihārena saddhiṃ bahūpi āvāsā ekalābhā kātabbā.

‘By agreement’ means by an agreement for equal gain. Therefore, He said, ‘Many dwellings are of equal gain.’ There, an agreement should be made thus: by the monks assembled in one monastery who, wishing to support another monastery, desire to make it of equal gain, taking its name and stating some reason, such as, ‘Such-and-such a monastery is ancient,’ or ‘It was inhabited by the Buddha,’ or ‘It has little gain,’ it should be announced three times: ‘Does it please the Saṅgha to make that monastery, together with this monastery, one of equal gain?’ By this much, one sitting in that monastery is as one sitting here. In that monastery too, it should be done by the Saṅgha in just the same way. By this much, one sitting here is as one sitting there. When a gain in one monastery is being divided, it is proper for one abiding in the other to take a share. Thus, with one monastery, many dwellings can also be made to have equal gain.

Bhikkhāpaññattiyāti attano pariccāgapaññāpanaṭṭhāne. Tenevāha – “yattha saṅghassa dhuvakārā kariyantī”ti. Tassattho – yasmiṃ vihāre imassa cīvaradāyakassa santakaṃ saṅghassa pākavaṭṭaṃ vā vattati, yasmiṃ vā vihāre bhikkhū attano bhāraṃ katvā sadā gehe bhojeti, yattha vā [M 0.0420] anena āvāso kārito, salākabhattādīni vā nibaddhāni, yena pana sakalopi vihāro [V 0.0395] patiṭṭhāpito, tattha vattabbameva natthi, ime dhuvakārā nāma. Tasmā sace so “yattha mayhaṃ dhuvakārā karīyanti, tattha dammī”ti vā “tattha dethā”ti vā bhaṇati, bahūsu cepi ṭhānesu dhuvakārā honti, sabbattha [P 5.1139] dinnameva hoti.

“By the designation of alms” means at the place of designating one's own offering. Therefore, He said, “Where permanent duties for the Sangha are performed.” Its meaning is: in whichever monastery a regular provision of cooked food belonging to this robe-donor for the Sangha exists; or in whichever monastery he, having made it his own responsibility, always feeds the monks in his house; or where a dwelling has been caused to be built by him, or where ticket-meals and so on have been permanently established; but as for one by whom the entire monastery has been established, there is nothing even to be said—these are called “permanent duties.” Therefore, if he says, “I give where my permanent duties are performed,” or “Give there,” even if there are permanent duties in many places, it is considered given in all of them.

Sace pana ekasmiṃ vihāre bhikkhū bahutarā honti, tehi vattabbaṃ – “tumhākaṃ dhuvakāre ekattha bhikkhū bahū ekattha appakā”ti. Sace “bhikkhugaṇanāya gaṇhathā”ti bhaṇati, tathā bhājetvā gaṇhituṃ vaṭṭati. Ettha ca vatthabhesajjādi appakampi sukhena bhājiyati. Yadi pana mañco vā pīṭhakaṃ vā ekameva hoti, taṃ pucchitvā yassa vā vihārassa ekavihārepi vā yassa senāsanassa so vicāreti, tattha dātabbaṃ. Sace “asukabhikkhu gaṇhātū”ti vadati, vaṭṭati. Atha “mayhaṃ dhuvakāre dethā”ti vatvā avicāretvāva gacchati, saṅghassāpi vicāretuṃ vaṭṭati. Evaṃ pana vicāretabbaṃ – “saṅghattherassa vasanaṭṭhāne dethā”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace tassa senāsanaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti, yattha nappahoti, tattha dātabbaṃ. Sace eko bhikkhu “mayhaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne senāsanaparibhogabhaṇḍaṃ natthī”ti vadati, tattha dātabbaṃ.

But if in one monastery the monks are more numerous, they should say, “In the places of your permanent duties, in one place the monks are many, in another they are few.” If he says, “Take it according to the number of monks,” it is proper to divide and take it accordingly. And here, even a small amount of requisites such as cloth, medicine, and so on, is easily divided. But if there is only one bed or bench, having asked him, it should be given to whichever monastery, or even in one monastery to whichever lodging, he decides. If he says, “Let such-and-such a monk take it,” it is proper. Then, if, after saying, “Give it at the place of my permanent duties,” he leaves without deciding, it is also proper for the Sangha to decide. It should be decided thus: it should be said, “Give it to the dwelling place of the Sangha's Elder.” If his lodging is complete, it should be given where it is insufficient. If one monk says, “In my dwelling place, there are no goods for use in the lodging,” it should be given there.

Saṅghassa detīti vihāraṃ pavisitvā “imāni cīvarāni saṅghassa dammī”ti deti. Sammukhībhūtenāti upacārasīmāya ṭhitena saṅghena ghaṇṭiṃ paharitvā kālaṃ ghosetvā bhājetabbaṃ. Sīmaṭṭhassa asampattassāpi bhāgaṃ gaṇhanto na vāretabbo. Vihāro mahā hoti, therāsanato paṭṭhāya vatthesu diyyamānesu alasajātikā mahātherā pacchā āgacchanti, “bhante vīsativassānaṃ diyyati, tumhākaṃ ṭhitikā atikkantā”ti na vattabbā, ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā tesaṃ datvā pacchā ṭhitikāya dātabbaṃ.

“He gives to the Sangha” means he enters the monastery and gives, saying, “I give these robes to the Sangha.” “By the Sangha that is present” means it should be divided by the Sangha established in the proximity sīmā, after having struck the bell and announced the time. One taking the share of a monk who is within the sīmā but has not arrived should not be prevented. If the monastery is large, and while the cloths are being given out starting from the Elder's seat, indolent senior elders arrive late, it should not be said, “Venerable sirs, it is being given to the elders of twenty vassas; your turn in the order has passed.” Halting the order, and having given to them, it should afterwards be given according to the established order.

Asukavihāre kira bahuṃ cīvaraṃ uppannanti sutvā yojanantarikavihāratopi bhikkhū āgacchanti, sampattasampattānaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya dātabbaṃ. Asampattānampi upacārasīmaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ antevāsikādīsu gaṇhantesu dātabbameva. “Bahiupacārasīmāya ṭhitānaṃ dethā”ti vadanti, na dātabbaṃ. Sace pana upacārasīmaṃ okkantehi ekābaddhā hutvā attano vihāradvāre vā antovihāreyeva vā honti, parisavasena vaḍḍhitā nāma hoti sīmā[M 0.0421], tasmā dātabbaṃ. Saṅghanavakassa dinnepi pacchā āgatānaṃ dātabbameva. Dutiyabhāge pana therāsanaṃ āruḷhe [P 5.1140] āgatānaṃ paṭhamabhāgo na pāpuṇāti, dutiyabhāgato vassaggena dātabbaṃ.

Having heard, “It is said that much robe-cloth has arisen in such-and-such a monastery,” monks come even from a monastery a yojana away. It should be given to all those who have arrived, starting from the place where they stand. Even for those who have not yet arrived at the distribution, if they have entered the proximity boundary and their resident pupils and so on are receiving on their behalf, it should indeed be given. If they say, “Give to those standing outside the proximity boundary,” it should not be given. But if, having become a single connected group with those who have entered the proximity boundary, they are at their own monastery gate or just within the monastery, the boundary is said to be extended by the power of the assembly; therefore, it should be given. Even after it has been given to the most junior monk of the Sangha, it should indeed be given to those who arrive later. But in the second round of distribution, when the elder's seat has been reached, the first portion does not accrue to those who arrive after; from the second portion, it should be given according to seniority by rains-residence.

Ekasmiṃ vihāre dasa bhikkhū honti, “dasa vatthāni saṅghassa demā”ti denti, pāṭekkaṃ bhājetabbāni[V 0.0396]. Sace “sabbāneva amhākaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gahetvā gacchanti, duppāpitāni ceva duggahitāni ca gatagataṭṭhāne saṅghikāneva honti. Ekaṃ pana uddharitvā “idaṃ tumhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti saṅghattherassa datvā “sesāni amhākaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gahetuṃ vaṭṭati.

In one monastery there are ten monks. Donors give, saying, “We give ten cloths to the Sangha.” They should be divided individually. If the monks take them and go, saying, “All of them accrue to us,” they are both improperly caused to be received and improperly taken, and in every place they go, they remain Sanghika property. But it is proper, having set one aside and given it to the Sangha's elder saying, “This accrues to you,” to then take the remaining ones, saying, “The remaining ones accrue to us.”

Ekameva vatthaṃ saṅghassa demāti āharanti, abhājetvāva amhākaṃ pāpuṇantīti gaṇhanti, duppāpitañceva duggahitañca. Satthakena pana haliddiādinā vā lekhaṃ katvā ekaṃ koṭṭhāsaṃ “imaṃ ṭhānaṃ tumhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti saṅghattherassa pāpetvā “sesaṃ amhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gahetuṃ vaṭṭati. Yaṃ pana vatthasseva pupphaṃ vā vali vā, tena paricchedaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sace ekaṃ tantaṃ uddharitvā “idaṃ ṭhānaṃ tumhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti saṅghattherassa datvā “sesaṃ amhākaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gaṇhanti, vaṭṭati. Khaṇḍaṃ khaṇḍaṃ chinditvā bhājiyamānaṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

They bring just one cloth, saying, “We give this to the Sangha.” Without dividing it, they take it, thinking, “It accrues to us.” This is both improperly caused to be received and improperly taken. But it is proper, having made a mark with a small knife or with turmeric and so on, and having caused one portion to reach the Sangha's elder, saying, “This part accrues to you,” to then take the remaining part, saying, “The remainder accrues to us.” However, it is not proper to make a division by means of a flower or a fold that is part of the cloth itself. If, having pulled out a single thread and given it to the Sangha's elder, saying, “This part accrues to you,” they take the rest, saying, “The remainder accrues to us,” it is proper. It is indeed proper for it to be divided by cutting it into piece after piece.

Ekabhikkhuke vihāre saṅghassa cīvaresu uppannesu sace pubbe vuttanayeneva so bhikkhu “sabbāni mayhaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gaṇhāti, suggahitāni, ṭhitikā pana na tiṭṭhati. Sace ekekaṃ uddharitvā “idaṃ mayhaṃ pāpuṇātī”ti gaṇhāti, ṭhitikā tiṭṭhati. Tattha aṭṭhitāya ṭhitikāya puna aññasmiṃ cīvare uppanne sace eko bhikkhu āgacchati, majjhe chinditvā dvīhipi gahetabbaṃ. Ṭhitāya ṭhitikāya puna aññasmiṃ cīvare uppanne sace navakataro āgacchati, ṭhitikā heṭṭhā orohati. Sace vuḍḍhataro āgacchati, ṭhitikā uddhaṃ ārohati. Athañño natthi, puna attano pāpetvā gahetabbaṃ.

In a monastery with a single monk, when robes for the Sangha have arisen, if that monk, in the way previously stated, takes them all, saying, “All of these accrue to me,” they are well-taken, but the established order does not stand. If he takes them one by one, saying, “This one accrues to me,” the established order stands. In this case, when the established order does not stand, if another robe arises and another monk arrives, it should be cut in the middle and taken by both. When the established order stands, if another robe arises and a more junior monk arrives, the established order descends. If a more senior monk arrives, the established order ascends. If there is no other, it should again be caused to accrue to himself and be taken.

“Saṅghassa demā”ti vā “bhikkhusaṅghassa demā”ti vā yena kenaci ākārena saṅghaṃ āmasitvā dinnaṃ pana paṃsukūlikānaṃ na vaṭṭati, “gahapaticīvaraṃ paṭikkhipāmi paṃsukūlikaṅgaṃ samādiyāmī”ti vuttattā, na pana akappiyattā[M 0.0422]. Bhikkhusaṅghena apaloketvā dinnampi na gahetabbaṃ. Yaṃ pana bhikkhu [P 5.1141] attano santakaṃ deti, taṃ bhikkhudattiyaṃ nāma vaṭṭati, paṃsukūlaṃ pana na hoti. Evaṃ santepi dhutaṅgaṃ na bhijjati. “Bhikkhūnaṃ dema, therānaṃ demā”ti vutte pana paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭati. “Idaṃ vatthaṃ saṅghassa dema, iminā upāhanatthavikapattatthavikaāyogaaṃsabaddhakādīni karontū”ti dinnampi vaṭṭati.

A gift given by referring to the Sangha in any way whatsoever, whether saying, 'We give to the Sangha,' or 'We give to the Sangha of monks,' is not allowable for a wearer of rag-robes. This is because it has been said, 'I reject a householder's robe; I undertake the rag-robe observance,' and not because it is unsuitable. Even if given after being announced by the Sangha of monks, it should not be taken by a wearer of rag-robes. But what a monk gives of his own property is called a 'gift from a monk' and is allowable, but it is not a rag-robe. Even so, the ascetic practice is not broken. However, when it is said, 'We give to the monks,' or 'We give to the elders,' it is allowable even for wearers of rag-robes. A cloth given with the words, 'We give this cloth to the Sangha; with this let them make shoe-bags, bowl-bags, waistbands, shoulder straps, and so on,' is also allowable.

Pattatthavikādīnaṃ atthāya dinnāni bahūnipi honti, cīvaratthāyapi pahonti, tato cīvaraṃ katvā pārupituṃ vaṭṭati. Sace pana saṅgho bhājitātirittāni vatthāni chinditvā upāhanatthavikādīnaṃ [V 0.0397] atthāya bhājeti, tato gahetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Sāmikehi vicāritameva hi vaṭṭati, na itaraṃ.

Even if many cloths are given for the purpose of bowl-bags and so on, and they are also sufficient for the purpose of a robe, it is allowable to make a robe from them and wear it. But if the Sangha, having cut up the cloths left over from distribution, distributes them for the purpose of shoe-bags and so on, it is not allowable to take from that. For only what has been designated by the owners is allowable, not what is other than that.

“Paṃsukūlikasaṅghassa dhamakaraṇapaṭādīnaṃ atthāya demā”ti vuttepi gahetuṃ vaṭṭati, parikkhāro nāma paṃsukūlikānampi icchitabbo. Yaṃ tattha atirekaṃ hoti, taṃ cīvarepi upanetuṃ vaṭṭati. Suttaṃ saṅghassa denti, paṃsukūlikehipi gahetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ tāva vihāraṃ pavisitvā “imāni cīvarāni saṅghassa dammī”ti dinnesu vinicchayo.

Even when it is said, 'We give to the Sangha of rag-robe wearers for the purpose of water-strainer cloths and so on,' it is allowable to take them, for a requisite is indeed to be desired even by wearers of rag-robes. Whatever thereof is in excess, it is allowable to apply that also to a robe. If they give thread to the Sangha, it may be taken also by wearers of rag-robes. This, so far, is the ruling concerning robes given after entering the monastery and saying, 'I give these robes to the Sangha.'

Sace pana bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ addhānappaṭipanne bhikkhū disvā “saṅghassa dammī”ti saṅghattherassa vā saṅghanavakassa vā āroceti, sacepi yojanaṃ pharitvā parisā ṭhitā hoti, ekabaddhā ce, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ye pana dvādasahi hatthehi parisaṃ asampattā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti.

But if, outside the proximity boundary, having seen monks who are on a long journey, one informs either the Sangha's elder or the Sangha's most junior monk, saying, 'I give to the Sangha,' then even if the assembly is standing spread out over a yojana, if it is a single connected group, it accrues to all of them. But for those who have not reached the assembly by twelve cubits, it does not accrue to them.

Ubhatosaṅghassa detīti ettha “ubhatosaṅghassa dammī”ti vuttepi “dvidhā saṅghassa dammi, dvinnaṃ saṅghānaṃ dammi, bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunisaṅghassa ca dammī”ti vuttepi ubhatosaṅghassa dinnameva hoti. Upaḍḍhaṃ dātabbanti dvebhāge same katvā eko dātabbo. “Ubhatosaṅghassa ca tuyhañca dammī”ti vutte sace dasa dasa bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca honti, ekavīsati paṭivīse katvā eko puggalassa dātabbo, dasa bhikkhusaṅghassa, dasa bhikkhunisaṅghassa yena puggaliko laddho so saṅghatopi attano vassaggena gahetuṃ labhati. Kasmā? Ubhatosaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā.

Herein, concerning 'gives to the dual Sangha,' the ruling is to be understood thus. Even when it is said, 'I give to the dual Sangha,' or when it is said, 'I give to the Sangha in two parts; I give to the two Sanghas; I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus and to the Sangha of bhikkhunīs,' it is indeed a gift given to the dual Sangha. When it is said, 'Half should be given,' it means that having made two equal portions, one portion should be given to each. When it is said, 'I give to the dual Sangha and to you,' if there are ten bhikkhus and ten bhikkhunīs, then having made twenty-one shares, one share should be given to the individual, ten to the Sangha of bhikkhus, and ten to the Sangha of bhikkhunīs. The one who has received the individual share is able to take from the Sangha's share as well, according to his seniority. Why? Because of being included by the term 'dual Sangha'.

“Ubhatosaṅghassa [M 0.0423] ca cetiyassa ca dammī”ti vuttepi eseva nayo. Idha pana cetiyassa saṅghato pāpuṇanakoṭṭhāso nāma natthi, ekapuggalassa [P 5.1142] pattakoṭṭhāsasamova koṭṭhāso hoti.

Even when it is said, 'I give to the dual Sangha and to the shrine,' this is the same principle. Here, however, there is no portion whatsoever receivable by the shrine from the Sangha's share; the portion is one that is just like the portion received by a single individual.

“Ubhatosaṅghassa ca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana dvāvīsati koṭṭhāse katvā dasa bhikkhūnaṃ, dasa bhikkhunīnaṃ, eko puggalassa, eko cetiyassa dātabbo. Tattha puggalo saṅghatopi attano vassaggena puna gahetuṃ labhati, cetiyassa ekoyeva.

However, when it is said, 'To the dual Sangha, and to you, and to the shrine,' then having made twenty-two portions, ten should be given to the bhikkhus, ten to the bhikkhunīs, one to the individual, and one to the shrine. In this case, the individual is able to take again from the Sangha's share according to his seniority; for the shrine, there is only one portion.

“Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca dammī”ti vutte pana na majjhe bhinditvā dātabbaṃ, bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā dātabbaṃ. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañcā”ti [V 0.0398] vutte pana puggalo visuṃ na labhati, pāpuṇanaṭṭhānato ekameva labhati. Kasmā? Bhikkhusaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyassa ekapuggalapaṭivīso labbhati, puggalassa visuṃ na labbhati, tasmā ekaṃ cetiyassa datvā avasesaṃ bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā bhājetabbaṃ.

However, when it is said, 'I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs,' it should not be given by dividing it in the middle; it should be given after counting the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. However, when it is said, 'I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus, to the bhikkhunīs, and to you,' the individual does not receive a separate share; he receives only one share from the group to which it is due. Why? Because of being included by the term 'Sangha of bhikkhus.' Even when it is said, 'I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus, to the bhikkhunīs, to you, and to the shrine,' the shrine receives a share for one individual, but the individual does not receive a separate share. Therefore, having given one share to the shrine, the remainder should be divided after counting the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs.

“Bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca dammī”ti vuttepi majjhe bhinditvā na dātabbaṃ, puggalagaṇanāya eva vibhajitabbaṃ. “Bhikkhūnañca bhikkhunīnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti evaṃ vuttepi cetiyassa ekapuggalapaṭivīso labbhati, puggalassa visuṃ natthi, bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca gaṇetvā eva bhājetabbaṃ. Yathā ca bhikkhusaṅghaṃ ādiṃ katvā nayo nīto, evaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ ādiṃ katvāpi netabbo. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tuyhañcā”ti vutte puggalassa visuṃ na labbhati, vassaggeneva gahetabbaṃ. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana cetiyassa visuṃ paṭivīso labbhati. “Bhikkhusaṅghassa ca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyasseva labbhati, na puggalassa.

Even when it is said, 'I give to the bhikkhus and to the bhikkhunīs,' it should not be given by dividing it in the middle; it should be divided only according to the count of individuals. Even when it is said thus, 'I give to the bhikkhus, to the bhikkhunīs, to you, and to the shrine,' the shrine receives a share for one individual; there is no separate share for the individual. It should be divided only after counting the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. And just as the principle has been applied beginning with the Sangha of bhikkhus, so too should the principle be applied beginning with the Sangha of bhikkhunīs. When it is said, 'I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus and to you,' the individual does not receive a separate share; it should be taken only by seniority. However, when it is said, 'I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus and to the shrine,' the shrine receives a separate share. Even when it is said, 'I give to the Sangha of bhikkhus, to you, and to the shrine,' only the shrine receives a share, not the individual.

“Bhikkhūnañca tuyhañcā”ti vuttepi visuṃ na labbhati. “Bhikkhūnañca cetiyassa cā”ti vutte pana cetiyassa labbhati. “Bhikkhūnañca tuyhañca cetiyassa cā”ti vuttepi cetiyasseva visuṃ labbhati, na puggalassa. Bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ ādiṃ katvāpi evameva yojetabbaṃ.

Even when it is said, 'To the bhikkhus and to you,' a separate share is not received. But when it is said, 'To the bhikkhus and to the shrine,' the shrine receives a share. Even when it is said, 'To the bhikkhus, to you, and to the shrine,' only the shrine receives a separate share, not the individual. Beginning with the Sangha of bhikkhunīs also, it should be applied in this very way.

Pubbe buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa dānaṃ denti, bhagavā majjhe nisīdati, dakkhiṇato bhikkhū vāmato bhikkhuniyo nisīdanti, bhagavā ubhinnaṃ saṅghatthero[P 5.1143], tadā bhagavā attanā laddhapaccaye attanāpi paribhuñjati, bhikkhūnampi [M 0.0424] dāpeti. Etarahi pana paṇḍitamanussā sadhātukaṃ paṭimaṃ vā cetiyaṃ vā ṭhapetvā buddhappamukhassa ubhatosaṅghassa dānaṃ denti. Paṭimāya vā cetiyassa vā purato ādhārake pattaṃ ṭhapetvā dakkhiṇodakaṃ datvā buddhānaṃ demāti, tattha yaṃ paṭhamaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ denti, vihāraṃ vā āharitvā idaṃ cetiyassa demāti piṇḍapātañca mālāgandhādīni ca denti, tattha kathaṃ paṭipajjitabbanti? Mālāgandhādīni tāva cetiye āropetabbāni, vatthehi paṭākā, telena padīpā kātabbā, piṇḍapātamadhuphāṇitādīni pana yo nibaddhacetiyajaggako hoti pabbajito vā gahaṭṭho vā, tasseva dātabbāni. Nibaddhajaggake asati āhaṭabhattaṃ ṭhapetvā vattaṃ katvā paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Upakaṭṭhe kāle bhuñjitvā pacchāpi vattaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva.

In the time of previous Buddhas, they gave offerings to the dual Saṅgha headed by the Buddha. The Blessed One would sit in the middle; on his right sat the bhikkhus, and on his left sat the bhikkhunīs. The Blessed One was the Elder of both Saṅghas. At that time, the Blessed One would himself consume the requisites he received and would also have them given to the bhikkhus. Now, however, wise people set up an image or a shrine containing relics and give offerings to the dual Saṅgha headed by the Buddha. Having placed a bowl on a stand in front of the image or shrine and having poured the water of dedication, they say, “We give to the Buddhas.” In that case, when they first give hard food or soft food, or when, having brought it to the monastery, they give almsfood and garlands, perfumes, and so on, saying, “We give this to the shrine,” how should one proceed? Firstly, the garlands, perfumes, and so on should be placed upon the shrine. With cloths, banners should be made. With oil, lamps should be made. However, almsfood, honey, molasses, and so on should be given only to the one who is the regular caretaker of the shrine, whether ordained or a householder. If there is no regular caretaker, it is permissible to set aside the food that was brought, perform one’s duties, and then consume it. When the time is near, it is permissible to eat first and perform one’s duties afterwards.

Mālāgandhādīsu [V 0.0399] ca yaṃ kiñci “idaṃ haritvā cetiyassapūjaṃ karothā”ti vutte dūrampi haritvā pūjetabbaṃ. “Bhikkhaṃ saṅghassa harā”ti vuttepi haritabbaṃ. Sace pana “ahaṃ piṇḍāya carāmi, āsanasālāya bhikkhū atthi, te āharissantī”ti vutte “bhante tuyhaṃyeva dammī”ti vadati, bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Atha pana “bhikkhusaṅghassa dassāmī”ti harantassa gacchato antarāva kālo upakaṭṭho hoti, attano pāpetvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati.

And regarding garlands, perfumes, and so on, if anything is given with the words, “Take this and make an offering to the shrine,” it should be taken even to a distant place and offered. Even when it is said, “Take this almsfood for the Saṅgha,” it should be taken. If, however, when one says, “I am going for alms; there are bhikkhus in the dining hall, they will bring it,” the donor says, “Venerable sir, I give it only to you,” it is permissible to eat it. Or, if a bhikkhu, while going and carrying it with the intention, “I will give this to the Bhikkhu Saṅgha,” finds that the time is near while he is still on the way, it is permissible for him to appropriate it for himself and eat it.

Vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa detīti vihāraṃ pavisitvā “imāni cīvarāni vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa dammī”ti deti. Yāvatikā bhikkhū tasmiṃ āvāse vassaṃvuṭṭhāti yattakā vassacchedaṃ akatvā purimavassaṃvuṭṭhā, tehi bhājetabbaṃ, aññesaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Disāpakkantassāpi sati paṭiggāhake yāva kathinassubbhārā dātabbaṃ, anatthate pana kathine antohemante evañca vatvā dinnaṃ, pacchimavassaṃvuṭṭhānampi pāpuṇātīti lakkhaṇaññū vadanti. Aṭṭhakathāsu panetaṃ na vicāritaṃ.

Regarding 'gives to the Saṅgha that has completed the rains-residence': Having entered a monastery, one gives, saying, 'I give these robes to the Saṅgha that has completed the rains-residence.' It should be divided among however many bhikkhus in that dwelling have completed the rains-residence—that is, those who have completed the earlier rains-residence without a break. It does not reach others. Even for one who has departed to another region, it should be given until the time of the lifting of the Kathina, if there is someone to receive it on their behalf. However, if the Kathina has not been spread, a gift given within the winter season after speaking thus also reaches those who have completed the later rains-residence. Thus say those who know the characteristics of the Vinaya. But in the commentaries, this matter has not been investigated.

Sace pana bahiupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhito “vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassa dammī”ti vadati, sampattānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Atha “asukavihāre vassaṃvuṭṭhasaṅghassā”ti vadati, tatra vassaṃvuṭṭhānameva yāva kathinassubbhārā pāpuṇāti. Sace pana gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato [P 5.1144] paṭṭhāya evaṃ vadati, tatra sammukhībhūtānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Kasmā? Piṭṭhisamaye uppannattā. Antovasseyeva “vassaṃ vasantānaṃ dammī”ti vutte chinnavassā na labhanti, vassaṃ vasantāva labhanti. Cīvaramāse [M 0.0425] pana “vassaṃ vasantānaṃ dammī”ti vutte pacchimikāya vassūpagatānaṃyeva pāpuṇāti, purimikāya vassūpagatānañca chinnavassānañca na pāpuṇāti.

However, if one stands outside the precincts and says, 'I give to the Saṅgha that has completed the rains-residence,' it reaches all who have arrived. Or, if one says, 'to the Saṅgha that has completed the rains-residence in such-and-such a monastery,' it reaches only those who have completed the rains-residence there, until the lifting of the Kathina. However, if one speaks thus starting from the first day of the hot season, it reaches all who are present there. Why? Because it has arisen in the post-season period. If, within the rains-residence itself, it is said, 'I give to those observing the rains,' those with a broken rains-residence do not receive it; only those observing the rains receive it. However, in the robe-month, if it is said, 'I give to those observing the rains,' it reaches only those who have undertaken the later rains-residence; it does not reach those who have undertaken the earlier rains-residence nor those with a broken rains-residence.

Cīvaramāsato paṭṭhāya yāva hemantassa pacchimo divaso, tāva vassāvāsikaṃ demāti vutte kathinaṃ atthataṃ vā hotu anatthataṃ vā atītavassaṃvuṭṭhānameva pāpuṇāti. Gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya vutte pana mātikā āropetabbā – “atītavassāvāsassa pañca māsā atikkantā, anāgato catumāsaccayena bhavissati, kataravassāvāsassa detī”ti? Sace “atītavassaṃvuṭṭhānaṃ dammī”ti vadati, taṃantovassaṃvuṭṭhānameva pāpuṇāti, disāpakkantānampi sabhāgā gaṇhituṃ labhanti.

Starting from the robe-month up until the last day of the winter season, if it is said, 'We give the rains-residence requisite,' then whether the Kathina has been spread or not, it reaches only those who have completed the past rains-residence. However, if this is said starting from the first day of the hot season, a formal question should be raised: 'Five months have passed since the past rains-residence, and the future one will occur after four months have passed. For which rains-residence is one giving?' If one says, 'I give to those who have completed the past rains-residence,' it reaches only those who completed the residence within that rains-period, and even for those who have departed to other regions, those entitled to a share may receive it.

Sace “anāgate vassāvāsikaṃ dammī”ti vadati, taṃ ṭhapetvā vassūpanāyikadivase gahetabbaṃ. Atha “agutto vihāro, corabhayaṃ atthi, na sakkā ṭhapetuṃ, gaṇhitvā vā āhiṇḍitu”nti [V 0.0400] vutte “sampattānaṃ dammī”ti vadati, bhājetvā gahetabbaṃ. Sace vadati “ito me bhante tatiye vasse vassāvāsikaṃ na dinnaṃ, taṃ dammī”ti, tasmiṃ antovasse vuṭṭhabhikkhūnaṃ pāpuṇāti. Sace te disā pakkantā, añño vissāsiko gaṇhāti, dātabbaṃ. Atha ekoyeva avasiṭṭho, sesā kālaṅkatā, sabbaṃ ekasseva pāpuṇāti. Sace ekopi natthi, saṅghikaṃ hoti, sammukhībhūtehi bhājetabbaṃ.

If one says, 'I give the rains-residence requisite for the future,' it should be set aside and taken on the day of entering the rains-residence. Or, if it is said, 'The monastery is not secure, there is danger from thieves, it is not possible to keep it, nor is it possible to take it and wander about with it,' and one then says, 'I give to those who have arrived,' it should be divided and taken. If one says, 'Venerable sir, in the third year back from this one, I did not give the rains-residence requisite; I give it now,' it reaches the bhikkhus who completed the residence within that rains-period. If they have departed to other regions, another trustworthy bhikkhu may receive it; it should be given. Or, if only one remains and the rest have passed away, everything reaches that one alone. If not even one remains, it becomes property of the Saṅgha and should be divided by those who are present.

Ādissa detīti ādisitvā paricchinditvā deti; yāguyā vātiādīsu ayamattho – yāguyā vā…pe… bhesajje vā ādissa deti. Tatrāyaṃ yojanā – bhikkhū ajjatanāya vā svātanāya vā yāguyā nimantetvā tesaṃ gharaṃ paviṭṭhānaṃ yāguṃ deti, yāguṃ datvā pītāya yāguyā “imāni cīvarāni, yehi mayhaṃ yāgu pītā, tesaṃ dammī”ti deti, yehi nimantitehi yāgu pītā, tesaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Yehi pana bhikkhācāravattena gharadvārena gacchantehi vā gharaṃ paviṭṭhehi vā yāgu laddhā, yesaṃ vā āsanasālato pattaṃ āharitvā manussehi nītā, yesaṃ vā therehi pesitā, tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti. Sace [P 5.1145] pana nimantitabhikkhūhi saddhiṃ aññepi bahū āgantvā antogehañca bahigehañca pūretvā nisinnā, dāyako ca evaṃ vadati – “nimantitā vā hontu animantitā vā, yesaṃ mayā yāgu dinnā, sabbesaṃ imāni vatthāni hontū”ti sabbesaṃ pāpuṇanti. Yehi pana therānaṃ hatthato yāgu laddhā[M 0.0426], tesaṃ na pāpuṇanti. Atha so “yehi mayhaṃ yāgu pītā, sabbesaṃ hontū”ti vadati, sabbesaṃ pāpuṇanti. Bhattakhādanīyesupi eseva nayo.

“Gives having designated” means one gives after designating and specifying. In “with rice-gruel, etc.,” this is the meaning: one gives having designated with rice-gruel... or with medicine. Herein is the application: Having invited bhikkhus for today’s or tomorrow’s rice-gruel, one gives them rice-gruel when they have entered the house. After giving the rice-gruel and it has been drunk, one says, “These robes, I give to those by whom my rice-gruel was drunk.” It then reaches only those invited ones by whom the rice-gruel was drunk. However, it does not reach those who received rice-gruel while going by the house-door on their alms-round or having entered the house; nor those to whom it was brought by laypeople who had fetched their bowls from the dining hall; nor those to whom it was sent by the elders. However, if many other bhikkhus come together with the invited bhikkhus, fill the inside and outside of the house and are seated, and the donor says, “Whether invited or uninvited, let these cloths be for all to whom I have given rice-gruel,” then they reach all of them. But they do not reach those who received rice-gruel from the hands of the elders. Or, if the donor says, “Let them be for all by whom my rice-gruel was drunk,” they reach all of them. This same method applies also to boiled rice and other foods.

Cīvare vāti pubbepi yena vassaṃ vāsetvā bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ dinnapubbaṃ hoti, so ce bhikkhū bhojetvā vadati – “yesaṃ mayā pubbe cīvaraṃ dinnaṃ, tesaṃyeva imaṃ cīvaraṃ vā suttaṃ vā sappimadhuphāṇitādīni vā hontū”ti, sabbaṃ tesaṃyeva pāpuṇāti. Senāsane vāti yo mayā kārite vihāre vā pariveṇe vā vasati, tassidaṃ hotū”ti vutte tasseva hoti. Bhesajje vāti “mayaṃ kālena kālaṃ therānaṃ sappiādīni bhesajjāni dema, yehi tāni laddhāni, tesaṃyevidaṃ hotū”ti vutte tesaṃyeva hoti.

Regarding “or with a robe”: This refers to a donor who, having previously provided for bhikkhus during the rains-residence, had given them a robe. If that donor, after feeding the bhikkhus, says, “Let this robe, or this thread, or these things such as ghee, honey, and molasses, be only for those to whom a robe was given by me before,” then everything reaches them alone. Regarding “or with a lodging”: If it is said, “Let this be for whoever resides in the monastery or enclosure that I had built,” it is for that one alone. Regarding “or with medicine”: If it is said, “We from time to time give medicines such as ghee to the elders; let this be only for those by whom those things were received,” it is for them alone.

Puggalassa detīti “imaṃ cīvaraṃ itthannāmassa dammī”ti evaṃ parammukhā vā pādamūle ṭhapetvā “imaṃ bhante tumhākaṃ dammī”ti evaṃ sammukhā vā deti. Sace pana “idaṃ tumhākañca tumhākaṃ antevāsikānañca dammī”ti evaṃ vadati, therassa ca antevāsikānañca pāpuṇāti. Uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgato gahetvā gacchanto ca atthi, tassāpi pāpuṇāti. “Tumhehi saddhiṃ nibaddhacārikabhikkhūnaṃ [V 0.0401] dammī”ti vutte uddesantevāsikānaṃ vattaṃ katvā uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantānaṃ sabbesaṃ pāpuṇāti. Ayaṃ puggalassa detīti imasmiṃ pade vinicchayo. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

Regarding “gives to an individual”: one gives either in the person's absence, saying, “I give this robe to so-and-so,” or in their presence, placing it at their feet and saying, “Venerable sir, I give this to you.” If, however, one says, “I give this to you and to your resident pupils,” it reaches both the elder and the pupils. If there is a pupil who has come to receive instruction and one who is departing after having received it, it reaches him also. When it is said, “I give this to the monks who constantly wander with you,” it reaches all pupils receiving instruction who, having performed their duties, wander about while receiving instruction, questioning, and so on. This is the determination in the phrase “gives to an individual.” The rest is clear everywhere else.

Cīvarakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Chapter on Robes is concluded.

9. Campeyyakkhandhakaṃ

9. The Chapter on Campeyya

Kassapagottabhikkhuvatthukathā

The Story of the Bhikkhu of the Kassapa Clan

380. Campeyyakkhandhake [M 0.0427][V 0.0402] – gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīreti gaggarānāmikāya itthiyā kāritapokkharaṇiyā tīre. Tantibaddhoti tasmiṃ āvāse kattabbatātantipaṭibaddho. Ussukkampi akāsi yāguyātiādīsu manussehi āgantukesu āgatesu [P 5.1146] ācikkheyyāthāti vuttaṭṭhāneyeva ussukkaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati; na avuttaṭṭhāne. Gaccha tvaṃ bhikkhūti satthā tassa bhikkhuno tattheva senāsanaṃ sappāyanti addasa, tenevamāha.

380. In the Chapter on Campeyya: “At the bank of the Gaggarā pond” means at the bank of the pond caused to be made by a woman named Gaggarā. “Bound by duty” means one who is bound by the duty of what ought to be done in that monastery. Regarding such phrases as “he also made an effort concerning the gruel,” it is proper to make an effort only in the place where it was said, “You should inform us when newcomers arrive”; it is not proper to do so in a place where this was not said. Regarding “Go, monk,” the Teacher saw that a lodging right there was suitable for that bhikkhu; therefore, he spoke thus.

382. Adhammena vaggakammaṃ karontītiādīnaṃ parato pāḷiyaṃyeva nānākaraṇaṃ āgamissati.

382. Regarding “they perform a factional act unlawfully,” and so on, the distinctions will come later in the Pāḷi text itself.

385. Aññatrāpi dhammā kammaṃ karontīti aññatrāpi dhammaṃ kammaṃ karonti, ayameva vā pāṭho. Bhūtena vatthunā kataṃ dhammena kataṃ nāma hoti, tathā na karontīti attho. Aññatrāpi vinayā kammaṃ, aññatrāpi satthusāsanā kammanti etesupi eseva nayo. Ettha pana vinayoti codanā ca sāraṇā ca. Satthusāsananti ñattisampadā anussāvanasampadā ca; tāhi vinā kammaṃ karontīti attho. Paṭikuṭṭhakatanti paṭikuṭṭhañceva katañca; yaṃ aññesu paṭikkosantesu kataṃ taṃ paṭikuṭṭhañceva hoti katañca; tādisampi kammaṃ karontīti attho.

385. Regarding “they perform an act apart from the Dhamma”: this means they perform an act apart from the Dhamma; or, this very reading is the correct one. An act done with an actual basis is called “done according to the Dhamma”; the meaning is that they do not do so. Regarding “an act apart from the Vinaya” and “an act apart from the Teacher’s instruction,” this same method applies to these as well. Here, however, “Vinaya” means accusation and admonition. “The Teacher’s instruction” means the completeness of the motion and the completeness of the proclamation; the meaning is that they perform an act without these. “A censured and performed act” means that which is both censured and performed. That which is done while other monks are protesting is both “censured” and “performed”; the meaning is that they perform even such an act.

387. Chayimāni bhikkhave kammāni adhammakammantiādīsu pana “dhammo”ti pāḷiyā adhivacanaṃ. Tasmā yaṃ yathāvuttāya pāḷiyā na kariyati, taṃ adhammakammanti veditabbaṃ. Ayamettha saṅkhepo, vitthāro pana pāḷiyaṃyeva āgato. So ca kho ñattidutiyañatticatutthakammānaṃyeva vasena. Yasmā pana ñattikamme ñattidutiyañatticatutthesu viya hāpanaṃ vā aññathā karaṇaṃ vā natthi, apalokanakammañca sāvetvāva kariyati, tasmā tāni pāḷiyaṃ na dassitāni, tesaṃ sabbesampi kammānaṃ vinicchayaṃ parato vaṇṇayissāma.

387. In the passage beginning “Monks, these six acts are unlawful acts,” “Dhamma” is a designation for the Pāḷi text. Therefore, whatever is not done according to the Pāḷi text as it has been stated, that should be understood as an “unlawful act.” This is the summary here; the detailed explanation, however, is found in the Pāḷi text itself. And that pertains only to the ñattidutiya and ñatticatuttha acts. However, since in a ñatti act, unlike in ñattidutiya and ñatticatuttha acts, there is no omission or alteration, and an apalokana act is performed only after being announced, these were not shown in the Pāḷi. We will explain the determination of all these acts later.

Catuvaggakaraṇādikathā

The Discourse on Performing Acts by a Quorum of Four, etc.

388. Idāni [M 0.0428][V 0.0403] yadidaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ dhammena samaggakammaṃ nāma, taṃ yehi saṅghehi kātabbaṃ, tesaṃ pabhedaṃ dassetuṃ “pañca saṅghā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kammappattoti kammaṃ patto, kammayutto kammāraho; na kiñci kammaṃ kātuṃ nārahatīti attho.

388. Now, to show the distinctions between the Sanghas by whom this sixth act, called “an act of concord according to Dhamma,” is to be performed, it is said, “five Sanghas,” etc. “Kammappatto” means one who has arrived at the act, is suitable for the act, is worthy of the act; the meaning is that he is indeed worthy to perform any act.

389. Catuvaggakaraṇañce bhikkhave kammaṃ bhikkhunicatutthotiādi parisato kammavipattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha ukkhittakaggahaṇena kammanānāsaṃvāsako gahito, nānāsaṃvāsakaggahaṇena laddhinānāsaṃvāsako. Nānāsīmāya ṭhitacatutthoti sīmantarikāya vā bahisīmāya vā hatthapāse ṭhitenāpi saddhiṃ catuvaggo hutvāti attho.

389. Monks, the passage beginning, 'And an act to be performed by a group of four, with a bhikkhunī as the fourth,' was stated to show the failure of an act on account of the assembly. Therein, by the taking of a suspended one, one of different communion due to an act is taken; by the taking of one of different communion, one of different communion due to doctrine is taken. 'Nānāsīmāya ṭhitacatuttho' means: having become a group of four together with one standing within arm's reach, either in an intermediate boundary or outside the boundary.

393. Pārivāsikacatutthotiādi [P 5.1147] parivāsādikammānaṃyeva parisato vipattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, tesaṃ vinicchayaṃ parato vaṇṇayissāma.

393. The passage beginning, 'With one on probation as the fourth,' was stated to show the failure on account of the assembly only in regard to acts beginning with probation. We will explain their determination later.

394. Ekaccassa bhikkhave saṅghamajjhe paṭikkosanā ruhatītiādi paṭikuṭṭhakatakammassa kuppākuppabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Pakatattassāti avipannasīlassa pārājikaṃ anajjhāpannassa. Ānantarikassāti attano anantaraṃ nisinnassa.

394. Monks, the passage beginning, 'For some, a protest arises in the midst of the Sangha,' was stated to show the state of being valid or invalid of a protested-and-performed act. 'Pakatattassa' means: of one with unbroken virtue, who has not fallen into a pārājika offense. 'Ānantarikassa' means: of one seated immediately next to oneself.

Dvenissāraṇādikathā

The Discourse on the Two Expulsions, etc.

395. Dvemā bhikkhave nissāraṇātiādi vatthuto kammānaṃ kuppākuppabhāvadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha “appatto nissāraṇaṃ, tañce saṅgho nissāreti, sunissārito”ti idaṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Pabbājanīyakammena hi vihārato nissārenti, tasmā taṃ “nissāraṇā”ti vuccati. Tañcesa yasmā kuladūsako na hoti, tasmā āveṇikena lakkhaṇena appatto. Yasmā panassa ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho pabbājanīyakammaṃ kareyyāti vuttaṃ, tasmā sunissārito hoti. Tañce saṅgho nissāretīti sace saṅgho tajjanīyakammādivasena nissāreti, so yasmā tattha “tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhave bhikkhūnaṃ ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho tajjanīyakammaṃ kareyya – eko bhaṇḍanakārako hoti kalahakārako vivādakārako bhassakārako saṅghe adhikaraṇakārako, eko bālo [M 0.0429] hoti abyatto āpattibahulo anapadāno, eko gihisaṃsaṭṭho viharati ananulomikehi [V 0.0404] gihisaṃsaggehī”ti (cūḷava. 395) evaṃ ekekenapi aṅgena nissāraṇā anuññātā, tasmā sunissārito.

395. Monks, the passage beginning, 'These two are expulsions,' was stated to show the state of being valid or invalid of acts on account of their basis. Therein, the statement, 'He has not reached the point of expulsion, but if the Sangha expels him, he is well-expelled,' was said with reference to the act of banishment. For by the act of banishment, they make him leave the monastery; therefore, it is called 'expulsion.' And since this person is not a corrupter of families, he has not reached it by its specific characteristic. However, because it was said, 'If the Sangha wishes, it may perform the act of banishment upon him,' he is therefore well-expelled. As for 'And if the Sangha expels him': if the Sangha expels him by means of an act of censure or the like, because it is stated therein that expulsion is permitted even for a single factor—'Monks, if the Sangha wishes, it may perform an act of censure against one of three monks: one who is quarrelsome, contentious, disputatious, a maker of noise, a creator of legal issues in the Sangha; one who is foolish, incompetent, full of offenses, and without demarcation; or one who lives closely associated with householders in inappropriate ways'—he is therefore well-expelled.

396. Osāraṇāti pavesanā. Tattha tañce saṅgho osāretīti upasampadakammavasena paveseti. Dosāritoti duosārito. Sahassakkhattumpi upasampādito anupasampannova hoti ācariyupajjhāyā ca sātisārā, tathā seso kārakasaṅgho, na koci āpattito muccati. Iti ime ekādasa abhabbapuggalā dosāritā. Hatthacchinnādayo pana dvattiṃsa suosāritā, upasampāditā upasampannāva honti, na te labbhā kiñci vattuṃ. Ācariyupajjhāyā pana kārakasaṅgho ca sātisārā, na koci āpattito muccati.

396. 'Osāraṇā' means admission. Therein, 'if the Sangha admits him' means they admit him by means of the act of higher ordination. 'Dosārito' means badly admitted. Even if ordained a thousand times, he is not truly ordained, and the preceptor and teacher have committed a transgression, as has the rest of the acting Sangha; no one is freed from an offense. Thus, these eleven unfit persons are badly admitted. But the thirty-two, beginning with one with a severed hand, are well-admitted; having been given higher ordination, they are indeed ordained, and it is not possible to say anything against them. However, the preceptor, teacher, and the acting Sangha have committed a transgression; no one is freed from an offense.

397. Idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhussa na hoti āpatti daṭṭhabbātiādi abhūtavatthuvasena adhammakammaṃ, bhūtavatthuvasena dhammakammañca dassetuṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha paṭinissajjitāti paṭinissajjitabbā.

397. Here, monks, the passage beginning, 'A monk has no offense to be seen,' was stated to show an unlawful act by means of a non-existent matter and a lawful act by means of an existent matter. Therein, 'paṭinissajjitā' means 'to be given up.'

Upālipucchākathā

The Discussion of Upāli’s Questions

400. Upālipañhesupi vatthuvaseneva [P 5.1148] dhammādhammakammaṃ vibhattaṃ. Tattha dve nayā – ekamūlako ca dvimūlako ca. Ekamūlako uttānoyeva. Dvimūlake yathā sativinayo amūḷhavinayena saddhiṃ ekā pucchā katā, evaṃ amūḷhavinayādayopi tassapāpiyyasikādīhi. Avasāne pana upasampadārahaṃ upasampādetīti ekameva padaṃ hoti. Parato bhikkhūnampi sativinayaṃ ādiṃ katvā ekekena saddhiṃ sesapadāni yojetabbāni.

400. In Upāli’s questions, a lawful act and an unlawful act were distinguished based on the grounds themselves. Therein, there are two methods: the one-rooted and the two-rooted. The one-rooted is straightforward. In the two-rooted, just as the verdict of mindfulness was made as one question together with the verdict of past insanity, so too were the verdict of past insanity and others made as individual questions together with the verdict for specific depravity and others. At the end, however, 'He ordains one who is worthy of ordination' is just a single phrase. Furthermore, for the monks, beginning with the verdict of mindfulness, the remaining phrases should be connected with each one.

Tajjanīyakammakathā

The Discussion of the Act of Censure

407. Idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārakotiādi “adhammenavaggaṃ, adhammenasamaggaṃ; dhammenavaggaṃ, dhammapatirūpakenavaggaṃ, dhammapatirūpakenasamagga”nti imesaṃ vasena cakkaṃ bandhitvā tajjanīyādīsu sattasu kammesu paṭipassaddhīsu ca [M 0.0430] vipattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Tattha anapadānoti apadānavirahito. Apadānaṃ vuccati paricchedo; āpattiparicchedavirahitoti attho. Tato paraṃ paṭikuṭṭhakatakammappabhedaṃ dassetuṃ sāyeva pāḷi “akataṃ kamma”ntiādīhi saṃsanditvā [V 0.0405] vuttā. Tattha na kiñci pāḷianusārena na sakkā vidituṃ, tasmā vaṇṇanaṃ na vitthārayimhāti.

407. Here, monks, 'a monk is quarrelsome,' and so forth—this was spoken to show the failure in the seven acts beginning with censure and in their acts of revocation, having bound the wheel by means of these: 'unlawfully as a divided group, unlawfully as a united group; lawfully as a divided group, seemingly lawfully as a divided group, seemingly lawfully as a united group.' Therein, 'anapadāna' means 'devoid of apadāna.' 'Apadāna' is called a demarcation; the meaning is 'devoid of the demarcation of an offense.' After that, to show the classification of the protested and performed act, that same Pāḷi text was spoken, connecting it with the passages beginning with 'the act not done.' Therein, there is nothing that cannot be known by following the Pāḷi; therefore, we have not elaborated on the commentary.

Campeyyakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Campeyya Section is concluded.

10. Kosambakakkhandhakaṃ

10. The Kosambī Chapter

Kosambakavivādakathā

The Kosambī Dispute

451. Kosambakakkhandhake [M 0.0431][V 0.0406] – taṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṃsūti ettha ayamanupubbikathā – dve kira bhikkhū ekasmiṃ āvāse vasanti vinayadharo ca suttantiko ca. Tesu suttantiko bhikkhu ekadivasaṃ vaccakuṭiṃ paviṭṭho ācamanaudakāvasesaṃ bhājane ṭhapetvāva nikkhami. Vinayadharo pacchā paviṭṭho taṃ udakaṃ disvā nikkhamitvā taṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchi – “āvuso, tayā idaṃ udakaṃ ṭhapita”nti? “Āmāvuso”ti. “Kiṃ tvaṃ ettha āpattibhāvaṃ na jānāsī”ti? “Āma, na jānāmī”ti. “Hoti, āvuso ettha āpattī”ti? “Sace hoti, desissāmī”ti. “Sace pana te, āvuso, asañcicca asatiyā kataṃ, natthi [P 5.1149] āpattī”ti. So tassā āpattiyā anāpattidiṭṭhi ahosi.

451. In the Kosambī Chapter—regarding 'they suspended that monk for not seeing the offense'—here is the sequential story: Two monks, it is said, were living in one monastery, one a Vinaya-master and the other a Sutta-master. Among them, the Sutta-master monk one day entered the toilet and, having left the remaining rinsing water in a vessel, departed. The Vinaya-master, entering afterward, saw that water, and upon departing, asked that monk, 'Friend, was this water left by you?' 'Yes, friend.' 'Do you not know that this constitutes an offense?' 'Yes, I do not know.' 'Friend, there is an offense in this.' 'If there is, I will confess it.' 'But if, friend, it was done by you unintentionally and without mindfulness, there is no offense.' He then came to hold the view of 'no offense' regarding that offense.

Vinayadharopi attano nissitakānaṃ “ayaṃ suttantiko āpattiṃ āpajjamānopi na jānātī”ti ārocesi. Te tassa nissitake disvā “tumhākaṃ upajjhāyo āpattiṃ āpajjitvāpi āpattibhāvaṃ na jānātī”ti āhaṃsu. Te gantvā attano upajjhāyassa ārocesuṃ. So evamāha – “ayaṃ vinayadharo pubbe anāpattī”ti vatvā “idāni āpattī”ti vadati. Musāvādī esoti. Te gantvā “tumhākaṃ upajjhāyo musāvādī”ti evaṃ aññamaññaṃ kalahaṃ vaḍḍhayiṃsu. Tato vinayadharo okāsaṃ labhitvā tassa āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ akāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – “taṃ bhikkhuṃ āpattiyā adassane ukkhipiṃsū”ti.

The Vinaya-master also informed his resident pupils, 'This Sutta-master, though he commits an offense, does not know it.' They, seeing the resident pupils of that Sutta-master, said, 'Your preceptor, even after committing an offense, does not know it is an offense.' They went and reported this to their own preceptor. He said thus: 'This Vinaya-master, having previously said, "It is not an offense," now says, "It is an offense." He is a liar.' They went and said, 'Your preceptor is a liar,' thus they increased the quarrel among one another. Then, the Vinaya-master, having found an opportunity, performed the act of suspension on him for not seeing the offense. Therefore it was said: 'They suspended that monk for not seeing the offense.'

453. Bhinno bhikkhusaṅgho bhinno bhikkhusaṅghoti ettha na tāva bhinno; apica kho yathā deve vuṭṭhe “idāni sassaṃ nipphanna”nti vuccati, avassañhi taṃ nipphajjissati, evameva iminā kāraṇena āyatiṃ avassaṃ bhijjissati, so ca kho kalahavasena na saṅghabhedavasena, tasmā “bhinno”ti vuttaṃ. Sambhamaatthavasena cettha āmeḍitaṃ veditabbaṃ.

453. 'The community of monks is divided, the community of monks is divided'—herein, it is not yet divided. However, just as when the rain has fallen, it is said, 'Now the crop is produced'—for that crop will surely be produced—even so, due to this cause, the Saṅgha will certainly be divided in the future. And it will be divided by means of a quarrel, not by means of a schism of the Saṅgha. Therefore, it was said by the Blessed One to be 'divided.' And here, the repetition should be understood as being due to the meaning of agitation.

454. Etamatthaṃ [M 0.0432][V 0.0407] bhāsitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti kasmā evaṃ bhāsitvā pakkāmi? Sace hi bhagavā ukkhepake vā “akāraṇe tumhehi so bhikkhu ukkhitto”ti vadeyya, ukkhittānuvattake vā “tumhe āpattiṃ āpannā”ti vadeyya, “etesaṃ bhagavā pakkho, etesaṃ bhagavā pakkho”ti vatvā āghātaṃ bandheyyuṃ, tasmā tantimeva ṭhapetvā etamatthaṃ bhāsitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.

454. Having spoken on this matter, he rose from his seat and departed. Why did he speak thus and depart? For if the Blessed One were to say to those who performed the suspension, 'You have suspended that monk without cause,' or to the followers of the suspended one, 'You have committed an offense,' they might say, 'The Blessed One is on their side, the Blessed One is on their side,' and thus harbor animosity. Therefore, setting aside that very textual tradition, he spoke on this matter, rose from his seat, and departed.

455. Attanā vā attānanti ettha yo saṅghena ukkhepanīyakatānaṃ adhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe nisinno “tumhe kiṃ bhaṇathā”ti tesañca itaresañca laddhiṃ sutvā “ime adhammavādino, itare dhammavādino”ti cittaṃ uppādeti, ayaṃ tesaṃ majjhe nisinnova tesaṃ nānāsaṃvāsako hoti, kammaṃ kopeti, itaresampi hatthapāsaṃ anāgatattā kopeti. Evaṃ attanā vā attānaṃ nānāsaṃvāsakaṃ karoti. Samānasaṃvāsakanti etthāpi yo adhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe nisinno “adhammavādino ime, itare dhammavādino”ti tesaṃ majjhaṃ pavisati, yattha vā tattha [P 5.1150] vā pana pakkhe nisinno “ime dhammavādino”ti gaṇhāti, ayaṃ attanā vā attānaṃ samānasaṃvāsakaṃ karotīti veditabbo.

455. Regarding 'By oneself, oneself': Herein, whichever monk—sitting in the faction of the wrong-speakers upon whom the act of suspension has been performed by the Saṅgha, asks 'What do you say?' and, having heard the doctrine of both them and the others, generates the thought, 'These are wrong-speakers, the others are right-speakers'—this one, even while sitting in their midst, becomes one of different communion from them. He invalidates the act. And because he has not come within the reach of the others, he invalidates the act. Thus, 'by oneself, one makes oneself one of different communion.' Regarding 'one of the same communion': Herein also, whichever monk, sitting in the faction of the wrong-speakers and knowing 'These are wrong-speakers, the others are right-speakers,' enters the midst of the latter; or else, sitting in whatever faction, holds the view, 'These are right-speakers'—this one should be understood as 'one who by oneself makes oneself one of the same communion.'

456. Kāyakammaṃ vacīkammanti ettha kāyena paharantā kāyakammaṃ upadaṃsenti, pharusaṃ vadantā vacīkammaṃ upadaṃsentīti veditabbā. Hatthaparāmāsaṃ karontīti kodhavasena hatthehi aññamaññaṃ parāmasanaṃ karonti. Adhammiyāyamāneti adhammiyāni kiccāni kurumāne. Asammodikāvattamānāyāti asammodikāya vattamānāya. Ayameva vā pāṭho. Sammodanakathāya avattamānāyāti attho. Ettāvatā na aññamaññanti ettha dve pantiyo katvā upacāraṃ muñcitvā nisīditabbaṃ, dhammiyāyamāne pana sammodikāya vattamānāya āsanantarikāya nisīditabbaṃ, ekekaṃ āsanaṃ antaraṃ katvā nisīditabbaṃ.

456. Herein, regarding 'bodily action, verbal action,' it should be understood that those who strike with the body show bodily action, and those who speak harshly show verbal action. As for 'they engage in mutual handling,' it means they handle each other with their hands out of anger. 'When engaging in what is not in accordance with the Dhamma' means when performing actions that are not in accordance with the Dhamma. 'When there is disharmony' means when disharmonious speech occurs. Or, this is the reading itself. The meaning is: when there is no harmonious talk. Herein, regarding 'to this extent, not with each other,' having formed two rows, one should sit, abandoning close proximity. But when a matter in accordance with the Dhamma is being performed and there is harmonious speech, one should sit with a seat's space in between, that is, having made a space of one seat each.

457-458. Mā bhaṇḍanantiādīsu “akatthā”ti pāṭhasesaṃ gahetvā “mā bhaṇḍanaṃ akatthā”ti evamattho daṭṭhabbo. Adhammavādīti ukkhittānuvattakesu aññataro.
