Ayaṃ pana bhikkhu bhagavato atthakāmo, ayaṃ kirassa adhippāyo [M 0.0433] “ime bhikkhū kodhābhibhūtā satthu vacanaṃ na gaṇhanti, mā bhagavā ete ovadanto kilamitthā”ti tasmā evamāha. Bhagavā pana “pacchāpi saññaṃ labhitvā oramissantī”ti tesaṃ anukampāya atītavatthuṃ āharitvā kathesi. Tattha anatthatoti anattho ato; etasmā me purisā anatthoti vuttaṃ hoti. Atha vā anatthatoti anatthado. Sesaṃ pākaṭameva.

457-458. In the phrases beginning with 'mā bhaṇḍanaṃ,' taking the remainder of the text as 'akattha,' the meaning should be understood thus: 'Do not make a quarrel.' As for 'one who speaks not in accordance with the Dhamma,' he is one among the followers of the suspended monk. But this monk desires the welfare of the Blessed One. This, it seems, was his intention: 'These monks, being overcome by anger, do not accept the Teacher's word; may the Blessed One not become weary admonishing them.' Therefore, he spoke thus. The Blessed One, however, thinking, 'Later, having regained awareness, they will desist,' out of compassion for them, brought forth a story of the past and taught. Therein, 'anattho' means 'harm from this'; it is said, 'From this man, harm comes to me.' Alternatively, 'anattho' means 'one who gives harm.' The rest is clear indeed.

464. Puthusaddotiādigāthāsu [V 0.0408] pana puthu mahā saddo assāti puthusaddo. Samajanoti samāno ekasadiso jano; sabbo cāyaṃ bhaṇḍanakārakojano samantato saddanicchāraṇena puthusaddo ceva sadiso cāti vuttaṃ hoti. Na bālo koci maññathāti tattha koci ekopi “ahaṃ bālo”ti na maññittha; sabbepi paṇḍitamāninoyeva. Nāññaṃ bhiyyo amaññarunti koci ekopi “ahaṃ bālo”ti ca na maññittha; bhiyyo ca saṅghasmiṃ bhijjamāne aññampi ekaṃ “mayhaṃ kāraṇā saṅgho bhijjatī”ti idaṃ kāraṇaṃ na maññitthāti attho.

464. But in the verses beginning with 'puthusaddo,' 'puthusaddo' means 'it has a great, loud sound.' 'Samajano' means a group of people who are similar, of one likeness. And it is said that this entire group of quarrel-makers, by emitting sound all around, is both 'puthusaddo' (having a loud sound) and 'sadiso' (similar, i.e., in their disposition for quarreling). As for 'Let no one think he is a fool,' therein not even a single one thought, 'I am a fool'; all were conceited, thinking themselves wise. As for 'They did not think of another more,' not even one thought, 'I am a fool'; and furthermore, when the Saṅgha was splitting, not one understood this other matter: 'The Saṅgha is splitting because of me.' This is the meaning.

Parimuṭṭhāti parimuṭṭhassatino. Vācāgocarabhāṇinoti rākārassa rassādeso kato[P 5.1151], vācāgocarā na satipaṭṭhānādigocarā. Bhāṇino ca kathaṃ bhāṇino? Yāvicchanti mukhāyāmaṃ yāva mukhaṃ pasāretuṃ icchanti, tāva pasāretvā bhāṇino, ekopi saṅghagāravena mukhasaṅkocaṃ na karotīti attho. Yena nītāti yena kalahena imaṃ nillajjabhāvaṃ nītā. Na taṃ vidūti na taṃ jānanti, “evaṃ sādīnavo aya”nti.

'They are bewildered' means their mindfulness is utterly lost. Regarding 'speakers whose pasture is speech,' the letter 'rā' has undergone shortening. Their pasture is speech; it is not the foundations of mindfulness and so on. And they are speakers. In what way are they speakers? As for 'as much as they wish, the stretching of the mouth,' it means they are accustomed to speaking, stretching their mouths open as much as they wish. Not even one contracts their mouth out of respect for the Saṅgha; this is the meaning. 'By which they are led' means the quarrel by which they have been led to this state of shamelessness. 'They do not know that' means they do not know that quarrel, thinking, 'This is so fraught with fault.'

Ye ca taṃ upanayhantīti taṃ “akkocchi maṃ, avadhi ma”ntiādikaṃ ākāraṃ ye ca upanayhanti. Sanantanoti porāṇo.

As for 'And those who bind that,' it refers to those who bind that state of enmity, such as 'He abused me, he struck me,' and so on. 'Sanantano' means an ancient principle.

Pareti paṇḍite ṭhapetvā tato aññe bhaṇḍanakārakā pare nāma. Te ettha saṅghamajjhe kalahaṃ karontā “mayaṃ yamāmase upayamāma; satataṃ samitaṃ maccusantikaṃ gacchāmā”ti na jānanti. Ye ca tattha vijānantīti ye tattha paṇḍitā “mayaṃ maccusamīpaṃ gacchāmā”ti vijānanti. Tato [M 0.0434] sammanti medhagāti evañhi te jānantā yonisomanasikāraṃ uppādetvā medhagānaṃ kalahānaṃ vūpasamāya paṭipajjanti.

As for 'others,' setting aside the wise, the other quarrel-makers are called 'others.' While making a quarrel here in the midst of the Saṅgha, they do not know this: 'We are perishing here; constantly, unceasingly, we go to the presence of death.' As for 'And those who know it there,' it means those wise ones there who know, 'We are going near death.' As for 'Thereby quarrels are stilled,' indeed, those wise ones, knowing thus, having generated wise attention, practice for the appeasement of quarrels and disputes.

Aṭṭhicchinnāti ayaṃ gāthā brahmadattañca dīghāvukumārañca sandhāya vuttā. Tesampi hoti saṅgati, kasmā tumhākaṃ na hoti, yesaṃ vo neva mātāpitūnaṃ aṭṭhīni chinnāni, na pāṇā hatā, na gavāssadhanāni haṭānīti.

This verse beginning with 'aṭṭhicchinnā' was spoken with reference to King Brahmadatta and Prince Dīghāvu. Even for them, reconciliation occurred. Why can there not be reconciliation for you, for whom the bones of your parents were not cut, lives were not taken, and cattle, horses, and wealth were not seized? This is the meaning.

Sace labhethātiādigāthā paṇḍitasahāyassa ca bālasahāyassa ca vaṇṇāvaṇṇadīpanatthaṃ vuttā. Abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayānīti pākaṭaparissaye ca paṭicchannaparissaye ca abhibhavitvā tena saddhiṃ attamano satimā careyya.

The verse beginning with 'sace labhetha' was spoken for the purpose of showing the virtues and non-virtues of a wise companion and a foolish companion. As for 'having overcome all dangers,' it means having overcome both manifest dangers and concealed dangers, one should wander with him, gratified and mindful.

Rājāva [V 0.0409] raṭṭhaṃ vijitanti yathā attano vijitaṃ raṭṭhaṃ mahājanakarājā ca arindamamahārājā ca pahāya ekakā cariṃsu; evaṃ careyyāti attho. Mātaṅgaraññeva nāgoti mātaṅgo araññe nāgova. Mātaṅgoti hatthī vuccati; nāgoti mahantādhivacanametaṃ. Yathā hi mātuposako mātaṅganāgo araññe eko cari, na ca pāpāni [P 5.1152] akāsi. Yathā ca pālileyyako, evaṃ eko care, na ca pāpāni kayirāti vuttaṃ hoti.

As for 'like a king a conquered kingdom,' the meaning is: just as King Mahājanaka and the great King Arindama, having abandoned their own conquered kingdom, wandered alone, so should one wander. As for 'like a mātaṅga elephant in the forest,' it means like a great mātaṅga elephant in the forest. An elephant is called 'mātaṅga'; this word 'nāga' is a term for 'great.' Indeed, just as the great mātaṅga elephant that supported its mother wandered alone in the forest and did no evil deeds, and just as Pālileyyaka did, so it is said that one should wander alone and should not do evil deeds.

Pālileyyakagamanakathā

The Story of the Journey to Pālileyyaka

467. Pālileyyake viharati rakkhitavanasaṇḍeti pālileyyakaṃ upanissāya rakkhitavanasaṇḍe viharati. Hatthināgoti mahāhatthī. Hatthikalabhehīti hatthipotakehi. Hatthicchāpehīti khīrūpakehi daharapotakehi. Chinnaggānīti tehi purato purato gacchantehi chinnaggāni khāyitāvasesāni khāṇusadisāni tiṇāni khādati. Obhaggobhagganti tena hatthināgena uccaṭṭhānato bhañjitvā bhañjitvā pātitaṃ. Assa sākhābhaṅganti etassa santakaṃ sākhābhaṅgaṃ te khādanti. Āvilānīti tehi paṭhamataraṃ otaritvā pivantehi ālulitāni kaddamodakāni pivati. Ogāhāti titthato.

467. As for 'He dwells in Pālileyyaka, in the Rakkhita forest grove,' it means: he dwells in the Rakkhita forest grove, depending on the village of Pālileyyaka. As for 'a great elephant,' it means a large elephant. As for 'with young elephants,' it means with elephant calves. As for 'with baby elephants,' it means with young, milk-drinking calves. As for 'with tips cut off,' it means: he has to eat grasses with tips cut off, the remains after being eaten, like stumps, by those going ahead of him. As for 'broken and broken again,' it means broken and broken again and caused to fall from a high place by that great elephant. As for 'his broken branch,' it means: they eat the broken branch belonging to him. As for 'stirred up,' it means: he has to drink the stirred-up muddy water from those who went down and drank first. As for 'enters the water,' it means from the landing place.

Nāgassa nāgenāti hatthināgassa buddhanāgena. Īsādantassāti rathaīsāsadisadantassa. Yadeko ramatī vaneti yasmā buddhanāgo viya ayampi hatthināgo eko pavivitto vane ramati; tasmāssa nāgassa [M 0.0435] nāgena cittaṃ sameti, ekībhāvaratiyā ekasadisaṃ hotīti attho.

As for 'of the great elephant with the Great One,' it means of the bull elephant with the Buddha, the Great One. As for 'with tusks like chariot poles,' it means with tusks similar to chariot shafts. As for 'as he delights alone in the forest,' it means: because this bull elephant also, like the Buddha, the Great One, delights alone and secluded in the forest; therefore, the mind of this great elephant accords with the mind of the Great One; the meaning is that it becomes identical through delight in the state of solitude.

Yathābhirantaṃ viharitvāti ettha temāsaṃ bhagavā tattha vihāsīti veditabbo. Ettāvatā kosambakehi kira ubbāḷho bhagavā temāsaṃ araññaṃ pavisitvā vasīti sabbattha kathā patthaṭā ahosi.

In the phrase 'Having dwelled as long as he pleased,' it should be understood that the Blessed One dwelled there for the three months of the rains retreat. By that time, the talk had spread everywhere that the Blessed One, having been harassed by the monks of Kosambī, reportedly entered the forest and dwelled there for the three months.

Atha kho kosambakā upāsakāti atha kho imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ sutvā kosambivāsino upāsakā.

As for 'Then the lay followers of Kosambī,' it means: then, having heard this conversation, the lay followers residing in Kosambī consulted.

Aṭṭhārasavatthukathā

The Discourse on the Eighteen Grounds

468. Adhammaṃ dhammotiādīni aṭṭhārasa bhedakaravatthūni saṅghabhedakakkhandhake vaṇṇayissāma.

468. We will explain the eighteen grounds for causing division, beginning with 'what is not Dhamma as Dhamma,' in the chapter on schism in the Saṅgha.

475. Taṃ [V 0.0410] ukkhittakaṃ bhikkhuṃ osāretvāti taṃ gahetvā sīmaṃ gantvā āpattiṃ desāpetvā kammavācāya osāretvā. Tāvadeva uposathoti taṃdivasameva uposathakkhandhake vuttanayeneva sāmaggīuposatho kātabbo.

475. As for 'Having reinstated that suspended monk,' it means: having taken him, gone to the boundary, made him confess the offense, and reinstated him by means of a formal act. As for 'That very Uposatha,' it means: on that very day, the Uposatha of concord should be performed in accordance with the method stated in the Uposatha section.

476. Amūlā mūlaṃ gantvāti na mūlā mūlaṃ gantvā; taṃ vatthuṃ avinicchinitvāti attho. Ayaṃ vuccati upāli saṅghasāmaggī atthāpetā byañjanūpetāti atthato apagatā, “saṅghasāmaggī”ti imaṃ pana byañjanamattaṃ upetā.

476. As for 'Not having gone from the root to the root,' it means: not having gone from the root to the root; the meaning is, not having decided that matter. This, Upāli, is called a 'harmony of the Saṅgha that has abandoned the meaning but is endowed with the letter'—meaning, it is devoid of the meaning, but is endowed with just this expression 'harmony of the Saṅgha.'

477. Saṅghassa kiccesūti saṅghassa karaṇīyesu uppannesu. Mantanāsūti [P 5.1153] vinayamantanāsu. Atthesu jātesūti vinayaatthesu uppannesu. Vinicchayesūti tesaṃyeva atthānaṃ vinicchayesu. Mahatthikoti mahāupakāro. Paggahārahoti paggaṇhituṃ vutto.

477. As for 'in the Saṅgha's affairs,' it means: when duties for the Saṅgha have arisen. As for 'in discussions,' it means: when Vinaya discussions have arisen. As for 'when meanings have arisen,' it means: when meanings of the Vinaya have arisen. As for 'in decisions,' it means: in decisions regarding those very meanings. As for 'of great benefit,' it means: of great assistance. As for 'worthy of encouragement,' it means: suitable to be encouraged.

Anānuvajjo paṭhamena sīlatotiādimhiyeva tāva sīlato na upavajjo. Avekkhitācāroti apekkhitācāro; ālokite vilokite sampajānakārītiādinā nayena upaparikkhitācāro. Aṭṭhakathāsu pana “appaṭicchannācāro”ti vuttaṃ.

As for 'Not blameworthy in the first virtue,' it means: first of all, in the beginning itself, not blameworthy in terms of virtue. As for 'of considered conduct,' it means: of considered conduct; of scrutinized conduct, in the manner of 'acting with full awareness in looking forward and looking around,' and so on. But in the commentaries, it is said, 'of unconcealed conduct.'

Visayhāti [M 0.0436] abhibhavitvā. Anuyyutaṃ bhaṇanti anuññātaṃ anapagataṃ bhaṇanto. Yasmā hi so anuyyutaṃ bhaṇati, usūyāya vā agatigamanavasena vā kāraṇāpagataṃ na bhaṇati, tasmā atthaṃ na hāpeti. Usūyāya pana agatigamanavasena vā bhaṇanto atthaṃ hāpeti, kāraṇaṃ na deti, tasmā so parisagato chambhati ceva vedhati ca. Yo īdiso na hoti, ayaṃ “paggahāraho”ti dasseti.

As for 'having overcome,' it means: having overwhelmed. As for 'he speaks what is consistent,' it means: speaking what is permitted, what is not devoid of reason. For because he speaks consistently, and does not speak what is devoid of reason out of envy or by way of going down a wrong course, therefore he does not cause the meaning to be lost. But one who speaks out of envy or by way of going down a wrong course causes the meaning to be lost and does not give a reason; therefore, having gone to an assembly, he becomes stiff and trembles. One who is not like this is shown to be 'worthy of encouragement.'

Kiñca bhiyyo “tatheva pañha”nti gāthā, tassattho – yathā ca anuyyutaṃ bhaṇanto atthaṃ na hāpeti, tatheva parisāya majjhe pañhaṃ pucchito samāno na ceva pajjhāyati, na ca maṅku hoti. Yo hi atthaṃ na jānāti, so pajjhāyati. Yo vattuṃ na sakkoti, so maṅku hoti. Yo pana atthañca jānāti, vattuñca sakkoti; so na pajjhāyati, na maṅku hoti. Kālāgatanti kathetabbayuttakāle āgataṃ. Byākaraṇārahanti pañhassa atthānulomatāya byākaraṇānucchavikaṃ. Vacoti vadanto; evarūpaṃ vacanaṃ bhaṇantoti attho. Rañjetīti toseti. Viññūparisanti viññūnaṃ parisaṃ.

What more is to be said? The verse beginning "just so with a question." Its meaning is as follows: Just as one speaking consistently does not cause the meaning to be lost, in the same way, when asked a question in the midst of an assembly, he neither broods nor becomes downcast. For one who does not know the meaning broods. One who is not able to speak becomes downcast. But one who both knows the meaning and is able to speak, he neither broods nor becomes downcast. "Arrived at the time" means: arrived at the time suitable for speaking. "Worthy of explanation" means: suitable for explanation due to its conformity with the meaning of the question. "Speech" means: speaking; the meaning is speaking such a word. "He pleases" means: he satisfies. "The assembly of the wise" means: the assembly of the wise.

Ācerakamhi [V 0.0411] ca saketi attano ācariyavāde. Alaṃ pametunti vīmaṃsituṃ taṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ paññāya tulayituṃ samattho. Paguṇoti kataparicayo laddhāsevano. Kathetaveti kathetabbe. Viraddhikovidoti viraddhaṭṭhānakusalo.

"And in his own teacher's" means: in his own teacher's doctrine. "Able to measure" means: able to investigate, to weigh that and that reason with wisdom. "Proficient" means: one who has practiced, one who has obtained cultivation. "In what should be spoken" means: in what should be spoken. "Skilled in what is faulty" means: skilled in the place of error.

Paccatthikā yena vajantīti ayaṃ gāthā yādise kathetabbe paguṇo, taṃ dassetuṃ vuttā. Ayañhettha attho – yādisena kathitena paccatthikā ca niggahaṃ gacchanti, mahājano ca saññapanaṃ gacchati; saññattiṃ avabodhanaṃ gacchatīti [P 5.1154] attho. Yañca kathento sakaṃ ādāyaṃ attano ācariyavādaṃ na hāpeti, yasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ adhikaraṇaṃ uppannaṃ, tadanurūpaṃ anupaghātakaraṃ pañhaṃ byākaramāno tādise kathetabbe paguṇo hotīti.

The verse "By which opponents go" was spoken to show in what kind of speech one is proficient. This is the meaning here: by what kind of speech both opponents go to subjugation and the great populace goes to understanding; the meaning is, it goes to comprehension, to realization. And speaking which, one does not cause one's own view, one's own teacher's doctrine, to be lost. When explaining a question that is suitable to the matter in which the legal issue has arisen, and which is non-injurious, one is proficient in such speech.

Dūteyyakammesu alanti aṭṭhahi dūtaṅgehi samannāgatattā saṅghassa dūteyyakammesu samattho. Suṭṭhu uggaṇhātīti samuggaho. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti [M 0.0437] – yathā nāma āhunaṃ āhutipiṇḍaṃ samuggaṇhanti, evaṃ pītisomanassajāteneva cetasā saṅghassa kiccesu samuggaho, saṅghassakiccesu tassa tassa kiccassa paṭiggāhakoti attho. Karaṃ vacoti vacanaṃ karonto. Na tena maññatīti tena vacanakaraṇena “ahaṃ karomi, saṅghabhāraṃ nittharāmī”ti na mānātimānaṃ jappeti.

"Fit for messenger duties" means: because of being endowed with the eight qualities of a messenger, he is capable in the Sangha's messenger duties. `Samuggaho` means: he takes up well. This is what is said: just as they take up well an offering, a gift of almsfood, so too, with a mind born of joy and gladness, he is a good taker-up in the Sangha's affairs; the meaning is that in the Sangha's affairs, he is a receiver of this and that duty. "Carrying out the word" means: carrying out the word. "He is not conceited because of that" means: because of that carrying out of the word, he does not generate pride and conceit, thinking, "I am doing it, I am discharging the Sangha's burden."

Āpajjati yāvatakesu vatthūsūti yattakesu vatthūsu āpattiṃ āpajjamāno āpajjati. Hoti yathā ca vuṭṭhitīti tassā ca āpattiyā yathā vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti. Ete vibhaṅgāti yesu vatthūsu āpajjati, yathā ca vuṭṭhānaṃ hoti, imesaṃ atthānaṃ jotakā ete vibhaṅgā. Ubhayassāti ubhaye assa. Svāgatāti suṭṭhu āgatā. Āpattivuṭṭhānapadassa kovidoti āpattivuṭṭhānakāraṇakusalo.

"In as many grounds as one incurs an offense" means: in whatever number of grounds one, while incurring an offense, incurs it. "And in what way there is emergence" means: in what way there is emergence from that offense. "These are the analyses" means: these analyses are illuminators of these meanings—in which grounds one incurs an offense, and in what way emergence occurs. "Of both" means: both are his. "Well-come" means: well-arrived. "Skilled in the matter of offense and emergence" means: skilled in the cause of offense and emergence.

Yāni cācaranti yāni ca bhaṇḍanakāraṇādīni ācaranto tajjanīyakammādivasena nissāraṇaṃ gacchati. Osāraṇaṃ taṃvusitassa jantunoti taṃ vattaṃ vusitassa jantuno, yā osāraṇā kātabbā, etampi jānāti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

"And what things one practices" means: while practicing those things that are causes of quarrels and so on, one is subject to expulsion by means of an act of censure, etc. "Readmission for the being who has lived it" means: for the being who has lived that practice, what readmission should be done—he knows this also. The rest is clear everywhere.

Kosambakakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Kosambaka section is finished.

Samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

In the Samantapāsādikā, a commentary on the Vinaya.

Mahāvaggavaṇṇanā samattā.

The explanation of the Mahāvagga is concluded.

Mahāvagga-aṭṭhakathā niṭṭhitā.

The Mahāvagga Commentary is completed.
